title: Word search
Democratic right under pressure from government plans to expand information gathering
lead: The government is collecting more and more information from demonstrations and demonstrators. There are also plans to expand that data collection further, in the form of, for example, online monitoring, observations by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> on the street, camera surveillance and requesting data from organisers. The <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> warns that this may deter people from demonstrating. "Some municipalities ask you for everything, think of citizen service numbers and social media accounts", says Jon Schilder, emeritus professor of constitutional and administrative law at the VU, on Spraakmakers.

title: Klaassen leads Ajax to easy win over ADO Den Haag
lead: Ajax stayed in the wake of leaders PSV with a trouble-free win over ADO Den Haag (3-0). Davy Klaassen played a leading role in the Johan Cruijff ArenA with two goals and an assist before half-time. The visitors played with ten men from the 37th minute. Matteo Waem was shown a red card for pulling at the shirt of the breakaway Tolu Arokodare.

title: From climate blunder to cutting jab: why youth protest slogans go viral
lead: In several cities across Europe, mainly young people are taking to the streets to protest housing shortages, high prices and the decline of education. Striking are the handmade protest signs they carry. They are often (ironic) one-liners that catch the eye. What message lies behind them? "Young people feel: 'This is about me!'"

title: Underlying tension at CDA congress over future of cabinet, also because of VVD's course
lead: CDA leader Henri Bontenbal foresees an exciting week for the cabinet. He will do 'everything' to gather enough support from the opposition in the coming days, he promised at the CDA congress in Almere. Meanwhile, grumbling can be heard among the opposition factions about the cabinet's latest negotiating strategy.

title: Inspectie waarschuwt tegen bepaalde condooms na Europese terugroeping
lead: De Nederlandse Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd (<entity id="org:inspectie-gezondheidszorg-en-jeugd">IGJ</entity>) waarschuwt consumenten om een bepaald merk condooms niet te gebruiken, omdat er een grotere kans bestaat dat het latex tijdens seks scheurt of barst.

title: After months of wrangling, House approves capital gains tax in box 3
lead: The first hurdle to introducing a capital gains tax has been cleared. The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> on Thursday evening approved the proposal of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to largely overhaul box 3 from 2029. Now it is up to <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>.

title: Practically educated people do have political influence
lead: Our democracy has a major problem because politics would only listen to the theoretically educated and not to the practically educated. Will Tiemeijer argues that this finding is not correct, but is merely the result of the chosen analytical method. A few years ago it was a remarkable finding: research showed that, when it comes down to it, […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Fortuna Sittard also win away match against Go Ahead Eagles
lead: Fortuna Sittard continue to perform beyond expectations in the Eredivisie. The Limburg side also won the away match against Go Ahead Eagles on Sunday: 0-1. Fortuna are firmly in seventh place, 6 points behind leaders PSV. Fortuna lost only twice in the first thirteen rounds.

title: Environmental services still falling short
lead: On 1 April, the environmental services were all supposed to have met their goals, but several continue to fall short on multiple points. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity>, CDA) sets a new deadline of 1 July next year and wants an explanation from the services that will also fail to comply by then.

title: Packed courtroom listens to motive of 'brains' behind attack on Tarwekamp: 'I felt used'
lead: Moshtag B., the alleged brains behind the fatal attack on the Hague Tarwekamp, wanted revenge on his 'unfaithful' ex-girlfriend, he states in court. He wanted back the thousands of euros he had lent her. "I felt used and wanted financial revenge."

title: Prisoners can be released up to four weeks earlier due to cell shortage
lead: Earlier measures to address the shortage have so far been insufficient, state secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> writes in a letter to the House of Representatives. The cell shortage is currently causing prisoners held in police cells to be unable to be transferred.

title: Dekker (FvD) after neo-Nazi documentary: 'Root them out completely'
lead: Forum for Democracy parliamentary leader Ralf Dekker says the Zembla documentary, which shows FvD members attending neo-Nazi cage fights, is shocking. He has expelled six members. He also calls on FvD members who sympathise with that ideology to end their membership.

title: International Koopmeiners scores for winning Juventus
lead: Juventus have secured a comfortable win over Venezia in the Italian football league. The side coached by Luciano Spalletti were too strong for them in Turin, winning 4-0. At half-time it was still 0-0.

title: The government is 'unreliable' for farmers, says the National Ombudsman: farmer Benschop feels 'treated appallingly'
lead: Farmers have "suffered from the actions of the government", the National Ombudsman writes in a new report. Due to changing rules and contradictory, unclear policy, farmers' trust has, according to <entity id="person:reinier-van-zutphen">Reinier van Zutphen</entity>, been lost. Dairy farmer Jarno Benschop: "They are letting me flounder."

title: Kabinet hoopt op meerderheid voor plan belasting op vermogenswinst
lead: De plannen van het kabinet voor een belasting op vermogenswinst zijn op koers om beide Kamers van het parlement te passeren na drie...

title: Ukraine hits Putin where it hurts
More than 350 sports clubs report data breach after cyberattack on AllUnited
lead: More than 350 Dutch sports clubs have reported a data breach following a cyberattack on software supplier AllUnited on Monday evening. That is what the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity> reported on Wednesday. A spokesperson for AllUnited said earlier that the exact number of affected associations was not yet known.

title: First ever water turtle born in the Dutch wild
lead: For the first time, a water turtle has successfully bred in the Dutch wild. A nest with young turtles has been found in Dirksland, South Holland. According to nature organisation Faunawatch, it concerns the non-native red-eared slider.

title: HPV-vaccinatie voor kinderen voorkomt 12,800 kankerdiagnoses
lead: Op basis van de huidige vaccinatiegraad in Nederland voorkomt de HPV-vaccinatie naar schatting 12,800 kankerdiagnoses voor de huidige generatie 0- tot 9-jarigen, volgens

title: Civil service cooperation in Noordoost-Twente pays off
lead: Municipal cooperation in Noordoost-Twente brings a noticeable improvement in quality, but without active steering there is a risk of losing grip through the municipal councils. That is what research by the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Rekenkamer</entity> Noordoost-Twente shows. Both Noaberkracht and the <entity id="org:gemeente-losser">Losser</entity>-<entity id="org:gemeente-enschede">Enschede</entity> cooperation function well and clearly add value, but success therefore still calls for lasting alertness. The audit office advises setting clear goals and periodically checking whether the…

title: Rejected asylum seekers to be sent from the Netherlands to Rwanda
lead: The first return hub outside Europe, a so-called 'return hub', is coming to Rwanda. The Netherlands and four other European countries announced today in Vienna that they will work with Rwanda on such a centre. The intention is that rejected asylum seekers from, among other countries, the Netherlands will eventually be sent there. Initially there will be a hundred reception places.

title: Global warming mainly affects their future, which is why they are at the climate summit
lead: Whatever the agreements at the climate summit in Turkey turn out to be, it is clear that global warming will probably no longer be limited to 1.5 degrees. That mainly affects young people like Merel, Fizza and Sohanur, who are fighting for their future in Turkey.

title: American voters settle the score with Trump: the midterms from Bureau Buitenland
lead: President Trump and his policies have been hard punished in the midterm elections in the United States. The results are still coming in, but it is clear that the Republicans are not only losing their majority in the House of Representatives as expected, but also in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>.

title: Peter's little brother was murdered by his mother with rat poison: 'I will never forget her look'
lead: "Where is mama?" asked Peter Smitskam at age 13 when his mother had just been arrested by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. She had murdered his 5-year-old little brother Eddie. "That is something... You don't think of that." For decades he walked around with questions, the most important being: why did she do it? The answers only came last year.

title: Crisis talks on the Jetten cabinet drag on: do the parties actually still want to continue together?
Partij voor de Dieren dient opnieuw wetsvoorstel in om wrede slachtmethoden te verbieden
lead: De dierenrechtenpartij PvdD zet zich opnieuw in om een wetsvoorstel aangenomen te krijgen dat een aantal...

title: Kluivert scores for Bournemouth as Chelsea lose to Leeds
lead: Justin Kluivert contributed a goal to a home win for Bournemouth over Nottingham Forest (2-0). The Dutch national team international scored the home side's second goal.

title: Vmbo pupils are better at maths than before. 'Striking break in trend'
Minister van Weel recounted and agrees with the Court of Audit: many unprocessed tax returns
Making money from a country at war: 'If there is peace in Ukraine, the Netherlands must be at the front'
lead: As Russian bombs fall on Kyiv, minister <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Sjoerd Sjoerdsma</entity> (D66) is travelling to Ukraine for trade. Why now, as the country faces a harsh winter? What do companies have to do there? Our correspondent Niels Klaassen followed Sjoerdsma's first aid and trade mission in the war zone.

title: High chance of an extra-high VNG contribution from 2028
lead: It is admittedly temporary, but according to the VNG board, municipalities will top up the coffers of their umbrella organisation in 2028, 2029 and 2030. The proposal is to raise the contribution in those years so that the structural shortfall of millions at the Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten is eliminated more quickly.

title: Discrimination on the rental market still a problem, especially for people with Moroccan-sounding names
lead: The discrimination monitor for housing rental shows that candidates with a Moroccan-sounding name in particular are discriminated against more often in the rental process. <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Minister Boekholt-O’Sullivan</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-vro">Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening</entity> wrote a letter about this to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> this week. In it she says that the approach to discrimination on the housing market is continuing.

title: Dutch police switch off twenty servers in major cyber operation, securing 6.4 million stolen data records worldwide
lead: The Dutch police have switched off twenty servers used to distribute malicious software. This took place during an international operation against cybercrime. More than 6.4 million stolen data records have been secured worldwide, the police reported on Thursday.

title: Cabinet makes new attempt to curb high land prices
lead: By calculating the land price in a different way, the cabinet hopes to put an end to speculatively high land prices. Housing minister <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Elanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan</entity> stresses that the measure is not a 'quick fix'.

title: Development cooperation must be 'overhauled', argues government adviser; not for the first time
Ministry LVVN launches campaign: choose a dog that suits you
Cabinet starts new studies into redistribution of municipal fund
lead: The cabinet is launching new studies that are to lead to a new distribution of the billions from the municipal fund. That is what minister <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Pieter Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The studies start in December and are to form the groundwork for a definitive recalibration of the fund and to align better with municipal practice.

title: Judge: permit for 'TikTok fries shop' in Amsterdam rightly extended
lead: The municipality of Amsterdam did not act wrongly in 2024 by extending the permit of Fabel Friet, a chip shop in Amsterdam so popular that long queues form outside its door every day. Residents had filed a lawsuit against the municipality, but according to the judge they cannot sufficiently prove that the nuisance comes solely from Fabel Friet.

title: Anne Cappendijk (23) lost her father and translated that loss into 92 road signs: 'There is not one route for grief'
Aunt Theodora and the rancid stench of VVD 'lobbying'
lead: The 'representatives' who threaten to bring down a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> to prevent millionaires from paying an extra two hundred euros a year have themselves a dubious past when it comes to 'lobbying'

title: FC Barcelona line up recovered De Jong in starting XI against Villarreal
lead: FC Barcelona starts Frenkie de Jong in the starting line-up for the league match against Villarreal. The international missed the Netherlands' last Nations League match against Germany (5-0 defeat) due to an injury.

title: Hours of debate bring no breakthrough on tax plan: now it must happen behind the scenes
lead: With still about 48 hours to the deadline, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> again debated last night on the tax plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. But the real debate, the real negotiations, are taking place behind the scenes.

title: No disorders found in Chris Jude, suspect in Lisa murder case
lead: After extensive observation at the Pieter Baan Centrum (PBC), no psychotic disorders or personality disorders have been established in Chris Jude, suspect in the case of the murder of 17-year-old Lisa. Three experts will be heard at the substantive hearing of the criminal case in January.

title: Closing Time | Protomartyr
lead: Protomartyr comes from Detroit, the city of Motown, Iggy Pop and Jack White. And also of decaying factory buildings, empty premises, poverty and crime. It is not surprising that a band from that city hangs a whole album on the metaphor of a decaying building, in this case a hotel. Hotel Usana symbolises the decay [...] Read more posts at Sargasso

title: Tax plan approved, what now?
lead: After a day of debating the Tax Plan in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> an answer has come to the question: is there support for the plan? The answer is 'Yes': both the tax plan and the amendment by Pro and Volt won a majority. Awkward for the VVD: they voted against the amendment and the tax plan, while their minister has to implement the policy.

title: Nitrogen law presented: this is what the new plans entail
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to ensure, half a year earlier than planned, that businesses and, for example, housing projects with small nitrogen emissions no longer have to apply for a permit. That is what Agriculture <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity> (D66) writes in a letter.

title: One of the smallest municipalities in the Netherlands may cease to exist
lead: The <entity id="org:gemeente-rozendaal">gemeente Rozendaal</entity> in Gelderland will most likely cease to exist in a few years. It is one of the smallest municipalities in the Netherlands. Rozendaal will merge with the neighbouring municipalities <entity id="org:gemeente-rheden">Rheden</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-brummen">Brummen</entity>.

title: Man paid for child abuse in the Philippines, youngest was only 2 years old: years-long prison sentence demanded
lead: If the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has its way, a 41-year-old man from Rotterdam will go to prison for years for seriously sexually abusing five Filipino children for a camera. The man paid for the sex shows with children, which he watched from the Netherlands. The youngest victim was only 2 years old.

title: Data centres used 5 percent of Dutch electricity last year
lead: Data centres used 5 percent of all electricity in the Netherlands last year, compared with 4.6 percent a year earlier. In total this amounted to over 5,600 gigawatt hours. The Netherlands therefore has the highest share of electricity consumption by data centres within the European Union after Ireland, reports the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS).

title: Politie zoekt getuigen van val van peuter uit raam in Amsterdam
lead: De politie zoekt getuigen van een incident in Amsterdam vorige maand, waarbij een jongetje van 1 jaar uit een raam op de derde verdieping in Amsterdam-Zuid viel.

title: Have your say: anyone who wants a dog must first take a course
lead: On Tuesday the campaign 'Vrienden voor het leven word je niet zomaar' (Friends for life don't just happen) starts. This government campaign calls on prospective dog owners to properly orient themselves, so that they can make a conscious choice for a dog that suits them. In De Kwestie we put a question or statement to our readers about this. Please respond below as well.

title: Number of HIV infections rises, calls for the prep pill grow
Netherlands and Suriname seek witnesses to a 1986 mass murder in Suriname
lead: Investigators from the Dutch Team Internationale Misdrijven (TIM) are working with a Surinamese investigation team to gather information about a mass murder that took place in Suriname in 1986. Witnesses are being asked to come forward via the TV programme Opsporing Verzocht.

title: 25,000 fewer civil servants? 'Only possible if politics also wants to do less'
lead: For the umpteenth time, a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> wants to reduce the number of civil servants. Previously that never succeeded. How can it succeed this time? "Politics must clearly say: this we will do and this we will no longer do."

title: Minister after delay at climate summit: 'Many ideas to get away from fossil fuels'
lead: <entity id="pos:minister-van-klimaat-en-groene-groei">Minister van Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity> Stientje van Veldhoven (D66) has arrived at the climate summit in Turkey after some delay caused by the cabinet turmoil. She mainly sees energy among countries that, like the Netherlands, are presenting plans on how they want to get away from fossil fuels.

title: LIVE US Midterms | Polling stations open in more than half of the states, problems with voting machines in New York state
lead: Americans head to the polling stations on Tuesday for the midterms, which could significantly change the balance of power in Congress. Voters are choosing on Tuesday for the House of Representatives, <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>, governors and local representatives. Follow everything about the midterms via our liveblog below.

title: Majority within reach for box 3 adjustment plan in House of Representatives
lead: The cabinet's plan to quickly tax gains from wealth in box 3 appears set to win a majority in the House of Representatives. In addition to coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA, support appears to be emerging on the right. JA21, SGP, BBB and BBB splinter Robert van Gasteren also say they support the supplementary bill on the box 3 system.

title: Gerke (26) never thought she could buy anything, now she lives in 32 m² in the Jordaan
Premier spreekt over geweld tegen joden tijdens Kristallnacht-dienst, niet over Rode Lijn-protest
lead: De 88e herdenking van Kristallnacht werd maandagavond in Amsterdam gehouden. Premier <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> hield een toespraak waarin hij het toenemende antisemitisme in Nederland veroordeelde.

title: Jaitsen Singh (81) dies, the face of Dutch prisoners abandoned abroad
Short trackers take silver behind South Korea in the relay
lead: The Dutch short trackers finished second in the relay at the World Tour in Seoul. Kay Huisman, Teun Boer, Niels Kingma and Jens van 't Wout had to concede victory to South Korea. Canada took bronze.

title: Emergency landing in the Philippines: passengers leave aircraft by slide
lead: In the Philippines, an aircraft made an emergency landing. The passengers left the plane, which was en route from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea, via the emergency slides. All 146 people on board were unharmed.

title: Trump does not appear interested in the security concerns surrounding Nvidia: 'The shares are rising again!'
What if the tax plan fails? 'Elections or new formation'
lead: It remains difficult for the minority cabinet to find support for the tax plan. According to political reporter Frits Wester, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has therefore completely lost control of the process. And if this plan fails, the consequences could be serious.

title: The Netherlands will send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda: can it just do that?
lead: The Netherlands wants to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is convinced that the plan, unlike an earlier British plan, will hold up in court. Reporters Hanneke Keultjes and Sander van Mersbergen, who have followed the file for years, explain how that works.

title: VVD on collision course with CDA and D66 over left-wing proposal: this is what it says
lead: PRO and Volt want to raise the tax on wealth. According to the right-wing parties in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> the consequences will be unprecedented, while left-wing and centre parties think the proposal is "being inflated too much". We explain what the plan involves.

title: Ko Colijn on how Putin could exploit Trump's loss of face in Ukraine
lead: <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> expert Ko Colijn has been providing the Dutch with explanation of armed conflicts for fifty years. This time he discusses how Russian President Vladimir Putin could exploit the outcome of the midterms in the United States to force something more in Ukraine.

title: Cabinet saved, interim formation or new elections? 'Voters think anyway: what a mess'
lead: Tension in The Hague: can this cabinet still be saved, or is it curtains? Our political correspondent and commentator Hans van Soest explains the three scenarios. "Either way, the relations between the parties are completely poisoned. Between all parties."

title: Call out | What questions do you have about the turmoil in the cabinet? (closed)
lead: The vote on the tax plan led to a chaotic political week. The coalition held lengthy talks over the weekend about how to move forward. What questions do you have about the current political situation and the crisis week in The Hague?

title: No comfort for the Netherlands
lead: We watched poor Eva Wiessing of the NOS for days shivering at the gates of a Hilversum estate, where four Dutch politicians had to eat dust for the defeat they had inflicted on a female colleague.

title: Senate votes to expand embryo law: culturing embryos to be allowed for research
Coalition tries to patch things up today in crisis talks, but 'Jetten and Yesilgöz are miles apart'
lead: On Saturday the political crisis talks continue in Hilversum. There D66 prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> wants to try to save his minority cabinet. But chaos reigns, and a cabinet collapse seems no longer avoidable. VVD leader Yesilgöz demands a sharp shift to the right, but D66 and CDA cannot go along with that. Our reporter Niels Klaassen looks ahead.

title: 'My lamp is a bit too strong': during Amsterdam's evening rush hour, some cyclists are dazzled by bike lights
Cold, dry and sunny: wintry weather continues
lead: Good news for winter lovers: today the day starts with frost, although in some parts of the country there is a chance of mist banks. It remains cold today, though the sun shines brightly and it stays almost everywhere dry.

title: 'The decision has already been made': internal emails reveal Marechaussee criticism of border controls
lead: The Royal Netherlands Marechaussee (KMar) had serious reservations behind the scenes about the border controls of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Schoof. Internal emails show how KMar staff viewed the political decision-making and the practical feasibility of the controls, as well as the disappointing results. The legal restrictions on returning asylum seekers were also known before the introduction. This is evident from documents that journalists Noortje Smeltink and Wisse Beets obtained under the Open Government Act (Woo) for their VPRO podcast Grensgeval.

title: Netherlands national team to face Portugal in Nations League quarter-finals
lead: The Netherlands national team under head coach Xavi Hernández will take on Portugal in the Nations League quarter-finals. That is the outcome of the draw at the office of the European football association UEFA in Nyon.

title: The cabinet has reached a 'crucial moment', says CDA leader Bontenbal. 'Gambling on a majority is irresponsible'
Lawsuit against Tata: will the steel plant get a multi-million euro fine?
lead: Did Tata Steel deliberately emit harmful substances that are bad for the health of local residents? That question is central today in a major criminal case against the steel plant in IJmuiden. Reporter Simone Vogel is following the case.

title: Top executive Jensen Huang steps down at Nvidia, and exports to China stop immediately
lead: The American chip company Nvidia is stopping the supply of so-called Hopper chips to China. These chips are designed for artificial intelligence (AI). Sales of these chips to Chinese customers still brought the company 2.4 billion dollars in the third quarter.

title: Four men arrested for poaching hares with dogs
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> of Rotterdam has arrested four men on suspicion of poaching. The men chased hares in a field with hunting dogs, which is illegal.

title: VVD obstructs parliamentary debate on tax bungler Eelco Heinen (also VVD)
lead: Opposition parties called this "uncollegial" and "unhygienic"

title: AFM fears shift of high-risk clients to audit firms with less strict requirements
lead: The Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) points to possible risks now that increasing numbers of accountancy audits are being carried out by firms that are not subject to the strictest requirements.

title: At 11.00 am talks between Jetten and Yeşilgöz, future of coalition unclear
lead: The tax plan was passed yesterday by <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, but has no support from coalition party VVD. Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> (D66) is meeting this morning with deputy prime ministers Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA) and will 'do everything' to hold the coalition together. Follow everything in our live blog.

title: Isolated tribe in the Amazon asks for food during rare contact
lead: Remarkable images from the Brazilian Amazon: an isolated tribe has come into contact with outsiders there for the first time in decades. The images, shared by a British human rights organisation, show members of the Awá tribe. They reportedly asked for food. Their habitat is likely threatened by logging.

title: Geen treinen door Rotterdam Centraal op 7 en 8 november vanwege grote werkzaamheden
lead: Er rijden op zaterdag 7 november en zondag 8 november 2026 geen treinen naar, van of door Rotterdam Centraal, omdat ProRail het spoorseinsysteem rond het station vervangt.

title: Iris (36) had to turn her life around due to massive debt: 'Eating out, expensive workout classes, shopping: I don't do that anymore'
At Home in the Netherlands
lead: Roelant Siekman on 3 years ago

title: In a country with a water surplus, drinking water supply is far too fragile, says this hydrologist. 'That is a system failure'
lead: We need to move towards a less fragmented, resilient drinking water supply that can keep delivering drinking water even in times of drought, says this hydrologist. "We can carry on like this and wait for the next extreme drought. Or we can take the first steps now towards a transition."

title: Video: they took part in the Red Line demonstration in Amsterdam
Antonelli takes grid penalty for engine change in Las Vegas
lead: Kimi Antonelli, the Formula 1 world champion, must move five places back on the starting grid at next Sunday's Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Italian of Mercedes receives that grid penalty for replacing his combustion engine.

title: Group photo at G20 cancelled because ministers did not want to be pictured with Lavrov
lead: The traditional group photo at the start of the G20 meeting in Atlanta, United States, has been cancelled. Several ministers of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> did not want to be photographed with their Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov.

title: Sea swallowing Bonaire, 'Netherlands offers too little help'
lead: The southern part of Bonaire could be completely under water as early as 2040. Residents are trying to turn the tide, but feel that the Netherlands is doing too little to protect the island.

title: More ultrasounds, demands and nonsense advice from influencers: over 40-plus years, these OLVG midwives watched their profession change
Cabinet sticks to nitrogen plans despite criticism from farmers and 'right-wing trio'
Feyenoord expected to field new goalkeeper and recovered Hadj Moussa against FC Porto
lead: Feyenoord has had a difficult time in recent weeks. The side of Giovanni van Bronckhorst play the important Champions League match against FC Porto tonight. Follow it live here from 21.00 hours.

title: Why does FvD keep ducking and slipping away?
New institute must accelerate innovation
NOC*NSF wants Olympic village close to Thialf in Heerenveen in 2030
lead: NOC*NSF has CunaBula, a residential and sports complex in Heerenveen, in view as the location for the Olympic village during the 2030 Winter Games. Long-track speed skating will then take place at the Thialf ice stadium.

title: Joshua (19) cannot wait to move into rented rooms: 'My mother actively helps with the search'
Jetten cabinet 'chooses the way forward'
lead: Stubborn minority fails to secure a majority

title: Three moderators of subreddit r/Amsterdam on what they encounter: 'Station Lelylaan has really become an inside joke'
The theatre adaptation of Klaus Mann's "Mefisto" wants to get you thinking with discussions, poetry and song. But you do not get much time for it
lead: In Maya Arad Yasur's stage adaptation, Hendrik seems to struggle a little more and more sincerely with the choices that come his way. This is partly due to an extra character added to the story: that of the 'agent of the sun'.

title: ANWB staff may strike on Monday, but Wegenwacht must remain minimally staffed
lead: On Monday ANWB employees lay down their work for twelve hours due to the stalled collective labour agreement negotiations. That the nationwide strike will go ahead is certain, but the Wegenwacht and alarm centre may not be shut down completely, according to the court. Trade unions FNV and CNV must ensure minimum staffing to prevent dangerous situations.

"The time of concern is over, there is now talk of fear and danger," says mayor <entity id="person:jan-zwiers">Jan Zwiers</entity> of <entity id="org:gemeente-midden-drenthe">Midden-Drenthe</entity> to the Algemeen Dagblad.

title: Chaos complete: over the millionaire tax, VVD threatens to vote against its own cabinet's entire tax plan
lead: The VVD will vote against the cabinet's entire tax plan if the millionaire tax is retained. That makes the chaos complete: the coalition party would then vote against its own cabinet's proposal and against its coalition partners. And the tax plan will then really be defeated.

title: Ukrainian President Zelensky visits King Willem-Alexander and Prime Minister Jetten on Wednesday
Tens of millions of gamers play GTA 6 for over 4 hours a day, Sony also reports another record
lead: More than 39 million gamers have played Grand Theft Auto 6 on a PlayStation 5 in the first days after the game was released. That is what Sony, the company behind the PlayStation, reports. The new game in the popular series came out late on Wednesday night into Thursday last week, after thirteen years.

title: New setback for Jannik Sinner: top tennis player also misses Australian Open after knee operation
lead: Jannik Sinner has undergone a successful operation on his right knee, but will not return to the tennis court in the coming months. That is what his doctor Herbert Schönhuber told Rai Südtirol. It means the Italian world number 2 will at least miss the Australian Open.

title: Overheated labour market cools further
lead: The labour market remains tight, but slightly less so than before. In the third quarter of 2026 the number of unemployed rose slightly, according to figures from <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS).

title: Jetten: mostly positive reactions to baby news, negativity 'unfortunately is part of it'
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> responds on camera for the first time since he and his fiancé Nicolás Keenan announced the arrival of their baby.

title: Jetten leaves further adjustments to the tax plan to the House of Representatives
Behind closed doors | Yesilgöz gets a tip: 'Accept that you are no longer the biggest'
lead: In the column Binnenskamers, political reporter Edo van der Goot writes weekly about what strikes him in The Hague. This week: <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> must teach politicians what presenting oneself as vulnerable means.

title: Senate narrowly approves growing embryos for scientific research
lead: The Senate agrees to an expansion of the Embryo Act. From now on, embryos may be grown for scientific research. This could, among other things, make IVF treatments more successful and provide knowledge about hereditary diseases. Opponents emphasise the "protected status of an embryo as human life".

title: Cabinet: Landowner must contribute more to everything that makes a new neighbourhood liveable: from roundabout to city park
Nederlandse Kamerleden willen basisschoolleerlingen verbieden generatieve AI te gebruiken
lead: De <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity>, het lagerhuis van het Nederlandse parlement, wil basisschoolleerlingen verbieden generatieve artificiële intelligentie (AI) te gebruiken.

title: Man arrested over involvement in death of 19-year-old in Volendam swimming pool
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested a suspect on Monday in connection with a fatal incident in Volendam. In June, officers found the body of a nineteen-year-old man in a swimming pool.

title: FvD declares itself free of Nazism, but spreads virulent hatred of migrants
Collective agreement dispute in regional transport drags on: 'New strike unavoidable'
lead: A nationwide strike in regional public transport threatens again. A large majority of members of unions CNV and FNV do not agree with the employers' final offer. However, members are overwhelmingly in favour of new actions. "That will really be a full strike", says CNV spokesman Kees de Vos to RTL Z.

title: Minister has barely any insight into gold reserve of 72 billion euros, Court of Audit warns
lead: The <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> barely has themselves informed about the management of our national gold reserve of 612 tonnes, which is worth over 72 billion euros. The Algemene Rekenkamer, which is critical, concludes this.

title: Van Bronckhorst: Excelsior create more than us, that says it all
lead: Coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst is desperate for a win with Feyenoord. His side also lost the city derby against Excelsior (2-3). "Excelsior create more than we do here," he told ESPN. "That says it all."

title: Closing Time | R.L. Burnside
lead: This recording of blues singer and guitarist R.L. Burnside (1926 - 2005) was made by musicologist Alan Lomax at Burnside's house in Mississippi. Burnside had made music his whole life, but until then had never been able to live off it. Only in 1995 did that change, when Jon Spencer […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Paris Saint-Germain fear a long lay-off for injured Doué
lead: PARIS (ANP/DPA) - Paris Saint-Germain fear that Désiré Doué will be out for a long time. The French international has probably suffered a serious knee injury in Saturday's match against OGC Nice.

title: Group of Dutch people remain unharmed in attack in Krakow: 'It happened right in front of them'
lead: A group of friends from Rossum (Overijssel) remained unharmed in the attack this afternoon in the Polish city of Krakow. In the city centre, according to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, at least six people were killed and more than fifteen injured when a motorist opened fire indiscriminately. The people from Rossum were nearby.

title: Cow plague in North Macedonia: 'They eat everything bare'
lead: More than a thousand stray cows are causing considerable nuisance in a North Macedonian municipality. The mayor therefore wants the government to declare a state of emergency.

title: Another large turnout at Rode Lijn protest: 'Cheers erupt when the government or Prime Minister Jetten is criticised'
Cabinet wants to restrict transparency law
lead: The cabinet wants to save 3.5 billion over the coming years at central government. To achieve this goal, it is also overhauling the Open Government Act (Woo). That has major consequences for the transparency of public administration. Ministries want to review again which government documents can be requested by citizens and journalists.

title: The cabinet promises: within one week the Tax Plan will have a majority
lead: This week the Jetten cabinet is speaking with the opposition to build majorities. It has not freed up much negotiating room: the cabinet is considering a labour tax cut of 350 million euros.

title: Paternotte (D66) does not see talks with opposition as a desperate move: 'Certainly not'
lead: D66 parliamentary leader Jan Paternotte will talk with opposition parties about the tax plan, in the hope of gathering sufficient support for it in the House of Representatives and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. Paternotte does not think it is total chaos, nor a desperate move. "Certainly not."

title: Minister names 5 new locations for accelerated construction of 25,000 homes
Video | Confused Man Is Taken Away After Charging at Willem-Alexander
Let Guus Hiddink coach the coalition
After 4 days of talks still no white smoke: how the crisis meeting over the Jetten cabinet has gone so far
lead: The leadership of the coalition has now been in talks for 4 days over the cabinet crisis that has arisen. The outcome is still uncertain. And so the crucial question remains: will the Netherlands still have a cabinet at the end of the week?

title: Jetten speaks at Kristallnacht commemoration: 'Violence against Jews is never far away'
lead: "The lesson of history is that violence against Jews is never far away." That is what Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> said on Monday at the National Kristallnacht Commemoration in the Portuguese Synagogue in Amsterdam. He warned against the renewed stirring up of antisemitism in the Netherlands.

title: Women's football World Cup 2031 in US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica
lead: ZÜRICH (ANP/RTR) - The Women's World Cup football tournament will take place in 2031 in the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. FIFA announced this on Monday. The 2035 World Cup goes to England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

title: Amsterdam to keep Willinklaan asylum center open 10 to 15 years longer: 'Given the national chaos, I dare not promise other locations will close'
Podcast: Neo-Nazis, Nota Ruimte and fallen coalitions
lead: In the Binnenlands Bestuur series Bespreekt de Week, John Bijl, director of the Periklesinstituut, and Anna Pleijsier, editor and presenter at Binnenlands Bestuur, give you a weekly update on all the most important political and administrative local government news. This week: Is neo-Nazism connected to our politics? What does the Nota Ruimte mean for the provincial States elections in March? How did the elections go in <entity id="org:gemeente-hilversum">Hilversum</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-wijdemeren">Wijdemeren</entity>? Which coalitions have already fallen? And your wife…

title: Shortage of funds for infrastructure: 'The cake must not only get bigger, the cake can also get bigger'
lead: When it comes to infrastructure in the Netherlands, the shortage of money for replacement and renewal is one of the biggest challenges. This is again evident at the round table discussion that will be held on Wednesday in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> with governments and market parties.

title: Cabinet wants to legally ban smoking at petting farms and playgrounds
lead: Smoking at petting farms, managed playgrounds and on the outdoor grounds of childcare centres (bso's and kinderdagverblijven) will be banned by law. A proposal by Minister of Health <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> (VVD) will be discussed tomorrow in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, insiders at the political desk of RTL Nieuws confirm.

title: Ghent police investigate report about far-right fight clubs after Zembla documentary
lead: The police in Ghent have received a report about the possible presence of far-right fight clubs in the city. The report was made following the Zembla report and the VRT programme Pano about far-right networks.

title: Municipalities prepare for possible Gen Z protests this weekend, student unions pull out
Child of married couple no longer automatically receives father's surname
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants children to no longer automatically receive only their father's surname if the parents do not agree on the name. An adopted motion to that effect from PRO and D66 has been turned into a bill that goes into consultation in January. Stakeholders will then have the opportunity to give their views before the bill is submitted.

title: How Belgian cocaine money penetrates Belgium: 'It didn't use to be so deep in the system'
lead: Belgian justice wants to crack the business model of the cocaine trade, but still lacks the firepower. That is what the highest prosecutor and the highest judge at the Antwerp court of appeal say.

title: Jesse Klaver wins at international summit against billionaires
lead: 'A divided left loses, a united left wins'

title: House of Representatives wants a cheaper year-round public transport subscription, cabinet to act
lead: The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> wants it to become cheaper not only in summer but all year round to take a public transport subscription that allows travellers unlimited travel outside peak hours. The cabinet must now investigate whether that is possible and how it can be done.

title: Erasmus shooter received life imprisonment, OM demands 30 years' imprisonment and TBS on appeal
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has demanded thirty years' imprisonment and TBS with compulsory admission on appeal against the 35-year-old Fouad L., the so-called 'Erasmus shooter', for three murders among other things. L. was sentenced last year to life imprisonment.

title: Nobody knows how to do it, dying. Perhaps that is why we are so afraid of it
lead: However many rituals we hang around it, in the end we still die alone, writes Corine Nijenhuis. By seeing death as a carefully guarded secret, we may perhaps be able to overcome our fear of the uncertain end of our existence.

title: Customs intercepts 1.7 million counterfeit Pokémon cards in Rotterdam port
lead: Customs has intercepted more than 1.7 million counterfeit Pokémon cards in the port of Rotterdam. A customs officer did not trust the cards in a container. After checking, they turned out to be counterfeit. All cards have been destroyed.

title: Across the border: AI listens in when citizens get angry with officials
lead: In two meeting rooms of the town hall in the Japanese municipality of Toride, artificial intelligence listens in on conversations between officials and residents. The system is mainly meant to help prevent aggression and intimidation at the counter.

title: Now that the e-scooter is legal, no pedestrian's life will be safe
lead: The new electric scooter from Bas van Putten reaches nearly supersonic speeds at top speed. He thinks it has potential to succeed the fatbike as a socially divisive issue.

title: Oxfam Novib: Gaza Strip seriously polluted by Israeli violence
lead: Israeli military violence has seriously polluted the Gaza Strip, according to a new analysis based on satellite images by Oxfam Novib. It concerns the air, the soil and the water, where there are signs of toxic contamination. This is caused, among other things, by the large-scale use of explosives.

title: Netherlands nominates Knot as candidate for ECB presidency
lead: Former <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity> president Klaas Knot is considered one of the favourites to succeed ECB President Christine Lagarde. Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos is also said to have a good chance.

title: Will the cabinet fall?
lead: D66 and CDA have reached an agreement with the left on the tax plan. The tax burden shifts from labour to wealth as a result. The VVD, which strongly opposed this, is so far silent. Will the VVD cause the cabinet to fall because wealthy people have to pay more tax? Earlier I already wrote that for the VVD, governing is more important than […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Minister Berendsen: 'We will not be intimidated by Russia'
lead: The Netherlands will not be intimidated by Russia. That is what Minister <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> Berendsen (CDA) says after a tweet from the Russian embassy. Yesterday defence manufacturer Destinus announced that one of its missiles was involved in the attack on the Crimean Bridge. According to Russia, this means the Netherlands is directly drawn into the war.

title: Behind the scenes 'very ugly words' fell in coalition: 'Van den Brink's remark was revealing'
lead: Although the three coalition parties are continuing and speak of 'restored trust', the past week appears to have caused considerable damage. Behind the closed doors of the crisis talks 'very ugly words' were spoken, says parliamentary reporter Tobias den Hartog. "The slip of the tongue by Van den Brink at the press conference was revealing."

title: Can the minority cabinet still be saved? 'VVD is going all in'
lead: Will <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> fall tomorrow? That is the big question now that the VVD is openly doubting the coalition, after a deal between D66 and CDA with opposition parties PRO and Volt on the tax plan.

title: Bunschoten wants to explore legal steps against forced asylum reception
lead: The Utrecht municipality of Bunschoten wants to take legal steps to prevent forced reception of asylum seekers. A proposal calling on the college of mayor and aldermen to investigate this was adopted on Thursday by four of the five parties on the municipal council.

title: Cabinet is still playing bluff poker with its tax plan, which seems to be working in the House of Representatives, with the Senate still to come
Should our adult son adapt if we want to eat vegetarian?
LIVE | Brekelmans (VVD) demands reflection from Prime Minister Jetten on his own role, Bontenbal had 'no grip on communication deal'
lead: How can and should the minority cabinet of Prime Minister Jetten continue at all? Government parties D66 and CDA struck a deal with PRO and Volt, to the great fury of the VVD. From 10.15 a.m. <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> continues debating the tax plan. Follow everything on the rising political tensions in The Hague here in the liveblog and in the livestream above.

title: Cabinet wants its own AI course, but the US and China are never far away
lead: The Jetten cabinet will present a vision on AI on Friday. That vision states that the Netherlands is committed to achieving open strategic autonomy, but that at the same time 'targeted AI diplomacy' is being deployed to secure Dutch access to advanced AI capabilities.

title: Minor robbed of fatbike at gunpoint, police seek witnesses
The Hague investigates damage claims from people who incited violence
lead: The Hague alderman Richard de Mos (Economy and City Centre) wants to investigate how people who called for looting and violence on social media in recent days can be held financially liable for the damage suffered by Hague entrepreneurs as a result. He announced this on Sunday.

title: Coalition moves to an open marriage over tax plan: parties 'possibly' give each other free rein in the vote
Microsoft Edge browser scores worse on privacy than alternatives
lead: The central government commissioned a privacy study of various internet browsers. Microsoft Edge for Business does not come out well. SLM Cloud now advises providers of workplace services to investigate whether Mozilla Firefox Enterprise can serve as an alternative. For the longer term, Vivaldi Browser is a sovereign option.

title: Cabinet and opposition let it come to a head: chaos looms over taxes
lead: The Hague is still not used to working with a minority cabinet. Chaos looms at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> because the cabinet and parliament still disagree over new tax rules. Both sides are letting it come down to the last moment, hoping the other will give in.

title: Wild boar, unclaimed graves and rising maintenance costs: why burial in the municipality of Hattem may cost money
lead: The <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> debates municipal budgets on Tuesday. For many of them, money remains a problem, as has become clear in recent months. Sometimes the choice is not easy, as is evident at the Hattem cemetery.

title: 'The Netherlands is seen as a politically unstable country': professor Rob de Wijk on how the world views the cabinet crisis
lead: Europe is talking today and tomorrow in Dublin about security, autonomy and AI. But there is an empty chair. Almost all European heads of government are there, but <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> has to stay in The Hague because of the cabinet crisis. So the Netherlands is not taking part. "Regrettable."

title: Nearly all Anthropic staff become millionaires after IPO
lead: Following Anthropic's IPO, nearly the entire workforce of the company has become millionaires. They were partly paid in shares, and those are now worth a great deal of money. As a result, some are now worth on paper even more than 100 million dollars (91 million euros).

title: The man of $1000 mrd
lead: The problem with superstar CEOs is not so much a lack of countervailing power, but the unwillingness to use it, writes FD columnist Anna Dijkman.

title: How press photographer Bart Maat tries to take THE news photo during political chaos
lead: Every politician arriving at <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> is surrounded by TV cameras and photographers. How do you take THE news photo of the day in such conditions? Press photographer Bart Maat has spent the whole day in the centre of power during a political crisis.

title: Asylum minister stands up for threatened asylum seekers, citizens and councillors
lead: There is no incident code in police systems for a criminal offence committed by someone who also took part in a citizens' patrol. Adding one would impose too great an administrative burden on the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, and as far as is known there are no signs that this is happening on a large scale, so this is justifiable. That is what <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA), minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>, writes in a recent letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: OM wants to reach Sierra Leone residents with 2 million euro tip money
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is raising the reward for the golden tip about 'Bolle Jos' Leijdekkers to 2 million euros. With the higher reward, Justice also wants to reach the local population in Sierra Leone, in the hope that someone shares information about him. The drug criminal is said to be hiding there.

title: National Ombudsman: government pursued unreliable policy for farmers. 'They have suffered'
Kamerleden willen e-gates op Amsterdam Centraal om vertragingen van Eurostar-treinen naar Londen te beperken
lead: Een brede meerderheid in de <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> heeft opgeroepen tot elektronische poortjes bij de Eurostar-terminal op Amsterdam Centraal, om de doorstroming van reizigers door de verplichte grenscontroles te versnellen.

title: Jetten ahead of debate: 'Good if Mr Buma gives us a few lessons'
lead: Asked what vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> can do well and what he cannot, prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> points out that it would be good if he gives the minority cabinet 'a few good lessons'.

title: Dutch people hold 3.2 billion euros in crypto with Dutch providers, bitcoin by far the most popular
lead: Dutch people held 3.2 billion euros in crypto with Dutch providers at the end of June. That is about 1 percent of their total investments in shares, investment funds and bonds, according to new figures from <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity> (DNB). Most of the money was in bitcoin and other unbacked cryptocurrencies.

title: That Shalini C. (28) leaked police information to criminals for two years came about because she was under 'enormous pressure'
This is how the cabinet is seeking support for the budget
lead: The cabinet is still looking for a majority for the budgets. They would prefer the broadest possible support from both left and right. But the more parties, the more demands. In this video we explain how the cabinet hopes to find sufficient support.

title: PRO takes on Big Tech: ban on endless scrolling
lead: PRO MP Barbara Kathmann wants to curb the dubious business models of Big Tech

title: Universities and universities of applied sciences welcome slightly more new students this year
lead: Slightly more people have started a degree at a university or university of applied sciences this academic year than last year, with technical studies in particular proving popular. There are also more new international students, despite commitments by institutions to limit that intake.

title: FvD and far-right entanglement can no longer be denied: a change of course does not appear to be imminent
lead: Anyone who thinks FvD is cleaning house after images of a neo-Nazi fight tournament and glorification of Hitler is mistaken. Numerous others with ties to the far right are still embedded in the party's veins.

title: Dead and injured after shooting in Schiedam
lead: A shooting has taken place on Weverpad in Schiedam. One person has died. Another was injured. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports this.

title: Cabinet chooses AI that helps the Netherlands move forward
Police: officer used taser on parcel courier when he was grabbed by the wrist
lead: The police officer who came under fire for using a taser during the arrest of a parcel courier in Amsterdam was, according to the police, grabbed by the wrist. He used his taser after having given several warnings. Footage of the incident caused great outrage on social media.

title: Closure of outdated RIVM labs looms, site manager worried about outbreak risk
lead: The constantly postponed move of the RIVM is leading to an unsustainable situation at the old location in Bilthoven, the site manager believes. The RIVM may therefore have to close its laboratories for research into infectious pathogens.

title: Packed agenda, no desire, a nagging guilty feeling: the great having-to has started again
lead: The sacred obligation to gather with the holidays, which in hindsight is often actually quite pleasant.

title: Pangram is the new superhero of the web, but is this sharp judge of the written word trustworthy?
lead: The internet is being flooded with soulless texts from AI generators. The only one that seems able to do anything about it is Pangram. But how reliable is that programme? And how much do we trust each other if everything has to pass through a detector?

title: Deputy Prime Minister Van den Brink (CDA) does not want to choose a camp: 'I am in the cabinet camp'
lead: Deputy Prime Minister <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA) also speaks to the press after today's crisis talks. That crisis meeting will continue this coming weekend.

title: CDA think tank wants to get rid of all allowances, tax credits and tax deductions
Punk cabaret performer André Manuel, the man of hard jokes, is gloomy in his new show: 'I don't want to be a product'
lead: In his new show The Lonely Soul, André Manuel once again frets about what humanity is doing to itself. He is gloomy about the consequences of artificial intelligence: "This is the end of art as we know it."

title: New APV article to deter fake agents
lead: A new model APV article helps municipalities take action against fake agents. There is great need for such an instrument, says the <entity id="pos:burgemeester-bunnik">burgemeester van Bunnik</entity>, <entity id="person:ruud-van-bennekom">Ruud van Bennekom</entity>.

title: Live | Coalition crisis reaches boiling point: how the exceptional evening unfolded in The Hague
lead: Hello and welcome to this live blog. Here we (Sanne Oving, Edo van der Goot and Priscilla Slomp) keep you informed of political developments in The Hague.

title: From red line to government line: how Rob Jetten as prime minister cannot say the same thing as party leader
Verstappen wins after 35 lead changes: unreal race
lead: Max Verstappen lost the lead 35 times in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but regained the front position every time and so won the race with what is presumably the most overtakes ever in Formula 1.

title: The Nota Ruimte: binding for central government, guiding for others
lead: It becomes binding for central government and guiding for the decentralised authorities: the Nota Ruimte, which was sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> this morning. The Nota Ruimte is the national government's environmental vision and will have a decisive influence on the spatial choices the central government makes for around ten years.

title: House of Representatives wants a cheap train subscription all year round
lead: A majority in the House of Representatives wants the popular Dal Vrij train subscription from the summer to become a structural subscription. A proposal from PRO instructing <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to work out this plan has a majority. That is apparent from a survey by the political desk of RTL Nieuws.

title: Dutch nationals risk 750,000 euro fine after illegal rave in nature area in Luxembourg
lead: A group of Dutch nationals appears in court in Luxembourg this week after they organised an illegal rave in a small village in the summer of 2025. The participants risk a fine of 750,000 euros. The party caused national uproar because it was held on a farmer's meadow in a Natura 2000 area.

title: Mayors from Barcelona to Paris sound the alarm over US sanctions against the International Criminal Court in The Hague
lead: Mayors of eight European cities where international organisations are based call on the European Commission to actively contribute to protecting the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague. They do so after the American government announced sanctions against the ICC.

title: New twist in tax plan crisis: cabinet advises against millionaires' tax
lead: A new twist in the crisis surrounding the tax plan: the cabinet has concluded that the plan put forward by PRO and Volt is not well put together. In other words, a nice idea, but not a good plan in practice.

title: Muziekorganisatie dreigt met rechtszaak tegen Nederlands bedrijf dat AI-gegenereerde muziek verkoopt
lead: BumaStemra, de organisatie die Nederlandse muziekmakers vertegenwoordigt, dreigt YourNeuroTune aan te klagen voor het verkopen van AI-gegenereerde achtergrondmuziek.

title: Switching to another health insurer can save up to 54 euros a month
lead: Now that health insurance premiums are rising sharply, it may be worthwhile to switch health insurer. Those who switch from the most expensive to the cheapest health insurance can save 54 euros a month. Switching is possible until the end of the year.

title: Pieter Baan Centre cannot establish a psychiatric disorder in suspect in murder of Lisa
lead: Voices in his head are said to have driven Chris Jude to murder 17-year-old Lisa in August 2025. Experts have not been able to establish whether the suspect has a psychotic or personality disorder. "His inner world has remained a black box."

title: House wants to ban use of AI such as chatbots for primary school pupils
lead: Primary school pupils should not be allowed to use generative AI, believes <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. A large majority supports a motion by Volt and CDA asking <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to arrange a ban. Generative AI is artificial intelligence that can produce text, video or music, for example. Chatbots such as ChatGPT also fall under it.

title: Yellow armpits in your clothing? This is how to get rid of those nasty sweat stains
Box 3: D66 and CDA win the bluffing game against VVD, cabinet crisis complete
lead: On Tuesday 3 November Bontenbal put the knife to the VVD's throat in the talk show Eva. That coalition partner did not want to move on a portion of wealth, he said. As a result, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten failed to close a deal with opposition party PRO, according to the CDA leader, and it remained uncertain whether the tax plan would get a majority […]

title: PRO not agreeing with the nonsense plan of the Jetten cabinet to squeeze the super-rich again for billions
lead: According to Klaver, it shows "a complete lack of leadership"

title: VNG fears lawsuits over building land after new cabinet plans
lead: The Association of Dutch Municipalities (VNG) fears 'endless discussions and lawsuits' if the central government pushes through plans to assess land prices in a different way. The cabinet proposal is meant to give municipalities more room to recover costs, such as the construction of sewerage, from property developers. But according to the municipalities, the risk that the proposed method leads to considerable discussions is 'huge'.

title: Hepatitis A vaccine to become standard for men who have sex with men
lead: The hepatitis A vaccination will become standard for men who have sex with men. Minister <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity>) is adopting a positive recommendation from the <entity id="org:gezondheidsraad">Gezondheidsraad</entity> on the vaccination.

title: NCTV sees AI playing an increasingly large role in carrying out attacks

title: Housing market policy: a push for one comes at the expense of another
lead: Measures to help certain groups on the housing market may unintentionally have adverse effects on others. With a constant housing stock, a push upwards for one comes at the expense of another. For example, integration participants who work at least 28 hours a week will be allowed up to three years longer to complete their integration. Aartsen is also working on a new direction for the Participation Act, under the banner: 'a Participation Act that works'.

title: Tension rises ahead of crucial debate in the House of Representatives: 'Voting down the Belastingplan is unprecedented'

title: The New Towns are growing old and The Hague looks the other way
