lead: Relatives of the shot dead GP and teacher Jurgen Damen (43) have chosen to read their victim statements aloud themselves at the appeal hearing in the case against Erasmus shooter Fouad L. (35). Until now, the widow, his daughter and sister had not shared their feelings in public.

title: Three municipalities break Vlieland formation record
lead: The municipal councils of <entity id="org:gemeente-leidschendam-voorburg">Leidschendam-Voorburg</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-papendrecht">Papendrecht</entity> and Tiel today (2 November 2026) equal the Vlieland formation record from 2022. And because there is nothing to suggest that they will appoint a new coalition and executive board today, they will also break that formation record of 229 days.

title: Target of devastating attack on Tarwekamp addresses suspects: "You completely destroyed me"
lead: Her bridal fashion shop was the target of the attack on Tarwekamp, which claimed the lives of six innocent victims. More than two years after that catastrophic day in 2024, Maryam* tells her story in court. "You wanted to destroy me. Congratulations, you succeeded."

title: A substantial financial setback is already being created for the next cabinet: 'Surely the minister cannot present this with a straight face?'
lead: <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (VVD) claims to be a frugal <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity>: a so-called 'hawk' who guards the treasury with his life. But is that title really deserved? Because he leaves quite a few gaps in the budget.

title: Police arrest parcel delivery driver who drove into runners in Barneveld
lead: Police arrested the driver of a parcel van in Amersfoort on Friday evening on suspicion of attempted manslaughter. The 22-year-old man had driven into runners earlier that evening during a race in Barneveld. No one was injured.

title: Little change in seat poll after cabinet crisis, nor for FVD after neo-Nazi documentary
lead: Despite the commotion in The Hague, little changes in the latest seat poll. D66, VVD and CDA are roughly equal in size and remain in decline, while almost all constructive opposition parties are doing better than they did at the elections.

title: The Hague aims to be fully switched to open source by 2035
lead: The municipality of The Hague wants to have fully switched to open-source software by 2035 at the latest. A new strategy must pave the way for a phased transition to open source, reducing dependence on Microsoft and Oracle.

title: Can an electoral threshold prevent The Hague chaos? 'Germans are glad of it when they look at the Netherlands'
lead: If the Netherlands had an electoral threshold, several parties would disappear from parliament. And other parties would actually grow. Plenty of other countries have such a threshold. What can we learn from them, and is it really so beneficial? 'Parties that bring a different voice lose their seat in parliament.'

title: Horses Fuck on the candidate list: municipality badly gets it wrong with AI
lead: Horses Fuck, that is how candidate councillor Hester Bais suddenly appeared on the English election website of <entity id="org:gemeente-hilversum">gemeente Hilversum</entity>. The bizarre name change turns out to be the result of an AI blunder.

title: Six months in prison for officer who secretly searched police systems
lead: A former police officer has been sentenced to six months in prison because she illegally searched for data in the systems of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and passed it on to others. The judge does not believe she was pressured or threatened.

title: Single-member factions badly needed in the Senate, if the VVD also votes against the tax plan
Two robberies within half an hour at shops in Amsterdam-West, police investigating possible link
Too few forest rangers, yet they are given more and more tasks: 'You're a kind of neighbourhood police officer for the forest'
lead: <entity id="org:zbo-staatsbosbeheer">Staatsbosbeheer</entity> is looking for dozens of new forest rangers. Because of a structural shortage, Dutch nature has not been properly managed for years. As a result, more and more is being piled onto the forest ranger's plate, as ranger Erik de Jonge also observes.

title: Coalition continues talks Monday at the Catshuis
Stop this chaos: let parliament serve for four years and abolish interim elections
lead: A <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> always remains caretaker in that case, even if no new government has been formed after elections

title: Unique ruling by International Court of Justice: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
lead: According to a ruling by the world's highest court, the International Court of Justice, Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya population. The ruling is unprecedented: it is the first time a country has officially been found guilty of the charge of genocide.

title: It is a relief that Prime Minister Rob Jetten visits the theatre of his own free will
On the weekend we take life with a chance passer-by. This week: Josina and Roy look after each other
Man (42) admits shooting pregnant ex (34) dead in The Hague
lead: The 42-year-old Peter M., who is suspected of having shot his pregnant ex-partner (34) dead in her home in The Hague in August, has confessed. This emerged during a first preliminary hearing at the court.

title: Ruben recognised his maths teacher in documentary about neo-Nazis
lead: Ruben had three years of maths lessons from Egbert B., who is linked in a Zembla documentary to a neo-Nazi network. Ruben would never have suspected something like this behind his 'nice teacher'.

title: Darts with dextrose: does this help you throw 180?
lead: Dutch darts player Gian van Veen says he reached the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts thanks to grape sugar, or dextrose. According to the darts player, his arm began to tremble during the match. He decided to take dextrose and suddenly threw 180. The question is: is this really a miracle cure?

title: Career after politics: NSC members turn out to be surprisingly often advisers after leaving The Hague
lead: NSC, the 'party of Pieter Omtzigt', experienced a stormy rise and fall in Hague politics. The party won twenty seats in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> and took part in <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. But as quickly as they rose, most of the leading figures also disappeared again. What are they doing now?

title: Red Line protest passes off peacefully, organisation speaks of 200,000 participants
lead: The Museum Square in Amsterdam was full of demonstrators dressed in red who joined the Red Line protest. According to the organisation, 200,000 people took part. Some carried placards and banners with texts such as 'Zionisme is racisme', 'Geen Nederlandse steun aan apartheid' and 'Palestina Vrij'. Apart from a few arrests, the protest march passed off peacefully according to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>.

title: Four car fires in half an hour in Almelo, police issue message: 'Be alert'
lead: On Saturday evening at 23.45 hours, the police sent out an alert via Burgernet in connection with several car fires in the area of Almelo. There were four car fires within half an hour at different locations in Almelo.

title: King Winter shows his face next week: 'First serious winter cold'
lead: Winter is heading our way. Although it has already frozen in more and more places over the past nights, next week we will also face daytime temperatures only a few degrees above freezing.

title: 1,5 years in prison for serious group assault on 17-year-old boy in Haarlem
lead: The court in Haarlem on Thursday imposed prison sentences on two men for the assault of a 17-year-old boy from Haarlem. Footage of the violence was shared online.

title: Then report sick!
lead: Rather than staying in bed, Femmetje de Wind goes to the office, where at half strength she infects her colleagues, a habit she herself detests.

title: Is gaming also a good investment?
Large-scale security exercise at Schiphol on 19 November with military personnel and fire brigade
Controversial au pair agency Nina Care declared bankrupt
lead: The court of Haarlem has declared au pair agency Nina Care bankrupt. A former employee is still entitled to tens of thousands of euros in salary and requested the bankruptcy. Nina Care had already been in trouble for some time.

title: Debate on tax plan causes confusion in the House of Representatives: does this coalition still exist?
All those extra civil servants didn't fall from the sky, that was The Hague's policy
lead: Calling for cuts to the number of civil servants sounds appealing. As a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> you usually get a lot of applause from voters for it. But there is a reason why it keeps failing, writes political reporter Hans van Soest in this commentary.

title: VVD did have contact with DENK, minister Heinen quickly deleted the messages (but there are screenshots)
lead: By deleting those messages, Heinen may have acted in breach of the archiving rules of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>

title: State pension age remains 67 years and three months in 2032
lead: The age at which people receive the state pension remains 67 years and three months in 2032. Minister <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">Hans Vijlbrief</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity> informed <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> of this on Friday. We will not live longer as quickly as was thought.

title: Bird flu confirmed in Grootegast
Coach Lukkien misses FC Groningen - sc Heerenveen after hip operation
lead: Coach Dick Lukkien will miss Saturday's home match of his club FC Groningen against sc Heerenveen. FC Groningen announced this on its own website on Thursday. The 54-year-old coach has undergone an operation in which he received a new hip and describes himself as "not match fit".

title: Code yellow for dense fog across the country, sunshine later in the day: calm autumn weather continues
lead: Morning rush hour starts Friday grey and misty in many places. The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> has even issued a code yellow due to dense fog across the whole country. The days may also start misty next weekend, but almost every day the sun will quickly break through and it will be pleasant.

title: Justice Minister Van Weel's jibe about the police is more than a slip of the tongue
Open marriage between D66, VVD and CDA? 'The beginning of the end'
lead: The cooperation between D66, VVD and CDA was repeatedly compared to an open marriage yesterday during the difficult House debate on the tax plans: other parties may also join to support plans. But how do you make such a relationship work in practice? An open marriage requires clear agreements and commitment from everyone involved.

title: The incapacity of the Jetten cabinet exposes a deep crisis in the system
lead: The crisis in the Jetten cabinet will linger for a long time. The centre parties have almost entirely squandered their stabilising role. Political excess is becoming the norm.

title: Cabinet survives another day, but coalition still on a knife edge
lead: The Jetten minority cabinet will remain in place for now, but for the time being it looks like little more than a stay of execution. Leaders of D66, VVD and CDA will continue talking over the coming weekend. It looks like a desperate attempt.

title: What is that starling man doing with a beak full of flowers? He is on his way to a female
Victim of Schiedam shooting arrested, deceased man was 19
lead: One of the victims of the fatal shooting in Schiedam has been arrested. It concerns the man who ran away lightly injured after the shooting. The man who died is a 19-year-old from Schiedam, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports.

title: Health puts more people at a distance from the labour market
lead: The labour market remains tight, but nevertheless there is a growing group of non-workers who cannot get back on their feet due to health problems. In 2025 this concerned 867,000 people, according to research by the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity>. Three years earlier there were 828,000.

title: From exception to custom: elections after a cabinet collapse
lead: We are in the middle of a cabinet crisis. Normally, preparations would then be made for new elections, but nowhere is that officially recorded. That is why Mirjam Bikker submitted a motion last week: first to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> and not immediately new elections. A possible end to a decades-old tradition, which began in the late 1960s after the fall of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> Cals. Paul van der Steen, political historian and author of the biography of Jo Cals, draws parallels between then and now on OVT on Sunday.

title: What makes people happier: nice colleagues and a fixed routine, or that big change that emigrating or promotion brings?
lead: Emigrating, a new job, building your own house, quitting work, finally making that big trip. Big steps appeal to the imagination. But do they make you happy too?

title: Chief constable sees no link between racism and fatal police violence: 'I distance myself from that'
lead: Chief of the <entity id="org:politie">nationale politie</entity> <entity id="person:janny-knol">Janny Knol</entity> sees no link between racism and fatal police violence. "I distance myself from that," she said on Monday evening in response to figures that the independent organisation Controle Alt Delete (CAD) presented on the subject.

title: Unique: two cabinet members sent home sick during the same debate
lead: The <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> turned into a true sickbay on Tuesday evening. State Secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> (D66, Justice) became unwell during a debate later in the evening, forcing the debate to be halted. And also Minister of Justice <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> (VVD) fell ill. During the same debate he developed an inflamed eye.

title: Simultaneously on the municipal council and the House of Representatives? Why parties want to ban political dual roles
lead: Being a member of the House of Representatives and of the local municipal council, and being paid for both roles. PRO and D66 want politicians to no longer be able to do this soon. "A form of easy money grabbing."

title: America owes the internet and the coronavirus vaccine to it, now the Netherlands also has such an institute
lead: What do the internet, GPS, flat-screen TVs and coronavirus vaccines have in common? They were all initially developed for the American military. And now the Netherlands is also getting such an institute that must develop 'groundbreaking technology' for our armed forces. Task one: come up with a weapons system that protects our North Sea.

title: Broad support for Box 3 proposal, but vote postponed after irritation over Heinen's absence
World record on natural ice: Judith Krabbenborg skates almost 35 kilometres in an hour
lead: Judith Krabbenborg broke the women's world hour record on natural ice on Tuesday. She skated 34,878 kilometres in one hour at the De Witte Poorte Winterswijk ice rink.

title: The judges left the courthouse at 20.45 hours: they had only had a quarter of an hour of real break
Moto2 riders Veijer and Van den Goorbergh in top 10 at GP Portugal
lead: Motorcycle racers Collin Veijer and Zonta van den Goorbergh finished in the top 10 of Moto2 at the Portuguese Grand Prix. Two Dutch riders in the top ten had not happened before this year.

title: Quote of the day | discrimination in the House
lead: QUOTE - Markuszower and Keijzer suggested that DENK cannot be trusted because of the migration and Muslim background of the faction members. That is why the tax deal would not be above board. ... Annabel Nanninga (JA21) called the tax deal with DENK "a big problem for integration". She spoke about how "the Islamists" of DENK now "in the [...] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Is that actually allowed? Refusing to work with AI as a civil servant
lead: More and more municipalities are using artificial intelligence. Civil servants use AI to write texts, summarise documents or analyse large amounts of information. Not everyone is eager for this digital help. Some employees fear errors, discrimination or an infringement of their privacy. But are you allowed to refuse to work with AI as a civil servant?

title: 'The Serbian students almost always demonstrated non-violently, while the police acted harshly. That earns them an enormous amount of sympathy'
The style of Sammy-Lou (25): 'After school I took the train to Amsterdam, with a dress and a wig in my backpack'
Prime Minister Jetten wants to give the opposition a final offer 'by Tuesday at the latest': 'Opportunities to get out of this'
lead: Prime Minister Rob Jetten 'sees opportunities' to strike a deal with the opposition on the tax plan. Talks with the parties will continue in the coming days. Jetten expects to present a final offer to the parties 'by Tuesday at the latest'.

title: Frans Weekers puts himself forward as VVD lead candidate for the Senate: 'We must not rule anyone out'
British presenter (59) announces pregnancy live on TV
lead: British presenter Renée Hoenderkamp (59) has announced live on TV that she is expecting her third child. This came as a great surprise to her colleagues in the GB News studio.

title: Spectacular outcome of the Tax Plan with a deal on the left makes the pain for the VVD even worse: can the Jetten cabinet survive?
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> wants to do everything to keep his cabinet in place, but the manoeuvre of the CDA and D66 faction leaders to secure votes from the left for the Tax Plan in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, and the VVD's reaction to it, make that very difficult.

title: Senate passes bill for a strong local public broadcaster for everyone
What is the Minister of Defence up to?
How Ukraine brought out the EU's stubborn streak
lead: Europe is proving remarkably hard to exhaust.

title: Disadvantages for people with a disability still persist
lead: Ten years ago the Netherlands signed the UN Convention on Disability. In ten years it has not been possible to remove the disadvantages for the just over two million people in the Netherlands with a disability. This is shown by the Monitor National Strategy UN Convention on Disability, published on Tuesday. It also examines the role of municipalities.

title: AIVD: organizations overlook threat from within
lead: Given all the commotion about crypto hacks and runaway freezers, it is tempting to be extra vigilant about threats from outside. Yet organizations often overlook security risks from within, the General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) warns. Think of espionage, or of employees passing information on to organized crime.

title: Place the democratic rule of law at the centre of the participation declaration for newcomers
lead: The text of the participation declaration for new Dutch citizens needs to be revised, according to various experts. The declaration on the democratic rule of law should be given a more central place. In the experts' view, less attention should be paid to recent social developments or phenomena. This is revealed by research commissioned by the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity>.

title: Sybrand Buma begins task of making minority cabinet succeed
lead: Sybrand Buma starts on Monday as mediator for the coalition. It is up to the vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> to advise <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> on financial agreements with the opposition. That takes place behind closed doors. Buma has one month.

title: After crisis, Jetten introduces weekly top-level coalition meeting: Torentjesoverleg returns
lead: As one of the measures after the cabinet crisis, Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> reintroduces the weekly Torentjesoverleg. Every Monday, deputy prime ministers and parliamentary group leaders of D66, VVD and CDA join in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de kamer</entity> of the prime minister. Politically sensitive issues and financial files are discussed here. Sources report this to the political desk of RTL Nieuws.

title: DNB: for successful application of AI, the rigid polder model must be shaken up
lead: AI could give productivity in the Netherlands a boost, but vocational education and dismissal law will first need to be overhauled. That is what De Nederlandsche Bank says.

title: No total ban and no partial ban on discharging PFAS
lead: Is a national discharge ban for PFAS possible? No, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Schoof stated in July last year. PFAS are so ubiquitous that such a total ban would be socially disruptive, and would make, for example, drinking water production and earthworks impossible. Is a partial discharge ban then possible? No, not really either. That is the conclusion of the Jetten cabinet, through <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity>.

title: Lively and bubbling, but Rooie Nel makes a few embarrassing blunders
lead: Joël Broekaert had a pleasant and affordable evening at this "modern bistro on the Vecht", but had to put up with a few laughable misses.

title: Zembla documentary shows how the far right uses an 'explicit strategy' to normalise its ideas
lead: The Zembla documentary The Neo-Nazi Files zooms in on how the far right operates behind the scenes. The footage shows, among other things, how cage fights have been organised for years, including in the cellar of a village hall. The people present turn out to be banned from Forum voor Democratie, and include people who by day are maths teachers or mental healthcare workers. "The far right is following a normalisation strategy", says historian Robin te Slaa on Spraakmakers.

title: Pope Francis described encounters with the devil in rare diaries
lead: The late Pope Francis, by his own account, went through a spiritual crisis from 2021 that lasted two years. During several visions he is even said to have seen the devil. This emerges from a collection of his diaries published on Tuesday.

title: Rob Jetten seems to become increasingly lonely as prime minister. How much grip does he still have?
Pepper spray and fireworks at Don Toliver concert in Ziggo Dome, suspect handed over to police
XR demonstrators who dripped stinking butyric acid in Zara receive a fine
lead: Three Extinction Rebellion activists have today been given a fine of 150 euros for their protest action on 12 April last year. The three took action at the Zara in the centre of Nijmegen, where they dripped the very smelly butyric acid over themselves.

title: The influential and award-winning American philosopher Thomas Nagel hopes 'that there is no God'
lead: What is it like to be a bat? With his essay on that question, Thomas Nagel became known to a wide audience. This week a prestigious philosophy prize was awarded to him. A conversation in a riot-torn Paris, where he lives from time to time.

title: Public Prosecution Service employee suspected of corruption and election fraud
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> suspects an employee of its own of corruption, breach of official secrecy and election fraud. The man holds a political position in Oost-Brabant.

title: Boer Koekoek turned farmers' anger into politics
lead: On 1 October 2019 thousands of farmers drove their tractors to the Malieveld in The Hague to protest against the policy of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>. This action was presented in the media as something new, but these kinds of actions had existed since the 1950s. 'The Dutch army is being put on standby,' […]

title: Professor exposes vulnerability of digital building installations
lead: A climate installation at a primary school that can be accessed with standard login details, and a supermarket cooling installation that hangs unsecured on the internet. Computer science professor Chris Verhoef shows in two blogs for AG Connect how vulnerable the digital control of buildings can be. He warns that hackers can not only manipulate temperatures but, in the worst case, also cause dangerous situations.

title: NS cleaner dies after sip from beer bottle full of MDMA, 17 years in prison demanded
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> demands a 17-year prison sentence against 38-year-old Fela D. According to the justice system, he is responsible for three poisonings with liquid MDMA, one of which resulted in a death. "Heartbreaking consequences," the public prosecutor summed up. Nine years has been demanded against a second suspect.

title: Jetten calls cybersecurity a top priority, but who is in charge?
lead: "Cybersecurity is a top priority for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>", Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> said in October to RTL Nieuws, two days after the major cyber incident at Albert Heijn. But behind the scenes the same question keeps coming up: who takes the lead?

title: Reward of 2 million leads to multiple tips about Bolle Jos
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has received multiple tips about fugitive Jos Leijdekkers since the reward for the golden tip was increased to the astronomical sum of 2 million euros. That was announced on Monday in the programme Opsporing Verzocht.

title: The climate summit is dead, long live the climate summit! This is how the world's climate policy will go on from here
The CoalitieChecker: from three parties to political sudoku
lead: In 2006 a majority coalition of three parties already seemed quite an undertaking, let alone four. The CoalitieChecker then helped calculate what such a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> could look like. Since then Dutch politics has fragmented more than ever, and the checker itself is, after years of absence, ready for a new round. Just like our cabinet, probably. […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Estate agent Steffi (35) lives in 38 square metres: "You need far less space and belongings than you think"
Public professionals use informal consultation to avoid risks
lead: Professionals in the public sector face a number of risks in their work. One of the most commonly used coping mechanisms for dealing with these is informal consultation. That is what a study published today by Erasmus University shows.

title: JA21 and PRO are willing to do business, but not with a cabinet that cannot make choices itself
lead: Where will the struggling minority cabinet find its majorities in the coming period? With Jesse Klaver (PRO) on the left or with Joost Eerdmans (JA21) on the right? Both party leaders are urging the same thing: the cabinet must finally make a choice.

title: Climate change: why it seems that fewer and fewer people consider it important and what to do about it
lead: After a scorching hot summer - with major wildfires, failed harvests, dried-up rivers and heat deaths - climate still does not sit at the top of our to-do list. Not with political leaders and not with citizens. How can that be? "A spiral of doing nothing."

title: In search of the cosy beer-and-bitterballen liberals
lead: Opinion Ralph Kruizinga: 'The ever-smiling <entity id="person:mark-rutte">Mark Rutte</entity> has been swapped for the always sour Dilan Yesilgöz, who prefers doing business with anti-rule-of-law and deeply racist actors'

title: ACM: Investor HAL may take over construction company VolkerWessels
lead: Investor HAL may take over construction group VolkerWessels. The Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) has decided this after extensive investigation. Various conditions have been imposed, however. Several business units must be divested to prevent the company from gaining too much power after the takeover. Earlier, the ACM had already stepped in before the takeover.

title: GTA 6 is out, first reactions and reviews are glowing: 'Surprising depth'
lead: Since midnight Grand Theft Auto 6 has been playable in the Netherlands. The first reactions from gamers are positive. Reviews of the game are also glowing. "The sky-high expectations are largely met", writes The New York Times.

title: Prison sentence for far-right British activist over graffiti on migrant boat
lead: British anti-immigration activist Daniel Thomas, better known as Danny Tommo, has been sentenced to fifteen months in prison for daubing graffiti on a migrant boat in the Channel in September. He was arrested for his actions that same month. He has pleaded guilty.

title: What are HIMARS rocket systems?
lead: In 2022, State Secretary Christophe van der Maat (VVD) of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> already said that the war in Ukraine underlines the need 'to be able to act in all parts of the spectrum of violence'. That is why the Netherlands had to once again have rocket artillery. And that now looks set to be twenty HIMARS rocket systems. The Dutch Ministry of Defence says that the deal […]

title: 1 year after the elections, D66 nearly halved in seat poll, coalition at 44 seats
lead: One year after the elections, D66 has lost almost half of its voters. In the latest poll by EenVandaag and Verian, the party stands at 14 seats, compared with 26 at the elections. D66 is losing a much larger number of voters than other coalition parties.

title: Two explosions within a week at a house on Vrolikstraat in Amsterdam-Oost, window damaged
Trade unions and students join forces: French take to the streets en masse
lead: In France, hundreds of thousands of people have once again demonstrated today against the high cost of living and deteriorating public services. The French ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> puts the number of demonstrators at 600,000; according to the trade unions, there were one million more.

title: Brilliant
ABP is doing well, but the pension increase for civil servants is still uncertain
lead: The financial position of the civil servants' pension fund ABP improved further in the third quarter. The current coverage ratio rose to 132.2 percent, despite a negative investment return. This gives the fund a favourable starting position for the transition to the new pension system on 1 January 2027. How much the pensions of (former) civil servants can then increase is not yet known. For that, ABP looks at the coverage ratio on 31 December.

title: Widow of Tarwekamp explosion victim: 'Wait to cry until the children are asleep'
lead: Emotionally, the first next of kin and victims spoke on Tuesday about the consequences of the explosion on the Tarwekamp in The Hague. For them, these are heavy and emotional days in court. "What do you say when your daughter asks: when is Daddy coming back?"

title: Government: 4.5 per cent pay rise for civil servants
lead: Civil servants of the national government will, as far as their employer is concerned, receive a pay rise of 4.5 per cent: 3 per cent from 1 March 2027 and 1.5 per cent from 1 January 2028.

title: Klaver and Dassen happy with deal: 'Hope the way is clear for a majority on the tax plan'
lead: Jesse Klaver of PRO and Laurens Dassen (Volt) are pleased with the breakthrough that now appears to be there to help the tax plan win a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. If the watered-down amendment from both parties is adopted, the two left-wing opposition parties will agree to the tax plan, Klaver says when asked.

title: Almost a thousand parents, children and ex-partners are waiting for the agency that collects alimony
lead: Almost a thousand parents, children and ex-partners are still waiting for their request to collect overdue alimony to be processed. That is what State Secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity>, D66) writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Daan (52), winner of survival programme Alone, finds and keeps her 'wild self' in Amsterdam: 'The wilderness is everywhere'
Will disagreement between D66, CDA and VVD bring down the cabinet? 'That is disastrous for the business climate'
lead: There is trouble between the coalition parties. D66 and CDA have reached a deal with the opposition parties PRO and Volt, to the displeasure of their coalition partner VVD. Yesilgöz wants a 'fundamental reset', but D66 and CDA do not seem keen on that. Will this end in a cabinet collapse? "We cannot afford a stumbling <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>," says Barbara Baarsma, chief economist at PwC Nederland, on Spraakmakers.

title: Little Boot
lead: 55 years ago, little Ingrid put a boot instead of her shoe out for Sinterklaas. After all, plenty of sweets fit in it.

title: 'I always wanted pink hair, so after my second brain infarction I thought: if I don't do it now, when will I?'
Criticism of Van der Burg's civil servants plan
lead: Several parliamentary groups in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> voiced strong criticism on Tuesday evening of the cabinet plan to have some 25,000 fewer civil servants at central government from 2035. title: Government has caused farmers 'great suffering' over ten years, says National Ombudsman: 'Don't dismiss them as nutters, they aren't'
lead: The government has caused farmers 'great suffering' over the past ten years. That is the conclusion of the National Ombudsman in his latest report. According to him, farmers have been 'simply pushed into uncertainty' and treated as 'nutters'. Reporter Elodie Verweij talks with him.

title: Search for missing kitesurfer halted due to weather conditions
lead: The search for the missing water sports enthusiast off the coast of Scheveningen was halted again on Monday morning due to weather conditions. The missing person has not yet been found, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports.

title: Crisis talks between D66, CDA and VVD continue in Hilversum
lead: The crisis talks between D66, CDA and VVD continue on Sunday morning at 11.00 at the Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum. The leaders of the coalition parties already met there on Saturday. It is not clear what the talks have yielded.

title: Bezzecchi holds off Marc Márquez for pole at GP Portugal
lead: Motorcyclist Marco Bezzecchi kept Marc Márquez from pole position in qualifying for the Portuguese Grand Prix in MotoGP. The Italian Aprilia rider was faster at the Portimão circuit with a lap of 1.37,201 than Spaniard Márquez and compatriot Fabio Di Giannantonio.

title: Police in hot water: wrongly gave data on foie gras activists to Hanos in Nieuwegein
lead: The police wrongly provided name and address details of activists from Active for Justice to catering wholesaler Hanos. This happened after a demonstration at a branch in Nieuwegein against the sale of foie gras got out of hand. The staff acted roughly towards the activists during the incident.

title: Political crisis continues, but cabinet collapse averted for now
Tackle hyper-nervous society by turning Sunday into a day of rest? 'We need to search collectively for rest'
lead: Individualism and performance pressure make our society too nervous, and that comes at the expense of mutual connection and our mental health. Reintroducing Sunday rest would be the remedy, seven Christian organisations believe. "Having the conversation about how we can slow down together is needed," says <entity id="person:jet-bussemaker">Jet Bussemaker</entity>, chair of the <entity id="org:raad-voor-volksgezondheid-en-samenleving">Raad voor Volksgezondheid en Samenleving</entity>, speaking on Spraakmakers.

title: Four car fires in half an hour, police urge residents of Almelo to stay alert
lead: In a short time yesterday evening, four cars were set on fire in Almelo. Police warned residents of the municipality via a Burgernet alert to stay alert. This morning a 43-year-old suspect was arrested.

title: Construction goes skyward
lead: The construction task in the Netherlands is still enormous. Does that affect what is being built now? Fewer single-family homes are planned and more apartments. The big cities are popular, but due to lack of space homes are getting smaller and being stacked. And so new-build projects are increasingly going skyward.

title: A wheelchair basketball player, a pastor, a lumberjack: the Democrats bring new diversity to the Senate
lead: In the battle for Senate seats in Washington, some Democratic candidates unexpectedly won. Their backgrounds differ, as do their views on the party's direction. Six portraits.

title: "Geen beweging" in kabinetsonderhandelingen te midden van links-rechtse impasse
lead: De poging van het kabinet om de links- en rechtse oppositiepartijen binnen te halen in de lopende onderhandelingen over het belastingplan, mislukte opnieuw op...

title: Rob Jetten, not joining the Red Line but joining Israel
lead: Opinion by Eric van 't Hoff: 'Rob Jetten, with your choice you harshly let down a large part of the voters who voted for D66 because of your participation in the Red Line'

title: On appeal, the Public Prosecution Service demands 30 years and life imprisonment for Sharona and Bill for double murders in Lieshout and Amsterdam
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> on Tuesday again demanded life imprisonment against Bill C. (55) for two murders. One of the victims was Willem van der Willigen from Lieshout. Against co-defendant Sharona de J. the Public Prosecution Service demanded 30 years' imprisonment on appeal. After the murders, the two stayed in the homes of the victims as if they were their own.

title: Moerdijk residents cautiously positive about village's survival, but want guarantees
lead: Residents of the North Brabant village of Moerdijk are cautiously positive about the village being preserved, but see no guarantees yet. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is committed to ensuring their hometown continues to exist, but 100 percent certainty on that has not yet been achieved.

title: We do not control success, says sociologist Thijs Bol: 'At birth we receive a kind of menu of options'
Within a day everyone was sure: the Holy Grail of mathematics has really been solved
lead: Mathematician Levent Alpöge, with help from the AI model Claude, has solved the Riemann hypothesis. "Claude flew, danced and shone." On Friday he put his work online and within a day confidence in his solution rose from 'almost certainly correct' to 'certainly correct'.

title: How Klaver puts the coalition on the spot with a millionaire tax
Will municipalities take the lead on civic integration?
lead: A lack of capacity at municipalities is a bottleneck for the implementation of civic integration trajectories. The trajectory is also quickly falling behind schedule. This is shown by an interim evaluation of the Civic Integration Act 2021. The <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity> ministry shared that interim evaluation with <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> this week.

title: Prosecution demands 22 years in prison for murder of partner, who was made to look like suicide
lead: If it is up to the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the 27-year-old Esmée D. from Assen should go to prison for 22 years. She allegedly poisoned her partner, the 34-year-old Ruben, with an overdose of MDMA and the designer drug flubromazepam.

title: Nature organisations: 'Don't take money for bridges and roads from the nature fund'
lead: Minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> recently announced that he needs around 80 billion euros for the maintenance and improvement of the Dutch infrastructure. To finance that maintenance, he wants to withdraw well over one billion euros from planned nature projects, such as restoring the tidal flow in the Grevelingen. Even though that has a positive effect on water quality. Nature organisations such as Vogelbescherming Nederland, the Waddenvereniging, Natuurmonumenten, the Wereldnatuurfonds and LandschappenNL strongly disagree. "Don't cut back on what makes the Netherlands resilient," says Judy Koppenjan in Vroege Vogels.

title: What are we talking about when we talk about the new nitrogen plans?
lead: The nitrogen crisis, which has been dragging on for years, is so complex that it is good to step back every now and then. On Tuesday, agriculture minister <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">Jaimi van Essen</entity>, from D66, presented his further developed nitrogen plans, which are meant to offer a solution to the permit crisis that arose in May 2019 after a devastating ruling by the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> on the then only four-year-old Programma Aanpak Stikstof (PAS). One important step that Van Essen is taking is submitting…

lead: Jensen Huang is returning to chip giant Nvidia, which is convinced that Jensen Huang is the right person to lead the company. Following the news, the company's share prices immediately rose explosively.

title: Cabinet still in place, but for how long? 'VVD does not want to be seen with PRO'
lead: Tension is running high in politics in The Hague: a deal on the tax plan between CDA, D66, PRO and Volt has put the minority cabinet under strain. Political commentator Joost Vullings saw today a crisis that actually began months ago.

title: Will the Netherlands still have a cabinet? Jetten and Yeşilgöz are settling it behind closed doors
lead: After Thursday's political drama, days of crisis talks followed between <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> (D66), Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA). lead: Nature peat in the Netherlands is in a deplorable state, the Court of Audit reports: only in 18 of the 173 areas examined is it doing well. Meanwhile: "Peat prevents CO2 emissions and contributes to water storage, cooling and climate adaptation."

lead: The cabinet remains together for now, but the crisis atmosphere is not over. title: Involve residents from the drawing board onwards in policy

title: William and Catherine on Vogue's list of best-dressed celebrities: 'Royal allure and approachable'

title: The region is now mainly: not the Randstad
lead: Every region counts! Originally this was a recognition of the mutual equality of the various regions of the Netherlands. Much as the King and Sinterklaas carefully divide their visits across the country and make sure they skip no corner. Wherever they jovially step out of the royal bus or the steamboat, every unique traditional costume is equally dear to them and every local delicacy equally precious.

title: Sleepless nights test

Fresh from the press, new scientific research by Swedish political scientists Josefina Erikson and Sandra Håkansson, affiliated with Uppsala University. Take a moment to sit down before the title: 'A Non-Gendered Approach to a Gendered Problem: Violence Mitigation Policy in the Swedish Parliament'.

title: New asylum forecasts: slightly fewer asylum seekers, yet more reception capacity needed

Additional reception places are needed, more lawsuits from rejected asylum seekers are expected, and the inflow of Ukrainian refugees remains high. Four points that stand out in the new asylum forecasts.

title: Cabinet must better defend press freedom, warns the Council for Culture
Imitating China is not the solution
lead: The alarm is being raised more and more often. The major powers China and the US are using trade as a geopolitical weapon. European prosperity is under threat, and unorthodox measures are necessary: high tariffs on a wide range of imports, generous subsidies for the production of cars and chips, or even currency manipulation like China's. Marcel Timmer discusses it.

title: Political parties mainly want to 'score' on social media, and that is exactly what makes cooperation difficult
lead: Political parties like to celebrate their victories on social media. But the urge to score makes cooperation harder, according to professor of politics and media Mariken van der Velden. "It is comfortable for a politician to sit in campaign mode."

title: Kadaster study: a quarter of new construction ends up in four major cities
lead: Just over a quarter of new homes will be built in the four largest municipalities of the Netherlands in the coming years. That is what the Kadaster reports following a study. The share of apartments will also become considerably larger in the coming years, although this type of home will become slightly smaller in floor area. The study is based on homes that have already been granted a permit or are under construction.

title: Monique Haak discovers cheap solution for tumours in unborn babies
lead: In some pregnant women, fast-growing tumours develop in the placenta, which are dangerous for their unborn child. Usually an attempt is made to eliminate such a tumour through a laser operation, a high-risk procedure that is not always successful. That must be possible differently, thought professor of obstetrics and foetal surgeon Monique Haak. And it turns out that it indeed is. A blood pressure pill that has been used for years turns out to be able to tackle these tumours too. Haak tells in NOS Met het Oog op Morgen about the discovery she made.

lead: The youth organisations of the coalition parties believe that the VVD in particular is responsible for the current cabinet crisis, according to a survey by RTL Nieuws. But D66 and CDA also come off badly. "It should have been decided much earlier whether they wanted to go left or right."

title: Irish boxer Lee Reeves (31) dies from effects of knockout
lead: Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died at the age of 31 from the effects of a serious brain injury. He sustained it during a boxing match in August, after which he spent three months in a coma.

title: Curaçao sees increasingly young criminals, minister concerned
lead: Curaçao is worried about youth crime on the island. According to Minister of Justice Shalten Hato, suspects are becoming involved in serious offences, such as armed robberies and murders, at an increasingly young age.

title: Kabinet-Jetten overleeft crisisoverleg voorlopig, impasse houdt aan
lead: Het crisisoverleg van het kabinet eindigde vrijdag na meer dan zeven uur in een impasse, en de coalitie zal overleven...

title: 'Government has been unreliable for farmers in recent years'
lead: The government has been unreliable for farmers in recent years, concludes the <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">Nationale Ombudsman</entity> after an investigation among the professional group. Plans were repeatedly adjusted, withdrawn or postponed, and important decisions remained uncertain for a long time. 'This unreliability has in recent years led to stagnation and a lack of future prospects for farmers.'

title: Young parents in politics have to work out for themselves how to combine work and care
The digital world is vulnerable, a theatre show teaches. 'Hands up: who went back to Hyves and now feels lonely there?'
lead: With his theatre lecture, Bernold Nieuwesteeg tries to increase the digital awareness of his audience. Even at the risk that this too contributes to 'cyber fatigue'.

title: Restless afternoon in The Hague, municipality extends emergency order
Women's front in House of Representatives urges media: report more often and more carefully on femicide
Housemates overpower burglar in student house, police arrest suspect
lead: A group of students managed to overpower a burglar after he had stolen items from their student house in Tilburg at night. The burglar did not manage to get away with it: he was held by the housemates until the police arrived.

title: Live Q&A: ask all your questions about the American elections here
lead: On Tuesday 3 November Americans will elect a new parliament. The big question is whether the Republicans will keep their majority in both the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Is it actually allowed: having a civil servant apply for their own job?
lead: When municipalities have to cut costs, which is the case for many municipalities, this can affect their staffing. Merging departments can eliminate posts and create new job profiles. This can mean civil servants, even after years of loyal service, have to apply again. Sometimes even for a role that looks suspiciously like their current job. But may a municipality simply ask that of a civil servant?

lead: The makers of New Kids want to put the province of Brabant back in the spotlight with Carnaval. The chaotic comedy tells the absurdist story of four friends who get into trouble but always stay cheerful. "Brabant's carnival is the perfect colouring page for that."

title: The last death rattle of the ice giants in the Alps
lead: The mighty glaciers in the Swiss Alps are getting smaller and smaller, and for some it is already certain that they will melt away in the coming decades.

title: Students demonstrate against growing militarisation and defence spending: 'An uncanny feeling, that is worrying'
