That is what Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reports at a press conference with the security services in Kraków. Most likely these are close family members of the man. Polish media report that they are the shooter's father, mother and sister. Tusk said he was convinced that the police will quickly arrest the shooter's "accomplices". There is still no clarity about a motive, although Minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said the shooter is presumably inspired by far-right ideologies. Other news from the night: And then just this: For the second time this autumn, people were able to skate on the natural ice rink in Winterswijk yesterday morning. Overnight a thin layer of ice was made there so that skates could be used. Hundreds of people were there extra early. Have a nice day!

title: More details known about Krakow attacker, motive of Michal O. still unclear
lead: The motive of the attacker who shot dead six people in the Polish city of Krakow yesterday is still not clear. However, more is gradually becoming known about his background. According to Polish media, the perpetrator is 24-year-old Michal O., a man from the southeast of the country. In the attack in the centre of Krakow, besides the fatal victims, four women and two men, fifteen people were also injured. Among them are some coachmen, two police officers and five foreigners. They are in hospital, a police spokesperson told news agency PAP this morning. One of the officers is in life-threatening condition. The police have called on the Polish public to donate blood for him. The gunman himself is in critical condition in hospital, after a shootout with the police. The perpetrator was wearing camouflage clothing and a bulletproof vest when he opened fire from a car yesterday afternoon. He fired with an AR-15, a semi-automatic weapon that can fire hundreds of shots per minute. He was also armed with a handgun and had more weapons and ammunition in his boot. This is how the attack unfolded moment by moment: Rumours that he was a former soldier were denied by the authorities yesterday. Minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said that O. was probably inspired by far-right ideologies and is an "ultranationalist". According to Polish media, Michal O. and his father both had a firearms permit and he is said to have taken the weapons from the family home. That home is in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town about 140 kilometres northeast of Krakow. That residence was searched last night: two women and a man were found dead there. The police have now confirmed that they are his parents and sister. 'Such a normal boy' Neighbours tell Polish media that they never expected Michal O. to be capable of such an act. "A boy, just a boy. He wore a hood and said hello. I cannot say anything bad about him", a neighbour tells Radio Swietokrzyskie. "He's such a normal boy, cheerful and happy", another neighbour tells the outlet Echo Dnia. "As far as I know, he used to win prizes at school." Information from news website Interia confirms that picture. As a young teenager he took third place in a religious art competition at school in 2013. And during his studies at a vocational school for automotive engineering, he won a competition together with two other classmates, according to Interia. His sister was three years younger than him and was an artist. According to Wirtualna Polska, Michal O. had two firearms registered in his name. He also trained at a shooting club, where his 53-year-old father Janusz was also active. According to the newspaper, the eleven firearms and the car from which the attack was carried out were registered in the father's name. The police investigation into the perpetrator's motive is still in full swing. The outlet Onet says it is likely that the public prosecutor will open a terrorism investigation today. A spokesperson says it will not be possible to question the perpetrator in the coming hours or days, given his condition. Investigators are still working at the scene of the attack. The area remains cordoned off. The city has a period of mourning until and including Wednesday, the mayor announced yesterday. Correction from the editors In an earlier version of the reconstruction video, an incorrect starting point of the attacker's route was marked. The route is now shown correctly.

title: Migrant boat that drifted for hours off the Belgian coast has sailed to France
lead: A boat carrying around thirty migrants that drifted for hours off the coast of the Belgian town of Nieuwpoort is now in French waters, Belgian media report. Belgian police received a report at around 05.30 of a boat in distress on the North Sea, near the coast. The occupants reportedly called the emergency services themselves, according to VRT. Only men are on board. They refused to leave the boat and to follow instructions, HLN reports. Poor visibility After the report, various means were deployed to trace the boat. A helicopter was among those sent up, a spokesperson for the local police said. Rescue and police boats were also deployed. "Due to poor visibility at sea it was not easy to find the boat," a police spokesperson told VRT. "But shortly before 08.00 the helicopter located it more than three kilometres off the coast of Nieuwpoort." The boat drifted for hours off the coast. "It is not taking on water, but it has clearly lost its way," a spokesperson said of it. At 14.45 the boat crossed the French border. The French authorities have taken over the rescue operation from Belgium. Boat off Zeeland A rubber boat carrying 38 people was pulled from the sea off the Zeeland town of Breskens just over a week ago. That boat had presumably set out from Dutch territory. The occupants were 36 Afghans and two suspected people smugglers from Sudan. The latter have been arrested. Six of the occupants were minors. It is not yet clear what the boat's intended destination was. Below are images of the boat at sea off the Dutch coast eight days ago:

title: At least 200,000 people at Rode Lijn demonstration in Amsterdam, says organisers
lead: In Amsterdam, according to the organisers, at least 200,000 people demonstrated against the Israel policy of the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. The Rode Lijn demonstration went off without major incidents, says the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Many demonstrators wore red clothing and waved red and Palestinian flags. There were also signs and banners with texts such as "Zionism is racism", "No Dutch support for apartheid" and "Free Palestine". Participants demanded that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> take a harder line against Israel because of the violence against Palestinians. "I still think we are not doing well in the Netherlands. This is already the third time I have walked along," said a woman who was marching. "It probably makes little difference, but it is the only thing you can do." The demonstrators marched around the Vondelpark, starting and ending at the Museumplein. There were some incidents, however. AT5 reported that on the Overtoom officers used batons against demonstrators. That happened when police wanted to arrest a man who was standing at a bus shelter and would not leave. Bystanders were also involved in the incident. The man was eventually arrested. Along the Overtoom a group of people stood with banners that included, among other things, "We support Hamas". The organisation had earlier said it could not completely rule out that Hamas supporters would join, but stressed that the demonstration is mainly about people standing up for human rights. Participants in the march also chanted that they would never be for Hamas, NOS reporters heard. Former politicians Job Cohen and Jozias van Aartsen joined the march, as was already reported yesterday. On the Museumplein a large stage hosted speeches. Among others, former minister Lilianne Ploumen, journalist Amal Helles from Gaza and Palestinian activist Omar Barghouti addressed the demonstrators. It was the fourth Rode Lijn demonstration. This time thirteen organisations took part, including Amnesty International, Oxfam Novib and Save the Children. The organisers demanded that the Jetten cabinet exert "maximum political, economic and diplomatic pressure to definitively end the illegal occupation of Palestine". At the previous protest, in October last year, an estimated 250,000 people joined. In May last year <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> was also there, but he is skipping this edition because he is prime minister. He says he is now "in a different role". As D66 leader, Jetten spoke of genocide in Gaza last year. As prime minister he no longer uses that term. Asked why he does not, he says the cabinet has a duty to do everything to prevent further escalation.

title: Cape Town argues over plan to lock up 'problem baboons'
lead: While the wolf is the topic of debate in the Netherlands, in South Africa it is the baboon. After years of attempts to let humans and baboons live together peacefully, the city of Cape Town wants to catch more than sixty baboons and house them in a fenced area. The plan is leading to protests. It is Bin Day in Simon's Town, at the southern tip of the Cape Peninsula. A baboon tips over a grey rubbish bin and rummages through the waste. It finds half a croissant and a carton of sour milk. Within seconds, the contents of the bin are scattered across the street. The baboons know exactly when to strike: on the day household waste is collected, food lies there for the taking. Some animals have even learned to open doors and windows to steal food from kitchens. The South African Adam Welz, who lives in another coastal town on the peninsula, has experienced this several times. He shows a video of a baboon eating a jar of peanut butter off his kitchen counter. "It looks funny, but he has sharp teeth, bigger than those of a lion. I worry about my young children and my dogs." As the residential areas keep growing further into the mountains, the baboons' living area is shrinking. The animals are therefore increasingly moving into built-up areas in search of calorie-rich food. Encounters between humans and baboons are thus becoming an increasingly frequent source of conflict. Around six hundred baboons live on the Cape Peninsula. The city is trying to drive the baboons back into the mountains with the help of baboon monitors. Armed with paintball guns, the monitors constantly chase the animals. But the baboons are fast and things regularly go wrong. Two troops of more than sixty animals each cause the city a great deal of nuisance. The city and wildlife management agencies therefore want to catch the animals and house them in a fenced area on the Cape Peninsula. The fences have already been put up. The site is roughly the size of seven football fields. There are also wooden platforms where the baboons can rest. "It is not ideal," says Gregg Oelofse, coastal and nature manager at the City of Cape Town. "But we have two choices: euthanise these baboons or lock them up. And we think we can give them a good life." Because a good life is what they do not have now, says Oelofse. "When baboons die, we take X-rays. Almost all of them have pellets in their bodies, because frustrated residents shoot at them. All that rubbish full of calories and sugar they eat is also bad for their health." The proposal, however, is meeting strong opposition. Where Oelofse sees a facility where the baboons can spend their old age in peace, opponents see a death camp. Residents who oppose the plan demonstrate at the fences every weekend. "They are taking them there to die out," says demonstrator Lucinda Bovill. "They are sterilising them so the group eventually disappears. Yet this is their natural habitat. They were here first. We have to adapt and take our responsibility. That way we can secure our bins better." The demonstrators fear that the holding site will set a precedent. "If the first relocations prove successful, the city could lock up more baboons in the future," says demonstrator Lauren Wild, who is standing with a plush baboon toy. "In the end I am afraid that not a single baboon will be left." The City of Cape Town disputes this and says the hundreds of other baboons can simply stay where they are. Adam Welz, who found the baboons in his kitchen, also prefers a different solution. Through his own small nature conservation organisation, the South Peninsula Nature Alliance, he does not argue for fences around the baboons, but for a fence between the residential areas and the mountains. "That way the baboons keep their natural habitat and we have peace in our homes." But according to Oelofse of the City of Cape Town, a hard reset is simply needed. "It is an illusion to think these troops of baboons lead a beautiful and wild life in nature. Locking them up is the only option. I am not happy about that either." The city is still waiting for the final permits for the capture operation but wants to catch the first baboons as soon as possible.

title: Dutch woman (81) dies after accident in which camper van tipped over on motorway in Belgium
lead: In an accident involving a camper van on the E313 motorway in Belgium, an 81-year-old Dutch woman has died. Belgian media report that the vehicle she was in landed on its side in the accident. It is still unclear how the fatal accident happened. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating. The 81-year-old woman was the only occupant of the vehicle. The accident happened at around 10.30 a.m. east of Antwerp. Emergency services have set the camper van upright again. Cars driving on the motorway where the accident happened had to turn around. The E313 was then partly closed for a number of hours. It has since reopened.

title: Woman hides from police in a wheelie bin, but is arrested anyway
lead: In Kwintsheul, South Holland, a woman was arrested after hiding from police in a waste container. Officers were searching for her following a report of vandalism. The police received a report this morning that a woman may have committed vandalism, Omroep West writes. Once on the scene, the officers did not find her. Neighbours had not seen where she had fled to. The woman was also not visible on camera footage. The officers therefore suspected she could not be far away. Strange noise While the officers were speaking with witnesses, they heard a sound coming from a wheelie bin. The officers went to the waste container and lifted the lid. They promptly found the woman they were looking for. She has been arrested. The police do not disclose what she is alleged to have damaged. "After this unusual find we were at least wide awake immediately", the officers write on Instagram.

title: Square in Krakow reopened after attack, victims commemorated with flowers and candles
lead: The square in the Polish city of Krakow where six people were shot dead yesterday has been reopened. The police have completed the investigation on site, so the central square in the historic centre is accessible to the public again. The square had been closed since yesterday afternoon after a man opened fire from a moving car. Four women and two men lost their lives in the attack and fifteen people were injured, including several coachmen, two police officers and a number of foreigners. The foreign victims come from the United Kingdom, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria. The suspected shooter Michal O. was seriously wounded in a shootout with the police and is in life-threatening condition. Far-right ideologies The masked 24-year-old O. wore camouflage clothing and a bulletproof vest during the shooting. He fired with a semi-automatic weapon capable of firing a hundred shots per minute, an AR-15. Also found in his car were a handgun and other weapons and ammunition. Not much is yet clear about his motive, but according to Polish minister Kierwinski of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, Michal O. was presumably inspired by far-right ideologies and is an "ultranationalist". The Polish Public Prosecution Service has started an investigation into a "crime with a terrorist character". Michal O. came from Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town about 140 kilometres northeast of Krakow. Neighbours describe him as "a boy, just a boy" and "a normal, cheerful and happy boy". In his early teenage years he reportedly won prizes in art and automotive technology. The family home was searched by the police yesterday evening. There the police found two dead women and a man: the father, the mother and the sister of the suspect. They are presumed to have been shot dead. Polish media report that both the suspected perpetrator and his father held a firearms licence. The weapons found in the car after the attack are registered in the name of father Janusz. The Public Prosecution Service has seized data carriers such as mobile phones and computers, as well as notes from the home. Seven more firearms were also found in the home. 9 ton for police In St Anne's Church, close to the central square of Krakow, people have gathered to commemorate the victims. The mayor of the city was also present there. Flowers are being laid and candles lit on the square itself. The officers who intervened after the shooting and overpowered O. are being praised in Poland for their heroism. One of them was seriously injured, was taken to hospital and had to undergo surgery. A fundraising campaign has been started for the "true heroes", as Polish prime minister Tusk called them yesterday. Thousands of donors have already contributed almost one million euros to the campaign.

title: Explosions at homes in Schiedam
lead: In Schiedam, explosions occurred shortly after each other at two homes. The first was around 8:15 p.m., Rijnmond reports, the second just after 9:00 p.m. No one was injured. The homes did sustain damage. They are about one kilometre apart. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> told Rijnmond that the explosions are being investigated as separate incidents. The police could or would not say whether they are connected to the fatal shooting in Schiedam yesterday afternoon. Unknown persons opened fire on three men who were working outside a house. One of them, a 19-year-old, was killed. The other two were injured, but not life-threateningly. The police are searching for three unknown men. A description of them has been circulated.

title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal coast: at least 34 dead
lead: A boat carrying migrants bound for Europe sank off the coast of Senegal. At least 34 people died, the Senegalese news agency APS reports. The boat sank off Kébémer, in northwestern Senegal. According to the Senegalese ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, it was a so-called pirogue, a traditional boat that is also used for fishing. It is still unclear how many people were on board. One survivor has been found. A search for possible missing persons is ongoing. The small boat was sailing the Atlantic route from West Africa to Europe, one of the deadliest migration routes in the world. Thousands of people died on that route in recent years. State of emergency: Yesterday a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro. Since early November, more than 3,300 migrants have arrived there on dozens of boats. As a result, public services on the island have come under pressure. The Spanish minister of Interior visited Senegal this week and called on the country to do more to stop the dangerous crossings.

title: Frans Weekers wants to change VVD course and runs for the Senate
lead: Former state secretary Frans Weekers (VVD) wants to be the VVD lead candidate for the Senate. With his candidacy he is going against the party leadership, which has put former minister Adriaansens forward as lead candidate. Weekers said on the programme Pauw, De Wit en Moggré that Halbe Zijlstra and Johan Remkes, among others, support his candidacy. The former state secretary said he wants to help the party board, but also that he wants to "bring the VVD back to the right course". Weekers wants, among other things, that "no party is excluded" from cooperation. Weekers criticised that during the election campaign the VVD ruled out parties, including Pro, in advance. With his remarks he voices part of the VVD base: mainly the more administratively minded VVD members do not support excluding Pro. According to Weekers, things are not going well for the VVD and many members are leaving. "Some think the VVD is sitting on D66's luggage rack, others think it is PVV-light." That needs to change, Weekers believes. He says he wants to help party leader Yesilgöz make the VVD more liberal again. Concerns about governability of the country: the remarks of Weekers come on the eve of a tense week awaiting the minority cabinet, which still has not found a majority for the tax plan. Weekers says he is very concerned about the governability of the country. This is partly because the coalition is divided internally over which opposition parties it should seek support from. D66 and CDA favour cooperation on the left, while the VVD wants to go to the right. Member of parliament and state secretary Weekers was a member of the Tweede Kamer from 2003 to 2010, and in the Rutte I and II cabinets he was <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity>. If Weekers pursues his candidacy, party members must decide who becomes lead candidate. They can vote digitally between 9 and 15 December. The lead candidate will be announced on 16 December. . Incidentally, Weekers has not called party leader Yesilgöz to inform her of his plans.

title: Trump calls announcement of UFC boss Dana White as White House press secretary a 'joke'
lead: US President Trump announced combat sports boss Dana White as the new White House press secretary on Saturday. This caused a stir, but now Trump is dismissing his announcement as "a joke". On his social media platform Truth Social, Trump wrote on Saturday that he had offered White the role of White House press secretary, with a number of well-known combat sports fighters as his assistants. Trump described White as a "violent fighter and warrior". He said he needs White and his team "to defend us against the left, the deranged extremists". Trump also wrote that White "would become a spokesperson like no other". Trump: 'It was just a joke' The striking announcement came a few days after the midterm elections, which were disastrous for the Republicans. The Democrats won the majority in both <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> and the House of Representatives. As a result, Trump faces a Congress dominated by his political opponents for the next two years. Speaking to journalists on Sunday evening US time, the president dismissed his announcement as a joke. "I can tell you that I was just joking," he said, adding that White himself thought it was "a great idea". "He is a very capable man," said Trump. It is not yet known who will become the new White House press secretary. Combat sports boss and confidant White (57) has been head of the UFC, the largest mixed martial arts (MMA) organisation in the world, for more than twenty years. He is also a close friend and confidant of Trump. White was involved in Trump's 2024 election campaign, for example, and stood on the stage when Trump was re-elected. The close ties between the two became clear in June of this year, when the White House became the setting for a UFC cage fight for the 250th anniversary of the US. MMA fighters then walked into the White House in shorts. The combat sports boss already said on Saturday evening that he would fly to Washington for a meeting with Trump. The US president confirmed that he will receive White tomorrow, but stressed that the conversation will be about "other matters". No press secretary The position of press secretary, one of the president's most important spokespersons, has been vacant since 16 October. Katie Zacharia then left after only five days as White House press secretary. Zacharia's first press conference went particularly poorly. There was also discussion about her past. Zacharia had repeatedly presented herself on social media as a lawyer, while she had not passed the required bar exam. The 41-year-old Zacharia was the successor to Karoline Leavitt (28). Leavitt stepped down in the summer because she wanted to spend more time with her family. She had a communication style similar to Trump's and did not shy away from confrontation with journalists. She was regarded as one of Trump's confidants. Chief of staff replaced After the midterms, which were dramatic for the Republicans, Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles on Friday with hardliner Stephen Miller. The chief of staff is regarded as a pivotal figure in the White House, someone who smooths over political differences by correcting or placating party colleagues and rivals.

title: Yellow warning in parts of Drenthe, Groningen and Overijssel due to dense fog
lead: The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> has issued a yellow warning from 02.00 tonight until 10.00 tomorrow morning for parts of the northeast of the Netherlands due to dense fog. The warning is in effect in parts of Drenthe, Groningen and Overijssel. In the second half of the morning the (dense) fog will gradually lift, according to the KNMI. The fog may arise suddenly tonight and this morning. In case of local fog, visibility is less than 200 metres. The KNMI advises road users, among other things, to drive more slowly, keep greater distances from other road users, and switch on their fog lights at the front (when visibility is less than 200 metres) and at the rear (when visibility is less than 50 metres). Road users must also take into account delays and dangerous situations on the road. First regional code Since this month, weather codes are no longer issued for entire provinces, but warnings are given more targeted. For example, when it was slippery in the south of Limburg, the KNMI issued a weather warning for the whole province. Now such a warning is given locally. On Saturday a regional warning was issued for the first time.

title: Nearly 400,000 Russian deaths in war with Ukraine, hacked data shows
lead: Nearly 400,000 Russians have died as a result of the war since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. That is what hacked data from the Russian statistics bureau Rosstat shows, which news agency Bloomberg has viewed and analysed. The Belarusian hacker group Cyberpartisans and the Ukrainian hacker organisation Silent Crow obtained the data from Rosstat, the Russian counterpart of the Dutch <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS). It is said to involve a dataset of more than 11 million Russian death records, including information on age, place of residence and place of death. Nearly 400,000 Russians dead. The data show that between February 2022 and late August 2026, 392,700 death records contain an explicit reference to the war with Ukraine. This happens through codes or descriptions such as "military operation", "bombing" or "drones". According to Bloomberg, the actual death toll is "almost certainly" higher. Some soldiers are missing, bodies have not been identified, and others may have died later from wounds without this being registered as war-related. Hacker group Silent Crow estimates the number of dead at around 450,000. Bloomberg could not definitively prove the database is authentic, but found no evidence of forgery during its investigation. The data largely matched previously published official Russian mortality figures. Hack. The hackers reported on 1 November that they had hacked Rosstat's systems. A few days later the statistics bureau confirmed that it had been the target of targeted cyberattacks, although Rosstat denied that confidential data had been stolen. Russia does not disclose the number of soldiers killed in the war with Ukraine. No official figures have been published on this since the first months after the invasion in February 2022. Rosstat has also increasingly stopped publishing mortality statistics since then.

title: Extra breakdowns on top of breakdowns today: roadside assistance strikes
lead: Motorists who break down on the road today will have to be patient. ANWB employees - including roadside assistance - are laying down their work for 12 hours, from 09.00 in the morning until 21.00 in the evening. The trade unions are taking action because negotiations on a new collective labour agreement have stalled. Among other things, they consider the workload at the ANWB too high and see problems with the rosters. The unions must, by court order, ensure minimum staffing. As a result, emergencies, such as a stalled car in a tunnel, can still be resolved.

title: Cabinet designates five more locations where homes must be built faster
lead: The cabinet designates five more locations where homes must be built faster. These concern locations in Assen, Best, <entity id="org:gemeente-roosendaal">Roosendaal</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-zuidplas">Zuidplas</entity> and the area around Middelburg and <entity id="org:gemeente-vlissingen">Vlissingen</entity>. In total, around 25,000 homes must be ready by 2040, sooner than planned. The municipalities have had plans to build homes here ready for some time. But bringing those plans to a successful conclusion often proves difficult in practice. This is partly due to time-consuming objection procedures by local residents and the nitrogen problem. The cabinet therefore already designated several locations where the national government will help municipalities, for example with those permit applications. There are now 31 of them, across all provinces. In total, it concerns just over 400,000 homes that must be built faster than planned. Which locations have now been precisely designated? In Assen, around 5,000 to 6,000 homes will be built in Kloosterveen, Stadskwartier and Zuidoost. In Best, it concerns 3,500 homes, mainly around the station. On the Zeeland island of Walcheren, around 5,000 homes will be built in and around Middelburg, Vlissingen and Veere. In Roosendaal, 5,000 to 6,000 homes will be built in the railway zone. In Cortelande in the South Holland Zuidplas, an entirely new village with around 6,000 homes will be created. That village is controversial, because it lies at the lowest point in the Netherlands. Extra money for infrastructure will not be provided at these five locations. According to <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan</entity>, this is also not necessary, because these places are already well accessible. On part of the sites where the homes are to be built, businesses are currently located. These may therefore need to relocate. Boekholt-O'Sullivan wants to make "careful agreements" about this, she writes in a letter to Parliament.

title: Polder talks about a new social accord, but why exactly?
lead: It is time for a new 'social accord', which is why talks on this are starting in 'the polder'. Among others, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and ministers Vijlbrief of Social Affairs are meeting with trade unions and employers today. But what exactly is a social accord, who decides on it, and why are they negotiating precisely now? That there will be talks about a social accord is quite remarkable: so far, six such national accords have been concluded. The first was in the early 1970s, and the latest accord dates back to 2013, although one could also argue that the 2019 pension accord falls under it. A social accord (sometimes also called a central accord) is an agreement between employees, employers and the government. These parties, who together are called 'the polder', make agreements on, for example, wage developments, benefits and working conditions. These frameworks must still be translated into legislation and, for example, sector collective labour agreements (cao's). Cabinet collapse. So a direction is agreed on in which the country is to move. And because so many stakeholders are involved, the agreements have broad support, is the idea. As a result, the plans hold up, even if, for example, a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> falls. A social accord has broad support because many parties sit at the table. On behalf of the employers, the employers' organisation VNO-NCW, the entrepreneurs' association MKB-Nederland and the agricultural organisation LTO are taking part. Together, they represent, by their own account, around 500,000 businesses. On behalf of the employees, the trade unions FNV, CNV and VCP are participating. Taken together, they have more than a million members. What makes the support a bit broader is that a number of political parties have long felt connected to one of the negotiating partners. For example, Pro has close ties with the FNV, CDA feels connected to the trade union CNV and the farmers' organisation LTO, and VVD has a lot in common with the business clubs VNO-NCW and MKB-Nederland. A social accord is not concluded at fixed moments. Trade unions, employers and the cabinet decide at some point, when things are brewing, that it is time for new agreements. In 1982, for example, the 'Wassenaar Accord' was concluded. The core then was that, under pressure from rising unemployment, wage increases were limited. Employees received in return that they would not have to work as much. The agenda of this accord This time, incapacity for work is an important theme, especially the WIA. WIA stands for Work and Income according to Labour Capacity Act and regulates a benefit for people who cannot work because they are ill. The system is under pressure, because more and more people are ending up 'in the WIA', and because they find it difficult to get out again. That costs billions of euros in benefits, and in addition the organisation that has to manage all of this, the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, cannot cope with it. This is the situation with the WIA: Alongside the WIA, the WW will also be discussed. The Unemployment Benefits Act regulates a temporary benefit for people who end up without work. The cabinet wants to reduce that benefit, but the unions think that is a bad idea. In the Netherlands, around 195,000 people receive a WW benefit. 'Work to work' is another important subject for the cabinet. The labour market is in motion, is the idea, and how do you prevent people from moving from work to an expensive benefit? Government pot. A more technical point for the negotiating table is the issue surrounding the so-called AOF premiums. That is money that employers pay into a government pot from which, among other things, the WIA is paid. That premium is a percentage of the wage that employers pay. And that percentage has risen in recent years, while the pot of money has only become fuller. The AOF premium is meanwhile also being used by the cabinet to pay for other things. Unions and employers want to change this. Furthermore, economic growth is also on the programme. Fewer rules and lower burdens for businesses fuel that growth, and a larger economy generates money, also for the treasury, is the argument of the employers' organisations. The starting point for this discussion is the report by former ASML top executive Peter Wennink. Whether or not to hurry. It is still unclear when all of this should lead to a new social accord. The cabinet, which hopes to save money with the agreements, earlier mentioned next spring as a possibility. But FNV chairman Hans Spekman has already indicated that he does not share that view. "I do not feel rushed." The chairman of the employers' organisation VNO-NCW, Coen van Oostrom, previously did not want to make a prediction. "I do not think time is that important. The most important thing, in my view, is that we genuinely succeed in getting economic growth going." The expectation is that after today's meeting a joint target date will become known. It may also become clearer which topics will be discussed.

title: Royal couple on state visit to Qatar, first trip to the Middle East
lead: <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima will make a state visit to Qatar next month. It is their first trip to the Middle East since Willem-Alexander became king. The visit runs from 9 to 11 December. The royal couple was invited by Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar. The invitation follows a visit by the Emir to the Netherlands in June 2024. The visit is intended to strengthen the ties between the Netherlands and Qatar. The royal couple will be accompanied on the trip by <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>, <entity id="pos:minister-van-defensie">minister van Defensie</entity> Yesilgöz, <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">minister Sjoerdsma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-bho">Buitenlandse Handel en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking</entity> and <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of Agriculture. State visit to the region in 2012. According to the <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity>, this will be the first Dutch state visit to the Middle East in fourteen years. In early 2012 Queen Beatrix visited the United Arab Emirates and Oman. Willem-Alexander and Máxima were there too. In 2022 there was discussion about a possible visit by the king to Qatar because of the World Cup. Opponents did not want the king to go to the World Cup because of the human rights situation in the country. The king said at the time that personal feelings would play a role in the decision to go. If Oranje had reached the final, a government delegation would have travelled to Qatar. The Dutch team was knocked out in the quarter-finals. Tightened travel advice Because of the war between the US and Iran and the rising tensions in the region, the travel advice for Qatar was tightened to orange earlier this year. In response to American attacks, Iran attacked US allies in the Middle East. The travel advice is now yellow. That means travel to the country is possible, but there are still security risks.

title: Does tear gas disrupt menstruation? Women in France want it investigated
lead: Severe cramps, unbearable pain or an early period. Thousands of women in France say their menstrual cycle has been seriously disrupted after being exposed to tear gas at recent protests. A link between serious menstrual complaints and tear gas has not been scientifically established, but the call to stop using the agent is growing louder. French police have frequently used tear gas at the large-scale protests against the state of education and rising living costs. On 17 October as many as 22,000 tear gas grenades were deployed against demonstrators, says <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Minister Nunez. Police also used tear gas at protests last week. Complaints collected After Eva Luna Tholance heard stories from women who experienced abnormal menstrual complaints after exposure to tear gas, she founded the collective Lacrymos de sang (Blood tear gas) on 8 October. More than 10,000 women from all over France have since reported their experiences. Tholance says she is shocked that so many women say they have the same complaints. "Women experience anything from mild pain to the worst cramps of their lives. But also severe blood loss, so that some have to go to hospital." Sometimes the complaints appear within 48 hours, says Tholance. "We don't know what the long-term consequences are. That has not been investigated." Lacrymo de sang also says it has received many reports from women with complaints who did not take part in a protest. For example, they were walking their dog or had opened a window. "Tear gas doesn't discriminate, it affects everyone", says Tholance. 'Unbearable pain' French women are also telling their stories on social media. "On 17 October I was at a demonstration where tear gas was used", says a young woman in a video on TikTok. She says she came into brief contact with tear gas, and that it was enough to get watery eyes and a burning throat. "I went home and the next evening, about 28 hours after the exposure, I got very severe cramps. I have never in my life experienced such pain." Another woman says on Instagram that she unexpectedly got her period a day after a protest this month. Despite pain medication, which she calls "unbearable", she could not get out of bed. She reported her complaints to the platform Lacrymos de sang. Professor of clinical and forensic toxicology Eric Franssen is surprised by the reports and calls them serious. Still, he is cautious about drawing a direct link between tear gas and menstrual complaints, because too little research has been done. "Tear gas is essentially a powder that is dispersed into small particles that irritate the nerves and mucous membranes. That is why you get tears in your eyes and itching. In some cases blisters also form on the skin and the agent can cause an allergic reaction." There are different types of tear gas. In the Netherlands mainly CS gas is used, says Franssen, who is affiliated with the University of Amsterdam. This type of tear gas is also used in France. Voluntary sign-ups In 2020 a Scottish university researched the effects of tear gas on women who took part in yellow vest demonstrations in France. The study suggested there is a link between exposure to tear gas and menstrual complaints. In the United States a doctor decided a year later to conduct research, after several American women reported changes in their menstrual cycle. They were exposed to tear gas at Black Lives Matter protests in Portland, in the state of Oregon, in 2020. Just over 54 percent of the 1,650 respondents said they had problems with their periods. Most complaints concerned increased menstrual cramps and heavy bleeding. According to the study, the symptoms occurred mainly among women who had been exposed to tear gas on several days. In another American study, from 2023, 83 percent of the 1,276 respondents say they have complaints such as cramps, sensitive breasts and an early period after police used tear gas at protests. However, the participants in the studies signed up voluntarily and filled in questionnaires themselves. The women therefore did not undergo medical examinations to establish menstrual complaints or a possible link with tear gas. Stress Although all three studies suggest a link, they also point to other factors that may play a major role in the disruptions, says Franssen, such as stress. "You are being chased by the police during a demonstration. That adrenaline rush and stress can also lead to a disrupted menstrual cycle", says the professor. "It is an interplay in the body in which all those things can have an effect. That makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions." According to Franssen there is a knowledge gap. He therefore calls for more research. "It does say something that there is little knowledge about this issue." It has long been known that healthcare for women lags behind that for men. In recent years more attention has been paid to women-specific health problems in research and treatment. Falling on deaf ears Tholance of Lacrymos de sang also calls for more research. But she does not believe stress is the main cause. Her collective wants the French government to stop using tear gas until more is known about its effects. But that demand is for now falling on deaf ears. Minister Nunez of the Interior defended the use of tear gas last week after questions in parliament about the consequences of tear gas for women. According to him, officers must "be able to defend themselves when they are attacked at demonstrations". Nunez also said he was "not aware of the harmful nature of tear gas". According to him, the effects of tear gas are short-lived. "That is why I will not suspend the use of tear gas."

title: Eight years in prison for rape and attempted rape in a forest in Zeist
lead: The court in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> has sentenced a 47-year-old Georgian with no fixed abode or residence to eight years in prison for a violent rape and an attempted rape, both in Zeist. He has also been convicted of an attempted sexual assault in <entity id="org:gemeente-bunschoten">Bunschoten</entity>-Spakenburg. In addition, he has been issued a contact ban with his victims and a location ban for both municipalities. He must also pay his victims thousands of euros in damages. Rape The man on 15 August last year approached a woman in a forest in Zeist, struck her in the face out of nowhere and grabbed her by the throat with both hands. He repeatedly shouted "I kill you", dragged her into the bushes and raped her. The man says he cannot remember the rape, but according to the court it is established that it was him, also because his DNA was found on the woman. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> tracked him down with help from images recorded by a security camera of a house in the area. These were shared, which yielded usable tips. Attempted rape The investigation further revealed that an hour and a half earlier, in the same area, he tried to rape a woman who was cycling past. He grabbed her by the upper arm, held her bicycle and pointed in the direction of the forest. The woman began to scream for help and kept doing so, even when the man put his hand over her mouth. Eventually he let her go and fled, leaving DNA evidence on the bicycle's luggage carrier. Attempted sexual assault The attempted sexual assault took place almost two weeks earlier in the outskirts of Bunschoten-Spakenburg. The man approached a woman who was walking there and took a selfie with her. When she wanted to keep walking, he became angry and kept following her. When she made contact with a group of birdwatchers, he cycled on. Half an hour to three quarters later she ran into him again. He told her he had a pistol on him, but that he did not use it against friends. When he put his hand on her shoulder, she made a defensive gesture, after which he turned around and cycled away.

title: VVD figures back Weekers, who wants a different course for the party
lead: It is not an attack on the party or the leadership, not at all. It is rather an offer of support, which he wants to give "from the back bench". That is what Frans Weekers said last night, when he surprised many VVD members by putting himself forward as a rival candidate for <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> in the programme Pauw, De Wit en Moggré. The board had already nominated former minister Adriaansens, but members of VVD branches in Limburg and Brabant will also nominate him soon. Weekers says he is worried about the party. Members are leaving. Some think the VVD sits too much on D66's luggage carrier, others think the VVD is a PVV-light. He wants the party to return to liberal ideas and stop excluding other parties. According to him, the VVD should never have done that in last year's election campaign, and it should not do so now either. Support for Remkes, Teeven, Zijlstra and De Krom This is criticism that VVD members active in local or provincial government have voiced more often. But Weekers' criticism and candidacy are now also openly supported by, among others, former minister Johan Remkes, former state secretary Fred Teeven, former minister Halbe Zijlstra and former state secretary Paul de Krom. Remkes and Teeven leave it at a statement of support, while De Krom and Zijlstra gave the NOS extensive interviews. They too want an end to excluding other parties and a debate about the course. Former parliamentary group leader and minister Zijlstra thinks Weekers' candidacy could be "a reset for the party". "Power and counterpower within a party are ultimately vital, and that has now slipped away too far," he thinks. Members should, according to Zijlstra, regain more influence. 'No attack on leadership' He calls anyone who starts on Yesilgöz's position "naive". The problem has existed for longer; in his view the VVD has strayed too far from its course. As for the timing of Weekers, in a week in which the minority cabinet is still looking for a way to agree on the tax plan, they see nothing strange. Candidates for the parliamentary group leadership can register until mid-December, and Weekers is "neatly following that route", according to Zijlstra and De Krom. 'Candidacy in itself already an attack' A former VVD minister who does not want to be named thinks Weekers' candidacy is in itself already an attack. Former minister Henk Kamp does not see it that way. According to him, Yesilgöz's party leadership is not up for discussion, not even because of this candidacy. "Dilan remains our leader for this term. The question of the lead candidacy only arises at new elections," says Kamp. A lead candidate election for the Senate fits the democratic process now, given the provincial elections next spring, he thinks. Kamp supports Adriaansens, who was nominated by the party board, but has no problem with Weekers putting himself forward now. On substance, Kamp does not agree with Weekers: the clarity Yesilgöz gave in the campaign about parties and plans the VVD wants nothing to do with, he saw as a clear course. That Weekers did not call Yesilgöz before sitting down in a TV programme is not strange, says De Krom. The board should have known, and he had informed it. On the NOS's questions to Yesilgöz herself, a spokesperson said today that she will not answer them.

title: Sinterklaasjournaal keeps things exciting, successor to De Walle still unclear
lead: In the first episode of Het Sinterklaasjournaal it has not yet become clear who will look after the Grote Boek from now on. Last September it became known that Stefan de Walle would hang up the red cape after fifteen years. Broadcaster NTR remained silent about his successor. That is still a mystery. In the first episode Hoofdpiet showed presenter Merel Westrik the steamboat, but Sinterklaas was nowhere to be seen. "We don't need to worry about Sinterklaas," said Hoofdpiet. "He's just hard at work in his study. He's sitting right here behind his desk. He can't be missed." But <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de kamer</entity> turned out to be empty. "I think I missed something," stammered Hoofdpiet. "I think so too," Westrik responded. "Sinterklaas is not on the steamboat," she said at the end of the episode. "Well, I never." On Saturday the Sint can at least be seen in all his glory. Then he and his helpers will set foot ashore in Grave, in the <entity id="org:gemeente-land-van-cuijk">gemeente Land van Cuijk</entity> in Brabant. According to <entity id="person:marieke-moorman">burgemeester Moorman</entity>, the historic city is ready for him. "We already have a lovely present for him," she said in Het Sinterklaasjournaal. "Tomorrow we are going to unveil it on the market." 'Hallootjes' The 61-year-old De Walle was responsible for the Grote Boek for fifteen years. "Dear Netherlands, with gratitude and with pain in my heart, after fifteen years my role as adviser to the national Sint is coming to an end," De Walle said in a statement in September. The actor called it an honour and a pleasure to have been Sinterklaas for many years. "Hallootjes" rang out every year as De Walle waved to the thousands of adults and children who had come along. His last national arrival was last year, when the steamboat docked in the harbour of Oudeschild on Texel. De Walle broke through to the general public in the 1990s with the role of Kees in the television series Flodder , about the antisocial Flodder family who move into the villa neighbourhood Zonnedael in the fictional city of Amstelhaeghe. Left voluntarily? It is not entirely clear whether De Walle's departure as Sinterklaas was voluntary. Just over a week ago, cabaret artist Karel de Rooij said to De Walle in his podcast Het bankje van Karel that it may be difficult to say goodbye to the role of Sinterklaas at some point. "Certainly," De Walle responded. "I will one day tell the full, detailed story of how all of that went and how this outcome came about," De Walle further said. The Instagram account SintTalk also discovered that De Walle will be seen as Sinterklaas again soon. On 2 December the actor performs two shows as Sint at Theater aan het Spui in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>. Rumours After the announcement that De Walle would stop, the rumour mill started up. For example, Matthijs Jansen of SintTalk reported that Daan Schuurmans would take on the role. The 54-year-old actor denied this report. He did say he knew who would be playing Sinterklaas, without giving further details. Although De Walle played the role of Sint Nicolaas for years, his predecessor, Bram van der Vlugt, was seen in the role for an even longer period: a quarter of a century. The actor, who died in 2020, was the Sint at the national arrivals and in Het Sinterklaasjournaal between 1986 and 2010. Sinterklaas on television through the years:

title: Political message at Kristallnight commemoration: 'Red Line protest is anti-Israel'
lead: In Amsterdam the Kristallnacht has been commemorated, 88 years ago today. The chairman of the Central Jewish Council (CJO), Chanan Hertzberger, chose a remarkably political message in his speech. He drew a direct link to yesterday's Red Line demonstration. Hertzberger thanked Jetten for not having gone into "the demands of the organisers of the anti-Israel demonstration". At his weekly press conference last week, the prime minister said that "the Netherlands is definitely taking a stand". According to him, it works better to put pressure on the Israeli government from Europe and with other international partners. At the Red Line demonstration against the Dutch government's Israel policy yesterday, according to the organisation at least 200,000 people took part. Demonstrators argue that violations of international law are being normalised and that this must stop. They demand, among other things, that military cooperation with Israel be halted. By wearing red, the demonstrators figuratively drew a red line. According to Hertzberger, the measures demanded "amount directly or indirectly to Israel being wiped off the map". 'Genocide lie' In his speech Hertzberger said that it "was to be expected that the extremes of the political spectrum would embrace the genocide lie". He is referring to the violence in Gaza. An independent UN investigative commission concluded last year that Israel is committing genocide in the Gaza Strip. According to Hertzberger, a judge determines whether there is genocide in Gaza. "Not demonstrators full of hate. Not politicians. Not journalists." According to the chairman, "Jews are collectively held responsible". "Who are being confronted in Arnhem, in Groningen, in Amsterdam about this so-called genocide? Us. The Jews. In our own city. On our street. In our children's class. We are being excluded and pushed to the margins of society," said the CJO chairman. In his speech Hertzberger draws parallels between history and now. "Ultimately the question is not how often antisemitism has been condemned, but what has actually been done to combat it," is his conclusion. Also, for the first time in ten years a Dutch prime minister gave a speech. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> spoke of anti-Jewish sentiments in the Netherlands. "Pogroms have occurred throughout history, and the lesson of history is that violence against Jews is never far away." The prime minister described antisemitism as "back, never having gone away". He described it as a smouldering peat fire, with flames of hatred flaring up again. "We see and hear it again in public debate and on social media, in antisemitic expressions that increasingly reach us unfiltered." Hertzberger stressed in his speech the importance of the presence of the prime minister, "especially now that Jewish life in the Netherlands is increasingly under pressure". What was Kristallnacht? In the night of 9 to 10 November 1938, Jews were attacked, arrested or murdered across Germany, Austria and parts of what was then Czechoslovakia. The violence spread as an organised pogrom by National Socialists. Hundreds of Jews were murdered, synagogues were set on fire, and shops and homes of Jews were looted and destroyed. Jewish schools and cemeteries were also targets. It is estimated that 30,000 arrested Jews were deported to concentration camps. Kristallnacht is also known as 'The Night of Broken Glass'. It was the prelude to the genocide of Jews in the Nazis' concentration camps and in large-scale executions in German-occupied territory. In the days after Kristallnacht in 1938, thousands of German Jews fled to the Netherlands. They sought a safe refuge, said Jetten. "The harsh truth is that most of them did so in vain." Resilient against antisemitism In his speech Jetten said that a few weeks ago he received a book from a young man, containing the story of his great-grandmother who survived the concentration camps. He quotes what the man wrote in it: "This is the story of my great-grandmother who survived the camps. Thanks to her willpower I am here. I hope my daughter has a future here in the Netherlands." Jetten said that it must never be the case that the man's daughter has no future in the Netherlands. According to him, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has earmarked funds for the protection of Jewish buildings and institutions. "But there is also a broader task, because combating antisemitism must be more than action and reaction. (...) As a society we must become more resilient against antisemitism. We must arm ourselves against it. Keep fighting it." Jetten said it is necessary for the Jewish community to remain visible in society. He says that he has hung a Delft blue mezuzah, a prayer scroll in a small case, by his front door. "To show that I want to be prime minister of a country in which Jewish life is visible."

title: France believes Iran was behind attack on supermarket cooling systems
lead: The French Public Prosecution Service has started an investigation into the leader of an Iranian group that allegedly sabotaged the cooling systems of about 700 French supermarkets in October. Major supermarket chains such as Intermarché and E.Leclerc had to throw away stock because hackers pushed the temperature in fridges and freezers up to 50 degrees. According to the French news channel BFM, the investigation is focused on the head of the hacker group Shahid Kaveh, which has ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the elite force of the Iranian state. French investigators conclude that this group was behind it from the "characteristic way of attacking", the use of the Persian language and IP addresses pointing to Iran. French Foreign Minister Barrot speaks on the news site France24 of an unprecedented act of aggression. "We will impose sanctions at European level on anyone responsible for this attack." He will also summon the Iranian ambassador in Paris. Also in the Netherlands Earlier this month, unknown persons attacked cooling systems of companies in the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden. In the Netherlands, large supermarkets were spared, but at least seventeen other companies were hit, including butchers and neighbourhood shops. In Belgium, the cooling in dozens of supermarkets was sabotaged, including those of Carrefour and Delhaize. In France, cooling systems at blood banks were attacked. This butcher in the Belgian town of Hove had damage of tens of thousands of euros:

title: Increasing electricity's share of energy use is a major task for the Netherlands
lead: This is one of the main items on the agenda of this year's climate summit: can the world use a larger share of its energy in the form of electricity? Electricity's share in the Netherlands is currently still 25 percent. Countries want to increase this worldwide to 35 percent within nine years. When done wisely, experts say this has several advantages. It saves energy, makes countries less dependent on energy imports, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions that warm the earth. 1200 degrees Celsius But it would be a major challenge for the Netherlands to reach this goal, especially given the problems with the overloaded electricity grid. Our country is switching to electricity, but should do so faster. "A lot really needs to happen for that," says Sanne de Boer, energy transition expert at RaboResearch. Especially in industry, transport and homes there are opportunities for electrification. De Boer expects industry's contribution to be limited in the coming years. Many factory processes take place at such high temperatures that they cannot (yet) run on electricity. Think of fertilizer production. In 'lighter' sectors such as paper and glass production more is possible, and this is already happening. At Isover in Etten-Leur, for example, they make insulation material from glass wool, made from a mixture of cullet, soda, sand and lime. This takes place in a furnace at 1200 degrees Celsius, and for two years now it no longer runs on gas alone. Industrial kettle The company built a furnace with electrodes that supply heat from electricity. "Like a kettle, but on an industrial scale," says factory director Jurgen Nooren. The furnace uses a quarter less energy and more than half less gas. "Still, industry is only electrifying sparingly," says Michèlle Prins, expert in industrial transformation at environmental organization Natuur & Milieu. In recent years expectations have been lowered. Many companies want to, but face numerous obstacles, such as the overloaded grid. Isover already made plans in 2020 to partly switch to electricity. The grid problems were less serious then, says factory director Nooren, and did not cause much delay. Companies are now on long waiting lists. Grid operators also keep charging higher and higher tariffs. And even if a company can electrify, that does not mean it is attractive. Isover received a subsidy from the European Union for the construction because it was an innovative project. But even now that it is running, the furnace is more expensive than a gas furnace, says Nooren, even with current gas prices. Here too, a subsidy narrows the difference. Struggling to survive Meanwhile European industry is having a hard time. The chemical industry in particular faces higher energy prices, an uneven playing field and fierce competition. "Where competition is fierce, companies are mainly busy surviving," says Prins. "So it is up to the government to step up sharp policy, such as scaling up offshore wind, expanding grids and a mandatory share of green electricity use." To still reach 35 percent, homes and transport would therefore have to electrify considerably. There are options for this: petrol cars can be replaced with electric cars, a home can be heated with a heat pump, and cooking can be done by induction. There are also fewer obstacles here than in industry, De Boer of RaboResearch explains. For example, the grid usually does not pose a problem. However, homes must be sufficiently insulated and have room for a heat pump. Furthermore, electrifying is often advantageous in the long term. People do have to make a considerable upfront investment. In new construction, heat pumps and induction cooking are already standard. Electricity is efficient Transport is also electrifying steadily. Hybrid and electric passenger cars are gaining ground. De Boer sees delivery vans and heavier transport increasingly switching to electricity too. That reaching 35 percent is still tough is, oddly enough, due to how efficient electricity use is. When a home switches to a heat pump, it needs only a third of the energy that was required to heat it with gas. So the share of electricity is increasing only slowly. If you want to reach 35 percent, you have to electrify far more than 35 percent of homes, De Boer explains. Say you have 100 homes heated with gas, you would need to install a heat pump in 60 homes. For passenger cars the difference is even larger. Especially if industry's contribution lags behind, the Netherlands can only come close to the goal with far-reaching electrification.

title: Much criticism of new box 3 proposal, but a majority is in sight
lead: In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> there is much criticism of the new cabinet proposal to introduce a capital gains tax in box 3 as soon as possible. Opposition parties in particular think the proposal is being rushed through parliament and that the funding is shaky. "An uncovered, blank cheque of 17 billion euros for the wealthy," said Pro MP Stultiens in tonight's debate. But because parties such as JA21 and the SGP were fairly positive about the proposal, a majority in the House is nonetheless in sight for the minority cabinet. The coalition parties CDA and D66 do have questions about how the minority cabinet intends to offset the lower tax revenue. "We find this exciting too," said CDA MP Van Dijk. But ultimately CDA and D66 are willing to support the proposal. Quick clarity D66 member Oosterhuis called the funding by <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> "a fairly creative interpretation of the budget rules". But the largest government party also sees no reason to block the proposal. In its view, clarity should come quickly "for households, entrepreneurs and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">belastingdienst</entity>" about box 3. "If it is somewhat responsible, we are willing to jump in," said CDA member Van Dijk. The House was supposed to discuss the whole proposal today, but a majority of the MPs present want to wait to make a decision until they have also been able to ask Heinen questions. He is in Brussels for a meeting with his EU colleagues, which is why <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had only delegated <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscaliteit) to attend. But it was Heinen who decided at the end of February that the plans for box 3, which after years of work were ready for consideration in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>, had to be overhauled again. The opposition mainly wants to question him about how the proposed adjustments are financially covered. Billion-euro gap after 2031. In Heinen's proposal we move to a tax on actual realised profit, which is only levied at the moment shares or property are sold. That system will, up to 2040, according to estimates, bring the state 22 billion euros less revenue compared with earlier plans. The annex to the proposal shows that the minority cabinet has largely covered this loss of revenue up to 2031. But after that, when this government term is over, a gap arises that could rise to 17.6 billion euros. "The rule always applies here: how are you going to pay for it? Except for Eelco Heinen," argued Stultiens of Pro. He called it "dirt-cheap botched work". The only reason this proposal is on the table now, in his view, is that minister Heinen and the VVD want it. Stultiens pointed out that the cabinet has meanwhile left room for postponing the introduction, from 2028 to 2029 at the latest. "So there is no reason to be in a hurry." ChristenUnie MP Grinwis agreed with him. He called it "undesirable and careless" that the proposal must be dealt with within a week. Grinwis thinks the plan is being "forced down the House's throat". Heinen's own party, the VVD, thinks the proposal is sufficiently covered despite the billion-euro gap. MP Van Eijk urged quick introduction, because in her view there must be calm and clarity for people who pay tax in box 3. The PVV is also in favour, but MP Vlottes called the financial underpinning "phantom funding". The PVV member did not yet want to say how his party will vote next Thursday, when the vote on the proposal is scheduled. "But if this cabinet wants to make itself dependent on the PVV, they may well come home from a cold fair," said Vlottes. Senate. Despite all the criticism, the minority cabinet does have a majority in sight in the House of Representatives, with the support of the right-wing opposition parties JA21 and SGP. It is still unclear how the proposal will be received in the Senate. The senate traditionally looks at the quality of legislation and its feasibility. Last week the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> was still scathing about the cabinet's haste. The Tax Administration and the banks, which must supply data on their customers to the fiscus, also indicate that a quick introduction will be difficult.

title: Trial with less supervision in prisons to deal with staff shortages
lead: In three prisons spread across the country, a trial begins to give a group of prisoners more independence. They receive less security and support due to staff shortages. The trial lasts one year and is part of the Actieplan Ruimte voor Recht, which aims to solve capacity problems in prisons, Omroep Zeeland reports. The Middelburg prison Torentijd is taking part in the pilot, as well as a prison in Ter Apel and one in Veenhuizen. Difference in amount of attention. The aim of the trial is that not every prisoner needs the same attention. By distinguishing between the amount of security, guidance and support, staff can be deployed more purposefully, explains Jannine van den Berg. She is director of Prison Service and Immigration Detention at the <entity id="org:dienst-justitiele-inrichtingen">Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen</entity> (DJI). Prisoners are only eligible for the trial if they meet set criteria. Clear agreements are made with those selected about, for example, behaviour, responsibilities and keeping agreements. During the trial, prisoners may independently use the recreation room and must divide fixed tasks among themselves. They also get more opportunities to reintegrate. At Torentijd 12 detainees have been selected, in Veenhuizen 24 and in Ter Apel 36. Possibly at more locations. The number of incidents and the sense of safety will be monitored regularly. The experiences will be used to develop the concept further and ultimately roll it out nationwide. "The experiences of the colleagues who now start working with this new concept are extremely important to learn what works, what could be better and what this asks of staff and detainees", says Van den Berg.

title: Fatal shooting in Schiedam: slightly injured suspect released
lead: A man who was slightly injured last Saturday in the fatal shooting in Schiedam and then ran away is no longer considered a suspect. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports this in a statement. Last Saturday, three young men were doing odd jobs in the front garden of a house on the Weverpad when they came under fire at around 17.00 hours. A 19-year-old man died in the shooting. Emergency services attempted to resuscitate him, but he died on the spot. One of the men was injured and had to go to hospital. He is out of danger. The slightly injured man, who ran away, was later found and arrested. He has been free since this afternoon. Search for perpetrators A large search for the shooters was launched after the shooting incident, still without result. The police call on local residents to share doorbell camera footage of the incident. The police have also shared the description of the suspects. One suspect wore a black cap and a grey hooded jacket. The other two suspects wore black beanies and black hooded jackets. All three wore black trousers and black sneakers. "Major event" The <entity id="pos:burgemeester-schiedam">burgemeester van Schiedam</entity>, <entity id="person:harald-bergmann">Harald Bergmann</entity>, speaks of a "dramatic event". Cameras have been installed in the area around the scene of the shooting. Homes may also be closed "to restore public order". A police spokesperson says they are taking into account that the 19-year-old man who died was not the intended target. "But several scenarios are being investigated." The mayor calls for people not to speculate. On Sunday evening a silent march was held for the 19-year-old victim. A few hours later there were two explosions in Schiedam. It is unclear whether there is a connection with the fatal shooting.

title: Woman from Baarle-Hertog assaulted after confronting boy about setting off fireworks
lead: In the Belgian municipality of Baarle-Hertog a woman was seriously assaulted on Saturday after she confronted a boy about setting off fireworks. The boy's father did not agree with this, she writes on Facebook. He allegedly knocked her to the ground twice and kicked her in the head. "According to the doctors at the hospital, I got off lightly with only external injuries and a bad concussion." The photos she posted with the message show that she got a black eye and injuries to an elbow, her hand and behind one ear. The woman's husband tells the daily BN DeStem that he was also assaulted. From their café he watched the man knock his wife down. "I went outside and tried to calm the man down, but there was no stopping him. I think he was even a trained kickboxer or something. I had to take a few kicks myself too." The man and the boy allegedly drove away in a van with a Dutch license plate. Both the woman and the mayor of Baarle-Hertog, Philip Loots, say the license plate has been recorded. According to the mayor, the man is also on video. The woman says she is going to file a report. Because, as far as is known, this has not yet happened, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in Baarle-Hertog cannot say anything about the case. Nuisance from Dutch people Baarle-Hertog is a Belgian municipality, just south of <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity>, surrounded by Dutch territory. For decades the municipality has been a popular destination for Dutch fireworks enthusiasts, because it sells fireworks that are banned in the Netherlands. Mayor Loots is completely fed up with the nuisance caused by Dutch people through the sale of fireworks. "Fireworks belong at professional, organised events, not in the hands of everyone who just wants to start using them", he says on Facebook. "95 percent of the customers come from the Netherlands", he tells the NOS. According to him, from August until New Year's Eve they are guilty of parking illegally, urinating in public, verbal aggression and testing fireworks by setting them off. "When I raise this issue, some in the fireworks sector dismiss it as exaggerated or as stirring up trouble", he says on Facebook. "Well, I invite them to talk to our residents." Bill The party of Loots, the N-VA, submitted a bill earlier this year for a ban on the sale of heavy fireworks. Fireworks in categories F2 and F3 would, after a mayor's permission, only be sold to professionals and could only be set off in a safe place.

title: Missing 13-year-old girl from Berlin found dead in house next to seriously wounded 22-year-old man
lead: A 13-year-old girl from Berlin who had been missing since last week Tuesday was found dead yesterday in an empty house in the village of Altglietzen, close to the border with Poland. The police also found a seriously wounded 22-year-old man there. He has been taken to hospital in critical condition and is being guarded there by the police. The Berlin police say they assume that the man is responsible for the abduction and murder of the girl Lisa. German media write that the man attempted suicide when the police entered the house. Officers reportedly found him with a life-threatening gunshot wound. He is in intensive care. 113 Are you thinking about suicide or worried about someone? Talking helps, and you can do so anonymously via the chat at www.113.nl or by phone on 113 or 0800-0113. The Public Prosecution Service (OM) reports that, like the girl Lisa, he comes from the Berlin district of Marzahn-Hellersdorf. He has no criminal record, but since August 2025 two investigations have been running into him for obtaining and possessing images of child abuse. For example, during a house search in March 2025, 900 "incriminating files" were seized from the man. Later, "a large number of other alleged child pornography items" were also found on his mobile phone. 'Mama misses you' Lisa's case has gripped Germany for days. The girl left her parents' home at around 7:15 a.m. last week Tuesday to go to school. According to her sister, she was texting a friend on the way, but the contact suddenly stopped, three minutes after she had left her house. She never arrived at her school. That same afternoon the police issued a missing person notice with a photo of Lisa. Her mother also appealed for people to look out for her daughter. On social media she wrote: "Mama hopes you come home safe and sound. Mama misses you so much." Massive search Neighbourhood residents distributed flyers about the disappearance in the following days, and the police deployed a helicopter and search dogs. Last Saturday more than 200 officers went door to door in the neighbourhood where Lisa lived. On Sunday a police chief said that a crime was being considered. Shortly afterwards, Lisa's body was found by chance in the empty house. According to German media, the police had received a report from the homeowner that unauthorised persons had entered the vacant property. Once inside, officers found both Lisa's body and the 22-year-old seriously wounded suspect. Lisa's discovery was a coincidence The police had no indication that Lisa would be there, a spokesperson says. "In the end it was purely by chance that this break-in led to her discovery," said a press spokesperson for the OM in Berlin to German media. According to the OM, an autopsy has been performed on Lisa's body, but no cause of death has yet been determined. It is also still unclear when she died. There are no indications that the suspect and the victim knew each other. The police say they assume Lisa was a random victim. The investigation of the empty house and of the man's home in Berlin is still ongoing.

title: Pensions for healthcare, construction, metal and technology sectors up slightly
lead: For pensioners from healthcare, construction, and the metal and technology sector, pension payouts will rise slightly from 2027. Retired healthcare workers will see their payouts rise by 0.75 percent. In construction, pensioners will get 0.8 percent more, and former metal workers 0.82 percent. Pension funds Zorg & Welzijn, BpfBouw and PMT announced this today. These are the three largest pension funds that switched to the new pension system at the start of this year. The funds face uncertainty in the financial markets. On the stock market there is optimism this year about the performance of tech companies, but the American attack on Iran has caused unrest and fluctuations. New pension system. In the new pension system, pension payouts of pensioners will, more than in the old system, move with the investment results of a pension fund. If those results are good, pensions can be increased faster than in the old system.
