If parties related to each other better in that way, a very different kind of politics would emerge, in her view. "What people may not fully realise is that right now, all across the Netherlands, everyone has long wished for that", Dijksma says. Live Commons debate on the NOS The Tweede Kamer debate on the tax plan can be followed live here. You can also read all the latest developments in this liveblog.

title: NOS articles about kidnapped Insiya to be blocked by Google in India
lead: NOS articles about the girl Insiya, who was abducted to India, will soon be blocked by Google in search results for users in India. Google says it is doing so on the order of a court order issued by a judge in New Delhi. In total, it concerns seventeen articles. Ten years ago, the two-year-old Insiya was abducted in broad daylight by four men in Amsterdam East. They took her by force to her father in India. Since then her mother Nadia Rashid has been trying with all her might to get her now 12-year-old daughter back. She has not seen her daughter since that fateful day. The abductors and the father were previously sentenced to prison terms in the Netherlands. The father of the child was sentenced in absentia to nine years' imprisonment. Child abductions are not recognised in India if the child stays with one of the two parents. In addition, India has not signed the Hague Convention on International Child Abduction and is therefore not bound by the agreements under it, which further complicates the case. Court order: On enquiry by the NOS, Google says it made the decisions on the basis of an order issued on 30 October. The NOS has this order in its hands. It states that the case was brought by Insiya's father and her paternal grandmother. It is unclear when the case was brought. They want the "offensive, defamatory and false content" produced by various media organisations removed. The family believes the girl has a right to privacy and should not have to be in the news all the time. The judge in India goes along with this and speaks of false and damaging articles from the Netherlands. Besides the NOS articles, according to the order, articles, videos and posts on this subject from dozens of other media organisations are also blocked. Google says it complies with court orders in countries where the company operates, after it has assessed them legally itself. However, Google stresses that the measure is limited to India and has no effect on search results for users of Google in other countries. 'Silenced' The NOS has among others contacted the lawyer of Insiya's mother. He says he has no further information. Insiya's mother says she has not been heard in the case. Following the blocking by Google, Insiya's mother posted a video on social media this week in which she says her social media accounts in India have also been blocked. "My daughter cannot see this, then," she says in the video. "The kidnapper who has been convicted gets off scot-free. As a mother I am being silenced, just like the free press." She calls it unprecedented and unacceptable and calls on <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to take action. Under the YouTube channel that mother Rashid started to campaign for her daughter's return, threatening comments about the father are said to be readable. Those threats are also mentioned as one of the reasons for the blocking. There is also talk of the impact of this campaign and the various news articles about Insiya. She is said to have been traumatised by it and even put in danger. How exactly is not clearly described. It is mentioned that she was recently recognised several times by strangers. While sitting in a café in a shopping mall in New Delhi, she is said to have been approached by people who recognised her. Another time she was reportedly approached by fellow pupils about her family situation. 'The matter has full attention' The case surrounding Insiya has the full attention of <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>, he said last week in a debate. According to the minister, the case is constantly mentioned and raised in the talks the Netherlands has with India. At the end of this month Berendsen travels to India, "then I will discuss this again". A Dutch delegation will also go to India in the short term. "We will then look at how we can make concrete steps". Berendsen points out that there are also court cases about this in India. "But it is clear to India that this issue is not going to be removed from our agenda." At the same time, the Dutch embassy in New Delhi is investigating whether the blocking is based on a legal procedure.

title: Nine men arrested in Rotterdam in major drugs investigation
lead: In Rotterdam, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested nine men suspected of taking part in a criminal organisation. This happened when arrest teams raided eleven addresses as part of a large-scale drugs investigation. On Monday the police searched homes and business premises in Crooswijk, Ommoord and Delfshaven. Narcotics, large sums of cash and several cars were seized. RTV Rijnmond writes that it is not known what kind of drugs were involved. Eight of the suspects are from Rotterdam and one is from The Hague. They are between 27 and 40 years old and are suspected of taking part in a criminal organisation in the drugs trade. Three of them are also suspected of money laundering. All suspects remain in custody. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is investigating the case and does not rule out further arrests.

title: Tax plan passed, and now the question is what the VVD will do
lead: A majority was finally found at the very last moment for the tax plan, but whether the coalition can survive this is very much in question. The VVD has taken a heavy blow from its coalition partners D66 and CDA, and relations within the minority coalition have reached a low point. "Appalling", was the conclusion of VVD-<entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractieleider Brekelmans</entity> at the end of an eventful day. He did not yet want to say whether this also means the end of this coalition. If it is up to <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> (D66), there is no question of that. He will "do everything" to hold the coalition together, he said this evening. Tomorrow morning Jetten wants to discuss this with deputy prime ministers Yeşilgöz (VVD) and Van den Brink (CDA). After a day full of debate, the tax plan, which had been wrangled over for months, passed with the smallest possible majority of 76 seats. That majority 'from the left' came about without the VVD. It voted against because earlier that evening an amendment by Pro and Volt was adopted. Jetten says he hopes for 'a fresh start': that amendment, on which a deal had been struck with D66 and CDA, states that people with large fortunes will pay more tax. The plan was untenable for the VVD, which felt ambushed by its coalition partners. So D66 and CDA set about finding another way to get the tax plan, which sets government revenue for next year, through <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity>. They found it by persuading Denk and the Party for the Animals just before the vote. In exchange for its support, the PvdD got higher tax on private jets, and CDA and D66 also promised that a rise in train ticket prices is off the table. What the two parties offered Denk to win it over is not known. Huge climbdown: That a coalition is split over something as essential as a tax plan is unprecedented. For the VVD, this has created an impossible situation. The tax plan has been reworked by 'the left', but must be carried out by VVD-<entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. The cracks already in the coalition have been considerably widened by this. "I did not expect CDA and D66 to make such a huge concession to the left", sighed Brekelmans. His party is taking time to reflect on everything this evening, he also said. 'No major decisions now', said Brekelmans. Like the prime minister, fellow parliamentary group leaders Paternotte (D66) and Bontenbal (CDA) urged the VVD not to break up. "I hope we come out of this stronger", said Bontenbal. "Go and talk about the serious fresh start the prime minister has offered", said Paternotte. VVD leader Yesilgöz was not at the debate today, but she said yesterday that a "fundamental reset" is needed in the coalition. What she meant by that she did not explain further, but tomorrow will probably show whether it will come to that.

title: Power struggle among Democrats over leadership in the Senate
lead: For the first time in years, the Democrats in the US Senate will vote on who will lead the caucus. Chris Van Hollen (67) is putting himself forward as a challenger to veteran Chuck Schumer (75). Schumer, from the state of New York, has been leader of the Democrats in the upper house of the US Congress since 2017. He has since been re-elected every two years by acclamation. No one has ever stood against him. Since the same was true of his predecessor, the last Democratic leadership election dates from 1994. Several party colleagues have been grumbling that Schumer would once again lead the caucus. On the one hand he is seen as one of the architects of last week's major Democratic victory, by personally choosing candidates such as Sherrod Brown, Roy Cooper and Mary Peltola, who made life difficult for Republicans in Ohio, North Carolina and Alaska. On the other hand he is seen as the old guard within the party, uninspiring and too old. Especially now that eight (perhaps even nine) newcomers have been elected, this is seen as the moment to shake things up. Schumer has been in the US parliament since 1981. Vote for change The new candidate Van Hollen stresses that it is not about Schumer himself. "It is not about one person. We must heed the call of the American people," Van Hollen says on announcing his candidacy. "The American people want change." Van Hollen has represented Maryland in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> since 2017. He is of Dutch descent and in 2006, together with the Dutch-born Republican Pete Hoekstra, founded the Congressional Caucus on the Kingdom of the Netherlands. That Congressional caucus works for good ties with the Netherlands. The influential Bernie Sanders is at any rate opposed to Schumer as caucus leader. Although Sanders is not officially a Democrat, he does vote with that caucus as an independent leftwing politician. "It is time for change," he said earlier. "That is why I will not support Chuck in his re-election." Delivering on the mandate Newly elected party colleague Abdul El-Sayed also earlier indicated that he wants Schumer gone. In the primaries Schumer had not backed him but Haley Stevens, the more moderate Democrat who, on the eve of the elections, suddenly expressed support for a Republican. "We must deliver on our mandate," El-Sayed said of Schumer. "If it becomes more of the same, I fear we do not deserve our mandate." He praised Van Hollen for visiting Kilmar Ábrego García, who had been deported, in El Salvador: "He took that risk so that he could keep talking about it." Schumer is convinced that enough colleagues will support him to remain caucus leader. Republican leaders already known The Democrats will choose their leader behind closed doors early next month. Before then the caucus in the House of Representatives must have chosen its leader. So far only the incumbent caucus chair Hakeem Jeffries is a candidate. Among Republicans in the House, Jim Jordan was earlier this week chosen as successor to Mike Johnson, who no longer wanted the role. Jordan, who is regarded as a conservative hardliner, was chosen with 106 votes to 73 in the contest with Steve Scalise. In the Senate, incumbent caucus chair John Thune was re-elected without a challenger.

title: Health insurance premiums rise sharply next year, but there are major differences
lead: The health insurance premium will become considerably more expensive next year. This is clear now that health insurers have announced the premiums for the mandatory basic insurance. These had to be presented before midnight. And there is something to choose. For example, the premium for the cheapest health insurance at Zilveren Kruis rises by 5.50 euros to 159.45 euros, while at CZ the basic insurance will cost 177.25 euros, an increase of just over 17 euros compared with last year. Health insurer Menzis charges a premium of 165.75 euros for the basic package in 2027, an increase of 9.50 euros. At another major insurer, VGZ, the monthly premium, just like at CZ, also exceeds 170 euros. Due to an increase of 16.50 euros, VGZ's Ruime Keuze package costs 170.75 euros next year. The Basis Keuze package becomes 17.50 euros per month more expensive and comes to 167.40 euros. Greater demand for care That health insurance premiums are rising sharply is no surprise. The smaller insurer DSW traditionally announced its premium in October already, well ahead of the other insurers. The premium for the basic insurance there rises by 14.75 euros per month to 173.25 euros. "In the eight years that I have worked here, I have never experienced such a large increase", DSW director Aad de Groot said at the time. That care costs are now rising so steeply is partly due to higher labour costs and hospitals with higher energy bills, but also because ever more people need care. "Ageing leads to greater demand for care, and the number of cancer diagnoses will also rise in the coming years", De Groot said last month. Financial windfall gone Last year premiums could remain almost the same compared with the previous year, 2024, thanks to more money in the health insurance fund. Insurers receive money from that government fund, which in turn is filled by premiums from employees and employers. The financial windfall from the health insurance fund was one-off. De Groot: "Actually, in this increase we are seeing two years of care costs in one." CZ writes that it has used 20 million euros of its own reserves "to limit the increase for policyholders. Without that contribution the premium would be higher". The health insurer calls the premium increase "necessary" and "a considerable setback for many people". Deductible also rising Menzis chief executive Dirk Jan Sloots calls the increase "unavoidable" because care costs have for years been rising faster than the economy grows. Menzis says it will use 116 million euros of its own reserves to somewhat limit the price increase. VGZ is taking 100 million euros from its reserves. Zilveren Kruis is drawing 230 million euros from its buffer. The <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> ministry had estimated that the premiums would rise by 12.50 euros per month. The deductible rises by 15 euros next year to 400 euros.

title: Morning briefing 13/11: What now in The Hague? • Netherlands face Greece in Nations League
lead: Good morning! In The Hague, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and the deputy prime ministers are meeting to discuss how the minority cabinet should proceed. In the evening, the Netherlands national team face Greece in the Nations League. First the weather: Today showers mainly in the coastal areas, alternating with sunny periods. It will be 9 or 10 degrees with a moderate northwesterly wind, strong on the coast. The forecast for the coming days and more weather news can be found here in the NOS Weer: Are you heading out today? Here you will find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What have you missed? Health insurance premiums will rise considerably next year. This is now clear after the health insurers published the premiums for the compulsory basic insurance . These had to be presented before midnight. And there is something to choose. For example, the premium for the cheapest health insurance at Zilveren Kruis rises by 5.50 euros to 159.45 euros, while at CZ the basic insurance will soon cost 177.25 euros, an increase of more than 17 euros compared with last year. Health insurer Menzis will charge a premium of 165.75 euros for the basic package in 2027, an increase of 9.50 euros. At the other major insurer, VGZ, the monthly premium, like at CZ, also goes above 170 euros. Other news from the night: And then one more thing: What would you say to politics or <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>? NOS reporters asked people on the street in various places. And what turned out: whether you are walking around the market in Hoogvliet, or that in Veendam or Oisterwijk, everywhere disappointment about national politics predominates. Many visitors say they are losing ever more trust in The Hague. What they think of the crisis in The Hague can be seen in this video: Have a nice day!

title: Crisis talks for Jetten over the future of the coalition, waiting for clarity from the VVD
lead: At the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-algemene-zaken">ministerie van Algemene Zaken</entity> <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> is making a last-ditch attempt to save his <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>. He wants a meeting at the ministry with his two deputy prime ministers. They are VVD leader Yesilgöz and CDA Minister of Asylum Van den Brink. The cabinet is in serious trouble now that <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> voted last night, by the narrowest possible majority and against the wishes of the VVD, in favour of the tax plan. D66 premier Jetten hopes the VVD will stay in the coalition and yesterday he spoke several times of a "serious fresh start". The most important question today is what the VVD will do. Is the coalition party so angry about the conduct of its coalition partners D66 and CDA that it will leave the coalition? According to the VVD, the other two coalition parties unexpectedly and unjustly struck a deal earlier this week with the left-wing opposition parties Pro and Volt. An impossible position At the last minute a proposal from Pro and Volt was added to the tax plan, meaning people with a lot of wealth will pay somewhat more tax. The VVD is adamantly opposed to levying extra tax on wealth and says that as a result entrepreneurs will leave the Netherlands. It has put the VVD in an impossible position: the tax plan has been amended by the left, but must be carried out by VVD <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. VVD <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity> did not want to give a substantive response after the vote. He called the move by his coalition partners appalling and said he would consult with his party colleagues. VVD leader Yesilgöz was not in the Tweede Kamer and was also not available for comment. There will no doubt have been a lot of telephone consultation. Podcast Yesterday the NOS podcast De Dag covered the situation in the VVD. The podcast can be heard via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. It is still unclear how it will end. Will the VVD accept Jetten's offer to talk about a "fresh start"? Jetten wants to talk about what is not going well in the mutual relationships and how things can be done better with the Kamer. "That calls for reflection on cooperation in the cabinet, on cooperation in the coalition and on how you as a minority combination can relate to parliament in an effective way." Yesilgöz said on Wednesday evening that a "fundamental reset" is needed in the coalition. She did not really explain what she meant by that, and the question is whether that will become clear today.

title: Schiphol gives 29 passenger buses to Ukraine, 'essential for education'
lead: Ukraine has received passenger buses from Schiphol airport. They are 29 electric buses that were until now used to bring passengers from landed aircraft to the gate. The vehicles are being taken to Ukraine to take children to and from school and for city transport. Yesterday the buses were handed over to the Ukrainian embassy. Schiphol chief Pieter van Oord came up with the idea of giving the buses to Ukraine when he saw that the Hoge Veluwe National Park had donated five off-road vehicles to that country. "I thought: what a wonderful initiative. Then, when I drove a round of the airfield and saw a long row of dozens of buses that we had by now replaced, I wondered what we were going to do with them." The buses turned out to be for sale, so the Schiphol chief decided to investigate whether there was a need for them in Ukraine. Enquiries with the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> and the Ukrainian embassy showed that the buses were very welcome there, so it was decided to donate them to Ukraine along with four charging stations. The Ukrainian embassy has determined where the buses will be most useful. Ambassador Andriy Kostin is grateful for the solidarity action, and says the buses will help people in Ukraine in their daily lives. Badly needed The vehicles have been filled by the Dutch foundation Protect Ukraine with generators and PowerStations, large charging stations. Protect Ukraine, which has good contacts in Ukraine, has since the Russian invasion regularly travelled to the country in convoys to deliver goods such as trauma packs, medical equipment and pick-up trucks. Founder Jaap Scholten says the goods in the bus are badly needed and are used by both civilians and soldiers at the front for electricity. But the buses themselves are also necessary, he says. "By deploying them in Ukraine, the practical barrier is removed: the transport from home to school or office and back." Khristina Matvienko agrees. She is a teacher in Kyiv and organises camps for mothers and wives of soldiers at the front. She says many schools have been destroyed by Russian attacks, and that the schools that are open are required to have a bomb shelter. Because not all schools have one and children sometimes live far away, the buses are "essential for education". After a Russian attack, the government in Ukraine decides whether it is safe for a school to open, she explains. When that is not possible, children must move to another school, but they must be able to get there. Buses help enormously with that. Many of the children she teaches know nothing other than that there is a war, says Matvienko. "From the sound of a rocket they recognise what kind of projectile it is and whether it is necessary to go to the shelter, sometimes better than adults." According to Scholten, Schiphol's gift is a fine example of how Dutch companies can help Ukraine. Business can do more, he thinks. The foundation has since the Russian invasion already raised 30 million euros in money and goods, of which just under 7 percent came from business. That share could, in his view, be larger. "It would be interesting if companies tried to imagine what they could spare, and what could be of use in Ukraine." Companies should then think of off-road vehicles, vans, generators and machines that they have written off but that people there could make very good use of, he says. Scholten stresses that the Dutch state does a lot, just as citizens do through foundations and initiatives. "Now business, too."

title: Zeeland second-hand shop wants to give photo album to king: 'Too special to sell'
lead: At a second-hand shop in Oostburg in Zeeland, a photo album full of old photos of the royal family was recently handed in. The volunteers at the second-hand shop want to ultimately give the photo album to <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity>: "We think the book is too special to sell in the second-hand shop for a few euros," says volunteer Gerry Fieret. The photo book was recently donated to the second-hand shop by a Belgian. When Fieret opened the album, she saw old photos and postcards of the Oranges. "We received this and thought: something has to be done with this. It really should end up with the family," she tells Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>. Fieret suspects the book is more than a hundred years old. An old postcard of a young Princess Juliana in Zeeland costume is one of the oldest examples in the book. The album runs up to the birth of Willem-Alexander. Fieret finds it difficult to choose a favourite photo, but she finds the picture of Princess Juliana in Zeeland regional dress especially special. "Women in my family also wore this costume, so that is certainly special." The photo book is currently still in the hands of volunteer Gerry Fieret, but must ultimately end up with the king: Fieret hopes that the album will eventually reach the king. She goes to Prinsjesdag with her sisters every year, but according to her that is not a suitable moment to hand over the book. That is why she hopes that <entity id="person:hugo-de-jonge">Hugo de Jonge</entity>, the King's Commissioner in Zeeland, will come to collect the album in Oostburg and take it to <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>. "I would most like Mr De Jonge to come to the second-hand shop in Oostburg one day to collect this book, put it in the back of his car and take it to The Hague." Fieret is realistic and understands that Willem-Alexander may well have more photo books at home. Still, she is not giving up. "Even if there are just one or two photos in it that he has never seen himself. Then our mission is already accomplished."

title: 13/11 on Nieuwsuur: How to proceed with the crisis in the minority cabinet?
lead: Crisis not yet resolved <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> appears saved after yesterday's tax plan for 2027 was adopted by a narrow majority 'with the left', without support from governing party VVD. The coalition still has to discuss in what form the three parties will continue and whether trust is great enough. So far they have not agreed on this. Talks continue this weekend. We discuss the latest news with, among others, political reporter Arjan Noorlander , head of Ondernemend Nederland (ONL) Erik Ziengs , and Gerben Boom , chair of the Nederlands Agrarisch Jongeren Kontakt (NAJK). Guests are: the <entity id="pos:burgemeester-utrecht">burgemeester van Utrecht</entity> and <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity> chair <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity> and professor of political science (University of <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>) Tom van der Meer .

title: Former D66 councillor in Boxtel, suspected of corruption and electoral fraud, released after pre-trial detention
lead: The corruption suspect Sohib H., who stepped down as a D66 municipal councillor in Boxtel earlier this week, is released after two weeks of pre-trial detention. The chamber of the <entity id="org:rechtbank-zeeland-west-brabant">rechtbank Zeeland-West-Brabant</entity> has decided this. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had wanted to extend H.'s pre-trial detention by 90 days, but the chamber did not agree. The chamber hearing was behind closed doors and no further explanation of the decision will be given. Once the investigation has been completed, the final file will be prepared and the case will be put before a judge, a spokesperson for the OM said. Corruption and electoral fraud. The 38-year-old H. was arrested on 27 October on suspicion of official corruption, computer trespass, forgery, breach of official secrecy and electoral fraud. After his arrest D66 suspended him for three months. Alongside his council work, the suspect was an employee of the Parket Centrale Verwerking Openbaar Ministerie. There had also been a criminal investigation into H. since May on suspicion of money laundering. Following that investigation the OM suspended him from duty. H. became a councillor in Boxtel in 2018. He was elected twice with a large number of preference votes.

title: Six arrests for violence against police officer in Amsterdam
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested six Amsterdam residents on suspicion of harassing and pelting a motorcycle officer in Amsterdam at the end of September. Four of the suspects are minors. They are suspected of public violence. The incident took place on 29 September in the Nieuw-West district. A motorcycle officer wanted to stop a boy on a scooter because he was not wearing a helmet. The officer signalled the driver to stop, but he ignored this. A short chase followed. At a nearby crossroads a group of several dozen people was present at that moment. According to the police, some of them ran at the motorcycle officer and began kicking the motorbike. Objects were also thrown at the officer. The motorcycle officer was not injured. An investigation led to the six arrests last Tuesday, reports city broadcaster AT5. These are two boys aged 16, two aged 17 and two men aged 18 and 21. The police do not rule out further arrests.

title: Another building under construction collapses in Nairobi: six dead
lead: In the Kenyan capital Nairobi at least six people have died after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed. Rescue workers are still searching for survivors under the rubble. The building was still under construction. It suddenly collapsed at around 10.00 local time while construction workers were on site. They became trapped under the rubble. Preliminary investigation shows the top floor caved in, causing part of the building to give way, local media report. It is still unclear how many construction workers were on the site. At least one person is missing. Red Cross rescue workers are searching for survivors under the rubble. Three rescued people have been taken to hospital, the aid organisation writes on X. Second building Last month a tower under construction with eighteen storeys also collapsed in Nairobi. At least eight people died there. Bodies were searched for under the rubble for two weeks, Citizen TV writes. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has opened an investigation into the owner of the building and the authorities that had given permission for the construction. Buildings under construction collapse more often in the Kenyan capital. According to the news agency AP, there is insufficient oversight of compliance with building regulations.

title: Police find 3D-printed punching bags and firearms in home in Eindhoven
lead: During a raid on a home in Eindhoven, the police found several weapons made with a 3D printer. They are six punching bags and five firearms made of 3D printer plastic. The police will not say why they raided the house; a spokesperson says the raid followed an investigation. Besides the weapons, two 3D printers were also found. The police say the home appears to have been set up as a workshop for this kind of weapon. Use is dangerous: according to the police such a find is relatively rare. Earlier it was assumed that printing weapons with this kind of device would rapidly increase in the criminal circuit, but that has not happened. According to the police, this is thanks to the efforts of the authorities, including those in other European countries. A weapon printed in 3D can fire both bullets made with the printer and ordinary ammunition. Not only can the weapons be lethal to people who are shot at, they are also dangerous for shooters. The weapons may jam, melt or burst apart. Possessing production files is also prohibited: in 2022 a 3D-printed semi-automatic firearm, firearm parts and a 3D printer were found in a home search in Zeeland. Last year police and justice said they were worried about this kind of lethal weapon. They are hard to recognise and look like toys, and there is barely any oversight, according to reporting by Nieuwsuur. Since July this year the Weapons and Ammunition Act has been amended. As a result it is a criminal offence to produce, possess or sell 3D weapons, but it is also prohibited to have a digital file with which such weapons can be made by a 3D printer.

title: Groningen port company: Eemshaven not a suitable location for nuclear power plants
lead: The Eemshaven in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> is not a logical location for nuclear power plants. That is the conclusion of port manager Groningen Seaports after an external study. The report shows that the arrival would have consequences for the local energy system and the security of electricity supply across the Netherlands. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> announced last summer that three sites are under consideration for two new nuclear power plants: two sites in the Eemshaven and one in <entity id="org:gemeente-terneuzen">Terneuzen</entity> in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>. The cabinet bases this choice, among other things, on an advisory report from grid operator Tennet, which has indicated that the Groningen port area is technically the best option. On behalf of Groningen Seaports, researchers examined the consequences for, among other things, the local energy system if two nuclear power plants were built in the north of Groningen. Closure of gas plant According to the research report, a choice for the Groningen port area would be "complex". Both locations present complications according to the researchers, particularly if the cabinet chooses to have the plants built on the current site of the Eemscentrale, the gas plant of energy company Engie. At the Emmapolder, west of the port area, this is less of an issue, although the researchers also see "possibly significant impact" on the energy system for that location. The Eemscentrale accounts for an annual production of 1.8 gigawatts. To make room for a nuclear power plant, the Eemscentrale would have to be closed by 2031 at the latest, while it takes until at least 2040 before a nuclear power plant could start operating on this site. In times of growing scarcity on the power grid, that could have consequences for the whole of the Netherlands, warns Groningen Seaports. According to the port manager, the arrival of the nuclear power plants would thwart the current energy policy of the Eemshaven. That policy focuses, among other things, on the combination of offshore wind energy, the production and import of hydrogen, and energy storage. For example, problems could arise on the local grid if the nuclear power plants, once they are in place, cannot get rid of the electricity they produce, writes RTV Noord. In the report, the researchers write that in the Eemshaven two nuclear power plants could be connected to the future high-voltage grid without extra investment, according to grid operator Tennet. This assumes 6.6 gigawatts of wind energy and an increase in local demand for electricity. "If more offshore wind energy comes ashore in the Eemshaven, or if local demand for electricity grows more slowly, a shortage of space on the electricity grid can still arise," says Groningen Seaports. "Wind energy and nuclear energy could then compete for the same capacity." Hydrogen network in trouble Furthermore, the arrival of nuclear power plants would clash with other energy projects in the Eemshaven that are in preparation or already under way. For example, it would throw the construction of the planned hydrogen network into disarray. For transport to the mainland, pipelines must be laid across the site of the Eemscentrale. This does not go together with a nuclear power plant on this location, the researchers conclude. Relocating the hydrogen infrastructure could be possible, but delays and higher costs must then be taken into account. The same applies to other planned investments in the energy system in the Eemshaven. Also, an agreement has been made with central government that part of the wind energy produced at sea in the future will come ashore on the Groningen coast. At the expense of other projects According to the report, all of this is incompatible with the construction of one or two nuclear power plants in the Eemshaven. "New energy sources must strengthen the energy system and must not come at the expense of developments that are already under way," says Bart Jan Hoevers, director of Groningen Seaports. Earlier it was already clear that there is considerable resistance in Groningen to the arrival of two possible nuclear power plants. For example, the province and municipalities see nothing in the cabinet's plans.

title: KLM files report after power bank fire involving Camiel Eurlings
lead: KLM has filed a report against a passenger over an "incident with a power bank during a flight in September". The airline confirms this, after questions from NOS. It is presumably about former KLM director Camiel Eurlings, whose power bank caught fire on that flight. A spokesperson does not want to say whether the report is against Eurlings. It has also not been disclosed exactly what the report concerns. KLM does confirm that it concerns the flight to Curaçao on 17 September. On that day, a Boeing 777 turned back after flying for hours, after a power bank on board caught fire. The fire was put out by the crew. Various media soon reported that it was the power bank of the former executive. Several sources on board the aircraft confirmed this news. Former politician Eurlings when he was at the helm of KLM: After the incident, KLM carried out an investigation into the matter. This is usual "in cases of serious violations of safety rules by passengers where the safety of a flight, passengers and crew is at stake", the airline writes in a statement. "Safety always comes first." The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> confirms that the report has been accepted. It concerns a criminal investigation, which is being carried out by the aviation police.

title: Wolves kill 35 sheep in Belgium, deadliest attack since predator's return
lead: In a nature reserve in Belgium, at least 35 sheep were mauled to death in a wolf attack last month. This is the deadliest wolf attack since the wolf returned to Flanders in 2018, the newspaper Gazet van Antwerpen writes. The sheep were found on 4 October by shepherd Bert Plasmans, but the attack is only now being reported. The animals belonged to a flock of 450 sheep that were deployed to graze the Groot Schietveld nature reserve in the municipality of Brecht. The area is military land and is used by the Belgian army as a training ground. The nature reserve is located near the Dutch border close to <entity id="org:gemeente-zundert">Zundert</entity>. Seventeen other sheep were injured, some of which have since also died. Three other animals are missing. 'Not a pile of meat.' The shepherd says most of the sheep that were killed were pregnant. They were all Flemish flock sheep, a rare breed, Flemish media write. Shepherd Plasmans found the mauled sheep "confronting to see". "It is not a pile of meat to us. These are animals you work with intensively", Plasmans tells Gazet van Antwerpen. "It is also a valuable piece of genetics that you lose." According to him, one sheep was actually eaten by a wolf. Flock guardian dogs: DNA research has confirmed that it was a wolf attack. Two wolves roam the area, called Ben and Emma. On the site there is a wolf-proof fence meant to protect the flock, but according to shepherd Plasmans that is insufficient because the area is not flat. As a result the wolf can still get to the sheep. Plasmans wants extra protection by deploying flock guardian dogs. These are currently still banned in Belgium. He is taking part in a trial for flock guardian dogs for this purpose. Wolf attacks in the Netherlands: several wolf attacks have also taken place in the Netherlands since the animal returned in 2015. In July 2024, 44 animals were killed by a wolf in Ede. That was the largest wolf attack in the Netherlands so far. This is according to figures from BIJ12, the organisation that handles wolf matters on behalf of the provinces. Last February, 41 sheep were killed in a wolf attack in Doornspijk.

title: Whole weekend no trains between Roermond and Sittard due to fault and works
lead: Since this morning, no trains have been running between Roermond and Sittard because of a signalling fault. According to railway infrastructure manager ProRail, the repair work will last all day. Train services on the route will also be suspended this weekend due to planned works. ProRail reports that a broken rail was discovered and there was a fire in a relay cabinet. "This presumably led to the signal and level crossing fault", says the network manager. "The damage is so great that the repair work will last all day." Train services are expected to be able to resume from Monday morning, the regional broadcaster L1 Nieuws reports. Express buses are running between Roermond and Sittard. Passengers should allow for a longer journey time. NS advises passengers to check the journey planner just before departure.

title: Podcast De Dag: how Jetten (mis)manages the cabinet crisis
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> is trying to make a "fresh start" with his minority cabinet. What role does he play in the emergence and resolution of the cabinet crisis? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. After a long debate in a crisis atmosphere, a gripping vote on the tax plan took place last night, which was adopted by the narrowest possible margin. This was achieved with the support of left-wing parties and without the support of coalition party VVD, which feels betrayed and cornered by the left-wing cooperation. Result: chaos and possibly an unworkable situation. In the podcast, political reporter Lars Geerts explains how the prime minister is managing this crisis and has partly caused it himself. Respond? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial: Max Smedes Final editing: Rosanne Sies

title: Child killed in accident on Utrecht cycle path, mini car possibly involved
lead: A child has died this afternoon in a traffic accident on a cycle path in the Utrecht district of Leidsche Rijn. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> also reports that a 30-year-old woman from Utrecht has been arrested. Her involvement is being investigated. Bystanders say that a bicycle and an electric mini car were involved in the accident, writes RTV Utrecht. That is remarkable, because such a mini car is not allowed on the cycle path. The mini car should use the carriageway among fast traffic, at a maximum of 45 kilometres per hour. No other victims The accident happened at around 11.45 am on the Kattenkruidweg, a heavily used cycle path in Leidsche Rijn. Emergency services, including a trauma helicopter, turned out in force, but their help was of no avail. According to a police spokesperson, there are no other victims besides the deceased. How the accident could have happened is unknown and is being investigated by the police.

title: Curaçao wants to cooperate with controversial government of El Salvador in justice
lead: Curaçao wants to cooperate with El Salvador in the areas of justice and security. The ministers of Justice of both countries signed a letter of intent for this at 17.00 Dutch time. The cooperation is striking, because Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele receives a great deal of international criticism for human rights violations in his approach to crime. The countries intend to exchange more knowledge, strengthen their judicial institutions and cooperate in combating crime. In July, Amnesty International published a report in which the organisation warns of possible crimes against humanity and erosion of the rule of law. "El Salvador very problematic" Dagmar Oudshoorn, director of Amnesty International Netherlands, calls the cooperation very worrying. "El Salvador is very problematic," she says. "There is a great deal of international criticism because of mass arrests, torture, enforced disappearances and deaths in prisons. It is a combination that adds up to possible crimes against humanity." Since 2022, President Bukele has been waging a tough fight against gang crime under a state of emergency. Over 90,000 people have since been arrested and imprisoned. The number of murders in El Salvador has fallen sharply, but human rights organisations warn that many people are being held without a fair trial. In April, changes to the law were also introduced in El Salvador, meaning children from the age of 12 can be sentenced to life imprisonment for serious crimes. Worrying Oudshoorn finds it remarkable that Curaçao wants to cooperate precisely with El Salvador. "I cannot imagine wanting to learn from a country that commits this form of human rights violation." Amnesty International has been researching the treatment of people seeking protection in Curaçao since 2018. According to Oudshoorn, the Curaçaon minister of Justice refuses to talk to Amnesty about the findings. Amnesty was also denied access to immigration detention during a recent visit. "He also refuses to speak to local NGOs. And entering into cooperation with someone who makes it impossible for NGOs to do their work is especially worrying," says Oudshoorn. Role of the Netherlands The cooperation also raises questions about the role of the Netherlands. Curaçao is an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, but foreign affairs are a Kingdom matter. "The Caribbean countries have limited freedom within the kingdom to maintain international contacts independently," says emeritus professor of Colonial and Postcolonial History Gert Oostindie. "Foreign relations belong to the Kingdom, and in practice the Netherlands has the final say on them." He calls it remarkable that Curaçao is doing this. "But it does fit in with what Curaçao constantly tries to do: show that it can do things without the Netherlands." According to Oostindie, cooperation in the area of justice is of a different order from earlier international contacts in areas such as tourism with Colombia. "This is less innocent." Oostindie points out that any binding international agreements do not only concern Curaçao but also the Kingdom. "The question is whether Curaçao is not going too far by making agreements independently." Oudshoorn also wonders how the Netherlands views the cooperation. "I am in any case very curious what the Netherlands thinks of this. Because in fact foreign policy rests with the Netherlands." "Justice and judicial cooperation is an autonomous matter for Curaçao," says the spokesperson for the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. "So Foreign Affairs has therefore not been involved in this (either)." Dick Drayer correspondent Caribbean Region Curaçao views El Salvador differently from the Netherlands. Curaçao mainly looks at the results of the tough crime-fighting under President Nayib Bukele. That difference in approach is also visible on Curaçao itself. The island is struggling with serious criminal violence. Shootings, firearm possession and international criminal networks are putting security under pressure. Curaçao sees how El Salvador has pushed back violent gangs and has also successfully deployed soldiers against organised crime in Haiti. On Curaçao, the outcome of security measures often weighs heavily, even when individual rights risk being compromised. This became apparent earlier during the Venezuelan migration crisis. Human rights organisations criticised the detention and expulsion of Venezuelans, while the Curaçaon government mainly pointed to border control and security. Minister Shalten Hato stresses that cooperation with El Salvador takes place within the law and with respect for fundamental rights. For the time being it concerns knowledge exchange and training. Concrete agreements on the use of Salvadoran investigative methods do not yet exist.

title: Klaas Knot's chances are shrinking, and it will be clear next week who becomes ECB president
lead: The chances of Klaas Knot becoming the new president of the European Central Bank are shrinking. Sources in Brussels and Dublin confirm this to the NOS. Support from Germany is essential for Knot, but the Germans have not yet decided whom they want to back. Federal Chancellor Merz says at a meeting of EU leaders in Dublin that he needs a few more days to make up his mind. Two candidates are competing for the influential post: the Dutchman Klaas Knot, former president of De Nederlandsche Bank, and the Spaniard Pablo Hernández de Cos, former president of the Spanish central bank. The French are leaning towards the Spaniard, according to reports in, among others, the British business newspaper Financial Times and the French newspaper Le Monde. French President Macron and Chancellor Merz discussed in the corridors of the European summit in the Irish capital who should become the new president of the European Central Bank. According to Merz, these are "intense negotiations that have not yet been concluded". Chefsache The decision is a 'chefsache', but the leaders of both candidates are absent. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> had to stay in the Netherlands to save his <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>, and his Spanish counterpart Sánchez opened his election campaign in his own country. The Netherlands saw no point in sending a delegation that could not get anywhere near the French and German leaders, and sent no one to Dublin. The Spanish camp did decide to deploy its EU ambassador to lobby for candidate Hernández de Cos in the corridors. Every little helps, is the Spanish reasoning. The post of ECB president became vacant after the current president, Christine Lagarde, stepped down at the end of October, eight months before her term was due to end. To become president of the ECB, support is needed from 16 of the 21 euro countries, which together represent at least 65 per cent of the population. The votes of the large countries France and Germany are therefore of essential importance. More and more countries appear to be expressing a preference for the Spanish candidate, according to what is heard behind the scenes in Dublin. Of the 27 EU countries, 21 have the euro. A large share of those countries lie in the south of the Union. In those countries, the fact that the Netherlands is known as frugal, thrifty, does not work in Knot's favour. Other thrifty countries such as Sweden and Denmark do not have the euro and are not relevant to Knot's struggle for the presidency. This contest does not stand on its own, but is being linked by the French and the Germans to other posts becoming vacant within the bank, namely that of board member for market supervision and chief economist. The Germans appear to have set their sights on the latter post. The French also had their eyes on the chief economist post earlier, but now appear ready to leave that position to the Germans. That would be a boost for Hernández de Cos. It is unlikely there would be support for a French chief economist alongside a Spanish ECB president. France and Spain are countries that, from the perspective of the thrifty countries, spend money rather lavishly. Although Knot's chances appear to be shrinking, a final decision has not yet been made. The appointment of the Spaniard is not yet a foregone conclusion.

title: Microsoft apologises after hours-long outage affecting Outlook among others
lead: Microsoft has apologised for the major outage that has been ongoing since yesterday. 'We are deeply sorry that this outage has affected our customers and partners. We know they rely on our services working and we take that responsibility extremely seriously', says the tech giant. The worldwide outage is easing, the company reports. Because of the outage, millions of users could not send or receive emails, and online meetings via Teams were also sometimes not possible. AI assistant Copilot was also affected. The outage began yesterday afternoon at around 17.00. The peak of outage reports on the Allestoringen website was this morning at around 09.00. Today at around 12.30 the reports began to drop off considerably. According to the company, server problems were the cause and there was no hack. The tech giant gives no further details, but refers to an 'increased load' which meant that 'a number of servers were unexpectedly unavailable'. Courts Problems were reported in more than seventy countries. In the Netherlands, courts among others could not be reached by email. Municipalities, including <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-barneveld">Barneveld</entity>, also reported problems with email. With software updates, the problems began to ease over the course of the day. In a number of Canadian hospitals communication became more difficult. For example, at several hospitals patient appointments could only be made or cancelled by phone, CBC News reports. The British police called on people to phone rather than fill in a form online. Government services in Japan, Singapore and India, among others, also experienced problems. 'Microsoft 364' Because services from Microsoft's subscription service Microsoft 365 were affected, many users joked on social media that the service could better be called Microsoft 364, since they had been unable to reach Outlook and Teams, among others, properly for a day.

title: Four minors arrested in Drunen for posing as police officers
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested four minors who posed as police officers. The group of four planned to swindle a 77-year-old man in Drunen. The suspects are between 15 and 17 years old and come from Amsterdam, the police write. The victim was called by a fake bank employee but did not trust it. He then contacted the police. Officers went to see him a day later to take his statement. During the visit, the man was called again by the same person. This time he recognised the voice of one of the fraudsters. During the second phone call, the suspect posed as a police officer and wanted to come round to collect valuable items for 'further investigation'. Caught in the act The suspect could be arrested in the act when he arrived at the victim's home. The police have arrested three other suspects in the area of the home. The suspects are in custody and are being questioned, the police say.

title: Dutch influencer arrested by US immigration agency ICE
lead: Dutch influencer Vera Dijkmans has been arrested by the US immigration agency ICE, according to RTL Nieuws . She was arrested on Wednesday evening after landing at Newark airport in New Jersey. Dijkmans had travelled to the United States because she was reportedly invited to a sporting event by the martial arts federation UFC. 'She works a lot in America and has a B2 visa here. With that you may stay in the country for a longer time than with an ordinary tourist visa', her mother tells RTL from the United States. The Dutch <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> said in a reply to NOS that, for privacy reasons, it does not comment on individual cases. Green card Dijkmans was reportedly starting a procedure to obtain a permanent residence permit (a green card ). 'A letter was sent saying she had to come to court for her residence permit', says her mother. 'But she missed that letter because she was travelling.' Her mother tells RTL that she has not been able to reach her daughter since her arrest. She went to the detention centre to speak to her daughter, but was turned away. Dijkmans is an influencer and OnlyFans model. On Instagram alone, the 29-year-old has 5.7 million followers. ICE database Dijkmans was still not to be found in ICE's online database on Friday afternoon, local time. Questions from NOS to the immigration agency about where she is being held, and the reasons for her arrest, have so far gone unanswered. Near Newark lies Delaney Hall, an ICE detention centre notorious for its poor conditions. In recent times three people have died there, and former prisoners and activists complain of poor food and a lack of adequate care. Senator for New Jersey Andy Kim has long opposed ICE's way of working and the conditions in detention centres such as Delaney. In conversation with NOS he says he is not aware of Dijkmans' case. 'I do not know the details of this', says Democrat Kim. 'We have now seen several situations in which people who are lawfully allowed to stay in the United States also run into these kinds of problems. That is what happens when you have such a harsh system.' Whether Dijkmans was lawfully staying in the US is unclear. Kim: 'Even American citizens are being locked up or getting caught up in the chaos. And that is clearly not what the American people want.' He hopes that the Democrats, who have had a majority in both chambers of the American Congress since January, can put a stop to the excesses. 'Keep up oversight and demand accountability', he says. 'There must be an investigation into the commercial companies earning hundreds of millions of dollars from this.' 'It will not be easy', he continues. 'Trump and the Republicans have already armed ICE to the teeth with money. We are going to see what we can do about that. And we want to do our utmost to give the people held there the due process and legal assistance to which they are entitled.'

title: Two women charged over complicity in fatal shooting in Stade
lead: In Germany two women have been charged with murder or complicity in murder over a shooting at a youth facility in Stade, west of Hamburg. Six people lost their lives in the shooting in broad daylight. The partner of the shooter, who has since died, is accused of six counts of murder. According to prosecutors she was aware of her husband's plans. The woman of Turkish origin is said to have supported him both in the preparation and the execution. The driver of the getaway vehicle is also accused of complicity in six counts of murder. According to prosecutors she helped with the preparation of the attack and drove the shooter away from the scene in the car afterwards. The perpetrator, 45-year-old Fatih G, was the father of one of the children staying at the centre. The facility was meant for mothers and their children. Shooting during a meeting. According to prosecutors he suddenly opened fire with a semi-automatic pistol. Four women and two men were killed. Three victims worked at the facility. The other three were employees of the youth care region Hannover and had come to Stade specifically for a meeting. According to the Public Prosecution Service, the victims, who were talking with each other, had no idea. The daughter and her mother were in the building during the attack but were not injured. After the shooting the suspect fled as a passenger in a car. The police began a chase, fired shots and were able to arrest both the shooter and the driver of the car. Guardianship. The man was placed in pre-trial detention, but was found dead in his cell in Bremervörde prison on 21 July. The criminal investigation against him was then ended. According to earlier findings of the detectives, a dispute over guardianship of a child lay at the root of the shooting. Parental authority had been taken from the parents after their three-month-old baby suffered a brain haemorrhage. Doctors suspected this was caused by shaken baby syndrome, which was later confirmed by an expert report. A judge then decided that the mother should stay with her child in the facility in Stade. Both parents appealed against that decision. Role of the two women. Separately, the Public Prosecution Service has charged the alleged seller of the murder weapon. The 49-year-old owner of a kiosk in Berlin has been in pre-trial detention since late August. He is said to have sold the pistol and 21 rounds to the later shooter a few days before the shooting. According to regional broadcaster NDR the pistol was worth 4000 euros. The Public Prosecution Service wants to join the cases against the two women and the arms seller. The court in Stade must now decide whether the case will be heard on its merits. Suspects are presumed innocent until their guilt has been proven.

title: Cabinet stays in place for now, but crisis atmosphere remains
lead: The cabinet remains together for now, but the crisis atmosphere is not over. That is the outcome of hours of talks between <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> (D66) and deputy prime ministers Yesilgöz (VVD) and Van den Brink (CDA). The three coalition parties did not agree today on how the cabinet should continue. The form of the cabinet, its course and the relationships are still under discussion. This weekend the three parties will continue talking. Jetten hopes that will happen "in complete calm", he said after the hours-long crisis talks. According to him, improvements must come in the "substantive, political and personal" areas. That this has not yet succeeded is related to the fact that we are in "a unique political situation", Jetten said. "If you had wanted to finish that today no matter what, it could also have gone wrong." The words of Jetten: Then VVD leader Yesilgöz spoke. The deputy prime minister struck a very different tone and spoke of the "failed experiment of the minority cabinet". According to her, substantive and political corrections must come. "In the current way we cannot continue." Yesilgöz accused her two coalition partners of looking "just too often" to the left. The VVD deputy prime minister suggests that a party could be added to the coalition. But, Yesilgöz warned, it could also end with the cabinet falling after all. This is what Yesilgöz said: The coalition is in heavy weather after <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> last night voted for the tax plan against the wishes of the VVD. D66 and CDA did vote for it, after they had concluded a deal with the opposition parties Pro and Volt.

title: Grow a large tree with lots of shade quickly? A trial must show which soil is best for it
lead: "This is more or less the best day of my life", says tree expert Hans Kaljee of the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">gemeente Amsterdam</entity>. Beside him stand many elms that have been dug out of the ground, roots and all. With the scan of the root ball and measurements from eight years of research, tree scientists will set to work to find out which soil is best for trees to grow in. That information is important. "In the past we wanted small trees that fitted neatly into the street and did not grow so fast", Kaljee explains. That sentiment has changed, partly due to extreme heat in summer. "Now we actually want a broad crown, so there is plenty of shade." But it takes a long time before a tree is that big. So the expert wondered: which soil do trees grow best in? He wanted to find that out together with researchers (now retired) from <entity id="org:gemeente-wageningen">Wageningen</entity> University and other tree experts. So eight years ago 180 identical elms were planted in fifteen different soil mixtures in the Amsterdam Harbour area. The municipality of Amsterdam is very keen to see the results of that research. "In our city there is little room underground", says alderman Groen Lian Heinhuis. "So it is quite difficult for trees to grow in the city." With the new knowledge the municipality wants to plant more trees, especially where cooling is most needed. "But actually this information is interesting for the whole world," says Heinhuis. "Other cities naturally have similar challenges." As a tree expert it is often guesswork how the roots in the soil are doing, says Kaljee. He had therefore wanted to do this tree trial for a long time. "But that costs an enormous amount of money." That it has finally succeeded makes it such a great day for him. The elms in the Harbour area were, for example, planted in tree sand or stony mixtures. "We also used mixtures we have been using in the city for about 25 years. But when we took the root ball out of the ground, we suddenly saw: oops, this is not the best soil", says Kaljee. That root ball has stayed smaller, with fewer fine roots. That is a pity, since those fine little roots in a tree's root system are very important for taking up water and nutrients. Gerrit-Jan van Prooijen runs a tree advisory bureau and is involved in the research into the best substrate. That report should be finished in spring. "That is still quite complicated", he says. Over the past eight years the trunks and crowns have often been measured. The scans of the roots come this week in addition. "Now we must properly link the above-ground data to the below-ground data." The scientists had to keep a close eye on the elms during the research. In some cases roots 'escaped' from the square patch of soil that had been enclosed by screens. That was not the intention, because during the trial all elms were given a plot of equal size. "Those roots are just like Houdini, a real master at escaping", says Van Prooijen about it. "Trees and roots are great return-thinkers. They are constantly looking for the spot with as much oxygen, moisture and nutrients as possible." Still, it is not certain whether the tree did not appreciate the soil mixture in those cases. "It could also be that a bit of grass grew over the screen, so the roots had the chance to escape." Which soil mixture comes out best from the test is still unclear. What Kaljee did already see is that the fineness of the mixture is probably important for good roots. "And we are not going to use granulate with clay in it anymore", he says. The 180 elms that have been dug out of the ground will get a new spot in the city. Most will probably go to parks, says Kaljee. "But some may get a spot on the street with a mixture that, based on first impressions, seems to work well", he thinks.

title: Several animals seized at private zoo of property developer
lead: Staff of the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> (NVWA) and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> carried out a large inspection yesterday at the private zoo of Gelderland property developer Ruben Marsman. They found young animals there and seized two king birds of paradise. Marsman keeps over a hundred exotic animals on his site in Elst. Forty of these are, according to the businessman, rescue animals that people on closer inspection cannot properly care for after all. For two years now, only mammals on the pet and hobby animal list may be kept. Animals not on that list that people were already caring for by then may stay on condition that they are not bred. The NVWA is therefore carrying out checks on the origin of protected animals. Servals. On Thursday morning the NVWA inspected Marsman's zoo, Omroep Gelderland reports. During this the inspector discovered young animals that are probably bred. According to daily De Gelderlander, these would include the cat-like servals, among others. What will happen to the young animals is not yet known. The young animals have in any case not been seized. The NVWA has urged Marsman to separate the males and females. A fine is still being considered. King birds of paradise and specimens. Furthermore, Marsman could not show documents of legal origin for two king birds of paradise. That is why those birds were seized, which does not immediately mean the birds were obtained illegally, the NVWA stresses. Marsman also could not show the correct documents for eleven stuffed animals. The specimens have therefore also been taken. Dangerous bird. Last week the police were also already at the site in Elst. At that time a helmeted cassowary had escaped. This bird has claws of around 12 centimetres and is very dangerous. The businessman managed to subdue the bird, Omroep Gelderland reported.

title: Podcast De Stemming: Small beer, a flower neighbourhood and Argentine footballers
lead: On Thursday evening the much-discussed amendment from Progressief Nederland and Volt was adopted by a small margin. And not long after, the tax plan also won a minimal majority. The VVD considers it a bad amendment and feels outmanoeuvred by its coalition partners D66 and the CDA. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has not yet fallen, that is the only thing that is really certain at the moment. The VVD does not want to continue 'in its current form', but what form the minority cabinet will take is unclear. Will it be the reset the VVD wished for yesterday, or perhaps the fresh start that <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> wants? De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister. You can also find all previous episodes there. As with all other well-known podcast platforms. About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings (EenVandaag, AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) go through the week in The Hague every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Police open case into comedian David Wallliams over 'serious sexual offences'
lead: The police in the United Kingdom have started an investigation into the British comedian, actor and children's author David Walliams, following reports of "serious sexual offences". The BBC reports this. The new reports are separate from the allegations that came to light earlier this week in a joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News. That showed that Walliams, known from the comedy programme Little Britain, used his power and fame to win over girls and young women for sex. The investigators spoke to thirty sources. Walliams has denied those allegations. He also unsuccessfully tried to stop the publications through the court. More reports The police are including the journalists' reporting in the investigation, in order to "establish whether there is evidence of criminal offences". More reports have been made in recent days, the police write today in a statement. They concern sex offences "that took place some time ago and involve a man in his fifties", according to the police. The list of allegations against the 55-year-old Walliams is therefore getting longer. The first reports showed that he had, among other things, allegedly had sexual contact with minors. In this article you can read more about those allegations: He is also said to have behaved inappropriately towards women at work. For example, he is said to have sought inappropriate contact behind the scenes of the popular talent show Britain's Got Talent with female production assistants of the television show. Walliams was replaced as a judge in 2022 after demeaning and sexually charged remarks about contestants recorded between filming. For example, he described one contestant as a "cunt" and said of someone else that "she thinks you want to fuck her, but you don't". He was not only removed from the talent show; late last year his publisher also dropped him. The reason was not shared at the time. According to The Telegraph, it was related to an investigation into allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards young women. Intimidating The police call on victims to come forward "to report and talk to us, regardless of when it happened". "We understand that reporting such allegations can be intimidating, but specialist staff are ready to support you, answer questions and guide you through the process", the police said in the statement.

title: It Could Still Go Wrong, Is the Conclusion After Hours of Crisis Talks
lead: From morning until evening, Jetten, Yesilgöz and Van den Brink sat together in The Hague to try to avert the coalition crisis between D66, VVD and CDA. That has not succeeded. On the contrary: it is still stuck fast and the crisis seems to have deepened. Quite striking was the difference in tone after the eight-hour meeting at the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-algemene-zaken">ministerie van Algemene Zaken</entity>. First, the prime minister and D66 leader Jetten came out to face the press. Things have not gone well and we are going to do better, was his message. "Our work is far from finished." Emotions and feelings "We all have feelings and emotions about how things have gone recently", the prime minister said conciliatorily about the VVD. And the three parties must continue talking "in complete calm". That talks will continue was roughly the only point on which VVD deputy prime minister Yesilgöz agreed with Jetten. Shortly after the prime minister, she came out and went on the attack. This minority cabinet experiment has failed, we cannot go on like this, she said. She had no kind words for her coalition partners CDA and D66, who, she said, look too often to the left. Harsh words from the VVD leader, reckless and escalating, can be heard behind the scenes from the other two parties. Does the VVD actually want to find a way out, D66 and CDA wonder. What is clear, in any case, is that there are two camps in the coalition facing each other directly. Watch the three statements after the long meeting here: Well, an improvement "is theoretically possible", said Yesilgöz. But that would require an "substantive correction" and a "political correction". With the latter she meant, for example, participation in the coalition or tolerance support from an additional right-wing party. During the formation, the VVD tried to bring JA21 into the coalition, but D66 and CDA were not keen on that then. For those parties, that is not on the table now either. Disillusionment D66 and CDA have recently looked more to the left than to the right, because things could be done more easily with the left. Yesterday this resulted in a majority for the tax plan with the left, without the VVD. And the VVD found that "disillusioning". Or in the words of the other deputy prime minister, CDA member Van den Brink, who came out third: "There has naturally been an enormous amount going on." After Yesilgöz and Jetten he had his say, but he did not want to comment on the other two. "I am not going to respond to loose statements." To the king Van den Brink stressed above all that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> bears a heavy responsibility in the national interest. "That is why we are going to continue the intensive talks." That will happen this weekend at the De Zwaluwenberg estate, where the parties will meet. And afterwards it may become clear whether the coalition can still keep the ball rolling a little further. But the outcome could also be, Yesilgöz emphasised, "that the three of us decide to go to the king". For the avoidance of doubt: when a cabinet falls, it offers its resignation to the king.

title: WSJ: America loses measles-free status
lead: America has lost its status as a measles-free country. The Wall Street Journal writes this, based on anonymous sources. According to the paper, the international health organisation Pan American Health Organization has withdrawn America's measles-free status. The US received that status in 2000 after the country eliminated the contagious infectious disease through a strong vaccination campaign and by making vaccinations free for many children. Over the past two years infections have increased enormously. This year alone the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has registered more than 5400 cases of measles. In 2025 there were 2289 in total and in 2024 only 285. The governor of New York attributes the rising infections to the policy of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>-Trump. According to her, the government has undermined trust in vaccinations. The vaccination rate has fallen in the past year and is now below the required 95 percent needed to keep the disease under control. In Wisconsin a baby died of measles earlier this month. That was the first fatal case in the state in 36 years. Shortly before that a child also died of the disease in the state of New York. Hundreds of people were infected in both states. To regain the status, the US must stop the spread of measles for at least twelve months. What are measles? Measles is one of the most contagious infectious diseases in the world. A measles infection usually runs mild, but serious complications can occur and the patient can die from it. The virus sits in the throat of someone who is infected. When someone with measles coughs or sneezes, tiny droplets of the virus enter the air. The infection most often affects babies under twelve months old. In the Netherlands children receive the MMR vaccination at 14 months and 3 years. The vaccination protects against measles, mumps and rubella. Since the introduction of the measles vaccination in 1976, a few dozen cases of measles have been reported each year in the Netherlands. According to the reports, eleven deaths due to measles have been known since 1981 in total.

title: D66, VVD and CDA continue crisis talks in Hilversum, outcome uncertain
lead: The crisis talks between D66, VVD and CDA about the future of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten continue today at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum. Here Jetten and D66 <entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity>, VVD leader Yesilgöz, VVD <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity>, deputy prime minister Van den Brink and CDA <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">leider Bontenbal</entity> come together. Jetten announced last night that he will hold "fundamental talks" this weekend to achieve improvements on a "substantive, political and personal" level. These talks are necessary after talks of more than eight hours on Friday evening at the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-algemene-zaken">ministerie van Algemene Zaken</entity> revealed that the coalition crisis has not yet been resolved. Yesilgöz immediately went on the attack after Jetten's conciliatory words. She called the minority cabinet a "failed experiment" and put a few demands on the table, with the underlying message that the two coalition parties D66 and CDA must no longer do business with the left, and that another right-wing party may still need to join the cabinet. See how Jetten and VVD leader Yesilgöz struck a different tone: That no way out has been found for the coalition crisis at the ministry of General Affairs is clear, and the outcome of the talks this weekend cannot be predicted. At D66 and the CDA they are shocked by Yesilgöz's hard approach. These parties find it difficult to judge whether the VVD really wants to reach a solution. That must become clear today and tomorrow at De Zwaluwenberg. Two camps now face each other, and this must be resolved for the cabinet to function well. The main players will not stay overnight at the estate, as happened before. And the chance is small that they will speak to the press during their "fundamental talks", which the press is also not allowed to enter the estate for.

title: Italian minister: schools not immediately closed after bomb threat
lead: Schools in Italy no longer have to be automatically evacuated after a bomb threat sent by email.
