That is stated in a guideline from Interior Minister <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Piantedosi, sent to regional administrators and police chiefs. That is reported by the Italian news agency ANSA. The occasion is the bomb threats that were sent to thousands of Italian schools on two consecutive days last week. More than 300 schools were evacuated. Prime Minister Meloni said earlier that the false reports appear intended to cause fear. The guideline sets out how the authorities must act in the event of new bomb threats. An evacuation is no longer automatic, but must be weighed on the basis of additional indications of danger. This includes, among other things, whether suspicious objects have been found and whether camera footage shows unusual situations. Furthermore, previous incidents or reports may point to a concrete threat. Identical threats: The way the threat is expressed also plays a role. Identical threats sent en masse from the same source to different recipients must, according to the guideline, be regarded as not credible. The police chief examines the threat as part of his approach and takes any necessary security measures. If evacuation is necessary, he proposes it to the prefect, who decides on it. Schools must immediately report any threats to the police.

title: Nvidia executive affair exposes risks of ties between tech world and American politics
lead: Now that Nvidia chip company's top executive Jensen Huang has stepped down, American politics is openly asking whether the close ties between the government and the top executive have created blind spots. Under President Trump, the way was cleared for unrestrained growth of artificial intelligence, but any risks seem to have been brushed aside. Last week it came to light that Huang had an affair with someone suspected of spying for China. In October last year, according to the New York Times, Trump was already informed of the affair and its possible dangers by American security services. Trump decided not to take any further action. What is more, two months later he allowed the sale of more powerful chips to China. Warnings about this from Secretary of State Marco Rubio were also brushed aside. Chip technology For almost ten years America has been trying to make things difficult for China when it comes to getting its hands on advanced chip technology, but under Trump that is no longer the case. Trump sees no problem, because according to him Nvidia's chips are 'too advanced to copy', he said this week. Another counterargument, according to Trump and Huang, is that it is important for the American economy if Chinese companies remain dependent on these American chips. And so Huang was also allowed to join two state dinners with Chinese President Xi in Beijing and in Washington. The success of Nvidia and the White House are becoming increasingly intertwined. In exchange for allowing chip exports to China, the government in some cases even receives up to 25 percent of the revenue from this sale. AI development is an important pillar for Trump's government and for economic growth. Probably from the end of next year, 4 percent of the entire American economy will be thanks to AI, according to a report by investment bank Goldman Sachs. Close ties There is little sign of reflection in the government so far. There are voices calling for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to be held responsible. Lutnick was, according to news website Axios, a constant obstacle whenever export restrictions were discussed within the government. He has had close ties with Jensen Huang for years. Moreover, according to the Wall Street Journal, Lutnick is an important link for tech companies to get close to the president. The question is whether Trump dares to sacrifice his good friend Lutnick in order to stay out of the wind himself. Trump himself, so far, mainly regrets that he has lost an important partner in Huang and called him a 'legend'. Other tech bros appear to feel the same. They will mainly fear that Huang's departure will have consequences for the rest of the AI world and are trying to limit the damage. Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk even offered Huang a job. China wants answers The Congress, on the other hand, is sharpening its knives. They want Huang to testify before <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> to give answers about the alleged spy. Lutnick has also been invited to testify. This will not stop there. Because with a Democratic Congress on the way after the elections, there is a good chance that more investigation will follow into the ties between business and the White House. It also still has to become clear whether important information actually ended up with China through Huang's extramarital relationship. Beijing still firmly denies this and says Asian women are being demonised by this accusation. Within the US it has also not yet been definitively established whether Huang indeed had an affair with a spy. China will in any case want answers if Trump travels to Shenzhen next week for an economic summit that Xi will also attend. At their last meeting, both leaders agreed to communicate better about AI and the rules surrounding it. The fear is that this affair has created a new distrust.

title: Wake-up call 14/11: cabinet crisis talks continue • Sinterklaas arrives in Grave
lead: Good morning! <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and his deputy prime ministers continue talks at the De Zwaluwenberg estate, after turbulent days in The Hague. And in Grave in Brabant, a high-profile visit is expected, as Sinterklaas comes ashore again there. First the weather: today it is fairly sunny and dry. There is a light or moderate south wind and it will be 8 to 10 degrees. Tomorrow morning it will start raining from the south. Later in the evening there will be more rain and it will become stormy. The new week starts unsettled with frequent rain. It will then be 8 to 11 degrees. It is fairly sunny, but in the north some clouds also drift across. It stays dry and with a light to moderate south wind it will be 8 to 10 degrees. In the evening the weather cools quickly and in the night towards Sunday it reaches light frost inland. For the coming days and more weather news, see the NOS Weather here: Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? In America, air traffic across the whole country was halted for hours overnight due to 'extraordinary circumstances'. A fault in the communications equipment of the American air traffic control is said to have caused the situation. According to Transport Minister Sean Duffy, equipment was overloaded by too much data. As a result, communication dropped out. The American Homeland Security Minister says a cyberattack is not ruled out, but there is currently no evidence for it. According to Minister Duffy, tens of thousands of people are stranded and many of them will have to spend the night at the airport. European flights to the US were also suspended at the request of the FAA. Air traffic has since resumed. Other news from overnight: And then just this: Last night went very easily for the Dutch national team. Oranje was too strong for Greece with a 7-0 win, so you can indeed speak of a monster victory. Xavi's side have taken a big step towards the quarter-finals of the Nations League. Oranje started superbly: after just over five minutes Crysencio Summerville scored the 1-0. Tijjani Reijnders scored three goals and then Timber and Malen also scored three goals between them. Frenkie de Jong started as captain of Oranje for the first time in an international. Virgil van Dijk was not fit enough to play. Brian Brobbey also had to withdraw from the squad. That De Jong was the playmaker became clear quickly... Have a good day!

title: Bird flu again in Hierden, 19,000 ducks and chickens killed
lead: In the village of Hierden in Gelderland, bird flu has been confirmed at a company for the third time this week. This time at a duck and laying poultry farm. The approximately 6,000 ducks and 13,000 laying hens will be culled by the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> to prevent the virus from spreading further. The company was also already a victim of bird flu in 2022. Within a zone of 10 kilometres around the company there are 14 other poultry farms. In the zone a transport ban applies with immediate effect. Birds, eggs, manure and litter may not be transported in that area. Housing requirement Earlier this week, 165,000 animals were culled at two other duck farms in Hierden due to an infection with bird flu. The NVWA is investigating how bird flu spread between the three companies in Hierden and is trying to establish how the companies became infected. According to a spokesperson, it is questionable whether that will succeed. The cause usually cannot be traced. Companies within 3 kilometres of the affected companies will be monitored more closely for signs of bird flu. Since late October a nationwide housing and protection requirement has applied to prevent further spread of bird flu.

title: 78-year-old suspect of genocide in Rwanda arrested in Belgium
lead: A man suspected of genocide and crimes against humanity in Rwanda has been arrested near the Belgian city of Leuven. In the 1990s, an estimated at least 800,000 people were massacred in the African country. The Public Prosecution Service suspects that this man had a share in this. The suspect is the 78-year-old Jean Baptiste R., a man from Rwanda with Belgian nationality. According to Belgian media he stayed with the Catholic congregation Broeders van Liefde in Bierbeek, near the city of Leuven. Rwanda itself raised the alarm with the Belgian authorities, after which an investigation into the man was launched. During the genocide in Rwanda in 1994, radical members of the Hutu population hunted, among others, Tutsis (another population group) and moderate Hutus. At least 800,000 people were slaughtered in three months, possibly even more than a million. Belgian blue helmets were also killed. This is what you need to know about the genocide in Rwanda: The Belgian Public Prosecution Service says that R. was director of a care home for people with physical disabilities in the place Gatagara during the genocide. Militias entered Gatagara on 24 April 1994. R. is said to have identified all Tutsi men who were hiding in the centre, after which they were taken away and murdered. In early May the extremists are said to have returned, after which R. again reported Tutsis. That day mainly involved women and children, according to the justice authorities. ID cards with ethnicity There is also evidence, according to the Public Prosecution Service, that R. had contact with the Hutu militias earlier in April. He is said to have organised and attended meetings to prepare the genocide. R. is said to have obliged staff and patients from his home to carry an identity card showing their ethnic origin. As a result they were easier for the extremists to recognise. Belgian prosecutors discovered evidence of this after they visited Rwanda in June of this year to hear witnesses and visit the care centre in Gatagara. According to the VRT, this is the first time someone in Flanders has been brought before the court over the genocide in Rwanda. In Brussels this has already happened six times before. A court case also took place in the Netherlands this year. The 66-year-old Eugène N. was sentenced to life imprisonment for his share in the atrocities.

title: Historic polder windmill near Stiens in Friesland destroyed by fire
lead: The Slagdijkster Molen near the Frisian village of Stiens, north of Leeuwarden, was destroyed by a major fire overnight. The polder windmill dated from 1864 and had been fully restored in 2006. "The mill was largely made of reed and can be considered lost", said Baukje Boekema of the fire service to Omrop Fryslân. Nobody was injured. The cause of the fire is unknown. The fire service received the first report of the mill fire just after 00:30 last night and turned out with heavy equipment. Quickly collapsed Even the fire service's cherry picker from Leeuwarden and a large-water transport from Harlingen were called in to fight the fire, but were ultimately not deployed. They could do nothing, because the mill collapsed soon after the first fire engines arrived. Because the fire was so fierce and sparks were flying around, the fire service kept a number of homes in the area wet during the blaze. The Slagdijkster Molen was special because already at its construction in the 19th century it was fitted with an underground, brick-built tunnel. This allowed the mill to pump water both into and out of the polder. Diesel engine In 1931 a large diesel engine was installed in the mill for pumping, which ended the wind-powered pumping of the polder. In effect the mill lost its function, and a few years later the cap and sails were removed. In 1975 it even looked as though the Slagdijkster Molen would be demolished. But it was placed on the list of monuments and, during the 2006 restoration, was fitted again with its cap and sails. Hell of the north The Slagdijkster Molen is a familiar sight to participants and TV viewers of the Elfstedentocht. The mill stands along the Finkumer Vaart, which forms part of the northernmost stretch of the Elfstedentocht, also known as the 'Hell of the North'.

title: Crisis talks between D66, VVD and CDA in Hilversum continue this morning
lead: The crisis talks on the future of the minority cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA were broken off last night after dinner and will continue this morning. D66 <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, VVD leader and deputy prime minister Yesilgöz, deputy prime minister Van den Brink (CDA), CDA <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">partijleider Bontenbal</entity> and the parliamentary group leaders Paternotte of D66 and Brekelmans of VVD spoke with each other yesterday at the De Zwaluwenberg country estate in Hilversum. Just before 8 p.m. those involved left the estate in blacked-out cars. Nothing is known about what was discussed or whether the three parties have moved closer together. The parties have agreed on radio silence and are not speaking to the press in the meantime. The crisis talks are necessary because the VVD indicated it wanted different coalition arrangements, after D66 and CDA had concluded a deal with Pro and Volt on the tax plan. Mutual trust has been damaged in recent days. Yesilgöz called the minority cabinet a failed experiment. The VVD may want a fourth coalition party. JA21 is mentioned in this regard, but that party has not yet responded to these reports. Over left or over right It is not expected that the other two parties will see this as a solution. It is not for nothing that the three parties ended up with a minority cabinet during the cabinet formation, less than a year ago. The parties could not agree on a choice for majorities in the <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> 'over links' or 'over rechts'. Last night Jetten announced that this weekend will be "fundamental conversations" to achieve improvements in "substantive, political and personal" terms.

title: Large cloud of vapour after explosion of nitrogen tank in Oss
lead: When a nitrogen tank exploded on an industrial estate in Oss in Brabant, a large cloud of vapour formed late last night. A man was injured by flying debris from the tank. The explosion of the tank was around 23.30 at the company Unipol, reports Omroep Brabant . At Unipol, raw materials are made for insulation and packaging. For a still unknown cause, the tank containing nitrogen burst apart. Large fragments flew over the rail track at the company and landed tens of metres away on the street. A sprinkler installation was also hit and drained. Nitrogen vapour: a large amount of nitrogen vapour was released in the explosion. Nitrogen does not fall under hazardous substances. In concentrated form it can lead to breathing problems, but according to a spokeswoman for the safety region the substance is 'normally' quickly diluted once oxygen is added. "We stayed on with the fire brigade for a while longer, because it was misty and the nitrogen therefore did not dilute as quickly as normal. To be on the safe side we also removed a number of parked cars in the area," said the spokeswoman. "But the danger had quickly passed." Cause unknown: the safety region cannot say anything about the seriousness of the man's injuries. The cause of the explosion in Oss is unknown.

title: 14/11 on Nieuwsuur: Is there a future for the Jetten cabinet? • Claus's wartime past is slightly different • Criticism of working from home
lead: Is there still a future for the Jetten cabinet? Coalition partners D66, VVD and CDA are holding crisis talks again today, as they did yesterday. This time not in The Hague but at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum. The subject of discussion is the future of the minority cabinet after the chaotic negotiations over the tax plan. The question is whether the cabinet will survive, and if so, in what form. We discuss all the events of this week with Thom de Graaf . The D66 member was for a long time vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> and is now a minister of state, an honorary title that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> awards in exceptional cases. We ask him how he views the future of this cabinet and what his vision is of Dutch democracy in 2026. Prince Claus did not desert the army of Nazi Germany Claus von Amsberg, husband of the former queen, Princess Beatrix, and father of <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity>, had a somewhat different wartime past than previously known. He did not desert the German army, as he later claimed, and his father was a member of the Nazi party, the NSDAP. This emerges from a new biography of the prince, who died in 2002. We speak with the authors Jutta Chorus and Bas Blokker. Criticism of working from home The 22 largest employers in the Netherlands and their staff are largely positive about working from home. At the same time, other voices are also heard: coaching and knowledge transfer become more difficult outside the office. Several large companies are therefore increasingly calling their employees back to the physical workplace. This evening is the second episode in our series on working from home. You can watch the first one here.

title: Cabinet wobbles as Hilversum votes: 'Perhaps the midterms for The Hague'
lead: While D66, VVD and CDA talk about the future of their minority cabinet at the De Zwaluwenberg estate, political parties are campaigning hard a few kilometres away. On Wednesday, the residents of Hilversum and <entity id="org:gemeente-wijdemeren">Wijdemeren</entity> elect a new municipal council. Does the political crisis play a role in their choice? Anyone walking through Hilversum today can hardly avoid it: the approaching municipal elections. Billboards stand in many places, and volunteers from political parties hand out leaflets. Right next to the regular Saturday market, an election market has been set up, where political parties from left to right are trying to persuade passers-by on this sunny morning to vote for them. Despite all the efforts, several campaigners at the market note that the election is mainly alive within the parties and among their supporters. They expect a low turnout, as is often the case with reorganisation elections. Why do Hilversum and Wijdemeren vote on Wednesday? Hilversum and Wijdemeren were the only two municipalities that did not take part in the municipal elections in March. That is because Hilversum and the six villages of Wijdemeren will together form the municipality of Hilversum from 1 January 2027. On Wednesday, the residents elect the municipal council of their new municipality. At the previous municipal elections in 2022, turnout in Hilversum was 51 per cent. In Wijdemeren it was almost 59 per cent. Almost 95,000 people live in Hilversum. In Wijdemeren, which consists of the villages Ankeveen, Breukeleveen, 's-Graveland, Kortenhoef, Loosdrecht and Nederhorst den Berg, slightly fewer than 25,000 people live. Alongside the volunteers and candidate councillors, the presence of national party figures stands out. For example, Pro Party MPs Mohammed Mohandis and <entity id="person:tom-van-der-lee">Tom van der Lee</entity> are at the election market, and BBB MPs Henk Vermeer and Caroline van der Plas walk around the market with the local campaign team. Vermeer, while handing out cheese cubes, describes the Hilversum reorganisation elections with a wink as "perhaps a bit of the midterms for The Hague". FVD leader Lidewij de Vos also appears in all kinds of places, though on screen: she features on billboards and on a large campaign bus that drives through Hilversum and Wijdemeren today. FVD MPs do not expect the local FVD list leader Willem Joustra at the market today. Concerns about trust There is no shortage of national attention, with four days to go until the election. Ronald (66) from Hilversum sees it that way too. He fears that the cabinet crisis will mainly discourage people from voting. He himself will vote for a local party, "as always". "We have, of course, just been through a political debacle. I think that trust has fallen as a result, and that affects the voting behaviour of many people." Taoufik (44) looks mainly at his own surroundings. "I work in education and see that children here need more space to play. I hear a lot about problems in the neighbourhood, about aggression and a lack of respect for older people." He mainly hopes that people will vote. National politics plays no role in his choice on Wednesday. 'Constructive and nuanced' How different it is for Nicole (50), who lets the national political situation weigh heavily when deciding who gets her vote. "I am choosing a party that takes a constructive approach, looks at society in a nuanced way and considers the climate and living together important. That weighs more heavily for me than local issues." Babette (33) says that parking and the level of municipal taxes are the key election issues for her. She does not yet know who she will vote for. "But mainly I am looking for a party that will do something about that." She says the national political crisis does not affect her vote. "I don't think the VVD is making any particularly strange choices now. The parties are, of course, continuing to talk this weekend, and that seems nothing but good to me." 'We are not exaggerating differences here' Campaigners from various Hilversum parties say that the political crisis in The Hague is being felt. There is more attention for the elections, they say, although that is "for the wrong reasons". CDA list leader Gerben van Voorden sees from the election market "mainly parties that are aware that after the elections they will have to get back to work together to shape the merger process". "It is a very complicated process," he says. "In The Hague, differences are exaggerated, but we don't do that here. We are aware of the great task we have, and The Hague can take an example from that."

title: Concern after death of cyclist (15) on Utrecht cycle path, 'my heart beats in my throat every time'
lead: In the child-rich Utrecht residential district of Leidsche Rijn, concern and fear are being voiced about yesterday's accident, in which a 15-year-old boy on a bicycle died. A neighbour (30) who was riding an electric mobility scooter on the cycle path was arrested by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> after the accident. "My own 11-year-old daughter cycles along this cycle path to school every day," says a resident to RTV Utrecht. "My heart beats in my throat every time. Here they ride at 40 or 50 kilometres an hour as standard. They ride flat out, especially the fatbikes." The accident happened yesterday afternoon on the long cycle path at Kattenkruidweg. What exactly happened is still unclear. The police did announce that the 30-year-old woman was riding an electric mobility scooter, a Birò, on the cycle path wrongly. Mobility scooters are not allowed on cycle paths. Flowers and candles: At the lamppost where the accident happened, a few bunches of flowers lie and some candles burn. A similar accident could have happened much earlier, thinks the father of the 11-year-old girl. "I have even seen crossbikes riding here. As far as I know you are allowed 25 kilometres an hour here. There should be much more enforcement. It is really life-threatening." Just like <entity id="org:gemeente-zandvoort">Zandvoort</entity>: His immediate neighbour, who like almost all the neighbours wants to remain anonymous, has also been worried for some time. "It's like the Zandvoort circuit here," he says. "Everything rides here. Motorbikes, speed pedelecs, souped-up fatbikes." He shows a photo from his doorbell camera, showing a white delivery van on the pavement. "That's from yesterday morning." A neighbour who steps into her house with her young children is shocked. "Often my visitors say: nice cycle path in front of the door, no cars. But then I say: I don't know if it's necessarily better," she says. "It's at least just as busy." Utrecht traffic alderman Matthijs Sienot (D66) says he is affected by the death of the 15-year-old boy. "Our thoughts are with his family, friends and classmates, who now have to bear an unimaginable loss. First of all this is a moment of sympathy with the bereaved and of room for the police investigation." Traffic safety: Sienot wants to await the results of the police investigation before responding further. "The safety of cyclists and other road users remains a constant concern for us," he says on behalf of the municipality.

title: Nothing is left of the historic windmill near Stiens: 'This was set on fire'
lead: Where a windmill stood yesterday, there is a ruin today. Charred wooden beams everywhere, and the familiar silhouette on the horizon in this part of North Friesland is gone. The characteristic Slagdijkstermolen from 1864, between the villages of Stiens and Feinsum, went up in flames last night. Miller Johan Nooi heard the sad news early this morning from a reporter and immediately jumped into his car. "You come here and the whole thing is simply flattened. Walls gone, sails all bent and broken. End of story, we can't do anything anymore." Disbelief Disbelief now prevails. How could this have happened? The question has been haunting the miller all day, as he took over the mill as a volunteer fourteen years ago. It wasn't lightning, and a short circuit certainly wasn't, he says resolutely. The mill had no gas or electricity connection. He also rules out friction as the cause of the fire. The mill sails were securely fastened as always. Yet fire could start and spread at lightning speed. By the time the fire brigade arrived, there was no saving it. "Someone must have done this," Nooi says repeatedly. "Who would even think of that? I hope they catch whoever did it." House defended Residents of a house further along saw the flames coming out of the mill around 00:30. They raised the alarm and warned the people who live in the former miller's cottage, right next to the Slagdijkstermolen. "They had to defend their house last night," says Nooi, "the flames were heading their way". Damage to the neighbours was limited to a scorched hedge and soot particles in the garden, partly thanks to the fire brigade, which kept their house and other buildings wet. The Slagdijkstermolen was built in 1864 and for years played an important role in draining the roughly 500 hectare Slagdijksterpolder. For participants and television viewers of the Elfstedentocht, the building beside the Finkumervaart was a familiar sight on the northern part of the route. The mill could pump water in and out with a single screw, Nooi explains. "That may not mean much to people, but it is unique. In wet periods it pumps water away, and in dry periods it pumps it back again." Talks with insurer Some of Nooi's private belongings were also lost in the fire. A rubber boat and an outboard motor, "both completely gone". The miller would like to see a new mill rise on the same spot. Identical to the mill that was lost, with a wooden frame and a thatched cap. The insurer comes by on Monday, and the board of owner De Fryske Mole will soon have a meeting with the <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-het-cultureel-erfgoed">Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed</entity> about the future of the mill.

title: Suriname's Justice Minister resigns
lead: Suriname's Minister of Justice has resigned. This comes as no surprise, as on Thursday President Simons already announced that Harish Monorath would step down, because his position had become untenable. Monorath came under fire for his conduct as chairman of the supervisory board of the official regulator Telecommunicatie Autoriteit Suriname (TAS). In 2021 he is said to have signed a contract that provided the director of the TAS with unusually favourable allowances and working conditions. In return, the TAS is said to have paid Monorath, officially for work on behalf of Ronnie Brunswijk, the chairman of Monorath's party. TAS director Wendy Jap-A-Joe had to leave earlier. Officially because her contract had expired, but she wanted to continue and took the matter to court. The appeal court also granted permission for her dismissal.

title: Thousands of secretly taken photos of breasts and bottoms in Achterhoek app group
lead: In a closed WhatsApp group, thousands of photos are being shared of women whose legs, bottoms or breasts were secretly photographed. More than a thousand men are in the app group called 't Haviksoog, reports the fortnightly investigative programme Pointer of KRO-NCRV. The programme found that the photographers and the unsuspecting women come mainly from the Achterhoek and other parts of the east of the Netherlands, and that the men also took and shared photos on holiday or elsewhere in the Netherlands. The group chat contains some 13,000 photos and videos. Reacting with emojis The images were made by the members, and the group description states that people should react with an emoji to the women's appearance. In dialect it can be read that the app group is "for real men who love women" and that no photos of "fat women or women photographed from a long distance" are allowed in the group, writes Omroep Gelderland. According to Pointer, people react with hearts, peaches and thumbs up, but also with emojis of a pig or a whale to the creepshots. According to the investigative programme, the WhatsApp group was created on 19 July 2019 by a man from Mariënvelde. That weekend the Zwarte Cross festival was held in the Achterhoek, and many of the secretly taken photos come from that region. Pointer analysed almost three thousand images from the group over half a year. The images are mostly taken from close up or from behind. As a result, many women are unrecognisable. From moving tractors Nevertheless, Pointer managed to establish the location of more than four hundred shared creepshots. Many of these were taken at events or festivals in the Achterhoek, but also in supermarkets, at places where people swim, or while going out. From moving tractors and other tall agricultural vehicles, photos were taken on country lanes of women cycling or running. The investigative programme reports that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> wants to submit the case to the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>. For this, women must file a report with the police. Everyday images taken in a sexual context can be punishable, says a sex crimes detective to Pointer.

title: Dead and seriously injured in collision with train at Strijp-S station in Eindhoven
lead: A man has died after a collision with a train at Strijp-S railway station in Eindhoven. He is a 49-year-old man from the Limburg <entity id="org:gemeente-leudal">gemeente Leudal</entity>, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. Another man, who was also hit by the train, a 37-year-old Belgian, was seriously injured. The accident happened at around 00:30. The police cannot yet say anything about how the accident happened, but they do not assume suicide. It appears to be a fatal accident. It is not clear how the men ended up on the track. Statements have been taken from witnesses. The witnesses were not acquainted with the victims, Omroep Brabant reports. It is not clear how many people saw the accident happen. Train traffic between Eindhoven and Den Bosch was halted for some time after the accident.

title: Administrators warn: prevent collapse of cabinet and new elections
lead: A group of prominent administrators and constitutional law experts is making an urgent appeal to D66, VVD and CDA: do not let the cabinet fall. And if it does happen anyway, at least make sure there are no new elections. The appeal comes at a time when the coalition is wobbling. The feuding party leaders are also holding crisis talks today at a Hilversum estate. The mood has sunk to rock bottom after D66 and CDA struck a tax deal with opposition parties Pro and Volt. The VVD calls the minority cabinet experiment a failure. Four administrators and constitutional law experts tell Nieuwsuur that nobody in the Netherlands benefits from a cabinet collapse. They argue that both coalition and opposition parties must seek a solution "in the national interest". They also criticise the "culture of party politics" that leads to "years of stagnation". "It is utterly irresponsible if this cabinet becomes caretaker", says <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity>, <entity id="pos:burgemeester-utrecht">burgemeester van Utrecht</entity> and chair of the <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten</entity>. "Also in an international context." D66 prominent Thom de Graaf agrees. "We are in such need of stability." The former vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> advocates appointing a process facilitator who can hold things together. Someone who, unlike <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, has no party political agenda. Should D66, VVD and CDA ultimately not continue together, then in De Graaf's view elections must be prevented. "What does that achieve? A long caretaker period, a long formation period and ultimately you end up with another minority cabinet." He would rather see premier Jetten consult with <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> about alternatives, such as a new coalition based on the current seat distribution. ChristianUnion <entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">fractievoorzitter Bikker</entity> presented a plan this week for such a restart attempt, and it could count on a majority in parliament. When D66 leader Jetten was forming his cabinet at the start of this year, UvA political scientist Tom van der Meer came along to advise on the draft minority coalition. A little over a year later, the professor concludes that it has become a "tragedy". The main reason? "They did not want to work with a fixed gedoogpartner on the left or right. Yet we know from research that a minority coalition benefits greatly from a fixed gedoogpartner. Then you can be more effective and stable." Van der Meer also says that a minority cabinet works mainly when politicians grant each other something. But the opposite happened: "The VVD celebrated on billboards a coalition agreement for which there was no majority, 'the left' made a big point of the 'millionaires' tax' and 'the right' tied themes to a tax plan that had little to do with tax." Should new elections come anyway, Pro is poised to become the largest party. JA21 also scores high in the most recent Peilingwijzer. Coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA are instead losing ground. But Thom de Graaf thinks those electoral shifts will not lead to an easily formed majority cabinet. "Broadly speaking the same balances return. It is very difficult to form a centre cabinet. And bringing together two flank parties is also difficult." Electoral threshold. Emeritus professor of constitutional law Paul Bovend'Eert shares that analysis. He believes the current electoral system no longer works well because of party fragmentation. Seventeen parties currently sit in the House of Representatives. In the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> there are even twenty. That makes cooperation and finding majorities very difficult. He therefore advocates an electoral threshold such as is common in some other European countries. In Germany, for example, parties must win at least 5 per cent of voters to enter parliament. "You take the voter a little by the hand by giving somewhat more limited choices." Bovend'Eert's proposal would mean that the current parliament has six parties: D66, VVD, Pro, PVV, CDA and JA21. Parties such as FVD, Groep Markuszower and BBB would then fall outside. "Then you can form majority coalitions much better. I think small parties can very well merge with larger parties, so that those political views are not lost. Moreover, you get far fewer splinter groups." The plan for an electoral threshold was still embraced by the coalition parties earlier this year. But before they could submit a proposal, it was already rejected by the opposition. Political scientist Van der Meer also finds the fragmented political landscape problematic, but he is sceptical about an electoral threshold. His solution to the political impasse? "Ultimately it lies in behaviour and culture. We must get out of the rut of coalition versus opposition and move more towards togetherness, willingness to give each other more room." De Graaf agrees. "In a minority cabinet you will all have to look at the greater interest: stability in governing the country without victories for individual parties."

title: Crisis talks between D66, VVD and CDA continue this morning in Hilversum
lead: The leaders of the three coalition parties will continue talks this morning at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum about the crisis of confidence within <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. The six key players are meeting again for crisis talks. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> first spoke alone yesterday with deputy prime ministers Yesilgöz (VVD) and Van den Brink (CDA). Later, parliamentary group leaders Paternotte, Brekelmans and Bontenbal joined them. After dinner everyone went home, but there was clearly enough reason to pick up the thread again today. The talks are needed to discuss the strained relations within the cabinet. These arose because D66 and CDA, with help from Pro and other left-wing parties, got an amended tax plan through <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. It was passed by parliament on Thursday by the narrowest possible majority, to the great fury of coalition partner VVD. Relaunch? For a long time it seemed the cabinet would collapse that very same day because of that manoeuvre, but after hours of talks Premier Jetten managed to agree to continue talking this weekend. He said he was open to "a serious relaunch". "When it comes to money, these have been a difficult few months. That also calls for a thorough reflection together on how we can restore that trust." VVD leader Yesilgöz said that same evening that this would require a major change of course. She called the minority cabinet, which took office less than a year ago, "a failed experiment" and proposed adding another right-wing party to the coalition, because she feels the coalition partners too often lean to the left. What the further talks in Hilversum yielded yesterday is not yet known. The discussions are taking place on a closed site of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>, and the parties are maintaining radio silence until conclusions have been drawn. So when the meeting ended shortly before 20.00 hours yesterday evening, the participants left the site in armoured cars, without speaking to the press.

title: Three quarters of municipalities grant no exemption for setting off fireworks
lead: The vast majority of Dutch municipalities are not granting any exemption from the fireworks ban for the coming New Year's Eve. That is what emerges from a survey by NOS and the regional broadcasters. This concerns at least three quarters of the municipalities. Some of the other municipalities are open to it, but it is not yet clear whether exemptions will actually be granted. With an exemption, people may still set off fireworks despite the fireworks ban. Municipalities are therefore handling applications differently. For example, ten of the twelve Drenthe municipalities allow exemptions to be applied for, but in the <entity id="org:provincie-utrecht">provincie Utrecht</entity> no applications can be submitted at all. Few exemptions are granted in Limburg, <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity>, Brabant, North and <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-overijssel">Overijssel</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>. Where municipalities do grant an exemption, applicants must meet strict national rules. For example, only associations or foundations with a clear local connection, such as a neighbourhood association or sports club, may submit an application. In addition, there must be a safety plan, among other things, in which applicants take into account fixed safety distances, and fireworks may only be set off between 18.00 on New Year's Eve and 02.00 on New Year's morning. A maximum of 200 kilos of F2 display fireworks is permitted. Strict zero policy. Although these national rules exist, a mayor may decide for themselves whether an exemption is granted. That therefore also applies to applicants who can meet the rules. "Municipalities may namely also choose this year to adopt a strict zero policy", says Annemarie Drahmann. She is professor of administrative law at Utrecht University. "Whether a municipality may also decide never to grant exemptions again is not self-evident. That is namely at odds with the purpose of the law." "At the moment municipalities are opting for a temporary stop, because the guidelines and assessment criteria surrounding the law are not yet finished. Although it does not deserve a beauty prize that a law comes into force while municipalities are not yet ready to answer applications, it is not in breach of the rules." Fireworks enthusiasts are not happy with the situation as it is. "I feel that a hobby of mine has been taken away from me, I feel deceived. It seems like a measure for show, because the government does not want to bear the risks", says Ruben van Wijk. He wanted to try to obtain an exemption in <entity id="org:gemeente-alphen-aan-den-rijn">Alphen aan den Rijn</entity>, but it became clear to him that the municipality would not accept that. "After it became known that Alphen aan den Rijn is not granting exemptions, I wondered whether the pros and cons of granting an exemption had actually been investigated. In my view an exemption does not have to be complicated, but they say it cannot be arranged." The municipality of Alphen aan de Rijn states that insufficient supervision could be organised to monitor compliance with the rules for exemptions. The municipality speaks of "a new task and limited preparation time". This applies to more municipalities, says the <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten</entity>. Fireworks enthusiast Ruud Vlemmix from Breda does not consider that a good reason. "The government must not simply lock the door because they did not have time to work out the rules. National legislation actually obliges municipalities to always assess applications for organised fireworks individually and on their merits." Van Wijk from Alphen will not be setting off fireworks himself this year. "I am going to sit, however sad it is, with my wife and our dog in a hut on the heath." Fireworks on the sports field. There are therefore also municipalities where associations can apply for an exemption. Jan Hoekstra is chair of Dorpsbelangen in the Frisian village of Reahûs, in the <entity id="org:gemeente-sudwest-fryslan">gemeente Súdwest-Fryslân</entity>. His application was approved. "We have been holding a joint fireworks gathering around New Year on the local sports field for years", he explains. On the advice of the municipality, Dorpsbelangen has therefore applied for an exemption this year. "We held a meeting at which residents promised that they would keep to the agreements on quantity, location and distance from the public. Those are rules we always had anyway and have tightened here and there, and we have now put that into an exemption."

title: Fourth outbreak of bird flu in Gelderland this week: 60,000 chickens culled
lead: For the fourth time this week, bird flu has been found at a Gelderland company, reports Omroep Gelderland. This time it concerns a poultry farm in Oosterwolde. The approximately 60,000 chickens are being culled under the supervision of the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> (NVWA). The previous culls were in the village of Hierden, about 20 kilometres away. The bird flu was detected at a laying hen farm. Within a radius of 10 kilometres there is a transport ban, to prevent further spread of the disease. No birds, eggs, manure or used litter may be transported. Eighteen other poultry farms lie within that zone. The NVWA is investigating whether animals or products were transported to or from the farm shortly before the infection was discovered. If necessary, additional measures will follow. Nationwide housing order: yesterday, at a poultry farm with ducks in Hierden, 19,000 ducks and chickens were killed due to a bird flu infection. Earlier this also happened at two duck farms in the area, where a total of 165,000 animals have been culled. Since late October a nationwide housing and screening requirement has been in force to prevent further spread of bird flu.

title: Minister Van Veldhoven to attend climate summit later due to cabinet crisis
lead: Minister Van Veldhoven of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kgg">Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity> will not travel to the large UN climate summit in Turkey until later because of the cabinet crisis. Her spokesperson says so. She was due to arrive tomorrow at the climate summit in Antalya, but tensions within the minority cabinet are now throwing a spanner in the works. As a result, the contribution of the Dutch <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> to the international climate summit is more chaotic than in most years. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> had already skipped the summit entirely earlier because of The Hague's troubles. As a result he did not speak at the so-called leaders' segment, where world leaders and other senior officials speak on behalf of their countries. Because of the political crisis at home, Minister Van Veldhoven will in any case miss a meeting at which the Netherlands wanted to put the circular economy on the map. She was due to speak there tomorrow, together with, among others, European Commissioner Roswall, ministers of various countries and a representative of the UN. Phasing out fossil fuels That the Netherlands' high-level representation is delayed or, in Jetten's case, not present at all in Antalya will not go unnoticed at the UN climate summit. The Netherlands is taking a leading role in efforts to phase out the use of fossil fuels. Although that is the only way to substantially curb global warming, the discussion about it has traditionally been very sensitive at the large climate summits. At the previous climate summit, in Brazil, the Netherlands quite unexpectedly announced together with Colombia that it would organise a special summit on the transition away from fossil fuels. In this way the Netherlands wanted to supplement the large UN summits, where this discussion is stuck. That extra summit took place this year in Santa Marta, Colombia, and Van Veldhoven intended to bring its results to the fore in Antalya. That she is arriving late at the summit in Turkey does not necessarily mean it will no longer be possible. Van Veldhoven hopes to travel to the climate summit after all on Tuesday and still represent the Netherlands. Whether she manages to do so will depend on the outcome of the crisis talks that the leaders of the three coalition parties are holding today in Hilversum.

title: Mishap at Amsterdam Sinterklaas arrival: steamboat cannot proceed due to broken bridge
lead: It seemed like a scene from Het Sinterklaasjournaal, but it was not planned in advance: at the arrival of Sinterklaas in Amsterdam, the last bridge the steamboat had to sail under would no longer open. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was ultimately deployed to get the good saint onto the quay after all. The arrival in the capital began this morning with a route along the Amstel towards the Scheepvaartmuseum. The Saint was due to disembark there and continue on horseback towards Leidseplein, but things went wrong at the last bridge. The bridge could not be opened, so the procession could not continue to the Scheepvaartmuseum, reports city broadcaster AT5. Police assistance was called in, after which the Saint and his helpers were transported the last stretch by police boat. On arrival at the Scheepvaartmuseum the procession was welcomed by many children and deputy mayor Esmah Lahlah. The Saint thanked the police for transporting him and his helpers, mounted his horse and set off for Leidseplein. The procession is due to arrive there around 5 p.m.

title: Coalition crisis talks at Hilversum estate ongoing for hours, outcome still uncertain
lead: Also today, discussions about the future of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> have been going on for hours at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum. Nothing is known about what is being discussed or which direction things are heading. The parties have agreed on radio silence and are not speaking to the press in the meantime. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity> of D66, Deputy Prime Minister Yesilgöz and <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity> of the VVD, and <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">fractievoorzitter Bontenbal</entity> and Deputy Prime Minister Van den Brink of the CDA arrived there this morning at around 11.00 a.m. They also talked for almost the whole day yesterday. After dinner, everyone went home. Again, nothing leaked about what had happened inside. Strained relations That this is not a problem with an easy solution became clear last Friday as well. Then too, for hours on end, there were talks at Jetten's ministry about the disturbed relations within the coalition. When Jetten and Yesilgöz came outside afterwards, they had a different message. Jetten said: "We all have feelings and emotions about how things have gone recently." The three parties must continue talking "in all calm", he said. Yesilgöz indicated that her party did not want to continue on this footing. She called the minority cabinet a failed experiment and wanted a "fundamental reset". CDA and D66 sought support from the left far too often, she said. "If you want to be in a coalition with Pro, say so!", she said. Tensions rise The relationships came under strain when the D66 and CDA parliamentary groups reached an agreement with Pro and Volt on amending the tax plan. In short, it provided that the wealth tax would rise by 1 billion euros and that this money would be used to lower income tax. The cabinet advised <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> not to agree, partly because the financial underpinning was not watertight. After complicated behind-the-scenes horse-trading over motions and amendments with almost all parliamentary groups, the House nonetheless agreed. The amended tax plan was a fact, against the wishes of the VVD. How that will turn out is also still unclear, incidentally, because the law was adopted with the smallest possible majority of 76 seats. If the parties that voted in favour in the House of Representatives also vote in favour in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>, there is still no majority there. The tax plan has thus led to a cabinet crisis and is also still a political problem. Most of the day the negotiators stayed inside, but this afternoon the prime minister took a short walk:

title: Cyclist dies after accident in Oudewater, ambulance crashes on the way
lead: A 54-year-old man died in a traffic accident in Oudewater last night. An ambulance on its way to the accident was itself involved in a crash and collided head-on with a car. Two people were injured in that collision. The first traffic accident happened around 01.00 on the Hoenkoopse Buurtweg. When the emergency services arrived, they found the seriously injured victim lying on the road, near his damaged bicycle. The man was taken to hospital in a critical condition, where he died of his injuries later in the day, RTV Utrecht reports. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating the cause of the accident and is calling on witnesses to come forward. Ambulance collides with car The accident on the Hoekoopse Buurtweg was not the only serious incident, as the ambulance on its way to this incident also got into trouble. Around 01.25 it collided with an oncoming car on the N228 in Montfoort. One of the occupants of that car, a 24-year-old man from Oudewater, was seriously injured. He has been taken to hospital. The 21-year-old passenger from Woerden was also injured and had to go to hospital. The ambulance driver was unhurt. The police are also investigating this accident. They are also looking at whether slippery road surfaces played a role, according to the police.

title: German authorities also oppose nuclear power plants in Eemshaven
lead: German authorities are turning against the possible arrival of two nuclear power plants in Eemshaven, just across the border in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>. German border municipalities and the state of Lower Saxony reject the plans. The mayor of the border municipality of Emden, Tim Kruithoff, tells the German broadcaster NDR: "We are a model region for renewable energy, and that is exactly where they want to build a nuclear power plant." The mayor of the island of Borkum in the Wadden Sea, east of Rottumerplaat, is also deeply worried. He calls the plans unacceptable and has written a worried letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. In the event of a nuclear disaster, the entire island would have to be evacuated. The state government of Lower Saxony has also already told the Netherlands that it rejects the plans. Demonstration In Groningen there is also strong resistance to building nuclear power plants in Eemshaven. This afternoon a demonstration was held in the city of Groningen, attracting around three hundred people. A German protest was there too. Some demonstrators had come over from Borkum to the mainland. They reinforced their protest with a skeleton in a coffin. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> announced last summer that three locations are under consideration for two new nuclear power plants: two locations in Eemshaven and one in <entity id="org:gemeente-terneuzen">Terneuzen</entity> in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>. The cabinet bases this choice partly on an advisory report from grid operator Tennet, which considers the Groningen port area to be the best option technically. Port authority Groningen Seaports concluded on Friday that Eemshaven is not a logical location, because any nuclear power plants could affect the local energy system and the security of electricity supply across the whole of the Netherlands. There is also little to no support for nuclear power plants in the province in Groningen politics. The cabinet is keeping the option for Groningen open, but has promised to keep to its pledge that Groningen will drop out if Zeeland is 'equally suitable'. In Terneuzen there is more support, but there are major technical challenges there. Tennet expects major bottlenecks in connecting to the high-voltage grid. The cabinet plans to make a final decision in early December.

title: Bomb attack on home of investigative journalist in Panama: 'This changes the rules of the game'
lead: The home of Panamanian investigative journalist Rolando Rodríguez was damaged in a bomb attack. His employer, the national newspaper La Prensa , reported this. The newspaper's deputy editor-in-chief was not at home at the time of the explosion in San Miguelito, the country's second city, located next to the capital Panama City. His wife was there, but she was not injured. She managed to escape with their pets. "This was an attack on my life and that of my family", Rodríguez told reporters. The perpetrator reportedly arrived at the house by taxi around 02:30 yesterday. He threw an object at the façade, causing an explosion. Two cars parked at the house went up in flames. New rules Panama is known as relatively safe for journalists. The country has press freedom. A bomb attack in particular is a form of violence against a journalist that is unprecedented in the country. "This changes the rules of the game in Panama, because now we all run the risk of this happening to us", said Rodríguez. President Mulino also spoke out against the violence on X. "Panama does not accept this kind of action under any circumstances. I have informed La Prensa of this and expressed my solidarity." Investigation Rodríguez is an experienced investigative journalist and columnist. He has contributed to and led many investigations into corruption in the Panamanian public sector, the judiciary and business. He is currently working on a news article about two former officials of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>, a large government contractor and the state electricity company Etesa. Three people involved who received a written questionnaire from Rodríguez last week have distanced themselves from the attack on the journalist and say they hope the investigation will quickly lead to the arrest of the perpetrator and the instigators. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> are investigating arson and say the charges may still be extended.

title: Yemeni government forces withdraw from area at key strait
lead: Yemeni government forces are withdrawing from the area around Bab al-Mandab, the important strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa in the Red Sea. They have failed to fully drive the Houthis out of the area or to regain the port city of Mocha. This brings an end to the counteroffensive, which lasted six weeks, to retake control of the western coastline from the Houthis. The armed group had seized the area in September, giving it control of Bab al-Mandab. The government army says it wants to focus on defending the most important base in Aden, on the southern coast of Yemen. Major setback. The withdrawal is a major setback for the Yemeni government troops, who are backed by neighbouring Saudi Arabia. Last month in the counteroffensive, the government forces had managed to retake important areas at the narrow strait at a rapid pace, including the district of Dhubab in the west of the country. The Yemeni <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> also reported that it had regained control of Bab al-Mandab. In response to the counteroffensive and to Saudi airstrikes on Yemen, the Houthis have stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks. Several airports in the country were bombarded with drone and rocket attacks. The Houthis say that today they also attacked the international airport of the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles. The airport was also attacked by the Houthis last month. The financial district of the city is also reported to have been hit. The Saudi government has not yet confirmed the attacks. The Houthis may now focus on Aden. The government of Yemen has been based there since the Houthis took the capital Sanaa in 2015. The Houthis are reportedly now at Tur al-Bahah, some 80 kilometres west of Aden. According to Yemeni military sources, government forces have moved to As Suqayyah, some 150 kilometres west of Aden, and are trying to drive the Houthis out of nearby coastal areas. Taiz. Meanwhile, fierce fighting continues near the besieged city of Taiz. The Houthis have surrounded Taiz since last month and the humanitarian situation has deteriorated since then. The delivery of emergency aid is being blocked and civilians cannot leave. About 300,000 people live in Taiz. Half of the residents are Yemenis from other parts of the country who have been displaced by the war.

title: Another full day of crisis talks without result, parties continue talking this morning
lead: D66, VVD and CDA have still not reached agreement and will continue talking today at 11.00 at the Catshuis in The Hague. The <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> reports this. The talks were intensive but good, according to the statement. The future of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> and cooperation within the coalition are at stake. The parties have agreed to observe radio silence and make no official statements to the press. After two days of talks at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum, those involved did not speak to the press afterwards. Restart: Behind the scenes it can be heard that a restart of the coalition is still being discussed, says political reporter Arjan Noorlander. It would still be too early to speak with other parties, which is why D66, VVD and CDA will continue talking tomorrow in the same composition as this weekend. This involves <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity> of D66, deputy prime minister Yesilgöz and <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity> of VVD, and <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">fractievoorzitter Bontenbal</entity> and deputy prime minister Van den Brink of CDA. They talked all day Friday in The Hague and met over the weekend in Hilversum. Last night the politicians also left without disclosing the outcome of their talks: because of the talks at the Catshuis, <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> is replacing the minister for Asylum and deputy prime minister Van den Brink at a meeting in Vienna. Today a top-level meeting takes place there with Germany, Austria, Denmark and Greece about a so-called return centre where small numbers of rejected asylum seekers would be sent. Tax plan: Relations within the coalition came under strain last week when the D66 and CDA factions reached an agreement with Pro and Volt on an amendment to the tax plan. In brief, it provided that wealth tax would rise by 1 billion euros and that this money would be used to lower income tax. The cabinet advised <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> not to agree, partly because the financial basis was not watertight. After complicated behind-the-scenes horse-trading over motions and amendments with almost all factions, the House nevertheless agreed. The amended tax plan became a fact, against the wishes of the VVD. VVD leader Yesilgöz announced on Friday that her party no longer wanted to continue on this basis. She called the minority cabinet a failed experiment and wanted a 'fundamental reset'.

title: Far too few aid goods are entering Gaza, Israeli figures show
lead: Only half of the agreed quantity of aid goods reaches Gaza. That is what the Israeli newspaper Haaretz writes, based on requested data from the Israeli army. At the ceasefire in October 2025, Israel promised to let just over 18,000 lorries of goods into Gaza every month. In practice, since March this has averaged only half of that target figure. In October it was just over 6,500 lorries, the lowest number since April. Haaretz bases its reporting on figures from the US-led Civil-Military Coordination Center (CMCC) in Israel. It received the data from Cogat, a part of the Israeli army that coordinates the flow of aid goods. According to the newspaper, the figures have been verified by the United Nations. It is the first time since the start of the ceasefire that Israeli data show the country is not keeping to its own agreements. Aid organisations have said so for longer. Cogat itself says in a response to Haaretz that the figures are not correct, without explaining why. In September Cogat also denied that insufficient goods were entering Gaza, when the Dutch Red Cross raised the alarm about a shortage of food, fuel, medicines and medical supplies, among other things. Food supply By far the largest share of aid goods is food, estimated at around 70 to 80 percent. Gazans have depended on imports for their food since the war began. According to the World Food Programme of the UN, two thirds of the population faces "acute food insecurity at crisis level, or worse". That is 1.4 million Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. Almost all food production has been destroyed by the Israeli army. Much of the farmland used lies behind the yellow line set by Israel, where Palestinians are not allowed to go by the army. Residents who cross the yellow markings or even come too close to them risk being shot dead. The United Nations estimates that of the farmland cultivated before the war, only around 3 percent is still in use. Only 5 percent of the livestock remains. Fishing is also hampered, as the Israeli navy permits it only to a very limited extent. Khaled Talal lives with his family close to the yellow line in Gaza. Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom have today, in a joint statement, called on Israel to allow immediate, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian aid into Gaza. The four countries describe the situation in Gaza as dire. They say 150,000 tents and other vital aid goods are being held back at the border. Because of heavy rainfall, tens of thousands of tents in Gaza have recently been flooded. A large part of the population lives in tents, as around 90 percent of Gazans have been displaced, with limited access to clean water and sanitation. Today in Jabalia in northern Gaza, 69 bodies that had lain under the rubble for more than three years were buried. According to the Palestinian authorities, more than 8,000 bodies are still under the rubble. Ongoing attacks and a shortage of equipment make it difficult to recover them. Israel and Hamas agreed a ceasefire in October 2025, but Israel has violated it almost daily. Since the ceasefire, according to UN-confirmed figures, at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza. Israel says it targets Hamas fighters, but civilians often also die in attacks. According to Israel, at least five Israeli soldiers have died over the past year. Correction from the editors: In an earlier version of this article, the headline stated that the Israeli army now also admits that too few aid goods are entering Gaza. That is not correct: the figures do come from Cogat, an organisation of the Israeli army, but that same organisation says in a response to Haaretz that the figures are not correct. That denial has been added to the current article.

title: Widow of murdered Haitian president now wants to become president herself
lead: Martine Moïse, the widow of the president of Haiti who was murdered in 2021, now wants to become president of the country herself. She has registered herself as a candidate for the first presidential elections in ten years, according to the website of the Haitian electoral council. The elections are scheduled for July next year. "Haiti will stand on its own two feet again, because politics needs to be tackled differently", Moïse wrote on X last week. At that time her registration as a presidential candidate had not yet been announced. Whether it will actually come to that is very much in question. The provisional candidate list currently has 33 people on it, who must meet various conditions to ultimately appear on the ballot paper. Candidates may not have a criminal record, for example. They must also stand on behalf of a political party or coalition, with a membership list of at least 30,000 registered supporters. The provisional list includes former presidents, a former prime minister and a former minister of Haiti. Only three women are on the list. Gang violence The last elections in Haiti took place in 2016. Since then, various leaders have allowed themselves to be influenced by armed groups, and new elections have been postponed several times. Leaders cited the unsafe situation in the country as the reason. Haiti has long been unsafe due to prevailing gang violence, political instability and a deep humanitarian and economic crisis. Moreover, the country is often hit by natural disasters such as earthquakes and floods. The former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert are registered on the provisional electoral list. They are accused of supporting armed gangs. Both deny any involvement in the abuses. Dozens of armed men Former president Jovenel Moïse was at the helm in Haiti from 2017 until his death in July 2021. On the night of 7 July 2021, Moïse was shot dead in his bedroom in the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince by twenty armed men. His wife was injured. Last May, four men were convicted for their role in the murder. Martine Moïse was a key witness in the trial over the murder of her husband.

title: Number of incidents with fake officers up sharply again, scam tricks ever more cunning
lead: The number of incidents involving fake officers continues to rise. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has recorded more than 14,000 incidents so far this year, figures obtained by NOS show. That is already more than in the whole of last year. Fake officers are part of a crafty scam aimed specifically at the elderly. Fraudsters phone with a story that, for example, burglars are in the area and that the police will come to the door to secure money and jewellery. Then someone appears at the door posing as an officer and takes away the valuables of the elderly. The number of incidents with this form of fraud has exploded within a few years: It is so far not possible to bring down the number of incidents with fake officers, the figures show. The total number of reports this year is likely to reach at least 16,000. "We do a great deal on prevention and we do a great deal on investigation," responds Sybren van der Velden Walda, national coordinator high impact crime at the police. "But evidently it is still so lucrative that criminals keep posing as fake officers to rob people." Obedient generation This year, almost 3,300 people have so far reported theft by a fake officer. The police say the reports show that at least a quarter of the victims were actually taken in. This is due, among other things, to the high age of the victims. The fraudsters focus entirely on seniors. The oldest victim robbed was 103 years old. "They come from a generation that has trust in authority," says Van der Velden Walda. "If the police call and say something is going on and that you need to put your things out, then this is a generation that still just does it." Cunning At the same time, the scam tricks are becoming ever more cunning. The fraudsters drop the names of existing neighbourhood officers or use privacy-sensitive data of their victims from data leaks. "They have, for example, your name, address and telephone number. But also the names of your children. And they use that information in the phone call to win your trust." The fraudsters often keep their victim on the line until the fake officer is actually at the door. The victim therefore gets no chance at all to reconsider. Young offenders Meanwhile, the fake officers who appear at the door are often quite young. "The youngest suspect we have arrested was 13 years old. We see that it is a vulnerable group, recruited by organised crime to do this sort of thing." This year the police have so far arrested 783 fake officers. Sometimes the collectors actually have something resembling police clothing, but often they say they are from the detective branch and deliberately do not wear a uniform. The loot mostly consists of money and jewellery, but sometimes also of phones or a tablet. This year the police see more and more combinations with bank helpdesk fraud. After a fake officer has taken the valuable items, the victim is connected to a so-called bank employee. That person then obtains the victim's login details and also empties the bank account. Suffering The suffering caused by the fraudsters is enormous. The elderly victims sometimes lose all their savings, but much more often they lose their most precious possessions. There are countless stories of victims who handed over the last jewellery of their deceased partner to fake officers. "The example that has stayed with me most is that they took someone to the kitchen to remove a ring with soap," says Van der Velden Walda. "Or they help take off a pendant that contains, for example, the ashes of a deceased partner. The impact is enormous." Consequences for the police The police see victims who become isolated, do not dare leave their home and completely lose trust in others. The police themselves are now also experiencing the consequences of the surge in fake officers. "I notice that my colleagues on the street have difficulty engaging with seniors, for example when they are conducting a neighbourhood inquiry because of a burglary. Older people no longer open the door, because they simply do not trust that a police officer is at the door." The police continue to stress that real officers never come to collect valuables and give older people as much information as possible about this kind of scam. Anyone who wants to check whether it really is the police at the door may call 112.

title: Wake-up call 16/11: Coalition continues crisis talks • International match Germany-Netherlands
lead: Good morning! After days of crisis talks, the discussions between D66, VVD and CDA about the future of this minority cabinet continue today. This evening the Dutch national football team plays Germany in the Nations League. First, the weather: today showers will pass over the country. There will be a brisk westerly wind. It will be 9 to 11 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, the founder of the first Mexican drug cartel and one of the best-known criminals in Mexican history, has died. He had been in poor health for some time and died in a hospital in the city of Guadalajara from the effects of pneumonia. 'El Jefe de Jefes', or 'the Boss of Bosses', was 80 years old. Félix Gallardo built an enormous drug empire in Mexico in the 1970s and 1980s, which was able to keep operating for decades thanks to a tightly run organisation and close ties with the authorities. At a time when the Colombian Medellín cartel under Pablo Escobar was sending tonnes of cocaine towards the United States, the Guadalajara cartel founded by Félix Gallardo ensured that these drugs actually crossed the border. Other news from overnight: And then just this: It looked like a scene from Het Sinterklaasjournaal, but it was not planned in advance: at the arrival of Sinterklaas in Amsterdam, the last bridge under which the steamboat had to pass would no longer open. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was eventually deployed to get the good saint onto the quay. You can read how that went in this article: Have a great day!

title: At least 11 dead after fire at motorbike rental company on Thai island of Phuket
lead: In a fire in the Thai seaside resort of Patong on the island of Phuket, eleven people died overnight. According to police, sixteen people were injured. According to the Bangkok Post, a transformer exploded at around 03.15 local time, after which the fire spread to a fuel dispenser of a motorbike rental company. The fire then spread to the apartments above and neighbouring buildings. Dozens of motorbikes were stored at the rental company. Petrol and lubricants were also stored there. The fire released a lot of smoke. According to the governor of Phuket, most of the victims probably suffocated in the smoke. After about two hours, the fire brigade had the fire under control. The Bangkok Post writes that some of those who died called friends and family while trying to escape the thick smoke and flames. Among the dead are eight women and three men. One of them came from Myanmar. The other victims were Thai nationals. According to police, there are no tourists among the dead or injured. The building where the fire raged stood near the popular Patong beach, on the west coast of the holiday island of Phuket. The authorities are still investigating the cause of the fire.

title: ACM to investigate the construction sector
lead: The competition authority ACM will conduct market research into the construction sector in the coming period. According to the Authority for Consumers and Markets, there is no direct reason for the investigation, but because of the high demand for construction projects, such as new housing, and the many renovations of infrastructure such as viaducts, fraud is a real risk. The regulator said this in an interview with the Financieele Dagblad. High fines In the newspaper, <entity id="person:martijn-snoep">Martijn Snoep</entity>, chair of the ACM, says that the risk of agreements between construction companies increases when more contracts become available. The ACM monitors the market and can, for example, block a takeover if it would leave too little competition in the market. The regulator also checks whether there is enough competition and, in this case, whether no illegal price agreements are being made in the sector. For such an infringement, the regulator can impose high fines of up to 900,000 euros per infringement. A fine can also be higher: the ACM can impose a fine equal to a percentage of a company's turnover. A team of about fifteen people will get to work on the investigation. They will speak with both clients and contractors and ask them about their experiences. For example, they ask whether clients are satisfied with the price set for the construction project. 25 years since construction fraud It is 25 years since the programme Zembla exposed large-scale fraud in the construction sector. Through that programme, whistleblower Ad Bos said that construction companies had made prohibited agreements and artificially kept prices high. Because of these price agreements, the government paid billions of euros too much.
