With that party alone, a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> was just missed. Choice of 'left' or 'right' A choice 'between left or right' then had to be made. But the VVD certainly did not want to govern with Pro, while D66 was not keen on cooperating with JA21. They decided to try it with the three of them, with a coalition ten seats short in the Tweede Kamer and sixteen in the Eerste. Thus on 23 February 2026 a minority cabinet stood on the king's doorstep, which constantly had to seek support from the opposition. But the non-coalition parties only wanted to cooperate if the cabinet first chose a political direction. Because Pro did not want to make a deal involving JA21, and vice versa. To this day the coalition parties have not agreed on the route to a majority. Will they turn left, right, or go down the middle? That question has never been answered. They have held on to the aim of as broad a majority as possible (of more than one hundred seats in the Tweede Kamer), but no agreements on this could be made in advance. 'Back to square one' Jetten admitted yesterday that he had thought about it too lightly. He had been "too nice", "too optimistic". From now on, cooperation must be sought with "a bloc of parties", such as Pro and Volt, JA21, SGP and BBB, or ChristenUnie and 50Plus, he said. Yesilgöz added that it genuinely makes no difference to her whether it is with the left or the right. But the question of who it will be has therefore been pushed back again. "We are back to square one", concluded <entity id="person:christine-teunissen">partijleider Teunissen</entity> of the Party for the Animals yesterday evening. "The only thing that has happened is that a cabinet collapse has been avoided", said Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity>. <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> Yesterday's debate in the Tweede Kamer also focused much on the role of Minister Heinen of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. It was his tax plan that caused much fuss over the past months, and against which his own party, the VVD, ultimately voted, after D66 and CDA had struck a deal with Pro and Volt on an amendment. That amendment means the most wealthy will pay more tax. Heinen's role was already not uncontroversial within the coalition. Heinen often seemed to pursue his own plan, and in August he came up with a draft budget which D66 and CDA considered far too right-wing. With this story he would definitively slam the door on Pro, the largest opposition party in both the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. Tensions also ran high then, and the cabinet briefly began to wobble. Now the story goes that Heinen tried to persuade parties such as Denk to vote against his 'own' tax plan. 'Divided house' It is not yet clear how things will proceed. The cabinet has asked <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity>, vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>, to help. It is not yet clear what exactly his role will entail. The choice of a specific bloc of parties has not yet been made. The House has little confidence that things are once again harmonious within the coalition. The relations between them are damaged, coalition faction leaders themselves also admitted. Many opposition parties think the cabinet could still fall within the foreseeable future. "A divided house cannot stand", concluded ChristenUnie <entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">leider Bikker</entity>. More on this topic? What is needed for the restart of the Jetten minority cabinet to succeed? An attempt at an answer can be heard in the podcast De Dag. You can listen to the podcast De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe.

lead: Last year, five hundred Dutch people were told they had contracted HIV. After years of decline, the number of HIV diagnoses has now risen for four years in a row. "The increase among young men who have sex with men is alarming," says Mark Vermeulen, director of Soa Aids Nederland.

title: Nearly half of asylum seekers find work after targeted guidance
lead: When asylum seekers receive targeted guidance, the chances are good that they find a job. A trial was carried out with this in five municipalities. Of the more than five hundred participating asylum seekers, nearly half found work. They often also managed to keep that job and dropout remained limited, concludes knowledge institute Platform31.

title: Helmet requirement also for children in electric cargo bikes
lead: Children transported in an electric cargo bike or on the back of an electric bicycle will soon have to wear a helmet. The helmet requirement for young people on fat bikes or e-bikes will also apply to those children. <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has decided that. The aim is for the rule to take effect on 1 September 2027. It was already known that the cabinet wants to introduce a helmet requirement for young people under 18 next year. The rule will apply to electric bicycles and light electric vehicles, such as fat bikes, electric cargo bikes, e-scooters and Segways. The cabinet's final decision states that the helmet requirement will apply to minor drivers "and passengers". That means children who are taken to school on an electric (cargo) bike must also wear a helmet. The parents do not need to wear a helmet. Brain injury The rule is intended to reduce the number of injuries from accidents. According to <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity>, young people suffered six times as much brain injury in 2024 as in 2020. "These are serious figures", he writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. "A serious accident can sometimes stay with you for the rest of your life. By making it compulsory to wear a helmet, we are specifically reducing the chance of serious injury." An exception is made for minor passengers in vehicles where the chance of brain injury is small due to additional safety measures. These are, for example, BSO buses used in childcare. The Tweede Kamer can still ask questions about the decision, which also goes to the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> for advice. But no major changes will be made.

title: Podcast De Dag: second attempt at the minority experiment
lead: The minority cabinet is carrying on after a long weekend of crisis talks. Vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> must help the three coalition parties to improve cooperation with <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity>. What is needed to make the restart of the minority cabinet Jetten succeed? Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. Claes de Vreese advised <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> during the formation on governing as a minority, as they have done in Denmark for decades. He is professor of political communication at the University of Amsterdam. D66, CDA and VVD disagreed from the start about where majorities could be sought. And parliament is also not yet in the mode of governing with a minority cabinet. If it continues in this way, a minority government has no chance, says De Vreese. But he can hardly imagine that in a country like the Netherlands, which grew great through consensus politics. Respond: email dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial: Rosanne Sies Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: FVD members active in neo-Nazi network and at cage fights, party expels two members
lead: People in and around Forum for Democracy (FVD) have ties to a violent neo-Nazi network that organises cage fights here and there across the country. This emerges from a broadcast by investigative programme Zembla. It involves, among others, Ramon van Asch, the FVD parliamentary group leader on the municipal council of 's-Hertogenbosch. He was 13th on the list in last year's House of Representatives elections, was until recently a staff member of the House of Representatives parliamentary group, and was convicted three times for assault. Van Asch attended a cage fight last summer in a party tent in the Brabant village of Oeffelt, where participants and spectators repeatedly gave the Hitler salute and shouted "Sieg Heil!". Zembla filmed him as he left the tent with a baby in his arms. These are images in Zembla's possession: Two members of the youth wing JFVD took part in such a fight themselves in Finsterwolde in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, including Luc Kluytmans. The latter is on social media one of the faces of Eerlijk Eten, the online meal service founded by FVD figures such as Thierry Baudet. According to Zembla, both JFVD members are also members of Wolvenrad, a neo-Nazi group that holds an annual commemoration gathering in Luxembourg for Adolf Hitler. FVD says in a response that it has expelled two members. They are councillor Van Asch and JFVD member Kluytmans. Van Asch has also been urged to stop as group leader in 's-Hertogenbosch, which he has done. Zembla made these images of the Hitler gathering in Luxembourg: Zembla's staff secretly filmed Kluytmans at that commemoration last April, where he took part in the burning of books by Jewish writers. This is a reference to the 1930s, when the Nazis in Germany and Austria organised book burnings of books they considered harmful, by writers, thinkers and scientists such as Karl Marx, Sigmund Freud, Albert Einstein, Bertolt Brecht, Thomas Mann and Erich Maria Remarque. Another man at the campfire asked: "Surely I can go hunting politicians with my gun?" Wolvenrad leader at JFVD gala At that same gathering, the leader of Wolvenrad, Timo Schook, said in a speech: "We thank our leader. We are grateful for the struggle he has fought for us, the sacrifices. Hail our Führer, Hail Hitler, Sieg Heil." A photo Zembla shows reveals that Schook attended the JFVD's Christmas gala at the end of last year, the youth movement that functions as an internal training institute. Several FVD members of the House come from the JFVD. 'Youthful sins' In the run-up to the municipal elections last March, FVD was already linked to neo-Nazis. Frank Folkerts, the current group leader on the <entity id="org:gemeenteraad-nieuwegein">gemeenteraad van Nieuwegein</entity>, was previously a member of the Nederlandse Volks Unie, which aims for a one-party state on the model of Nazi Germany. FVD leader Lidewij de Vos dismissed the extremist past of some candidates for the municipal councils in February as youthful sins. "It is part of the normal adult development of young people to try out radical views", she said in a YouTube video . "That doesn't mean they will stand by exactly those views for the rest of their lives." FVD's response On the new revelations, the current group leader in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, Ralf Dekker, responded laconically to the NOS this afternoon, before he had seen the footage. "Everyone must go where they want. It's good to orient yourself broadly. Especially those very young people, who experiment, want to see all sorts of things. I don't find that problematic at all." According to Dekker, Van Asch is no longer a policy adviser to the parliamentary group. "There is no particular reason for that. He has simply started doing something else." But according to Zembla, he only had this job removed as a secondary role from the Den Bosch municipal register on 10 November, a week after Zembla confronted FVD members of the House with its findings. About Timo Schook's attendance at the JFVD gala, FVD tells Zembla that he was not there by invitation in any case. "Ticket sales were public." Eerlijk Eten would have no relationship with the party at all. FVD also stresses that it is "opposed to every form of violence". Calling an ambulance not allowed The organiser of the cage fights shown in Zembla is Active Club Dietsland, part of a worldwide network of 'nationalist combat sports clubs'. The footage shows that things get rough there: fighters regularly lose consciousness and have to be revived by so-called medics. Calling an ambulance is strictly forbidden, an infiltrator for Zembla says in the programme, because the gatherings could then not be kept secret. Meanwhile, children sometimes watch. According to the latest 'threat picture' of the National Coordinator for Counterterrorism and Security (NCTV), the aim of these confrontations is "to increase and protect the physical resilience of the 'white race'". In the Netherlands this "does not for now pose a threat of violence", but it "could potentially increase the risk of possible willingness to use violence", the NCTV says. In other countries, members of the Active Clubs have committed violence. Zembla shows Swedes who took part in the fights in Finsterwolde, who were arrested a few months later in their own country for assaulting migrants. Three of them were sentenced to up to four years in prison. The Zembla investigation Zembla worked with the VRT investigative programme Pano . This included using an infiltrator in the neo-Nazi groups. Zembla also gained access to hundreds of videos of secret gatherings. At the Hitler commemoration last April, staff filmed unnoticed from 50 metres away. Sound equipment was also hidden beforehand, and cameras were concealed in birdhouses. The broadcast can be seen tomorrow in two parts on <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> 2: part 1 at 21.15 and part 2 at 23.45. The complete programme is also available from now on on NPO Start and on YouTube .

title: House of Representatives wants to prevent higher train fares, but it is a race against the clock
lead:
A majority in the House of Representatives wants the price of train tickets not to rise next year. A proposal from the Party for the Animals that calls on <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to stop this increase will gain a majority in tomorrow's votes. This appears to take the previously announced 4.7 percent increase in train tickets for 2027 off the table. MP Kostic of the Party for the Animals calls this "very good news for Dutch people, especially for people who already struggle to pay for a train ticket, for example to visit their grandchild". The proposal is supported by CDA, Pro, D66, Denk, 50Plus, SP and Volt. That the coalition parties D66 and CDA have also put their signatures to this proposal is a result of the deal they struck last Thursday over the tax plan. That same evening it emerged that coalition party VVD would vote against its own tax plan. CDA and D66 then looked for other parties to help get the tax plan through a majority without the VVD. The Party for the Animals was willing to do so, but wanted, among other things, a guarantee that the price of train tickets would not go up. That now appears to be settled.

Uncertain whether it will go ahead

After tomorrow's vote, <entity id="person:annet-bertram">staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> (CDA) for Public Transport must get to work on the plan. But she doubts whether she can carry out the deal that her party leader Henri Bontenbal struck on Thursday. "I have a lot of sympathy for the motion because it does something about the affordability of public transport," she said today. Even so, she advises the House of Representatives not to adopt the proposal tomorrow. Her reason is that she is already working on a structural solution to make public transport more affordable. She also doubts whether there is enough money to compensate the Dutch Railways if the increase does not go ahead.

How will this be paid for?

If the planned 4.7 percent price increase does not go ahead, it will cost the Dutch Railways money. Travellers will then still pay the same next year, while NS's costs do rise. This would amount to over 100 million euros, insiders confirm to the NOS. The Party for the Animals wants to compensate NS with money left over from the discount ticket on trains last summer. According to the Party for the Animals, that is around 65 million euros. That sum does not appear to be enough to compensate for the full price rise. But what that means for the plan is still unclear.

What makes all this even more complicated is that NS must know within the coming days whether the price increase will go ahead. It takes time to adjust the systems, subscriptions and all the ticket machines accordingly. That is partly why the House of Representatives is voting on the proposal tomorrow already.

Plaster

If the price increase for next year does not go ahead permanently, the travellers' association Rover considers that good news. "We are enthusiastic that there is attention for public transport, because it is incredibly expensive," says director Daan Zieren. "Our concern is only that this is not a structural solution. This is just another plaster that is only stuck on for a year." This plan only covers 2027. If nothing changes, train tickets will become 4.7 percent more expensive in 2028 after all, plus the increase for 2028 itself. In recent years it has happened a few times before that an increase in train tickets was prevented at the last minute. That too has always only been for one year. Experts have long been critical that the House of Representatives keeps pushing the problem ahead with one-off pots of money. They also warn that large increases, for example those for 2027 and 2028 passed on all at once, could drive many travellers off the train.

title: FVD expels two members after Zembla broadcast on neo-Nazis and Hitler worship
lead: Forum voor Democratie has expelled two members following the Zembla report on ties that people in and around the party maintain with a violent neo-Nazi network. Ramon van Asch, FVD faction leader in Den Bosch, has stepped down at the party's urging. Investigative programme Zembla discovered that members of the party and its youth wing JFVD attended cage fights this summer where the Hitler salute was given and "Sieg Heil!" was shouted. Members of JFVD were also at a commemoration event for Adolf Hitler. These are images of cage fights in Zembla's possession: FVD says it has taken note of the news "with disapproval". In a statement on X the party says that "unacceptable conduct and views" were displayed at the "fight event of an extremist group". The two members have been expelled and Van Asch was asked to step down, which he has done. Nonchalant FVD faction leader Ralf Dekker responded nonchalantly to the NOS this afternoon when asked about the Zembla revelations. "Everyone should go where they want to go. It is good to orient yourself broadly. Especially those very young people, who experiment, want to see all sorts of things. I don't find that at all problematic." Now the party is nevertheless taking measures. Dekker says in a reaction on X that when he was questioned he had "no knowledge" of the report or "the seriousness of the situation". FVD had already been approached earlier by Zembla for a response. The party was aware that Zembla would come with this broadcast. In the interview with the NOS Dekker was also confronted with what could be seen in the footage. Read here the conclusions from the Zembla broadcast: Van Asch has now also responded. He says he was invited to the cage fight by an acquaintance "without knowing exactly what the nature of it was". According to him, this is shown among other things by the fact that he went there with his little son. Zembla footage shows him leaving the tent with a baby on his arm. Van Asch says that he saw some people putting on a mask and that a referee announced a boxing match. He says that at that moment he was going home and heard nothing more of what took place afterwards. Van Asch says it was not his intention to link FVD to the organisation. Hitler commemoration The other expelled member is Luc Kluytmans, who according to Zembla himself took part in a neo-Nazi cage fight in Groningen. He is a member of youth wing JFVD and on social media is one of the faces of FVD's online meal service. In addition, according to Zembla he is a member of the neo-Nazi group Wolvenrad, which holds an annual commemoration event for Hitler in Luxembourg. Zembla made these images of the Luxembourg event: The Zembla investigation Zembla worked together with the VRT investigative programme Pano. Among other things, an infiltrator was used in the neo-Nazi groups. Zembla also gained access to hundreds of videos of secret gatherings. At the Hitler commemoration last April, staff filmed unnoticed from 50 metres away. Sound equipment had also been hidden beforehand and cameras were concealed in birdhouses. The broadcast can be watched tomorrow in two parts on NPO 2: at 21.15 part 1 and at 23.45 part 2. The complete programme is also available now on NPO Start and on YouTube.

title: Minister Van Weel believes FVD has some explaining to do, party expels six members
lead: Minister Van Weel of Justice has looked "with horror" at the Zembla broadcast about neo-Nazi fight clubs. That members of Forum voor Democratie (FVD) were present there he also finds appalling. Van Weel believes Forum voor Democratie must distance itself "forcefully" from the neo-Nazi fight clubs. "These clubs must not be given any room in political discourse in the Netherlands." It is not the first time members of Forum voor Democratie have turned up at far-right gatherings. "Until now it was always said that there were no direct ties. But I do think Forum has some explaining to do in light of these images", said the minister. Six FVD members expelled. FVD parliamentary group leader Ralf Dekker initially reacted casually yesterday to Zembla's revelations. "Everyone must go where they want. I don't find this problematic." Only after he had seen the images did the party leadership take action, and two FVD members involved were expelled. On social media, supporters mainly explain Zembla's revelations as an organised attempt to discredit FVD. But Dekker told RTL Nieuws today that six members have now been identified in the images and that all of them have been removed from the party. He also calls on all members who support neo-Nazi ideology to end their membership. "This must be rooted out root and branch." 'No thought police' Party leader De Vos, who returns from maternity leave next week, speaks on the SBS programme Nieuws van de Dag about "shocking images" and stresses that the party has taken measures by expelling the six FVD members. She wants to "move on to the order of the day". She also stresses that the party knew nothing of the views of the expelled members and that the party has nothing to do with them. "When violence is involved we draw a line, but we are not going to play thought police", said De Vos. Downplaying VVD parliamentary leader <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity> expresses via X his horror at the "chilling insight into the far right" shown in Zembla. He is critical of the FVD reaction, where he sees "the same pattern again". "Supporters of Forum voor Democratie who play the victim. Spout conspiracy theories. Downplay everything. But antisemitism and racism can never be downplayed", said Brekelmans. "It shows what filth is going on within FVD, behind the mask of feigned reasonableness." 'Threatens the rule of law' <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> will go further in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> on the Zembla broadcast and the danger of far-right extremist groups, without naming Forum voor Democratie. "That members of a political party maintain ties with a (violent) far-right extremist network can lead to far-right extremist ideas gaining further entry into Dutch politics and increasingly becoming normalised", write ministers Van Weel and Heerma of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>. "This threatens the rule of law." The cabinet fears that extremist ideas are being normalised and that the use of violence is being legitimised, and that this may affect national security, the letter states. Possible investigation OM According to Van Weel, the security services were already aware of the existence of this kind of fight club, where the Hitler salute is given and Nazi symbols can be seen. "Active investigation is also being carried out into this. But thanks to the excellent work of these journalists, everyone can now see what is going on there." If the party of Thierry Baudet and Lidewij de Vos does not distance itself "resolutely", the minister says they are making a mistake. "Then they indirectly normalise the ideology of these clubs." The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> says it will review the Zembla broadcast. "On that basis it will be decided whether an investigation into possible criminal offences will be launched."

title: Fons Lambie: 'It is a crisis in the minority coalition'
lead: "D66 and CDA have struck a deal with the left-wing opposition to secure a majority for the tax plan in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. But to the fury of the VVD. And as a result <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is wobbling", says political reporter Fons Lambie.

title: Sybrand Buma takes on task: 'He understands the complexity of a minority cabinet'
lead: Sybrand Buma can start on his task. The vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> is to advise <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> on how best to cooperate with "the constructive forces in parliament", says <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>. "Particularly with regard to financial decision-making." Buma will receive an official letter from the cabinet later today asking whether he can investigate whether a "financial foundation" can be laid under decision-making on budgets and the tax plan, and whether agreements can be made about "the rules of the game we use", Jetten says in his weekly press conference. He has already said 'yes'. Buma has been in the picture since the start of this week. He has already briefly spoken with Jetten about his task and "is positive about it", the premier says. He will be given a month to deliver advice. Jetten points out that Buma was involved as informateur in the formation of his minority cabinet. "So he understands that it is complex in a parliament with a great many political groups. He is keen to help with that, but will do so in his own way, so he will not shy away from putting his finger on the sore spot now and then." According to deputy prime minister Van den Brink (CDA), Buma is tailor-made for this role, because he has a long track record in politics. "He has been part of both coalition and opposition in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> and so can well empathise with the question at hand." Opposition raises questions Buma's involvement was received with little enthusiasm in the parliamentary debate on the crisis on Tuesday evening. Many opposition parties raised questions about it, also because of his job at the Council of State. The <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> has its highest, independent advisory body in the Council of State. The fear is that the vice-president is now helping to draw up political agreements that he will later have to assess himself. <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Minister Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says Buma was precisely asked "because of his role at the Council of State" as one of the cabinet's highest advisers. He thinks that is fine, because the question of how a minority cabinet should deal with the opposition "is new". And it has "not gone smoothly" in recent months, he admits. Who is Sybrand Buma? Sybrand van Haersma Buma has been vice-president of the Council of State since July of this year, making him in effect the leader of the government's most important advisory body. The king formally sits above him as chair, but has a ceremonial role. Before this, he was <entity id="pos:burgemeester-leeuwarden">burgemeester van Leeuwarden</entity> for seven years. Buma is a CDA member. He was a member of the House of Representatives for seventeen years (2002-2019), of which just under nine years as CDA parliamentary group leader. He was informateur at the end of last year. On 8 December 2025 he reported that he saw no possibility of forming a majority cabinet and proposed continuing the cabinet formation with D66, VVD and CDA. Buma will not respond personally today. He is on a working visit to Curaçao. There he spoke with the Council of Ministers about, among other things, legislative capacity on the island. The 'Torentjesoverleg' returns. A lot of other things will also need to happen alongside Buma's input "to ensure that we are in a somewhat more orderly process for the Voorjaarsnota and next year's Prinsjesdag", admits premier Jetten. The so-called 'Torentjesoverleg' is thus restored to improve cooperation within the coalition. This means that premier Jetten, deputy prime ministers Yesilgöz and Van den Brink, and parliamentary group leaders Paternotte (D66), Brekelmans (VVD) and Bontenbal (CDA) will meet on Mondays, bypassing <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, to discuss politically sensitive issues. If necessary, the <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> can also be invited, for example. The 'Torentjesoverleg', which had long since stopped taking place in the premier's Torentje, was also a custom under Jetten's predecessors such as Lubbers, Kok and Rutte. It was abolished when the Rutte IV cabinet took office. There was much criticism at the time of the 'sealed-off' decisions that came out of it.

title: Jetten on neo-Nazi documentary: party leaders must not only act after incidents
lead: Party leaders should act sooner against far-right interference and not "only once incidents become known". That is what <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> said about the Zembla broadcast showing that people in and around Forum voor Democratie have ties to a violent neo-Nazi network. According to Jetten, who spoke about this in the Gesprek met de minister-president, it is up to parties to act continuously against this danger. Forum voor Democratie says it has expelled the members involved, but Jetten believes more is needed. "It really requires a more fundamental look at how you can root this out completely." The Zembla documentary showed that the neo-Nazi network organises cage fights. "Truly shocking images," Jetten said. "These are gatherings where all kinds of antisemitic and far-right statements are made." No thought police FVD, which initially reacted casually, says it has now removed six members from the party. Forum leader Lidewij de Vos said yesterday that she now wants to "return to the order of the day". She also said her party draws a line at violence, "but we are not going to play thought police". Premier Jetten stresses that far-right extremists are trying to gain "more and more" influence in politics, both nationally and locally. Security services also recently warned of this. "We really must put a stop to that, otherwise it is a threat to our democracy," Jetten says. Book burnings One of the FVD members involved is Ramon van Asch. He was faction chair on the Den Bosch municipal council. Van Asch was on the FVD list for last year's House of Representatives elections, was until recently an employee of the House faction, and was convicted of assault three times. The Zembla broadcast shows not only cage fights where the Hitler salute is frequently given. Books by Jewish writers are also burned. This is a reference to the 1930s, when the Nazis in Germany and Austria organised book burnings. The killing of politicians is also discussed. Images of the book burning: This broadcast is not the first to show a link between FVD and the far right; there is now a considerable list. For example, guests with racist and far-right views attended a Christmas party of FVD's youth organisation last year. Years earlier it emerged that antisemitic messages were sent within the JFVD. In the last municipal elections, candidates for FVD appeared on electoral lists who had previously also been active in far-right organisations. De Vos did not distance herself from them at the time. World domination Such ideas have been part of the party for years and are also promoted by Forum voor Democratie founder Thierry Baudet. In 2022, for example, he was rapped over the knuckles by the National Coordinator for Combating Antisemitism because he spread a classic antisemitic conspiracy theory about world domination by a Jewish elite. Nieuwsuur concluded this week that FVD often uses words in parliament with an extremist connotation. These include, for example, 'remigration' and 'replacement'. According to security services <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> and NCTV, far-right groups influence society with this kind of euphemistic language, in order to sound more acceptable. Tomorrow FVD holds a party congress in Den Bosch. One of the invited guests is Dries Van Langenhoven. This Belgian is the founder of the radical right movement Schild en Vrienden and was also a parliamentarian. Van Langenhoven has been convicted of incitement to hatred and racism and of unlawful possession of weapons. FVD currently holds seven seats in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> and three seats in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>.

title: Despite promise, not all care-villa children have a new place yet
lead: Sixteen sick and disabled children receiving care from Villa ExpertCare have not yet found a new suitable place. For some of them, another care organisation will not be found in time, writes <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">minister Sterk</entity> (Long-term Care) in a letter to parliament. Earlier this year Villa ExpertCare announced that it would close its last four care villas. According to the company, the payments for the care provided are not high enough. The doors will definitely close at the end of this year. The closure is causing unrest among families, because it is difficult for these children to find the right care elsewhere. Minister Sterk then promised in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that the specialist care villas would remain open "for as long as care for the children has not yet been properly arranged". Emergency scenario According to Sterk, Villa ExpertCare was to help the children find a new place. When that process proceeded with difficulty, the minister appointed an independent intermediary. Meanwhile 61 children have found a new care organisation. But for two to seven children it is very doubtful whether this will succeed before the end of the year. For them, in the most extreme case, "an emergency scenario" can be put into effect. That means that the children will, for example, receive care at home, or if need be be temporarily admitted to a hospital. What is Villa ExpertCare? In the premises of Villa ExpertCare, children who need medical care can live or stay. It concerns specialist care that cannot simply be arranged elsewhere. The care company announced earlier this year that it would close the last locations, in Waalre, Rijswijk, Vleuten and Wezep. Two locations (Waalre and Vleuten) are already closed: the <entity id="org:inspectie-gezondheidszorg-en-jeugd">Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd</entity> intervened there because of a "lack of quality and safety of care". Minister Sterk says she also intends to continue working next year to find a new place for the last group of children. She also wants to look at how repetition can be prevented in future. "The situation surrounding Villa ExpertCare has shown that the continuity and accessibility of medical child care is vulnerable," she writes in the letter to parliament.

title: Party for the Animals celebrates 20 years in the House of Representatives as a 'thorn in the side'
lead: The Party for the Animals today celebrated an anniversary in Nieuwegein: it is twenty years since the party, to the surprise of many, first won seats in the House of Representatives. "Since then the Party for the Animals has become indispensable", party leader <entity id="person:christine-teunissen">Christine Teunissen</entity> said in her congress speech. "We are the thorn in the side of those in power, and by now we are a lot more than that." The party sees its own bill, which must put an end to the factory farming industry, as one of its crown jewels. "It is the reason we entered the House of Representatives 20 years ago", Teunissen said. A vote must take place early next year. Thorn in the side That the animal party can be a thorn in the side became clear two weeks ago during the votes on the tax plan. Teunissen first said her party would vote against the law. Until it turned out that D66 and CDA needed the animal party to secure a majority 'on the left'. In exchange for, among other things, cheaper train tickets and alternatives to animal testing, the PvdD ultimately decided to vote in favour. Teunissen said she did not intend to lift a finger for the VVD, but at the same time expressed pride that "we were able to break the power politics of the VVD". According to her, it has shown "what is politically possible when the VVD is not at the controls for once". Aftermath of senators' conflict During the congress the aftermath of the conflict between the PvdD senators was still felt. That arose last year when Niko Koffeman, one of the co-founders of the Party for the Animals, terminated his membership. He disagreed with his party's support for higher defence spending. The <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> group then split into two camps: Niko Koffeman and Peter Nicolaï on one side and Ingrid Visseren-Hamakers on the other. Because Nicolaï continued together with Koffeman, he was expelled from the party. The two men kept the name 'Party for the Animals'. Visseren-Hamakers continued as a one-person group, with the support of the party board. She is now also the lead candidate for the upcoming elections. Later, an appeals committee ruled that Nicolaï's expulsion was unjustified. To Nicolaï's annoyance, the board had not made that ruling public until now. A PvdD member made an attempt during the congress to rehabilitate Nicolaï. But he did not gain enough members' support. The party board also said it wanted nothing to do with rehabilitation and apologies, as long as Nicolaï and Koffeman remain sitting together in one group. "But you are still very welcome to join me", Visseren-Hamakers called out to him. Teunissen temporarily away After this congress, Teunissen is temporarily leaving the House of Representatives in connection with her pregnancy and maternity leave. <entity id="person:ines-kostic">Ines Kostić</entity> is taking over her duties. Teunissen's seat will in the meantime be filled by Debbie Mathijsen.

title: Netherlands sends delegation to India to retrieve abducted Insiya
lead: The Netherlands will step up efforts to get back the girl Insiya, who was abducted ten years ago. This week a delegation from the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> and <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> will travel to India for talks. That is what <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> (Foreign Affairs) tells NOS. He is on a working visit to India and has spoken with his counterpart Jaishankar. "It is clear to India that this situation is not acceptable to us", says Berendsen. The Dutch officials will discuss in India what is legally possible. Contact restoration Insiya was abducted in September 2016, at the age of two, from <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> on the orders of her father Shehzad Hemani. She was taken to India with false papers and has lived with him ever since. Her mother Nadia Rashid has not seen her since the abduction. Hemani was sentenced in the Netherlands to 8.5 years in prison, but India refuses to extradite him. In India, child abductions are not recognised if the child is staying with one of the parents. The country is also not a party to the Hague Child Abduction Convention. "It would be wonderful if the delegation could take the first steps towards contact restoration. We really want to make progress on this file", says Berendsen. "On the Indian side this is also a legally extremely complex case", he says. According to him, Hemani's extradition request is a subject of discussion. Search blockade In recent weeks the Insiya case has been back in the news in a big way. Since late October, hundreds of articles from Dutch and international media have no longer been findable via Google in India, on the order of an Indian judge. Berendsen calls that ruling "incomprehensible". "But because it is a court ruling, it is also a complicated situation." According to the minister, the content of the articles is still available online in India, but access via search engines is restricted. Halsema video Yesterday <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> of Amsterdam shared a video message on social media, with which she is trying to get around that blockade. The video was recorded earlier in November during her trade mission to India. In it she calls on people to spread her message so that it eventually reaches Insiya. Berendsen says he understands Halsema's involvement. "I think it touches every parent when you see this. I think attention to the case can help."

title: Return of boss Huang after pressure from Trump costs Nvidia board face
lead: The return of Jensen Huang as boss at Nvidia instantly made the chipmaker worth 1000 billion dollars more. Investors seem to back the decision, but how can the company move on after what has happened in recent weeks? A brief summary: according to American intelligence services, the boss had an affair with a Chinese spy. Shortly afterwards it turned out he had more affairs and he had to leave the company. The Nvidia board of directors said: "His resignation has been unanimously accepted and we do not intend to reappoint Jensen as CEO." Today, less than a week later, the picture has turned 180 degrees: "The board of directors believes that Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia." The choice to bring him back appears to be mainly the result of pressure from the White House. The American president told broadcaster CNBC: " I made the deal ", referring to Huang's return. On his return to the office the boss is cheered by hundreds of people. Nvidia founder Huang, who donated 25 million dollars towards the construction of Trump's ballroom, was at the cradle of one of America's most important companies in the AI revolution. That is a sector responsible for record levels on the stock market and to which an estimated 40 per cent of economic growth can be attributed. Trump regards the loss of Huang as a greater threat to America than his reappointment. The president seems to think: we get more out of Huang inside Nvidia than outside it. In the short term, besides Trump, investors are also delighted with Huang's return, but many questions remain unanswered. In Congress, tough questions are being asked. Was it purely about the money for Trump, the share price, or the importance of this company to the economy? Was it too big to fail, like the banks during the credit crisis, or did Huang know too much and is he therefore easier to tame this way? Members of Congress are seeking answers, particularly about American export restrictions. How could Chinese companies gain access to Nvidia's technology and use data centres in Malaysia and Indonesia, among other places, built by Jensen Huang's mistress? They may get answers when Huang comes to Congress next month, where he is expected for a closed-door briefing. Board bypassed The board of directors is being bypassed by Trump's decision, says Annemieke Roobeek, emeritus professor of strategy and transformation management at Nyenrode Business Universiteit. "It is therefore a question of how many people from the board will leave once the rules of 'good governance' no longer apply. If people leave, more political appointments will be made to replace them", says Roobeek. These people will have to concern themselves more with the changed geopolitical climate and national security. To guarantee national security, the company says a committee has been set up with independent directors. "But what is independent in Trump's America, Big Tech and shareholders on the Nasdaq?", Roobeek asks. Shares in the plus Investors are reacting positively. According to market analyst Reinder Wietsma of IBS, Trump's support immediately removes major risks for investors. In addition, they see Huang as indispensable to the company. Every year Nvidia came out with better chips. "Investors feared that the speed at which they are developed would decline without him", says Wietsma. That also partly explains why share prices of other tech companies are rising too. "Nvidia is also called the central bank of AI", says Wietsma. Many companies in the industry benefit from the availability of those ever-better computer chips. Wietsma does qualify the price fluctuations. "Stock prices have become much more turbulent in recent years." According to him, share prices react more violently than is justified by a company's financial position. Wietsma says this is because a large part of trading is now done by private investors. They do less often research whether a company is financially sound. You can clearly see that in the share price of ASML over the past week, says Wietsma. "The share price has gone up and down very sharply, while nothing has changed in ASML's order book", says Wietsma. "That is still full for a long time."

title: Failed climate summit makes environmental students more militant: 'Motivation to continue'
lead:
Environmental law lecturer Esther de Jong completely overhauled her lesson last night, she says the day after the failed climate summit. For most people something like this is demotivating, but that is not the case for her students, they say. "The fiery speech the Panamanian environment minister gave earlier during the summit really got to me", says the university of applied sciences lecturer. The minister spoke about the negative consequences of climate change for the Central American country and the role the oil industry plays in it. "I had to show them that", says De Jong. The more than 190 participating countries ultimately failed to reach agreement in the Turkish city of Antalya. Environmental studies lecturer De Jong makes a new attempt a day later in the classroom, where students reenact the climate summit. "You represent the islands of the Pacific Ocean", she assigns five students. They are given the task of writing the arguments of those countries on a large sheet of paper. Others take on Panama, China, the European Union and the oil-exporting countries (OPEC).

Outcome of the climate summit demotivating. That the summit has, in the words of EU climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra, "evidently failed", usually does not bode well for people's motivation, research shows. That is what climate behavioural scientist Reint Jan Renes of the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences says. "Research shows that we want to act, but then we also need to feel that the big parties such as industry and politics, whom we really need, are doing so too. If big parties decide not to act, then the value of my individual action also goes down, is the thinking." The environmental studies students of HAS Green Academy in Den Bosch do not suffer much from this. "I would very much like to live in a liveable world, and this gives me motivation to keep going with my studies", says one of them. "Because if I don't carry on, then nothing at all will happen." The failure of the climate summit does not, incidentally, mean that people stop their own actions, but that they do not do more, says Renes. "It is a collective issue. You can act yourself, but you simply need other people to also have a real effect." At lectures and classes Renes has already noticed recently that the attitude of students and others has changed. "If the prime minister does not go to the summit because of the fuss in The Hague and a minister postpones going, then those are political signals communicating that other things are more important." 'Still need to read up' The group in the Den Bosch class that represents the interests of China does not immediately have the country's arguments at hand. "We still need to read up a bit", a student admits with a laugh. De Jong walks through the classroom and checks whether the students are on the right track. "One of the agreements at the summit in Paris was that rich countries would financially help poor countries with subsidies", she helps a group recall an agreement from the climate accord concluded earlier. The students write a new argument on their paper. Then it is time for the presentations. "If nothing happens then there will only be more extreme weather", a student says on behalf of the Pacific islands. "We as small countries are not the cause of climate change, but we are the ones left with the problems." 'Will we reach agreement after all?' "OPEC countries, you have been able to sleep on it for a night in your little place in Dubai. How do you look back on it?", De Jong invites the next group. "We already give quite a lot of money to poorer countries", says a student. "And we think you should also look at developments such as storing CO2 in the soil." When everyone has had a turn, it is time to take stock. "Will we, a day later, finally reach agreement?", asks De Jong. "They need to listen carefully to other countries", someone tries. "I think they should send the money to the places that are hit hardest", says another. Esther de Jong looks on contentedly at her students, even though they too ultimately fail to reach an agreement. The arguments of the different countries also turn out to be too far apart here.

title: Russian embassy in The Hague asks for clarification on involvement of Destinus staff
lead: The Russian embassy in The Hague has taken an official complaint to the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> about the defence company Destinus, which is based in the Netherlands. The embassy has asked for clarification about "the possible involvement of staff of the company Destinus, based in Hengelo, in the attacks on the Russian Federation", the embassy announced on X. Last week the arms manufacturer made the news after the company itself reported that Ukraine had used its missiles and drones in the large attack on the Crimean Bridge. That bridge connects Russia with the Crimean peninsula, which Russia occupies. On that reporting the embassy wrote that "Moscow has been informed of the Dutch involvement" and that "the confession has been noted". 'Hunting Russian drones' Two days later NRC also published about the company. Destinus employees reportedly hunted Russian drones in Ukraine themselves. They also helped shoot down attack drones over Russia. This involvement could be the case. A civilian who directly takes part in hostilities loses the protection that international humanitarian law offers civilians. They also thereby become a possible target. Dutch embassy in Kyiv On that same day the Dutch embassy in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv was damaged by the impact of a projectile just behind the building. Foreign Minister Berendsen then summoned the Russian ambassador. "We should have no illusions about where this projectile came from", the minister said at the time. Later Russia made threatening remarks towards Dutch diplomats in Ukraine, which placed the impact in a new light. In doing so it strengthened the impression that the Dutch embassy had been deliberately targeted. Meanwhile, nothing has actually been established about the cause of the impact or whether it was deliberately caused or the result of a drone that went off course.

title: Three injured, including a baby, in drone attack on Colombian police base
lead: Drones carrying explosives hit a police base in the city of Cúcuta in northern Colombia. Three people, including a baby, were injured in the attack. Sixty homes were damaged. It is unclear who is behind the attack. In the area near the border with Venezuela, where the city lies, several armed groups are fighting each other. It is suspected that this attack too is an example of violence between two armed gangs, and that the drones were shot down by one of the two groups. According to a local official, these gangs are fighting each other over illegal trade, possibly in drugs. The area is rich in fields of coca plants, from which cocaine is made. Colombia is the world's largest cocaine producer and is plagued by drug cartels. In recent years, armed gangs have increasingly used cheap consumer drones, which they load with explosives and use against the government. The New York Times writes that the number of drone attacks in 2025 has more than quadrupled. War on drugs Because of the violence, thousands of people have been displaced. The far-right president Abelardo de la Espriella, who was sworn in in September, wants to end the drug cartels and other armed groups in the country. During the campaign he promised a tough approach to drug cartels, and on taking office he said criminal gangs have two choices: surrender to authority or face the country's security forces. Since mid-October De la Espriella has received support from the US, which, after countless attacks on alleged drug boats, expanded the 'war on drugs' to Latin American countries such as Panama, Honduras and also Colombia. Hundreds of soldiers have been sent to these countries for joint exercises, and the Americans will provide support and advice to teams carrying out operations against drug traffickers.

title: NATO sends radar aircraft to Poland after remains of Russian missiles are found
lead: NATO is sending a special radar aircraft to Poland because of the Russian violations of Polish airspace last week . According to the Polish public prosecutor, the remains of three Russian cruise missiles, which were due to have landed there on Friday, have been found in the east of the country. "This was a dangerous incident and Russia bears full responsibility", says a NATO spokesperson today. The decision to send a so-called Awacs aircraft was taken after consultation within the military alliance. Further measures are not ruled out. In Geilenkirchen in Germany, close to the border with Limburg, NATO has fourteen Awacs aircraft stationed. These Boeing aircraft have a large radar dome on top. Airborne Awacs can detect enemy activity many hundreds of kilometres away and are therefore suited to spotting attacks early. 'Deliberate provocation' The ambassadors of the 32 NATO countries met for an extraordinary meeting about the latest violations of Polish airspace. The Polish government, which called the impact of three Russian cruise missiles a deliberate provocation, briefed them at the headquarters in Brussels. The Kremlin has not responded to the accusation from Poland. Based on preliminary investigation results, the Polish prosecutor reported yesterday that three Russian missiles of the Kh-101 type had been found. Russia uses these cruise missiles almost daily to bomb Ukraine. Missile strikes are rare It regularly happens that Russian combat drones end up in Poland or other eastern NATO countries. Dutch F-35s, among others, were deployed last year to shoot down these unmanned aircraft. Missile strikes are however much rarer and carry a greater risk of escalation because of their destructive power. The Russian violations of Polish airspace last week increase concerns that NATO will be drawn into the war between Ukraine and Russia. According to Article 5 of the NATO treaty, an attack on one member state is considered an attack on all member states. Earlier missile strikes in Poland Last summer a missile also struck eastern Poland. According to the Polish government this was also probably a Russian Kh-101 missile. Nobody was injured at the time, as was also the case with last week's strikes. In the first year of the large-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine, two Polish farmers were killed by a missile strike. This appears to have been a Ukrainian air defence missile that was trying to fend off a Russian attack.

title: Investigation team seeks witnesses to 1986 Suriname mass murder via Opsporing Verzocht
lead: Nearly 40 years after the mass murder in the Surinamese village of Moiwana, Dutch police investigators are looking for witnesses. Last night, on the programme Opsporing Verzocht, they called on people who know more about the massacre to come forward. The killings took place during the Interior War (1986-1992), when a fight was waged between the National Army, led by Desi Bouterse, and his opponent and former bodyguard Ronnie Brunswijk, then leader of the Jungle Commando. In 1986 soldiers carried out a massacre in the village: 39 innocent civilians were shot dead, mainly women but also children, including babies, and elderly people. The official account was that Brunswijk had entrenched himself in the village while the Surinamese army was searching for him. According to survivors, Brunswijk was not in the village and the army began shooting immediately. The investigation into the tragedy stalled when in 1990 <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> inspector Herman Gooding, who led the case, was shot dead. Compensation For years nothing happened until relatives went to the Inter-American Court of Human Rights in Costa Rica. In 2005 the Court convicted the state of Suriname and ordered the country to track down and prosecute the perpetrators. Suriname also had to compensate the relatives with damages, offer apologies and invest in the reconstruction of Moiwana. Although President Ronald Venetiaan offered apologies in 2006, no further prosecution followed at that time. During the subsequent term in office of former president Desi Bouterse (2010-2020) there was little political will to investigate the soldiers who formally served under his command. The Surinamese <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> started a new investigation into the murders in 2023, and since late last year a judicial preliminary inquiry has been under way. The Dutch police investigation team is assisting with this, at Suriname's request. With the investigation, the Surinamese Public Prosecution Service hopes to map out who was involved and what their exact role was. A hundred people According to the investigators there were presumably around a hundred people at the massacre: soldiers, but also indigenous civilians who may themselves have fought. The investigation team hopes to hear from mainly former soldiers of the government army or other witnesses about who was involved. Witnesses may also be found in the Netherlands, which has a large Surinamese community, the investigation team thinks. During the Interior War many Surinamese fled to neighbouring French Guiana, but also to the Netherlands. This coming weekend it will be forty years since the tragedy took place. Every year there is a commemoration in memory of the Moiwana massacre, around the monument made by artist Marcel Pinas, himself from the area.

title: Gisèle Pelicot takes action against publisher that distributed nude photos
lead: Gisèle Pelicot is going to take action against a publisher that, without her consent, sent nude photos and video footage made by her ex-husband to several media outlets. The small publisher Éditions Tinbad released in a limited print run a book by psychoanalyst Sabine Prokhoris, one part of which is devoted to the Pelicot case. In her essay, which forms part of the book, the Frenchwoman is, according to the French weekly Le Canard enchaîné, "portrayed as an 'exhibitionist' who misled the justice system and the media". The weekly was the first to write about the images and video recordings that were sent to news media for promotion, last Thursday. Criminal case file Pelicot announced yesterday that she would take legal steps against the publisher, reports Le Parisien among others. Not only because of the leaked videos and photos, but also because of the content of the book. "I am deeply shocked that images of my most private life are displayed and used for commercial purposes", says Pelicot. "Today I feel humiliated, watched and hurt again. As if the ordeal of the trial was not enough." Nude photos According to the publisher there was "an unfortunate communication error". Tinbad further states that "no images of rape or pornographic videos" were sent to the press. However, according to Le Monde the publisher does not deny that nude images were distributed. Pelicot says she is appalled by the book, which "describes scenes of rape in which I was involved and gives an unbearable interpretation of my life". And, she continues, "above all I refuse to have my story rewritten by suggesting that I was complicit in what I went through". Out of anonymity Pelicot's ex-husband drugged and raped her for nearly ten years and also had other men rape her while she was unconscious. She came out of anonymity because she did not want the trial of her ex-husband and the other perpetrators to take place behind closed doors. She stressed that it is not she but the perpetrators who should be ashamed. In the case Pelicot's ex-husband was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment. The other fifty men were sentenced to prison terms ranging from 3 to 15 years. Last year Pelicot received her country's most important honour.

title: With Hortence Sarmaat (84), Curaçao loses another music icon within a week
lead: A few days after the death of Curaçaoan composer and singer Rudy Plaate, singer Hortence Sarmaat has also died. She was 84 years old. In the 1950s Sarmaat grew into one of the most popular singers of Curaçao. She performed various compositions by Plaate and also made the island's music known in the Netherlands. "Rudy has not even been buried yet", says Percy Pinedo, who at the time discovered Sarmaat at the Curaçaoan radio station Radio Hoyer. One of Plaate's first compositions, Felicidad , he gave to Sarmaat to record, because he found his own voice too hoarse. It became one of her best-known songs. Listen to the song: Pinedo knew the Sarmaat family from his own neighbourhood. Hortence began singing around the age of twelve, together with two sisters and accompanied by her brothers. She had never had singing lessons. In 1955 she was discovered during a talent programme of Radio Hoyer. "She was one of those who came to sing and immediately stood out", says Pinedo. "The radio station had a glass front back then. The artists stood inside singing behind the glass, and the people stood on the pavement watching. It was a kind of public Curaçaoan stage." Plaate also performed there, as did the Cuban singer Celia Cruz, Pinedo says. Radio Hoyer gave local musicians the chance to reach a large audience with songs in their own language, Papiamentu. At sixteen Sarmaat already had a big hit with Reduta , a song about gossip and backbiting. Her father came from Suriname, but she herself was born on Curaçao. Besides Papiamentu she also sang in Spanish, Dutch and Sranantongo. Before she moved to the Netherlands, she had, by her own account, made eleven records, recorded on Curaçao and pressed in the United States. Spanish in the Netherlands Despite her popularity, Sarmaat chose a different career. She was offered the chance to perform in the United States, but when a long-awaited study grant was awarded to her, she chose the Netherlands. In September 1962 she began a Spanish degree at the University of Amsterdam. "I regard singing as my hobby", she told the Dutch press four years later. In the Netherlands she remained active for Radio Hoyer. Together with other Antilleans she made radio programmes in which students and migrant workers described how things were going for them in the Netherlands. In this way they stayed in contact with their families on the islands. Music show She also performed on Dutch television. In September 1966 she took part in Friejarie Hoso , a music show by the KRO to mark the first anniversary of Surinamese television. With the Surinamese musician Alberto Gemerts she made the long-playing record Musical Meeting , on which Surinamese and Antillean music came together. In 2024 the album was re-released digitally. Curaçao now loses two icons from one musical generation within a few days: Plaate as composer and musician, and Sarmaat as the voice that made several of his early compositions famous. "Within a week they have both died. That cannot be a coincidence, very special", says Pinedo.

title: Dogs may resemble their owners, but they don't always suit them
lead: It is often said: dogs look like their owners, but often those dogs turn out not to suit those owners at all, with all the consequences that entails. Today a campaign therefore starts to get people to choose a particular dog breed more consciously. Research has shown that many Dutch people take a dog that does not suit their situation well. For example, dogs that need a lot of space end up in flats, dogs that need lots of walks go to owners who have no time for that, and dogs that are watchful and bark a lot end up with families with small children. A Life Together Such a poor match can lead to dogs showing 'difficult' behaviour, being 'got rid of' and ending up in a shelter. "A dog is not an impulse purchase, but a friend for life," says <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity>. He points out that people are also often unaware of the costs that come with a dog. "That is why it is important to think carefully beforehand about whether you can offer a dog the home situation it deserves." The campaign looks like a kind of dating app for dogs: Erkens himself has had a dog his whole life and so does not want to deter people with this campaign. "But you need to know what you're getting into." In the Netherlands there are between 1.5 and 2 million dogs and about 16 percent of households have one or more in the home. Each year nearly 160,000 new dogs are estimated to be acquired. Marktplaats and social media It is not known how often it proves not to be a good match and how many dogs end up in a shelter for that reason, but according to the ministry the problem is large enough for a campaign. "The trigger is the call from animal welfare organisations, veterinarians and politicians," a spokesperson says. The campaign will be visible from today in places where people look into getting a dog, such as Marktplaats and social media.

title: Morning briefing 24/11: Prosecution demands against Tarwekamp suspects • PSV and Feyenoord in European action
lead: Good morning! In The Hague the prosecution's sentencing demand against the four suspects in the fatal explosion on Tarwekamp will be announced today. Also tonight PSV and Feyenoord are in action in the Champions League. First the weather: It is cold and today it will be sunny in many places. Locally it may be misty. It will be 3 to 6 degrees. The days after that remain cold with 1 to 4 degrees during the day and lots of sun, and frost at night. The forecast for the coming days can be seen in this video: Are you going out today? Here you'll find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? A Dutch delegation hopes this week in India to make progress not only on the return of the abducted Insiya, but also on cases of other children. That is confirmed by the Dutch <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> to Nieuwsuur . According to the ministry, several requests have been submitted to bring children back from India to the Netherlands. How many children are involved and whether in all cases it concerns an abduction is unclear. Other news from the night: And then also this: For 167 years mathematicians have racked their brains over it: proving the Riemann hypothesis. With the help of AI that has now been solved. It is leading to astonishment and enthusiasm among mathematicians around the world, but there is also criticism. Have a nice day!

title: Space probe BepiColombo had problems on arrival at Mercury
lead: The European-Japanese space probe BepiColombo, which arrived at the planet Mercury on Saturday, appears to have had problems on arrival. The spacecraft unexpectedly went into standby, but it is now flying safely in a stable orbit around the planet, says the European Space Agency ESA. Last weekend the probe went into hibernation just after arrival, in which all non-essential components of the craft were switched off. Research by ESA shows this was caused by a software error. Hibernation mode is intended to prevent damage should a problem arise. Because of the software error the probe slowed down earlier than planned. As a result it threatened not to enter the ideal orbit, but in the end the probe's course could be corrected. Even if the space probe threatens to leave its orbit in the coming time, the craft can be corrected. Influence of the sun Astronomers want to learn more from the mission about the formation of our solar system. Scientists are also curious about the influence of the sun's heat on the magnetic field and surface of Mercury. What will BepiColombo investigate? The planetary explorer must find answers on Mercury to riddles left over after the missions of NASA probes Mariner 10 and Messenger. Those showed that the brownish-grey ball is geologically much more interesting than thought. Messenger found, for example, deposits in shadowy craters that may consist of water ice. That astonished astronomers. They had not even expected water on a planet so close to the sun. BepiColombo has instruments that can check whether there really is ice in those craters. The European-Japanese mission must also solve another riddle: what are the mysterious cavities on the surface of Mercury that Messenger discovered in 2013? They may have been caused by escaped gases from the ground, but that is a theory. If BepiColombo sees the cavities change, that would be evidence that Mercury is still geologically active. The eight-year journey to Mercury did not go smoothly. In 2024 a problem arose with thrusters that determine the spacecraft's course. These could no longer work at full power, so the journey was delayed by eleven months. Although Mercury is relatively close to Earth, it is still difficult to reach the planet. This is due to the gravity of other planets and the sun. A complicated route was needed of multiple orbits around the sun, via Venus, Earth and Mercury itself, to arrive at exactly the right speed at the right place. Probe splits in two In two weeks BepiColombo will split into a European part (MPO) and a Japanese part. The European MPO comes relatively close to Mercury, to about 480 kilometres, and has an orbit over the poles as its destination. The Japanese part would end up in a much higher orbit. The Japanese and European parts will work together from their different orbits.

title: Study: HPV vaccine could prevent 13,000 cancer diagnoses
lead: The new HPV vaccination could in the future prevent cancer in an estimated nearly 13,000 people. That emerges from research by the Netherlands Comprehensive Cancer Organisation (IKNL) and Erasmus MC. Researchers calculated that the benefit can be achieved among children who are currently between 0 and 9 years old. They can receive two jabs in the year they turn 10, which can prevent cancer diagnoses at a later age. This only applies if the current vaccination rate is maintained. HPV is very common in the Netherlands: over 80 per cent of people are at some point infected. Often people catch it as young adults, usually through sex. In many cases the virus disappears from the body by itself, but sometimes it lingers for a long time, so that cancer can develop. Not only women The most common form caused by HPV is cervical cancer. The new vaccinations available since September also protect against various other types, such as cancer of the penis, anus, vagina, vulva, oral cavity and throat. Vaccination therefore protects not only girls but also boys, IKNL stresses. The old vaccination protected only against two types of HPV. In the Netherlands the HPV vaccination rate is lower than in various countries around us. At 61 per cent, the Netherlands also scores below the European average. The World Health Organization WHO advises that 90 per cent of girls be vaccinated. According to cancer centre IKNL, the low vaccination rate is partly due to persistent misconceptions among parents. They doubt the safety, necessity and impact of the vaccine. Precisely to emphasise the impact, IKNL and Erasmus MC conducted this research. Regret for not vaccinating Gynaecologist-oncologist Luc van Lonkhuijzen of Amsterdam UMC contributed to the research. He hopes the results will persuade parents. "You see that many parents still make the decision not to do it. I think that is unwise. I see the misery in my consulting room of the women who then, for example, still develop cervical cancer. And sometimes the grief of those mothers too: should I not have had my child vaccinated after all?" Van Lonkhuijzen says he has also put that question to mothers and children. "Some say: nobody in the class did it. Or mothers say they did not see the benefit or that they were afraid of possible side effects. We have been vaccinating for fifteen years now and the number of side effects we see is really very limited." Each year an estimated 1100 women and 400 men get cancer as a result of HPV. Each year around 900 people in the Netherlands are diagnosed with cervical cancer. The disease mainly affects women between 30 and 45 years old.

title: Natural ice rinks open: marathon skater smashes world hour record
lead: At least three natural ice rinks in the country can be skated on this morning. Among others in De Lier, Doorn and Winterswijk, the skating fun can begin. In De Lier the ice masters of ice club Hard Gaat-ie worked all night to get a layer of ice on the track, reports Omroep West. At 08.30 the ice rink opened. "We made it," the Doornsche IJsclub enthusiastically reports on Facebook. According to the club there is "a fine ice surface for a morning of skating fun". On the natural ice track of the Winterswijk ice club, rounds could already be skated earlier this month and yesterday. Judith Krabbenborg This morning marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg had the track in Winterswijk to herself to break the women's world hour record on natural ice. That succeeded: in one hour she covered 34 kilometres and 878 metres. With that she smashed the old record by over 2 kilometres. The natural ice track then opened to other skaters. The ice rinks remain open as long as the weather allows. How long that will be is uncertain. This afternoon it will be 3 to 5 degrees and sunny everywhere. The expectation is that skating on natural ice can also continue in the coming days; it stays dry and cold this week, and at night it freezes lightly to moderately.

title: No evidence of psychiatric disorder for suspect in murder of Lisa
lead: Experts cannot establish a psychiatric disorder in the suspect in the murder of 17-year-old Lisa from Abcoude. That emerged today at the fifth preliminary hearing at the Amsterdam district court. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had instructed the Pieter Baan Centrum to investigate this. The suspect, who calls himself Chris Jude, has said that he had voices in his head that incited him to a rape, an attempt at it and the murder of Lisa. Earlier he said he could not remember anything about the murder. He has now admitted it . Jude's lawyer thinks it goes too far to rule out a disorder and says that experts simply did not succeed in establishing one. Extended investigation: The conclusion of the Pieter Baan Centrum is based on weeks of observation of Jude. The investigation lasted twice as long as usual. His lawyer says the investigation was limited, because it focused on observations, while little is still known about Jude's background. It is now certain that Jude has Nigerian nationality and stayed at an asylum centre in Amsterdam Southeast. He knows who his family is and also keeps in contact with them. Consequences for the criminal trial: The conclusion of the investigators may have major consequences for the criminal trial. Suspects with a disorder are assessed differently from people without one. An established disorder can lead to lighter sentences, something Jude therefore need not count on now. Jude himself was also present in the courtroom this time. He was given the chance to respond to the conclusion, but seemed surprised that he was allowed to say something. Jude had nothing to add and remained silent. The 17-year-old Lisa from Abcoude was found on 20 August last year by officers in the verge of a through road in Duivendrecht. After an evening out, she had been cycling home to her parental home in Abcoude. She felt threatened on the way and had managed to call 112, but when officers reached her they were too late; she had already died. Rape: Last year another woman also fell victim to Jude. In the night of 14 to 15 August she was taking a walk along the water of the Weesperzijde in Amsterdam, when Jude addressed her. He grabbed her, dragged her along and raped her. He has admitted that too.

title: Industry also introduces deposit scheme for large juice and milk bottles
lead: The industry association for the packaging sector will, during the course of next year, begin introducing a deposit system for plastic juice and dairy bottles of up to three litres. These bottles currently fall outside the deposit scheme introduced in 2021 for smaller plastic bottles. The industry association Verpact is thereby meeting the demand of minister Van Veldhoven of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kgg">Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity>, who wants 90 per cent of all plastic bottles on the market to be collectable by 1 January 2028. Van Veldhoven wants this to be arranged by 1 January 2028, and it is only feasible if a deposit scheme for juice and dairy bottles also comes in. "To enable a careful introduction by that date, Verpact is preparing a phased rollout in 2027 together with all the parties involved", Verpact says on its website. Adjustment of collection equipment To make the scheme a success, adjustments will have to be made. This concerns labels, collection equipment, IT systems and logistical processes, Verpact says. The EU requires producers to collect 90 per cent of all plastic bottles and cans by 2029.
