title: Politicians attacked in Germany, pepper spray in office of local Greens
lead: Once again, local politicians have been attacked in Germany. Last night a faction meeting of the Greens in Schwerte, near Dortmund, was violently disrupted. And this weekend a politician from the liberal FDP was attacked in Berlin. According to the regional broadcaster WDR, a masked person broke into a party office of the Greens last night. A faction meeting with ten people was taking place there at the time. The suspect reportedly sprayed pepper spray and hit someone. According to the WDR, three injured people were taken to hospital. The police in Dortmund say they are investigating a possible politically motivated offence. The suspect got away. A search for this person is still under way. Officers found a fire extinguisher on the spot. It is not yet clear whether it was used as a weapon. A sticker reading 'Better dead than red' had been stuck on the party office. According to the WDR, the sticker comes from the webshop of a well-known neo-Nazi. The police are investigating whether the sticker has anything to do with the attack. Attack at pro-Palestinian demonstration The attack in Berlin took place on Sunday. The police say that two women pushed and kicked the local FDP politician Karoline Preisler. This happened on the sidelines of a pro-Palestinian demonstration in the capital. The 55-year-old Preisler told the newspaper Jüdische Allgemeine that she was kicked in the stomach and was treated in hospital after the attack. One of the attackers, a 25-year-old woman, has been arrested. Preisler often stands on the sidelines of pro-Palestinian demonstrations. This time, according to the German TV news programme Tagesschau, she had a sign that read: "Rape is not resistance." With this she referred to the atrocities committed by Hamas militants during the terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. Increasing incidents The attitude towards politicians in Germany has hardened in recent years. The latest figures show that there was a considerable increase in incidents against politicians and party staff last year. There were 5140 offences, compared with 3690 in 2024, the police reported in May. Often these involve defamation and insults, but also violent incidents. Last year the AfD and the CDU were most often targeted. In the years before, members of the Greens were most frequently targeted.

title: How Nvidia boss Huang returned (and Trump is benefiting from it)
lead: That Jensen Huang has returned as head of chipmaker Nvidia came as a surprise even to the company's most senior executives. Less than two weeks ago he had to step down because of various affairs, including a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. According to several investigations, he also maintained a culture of fear in the workplace, yet he is back. And this is what his return at the Nvidia office looked like: More details are now emerging about how this could happen. For example, allies of Huang have set up a so-called "war room", reports the financial newspaper FT. They include Uber founder Travis Kalanick and John Underwood, an executive at Goldman Sachs. They took immediate action and argued for the top executive's return, both in public and behind closed doors. Publicly, Huang also received support from fellow tech bosses. "Great men make great mistakes, but nobody has ever been like that, not Elon Musk, nobody. All the success we are enjoying now, all the technological progress, is down to one man", said one of Huang's allies. Pressure from Trump on the board That President Trump felt the same way was already known. For example, he wrote on his social media platform Truth Social that Jensen Huang is indispensable and important for the health of the American AI sector, the stock market and the overall economy. It now also becomes clear that he personally exerted pressure on the board of directors. Trump spoke by phone to Nvidia's board members over the weekend, various media report. That the lines between the White House and Huang are short is said to be evident from a three-quarter-hour phone call with Vice President Vance. After Huang's reinstatement, the value of Nvidia shares rose. The company was suddenly worth 1,000 billion dollars more. Trump is also benefiting from this, the Financial Times reports. According to the newspaper, the American president held 370,000 Nvidia shares on 30 September. With Huang's reappointment, those shares became 15 million dollars more valuable. Whereas less than a week ago the board did not consider the return of the top executive, this is now a sudden about-turn. This will probably have consequences in the longer term, believes Annemieke Roobeek, emeritus professor in public administration. Internal espionage "It is interesting to see how a control freak like Jensen Huang moves within his own company. In that controlling he has failed, because he himself has become out of control", says Roobeek. The emeritus professor expects that over time a number of people from the board and other staff members will leave. "Such a powerful and important company, which builds these unique superchips, many other parties are also interested in that." That is why Roobeek would not be surprised if the internal espionage is much bigger than just the affair with the possible Chinese spy. Roobeek thinks American intelligence services will start looking over Huang's shoulder. In any case, Nvidia and Huang still face investigations. The FBI is examining whether there is espionage. The SEC, the American regulator of listed companies, is investigating the accounts. And on 3 December Huang himself must appear for a public hearing before the American Congress, about the export of chips.

title: Search for loose lion in Istanbul called off, no evidence found
lead: The Turkish authorities say they have "no concrete evidence" that the loose lioness that caused panic in Istanbul exists. On Sunday evening a large-scale search was launched to capture the predator. The authorities scanned a wooded area just north of the city with a drone fitted with thermal cameras. The animal was said to be roaming there. Bait was placed, as well as camera traps with motion sensors. The Turkish police wanted to capture the predator alive, but after a new assessment it was established that the animal in the footage is "not a lion or another large feline". The authorities told Turkish media as much. What kind of animal it is, is not clear. Still checks According to Turkish media, a resident of the Uskumruköy district, in the north of Istanbul, saw the animal wandering on Sunday and immediately alerted the police. Afterwards an animal resembling a lion was reportedly spotted on camera footage in an adjacent district. Thermal cameras reportedly also located the animal's hiding place. Residents were advised to stay indoors and the Belgrade Forest, an area of 54 square kilometres, was cordoned off. A team of specialists supported the police in the search, but according to them there is now no danger. The authorities say they will still carry out the necessary checks to ensure residents' safety. A team also stands ready to reassess the situation should new information come in.

title: More than 100 wrongful traffic fines in Zaanstad due to technical fault
lead: More than a hundred motorists were wrongly fined in Zaandam for driving over a bus bridge. They received a fine of 139 euros in the post, although the bridge was in fact open to motorists at that time. It concerns the bus bridge between Zaandam and Koog aan de Zaan. It connects the Westerwatering and Westerkoog districts, but is closed during rush hours so that no rat-running traffic arises towards the A8 motorway. At weekends and on public holidays the bridge can be used all day. Drivers who use the bridge during rush hour are fined, but 107 people who drove over the bridge on Sunday 25 October also received a fine. Technical fault According to the municipality, the fines were issued due to a technical fault. The system used for enforcement had glitches. "For those who received a wrongful fine this is of course annoying," says the spokesperson for mayor <entity id="person:jan-hamming">Jan Hamming</entity> of Zaanstad to regional broadcaster NH. Of the 107 fines, 79 have now been dismissed. They therefore do not need to be paid. The handling of the remaining 28 fines is still in progress. For this the municipality has contacted the Parket CVOM (Centrale Verwerking <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>) and the <entity id="org:centraal-justitieel-incassobureau">CJIB</entity> (Centraal Justitieel Incassobureau). The municipality did not receive any report of the fault at the time, so the incident remained unknown. According to the spokesperson, the municipality is investigating how to prevent this in future and to ensure Zaandam is informed more quickly should a fault occur again. Much to-do about the bridge. The bridge has for decades been a hot potato in the municipality. The municipality of Zaanstad would like to see the bridge open to car traffic 24 hours a day, but the process has been delayed due to national nitrogen rules. Many local residents are in favour of full opening, but there are also residents who are strongly opposed, as they fear a lot of rat-running traffic in the Westerkoog district.

title: Podcast De Dag: three mathematicians on the 'AI genius'
lead: In recent months, various AI models have solved a few of the biggest problems in mathematics. This weekend, what some call the 'holy grail' was added, the so-called Riemann hypothesis. You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Don't forget to subscribe. Mathematicians are responding to AI with a mix of hope and fear. Because if you use it cleverly, it can bring great progress (such as curing cancer or solving the climate problem), but also: why would you as a mathematician still get to work if AI can solve everything? And what is lost if the human mathematician fades into the background? In the podcast, three mathematicians, Clara Stegehuis (associate professor of Mathematics at the University of Twente), Gunther Cornelissen (professor of mathematics at Utrecht University) and mathematics student Lars Pos, talk about Riemann, about their love for the subject, their view on AI, on the future of mathematics and their role in it. Responses? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial team: Wouter Sloekers Final editing: Rosanne Sies

lead: For the CDA, the proposal by PRO and Volt to levy more tax on large fortunes and dividends goes too far, but <entity id="person:inge-van-dijk">Inge van Dijk</entity> cannot yet say whether her party can support the plan or will vote against it.

title: KNMI gaat vanaf maandag over op regiospecifieke weerwaarschuwingen
lead: Vanaf maandag zal het Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut (KNMI) niet langer één kleurgecodeerde waarschuwing toekennen aan een hele provincie.

title: Police on mistaken-identity murder of Jaison: 'Perpetrator changed clothes and returned to busy Tiendplein'
lead: Four years after the mistaken-identity murder of Jaison (30), the police have new information about the shooter. The hope is that this will finally lead to a breakthrough in the investigation into the shooting in the back of the Rotterdam resident on the busy Tiendplein. The perpetrator reportedly changed clothes and then returned to the scene of the crime.

title: Former AIVD officer Eric Schouten on hack of refrigeration systems: 'It is about weakening the enemy'
lead: Hackers have succeeded again. In several countries, including the Netherlands, shop refrigeration systems have been turned up. In some cases even to 70 degrees Celsius. Why is that cooling so interesting? And to whom? Former AIVD officer and espionage expert Eric Schouten answered those questions on <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> Met het Oog op Morgen.

title: Haagse Zaken | A cabinet collapse in slow motion?
lead: There is still a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>, and after a spectacular denouement the Tax Plan was also passed on Thursday after months of negotiation, but without the support of the VVD.

title: The animals once again remained invisible
lead: At a conference on 'DierMens Studies' – this is how the organiser spells it – I was supposed to read out a column.

title: Little known about the future of the cabinet, but here is what we do know
lead: Today the leaders of D66, VVD and CDA will continue talks at the Catshuis from 11.00 a.m. The future of the cabinet is still at stake after a row over the Tax Plan. Their lips have remained tightly sealed in recent days, but this is what we do know.

title: D66 and CDA went 'over to the left' and the VVD cannot stomach that: three crucial days for the Jetten minority cabinet
lead: The Jetten minority cabinet still exists, although the question is for how long. Out of resentment over the 'betrayal' and the deal with the left on the tax plan, the VVD seems able to leave the coalition. These were three tense days for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. In the timeline below we take you through the most important moments.

title: Concertgoers cough and splutter in Manchester due to unknown substance
lead: In Manchester, 12.000 people were evacuated during a concert by American rapper Don Toliver. Towards the end of his show, an unknown substance was released, causing people to cough, get eye irritation and have trouble breathing.

title: Free maternity care in Amsterdam-Zuidoost has an effect, Utrecht follows in 2027
lead: Families with money worries often cannot pay the own contribution for maternity care. The municipality of Utrecht is therefore starting a pilot for free maternity care in the Overvecht and Kanaleneiland neighbourhoods in 2027. In Amsterdam-Zuidoost a similar pilot has been running since September 2025. Over the past year, 77 families made use of that option.

title: FIFA: three official candidates for presidential election in March
lead: Three official candidates have put themselves forward for the FIFA presidential election in March 2027. The world football body confirmed this on Thursday in a press release. The current Swiss president Gianni Infantino is being challenged by Frenchman Philippe Diallo and Kohzo Tashima from Japan.

title: Commotion in Antalya over sudden absence of Prime Minister Jetten from UN summit: from "climate nag" to dropout
lead: Prime Minister Rob Jetten is not going to the climate summit in the Turkish Antalya for the time being. The prime minister is staying in The Hague to help gather support for the tax plan. The sudden decision does not go down well with Dutch climate activists already present at the conference: "A missed opportunity."

title: 'If Amsterdammers get rid of their cars because they become too expensive, it doesn't bring the municipality any money either'
Rare trappist beer promotion causes rush on Belgian supermarkets
lead: It is almost never possible to buy a bottle of the famous Westvleteren in a supermarket. Beer fans therefore headed early this morning to Belgian Colruyt branches, but far from everyone could take the coveted case of blonde beer home.

title: Cabinet teeters, fate of tax plan and box 3 uncertain
lead: All three coalition parties say it is not yet a crisis. But halfway through an added debate on the tax plan it is clear that the situation for the cabinet is precarious on Thursday.

title: Midfielder Brandt returns to Ajax squad after injury
lead: Julian Brandt can return to action for Ajax in Sunday's home match against ADO Den Haag. The German attacking midfielder has recovered from the injury he suffered in late October in the match against AZ at the Johan Cruijff ArenA. Brandt subsequently missed the away matches against Midtjylland in the Conference League (1-6) and FC Twente in the Eredivisie (2-2).

title: For 25 years an unfinished ghost castle has towered above the A6 near Almere. Soon that may be a thing of the past
lead: The municipality of Almere and a construction consortium are proceeding with the demolition of an unfinished castle along the A6; a new castle and a residential neighborhood are to take its place. Not everyone is happy about the demolition: 'That little bit of history we have, we must cherish.'

title: French lower house rejects 2027 budget, text goes back to Senate
lead: The Assemblée nationale, the French lower house, on Wednesday unanimously voted down the government's budget proposal. All 458 parliamentarians of the Assemblée Nationale who cast a vote voted against, French media report. Two parliamentarians abstained. <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">De Senaat</entity> will have to consider the text again.

title: Millionaire tax and cabinet could both still fall
AI companies are financing each other with billions and that is a risk
lead: From Anthropic to Nvidia, in a short time AI has become the driving force behind economic growth, mainly in the US, and rising share prices. But behind the explosive growth of AI companies lie financial arrangements that make economists nervous.

title: Quiet is the message during trade mission: it is time the Netherlands started earning money in Ukraine
lead: As Russian bombs fall on Kyiv, minister <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Sjoerd Sjoerdsma</entity> (D66) travels to Ukraine for trade. Why now, while the country faces a harsh winter? What do companies have to do there? Our reporter Niels Klaassen followed Sjoerdsma's first aid and trade mission in the war zone.

title: D66 en CDA sluiten deal met Pro om begroting te redden, VVD buitenspel gezet
lead: Coalitiepartijen D66 en CDA hebben op het laatste moment een deal gesloten met de linkse Pro om de impasse in de...

title: Hoekstra after 'evidently failed' climate summit: 'We cannot accept this'
lead: The climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has ended in disappointment. No agreement has been reached. Speaking to the camera of RTL Nieuws, EU commissioner Wopke Hoekstra describes it as an 'evident failure'.

title: Farmers' organisations still dissatisfied with nitrogen plans after talks with cabinet
lead: Farmers' organisation LTO and the association for young farmers NAJK cannot yet support the cabinet's nitrogen plans. The organisations demanded that the plans be amended in part, but feel that they are not being listened to sufficiently. "We will deliberate."

title: Man (30) convicted over deadly Los Angeles firestorm, faces possible 40 years in prison
lead: A 30-year-old American man has been found guilty of arson in Los Angeles by a US jury. During New Year's Eve 2024 into 2025, he set fire to brush with a lighter, after which the fire spread through the entire neighbourhood and burned for weeks. Twelve people died. Thousands of homes were damaged.

title: Trijntje (57) on her run-over daughter Tamar (14): 'I learned about Tamar through the eyes of others'
A pill costs 20 cents but brings in 20 euros: why the Dutch ecstasy trade remains so stubborn
lead: According to prosecutors, a drug organization in Zwijndrecht produced more than a million ecstasy pills per month. Next week the court will rule on nine of the eleven suspects. As the case nears its conclusion, new raids are taking place. "As long as demand remains this high, others will jump into that gap," says researcher Pieter Tops.

title: Why the Netherlands actually still does not have enough wolves
lead: The wolf has been back in the Netherlands for more than 5 years. There are now 14 packs living in our country, but according to research there is ecological room for 23 packs. But can our country actually cope with that? Opinions are divided on this.

title: Dozens arrested during unrest in The Hague, majority minors
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested 34 people on Saturday during unrest in The Hague. There were no riots or looting, but at one location the mobile unit had to intervene briefly. The vast majority of those arrested are minors.

title: Local governments demand 40 million euros for sovereign government cloud
lead: Municipalities, provinces and water boards want the national government to make at least 40 million euros available for developing a sovereign government cloud. They are willing to pay part of it themselves and want the first government organisations to be able to use the facility as early as 2027. According to the other tiers of government, the Netherlands otherwise risks remaining dependent on large non-European IT suppliers.

title: AFM concerned about growing cyber threats: 'The question is not whether, but when and how'
lead: The Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM) is concerned about growing cyber threats. The consequences of successful cyberattacks on financial institutions, such as banks, can be far-reaching. But public attention to this is still limited, notes AFM chair <entity id="person:laura-van-geest">Laura van Geest</entity>. "It is not a question of whether the financial markets will be hit by a cyberattack, but when and how."

title: Asylum minister overruled: safety of Syria not assessed properly enough
lead: The minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>, <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA), must reassess the security situation in Syria. The Council of State ruled on this today in a case brought by an asylum seeker from Syria.

title: Tbs for stalker from Terneuzen who bombarded radio DJs with messages
lead: The man from Terneuzen who bombarded DJs and staff of NPO Radio 2 with messages was sentenced on Thursday to tbs with forced psychiatric treatment. The court in Middelburg considers long-term treatment necessary to prevent repetition.

title: Who is Gavin Newsom, and could the governor of California become president in 2028?
lead: With his Hollywood looks, Silicon Valley network and outspoken attacks on Donald Trump, Gavin Newsom is one of the most striking Democrats at the moment. But who is the governor of California, really, and could he become president in 2028? 1. Who is Gavin Newsom? Background, youth and political career 2. How does Gavin Newsom's governorship go […]

title: House majority accepts 'fudged' funding for box 3: 'We have to make a leap once'
lead: A majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, like <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, wants to hurry the overhaul of box 3. The parties also accept the funding that minister <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) has proposed, even though a future cabinet will be saddled with a multi-billion gap.

title: Genefaas sold her family business: 'Emigrating doesn't work if you have a company to run'
lead: Mieke Genefaas joined Tebunus Tube Bending, her father's company, ten years ago. Now she is following her dream, moving to an old farmhouse in Italy. But not before she handed the company over in a good way: to a buyer she gets along with.

title: Scholieren en studenten komen in opstand tegen dienstplicht en defensie-uitgaven
lead: Middelbare scholieren en studenten door het hele land verlaten vrijdag om 13.00 uur hun klaslokalen tijdens een Nationale Vredes...

title: For the Dutch people who do feel disadvantaged, one issue dominates: housing
lead: There is a sharp divide between academically educated and practically educated people in feelings of disadvantage, according to research by the <entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">SCP</entity>. Practically educated people with and without a migration background often feel disadvantaged on the same themes: housing and political representation.

title: 'If I ever find out you call me 'little woman', I'm leaving you right away'
Gelderland temporarily buys municipal land for housing construction
lead: The province of Gelderland is for the first time temporarily buying land from a municipality, so that houses can be built more quickly. The province is taking over a plot of land in the <entity id="org:gemeente-westervoort">gemeente Westervoort</entity> on which some six hundred new homes are to be built. Around half of all Gelderland municipalities are interested in such an arrangement, says Gelderland.

title: House of Representatives wants to move away from the automatic assumption of new elections after a cabinet collapse
LTO chair Koopmans critical of cabinet after nitrogen talks: 'After five months they should have been further along'
lead: On Friday Van Essen must send his elaborated nitrogen plans to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, but talks with LTO Nederland and the Nederlands Agrarisch Jongeren Kontakt (NAJK) are still ongoing. The farming organisations want the cabinet to adjust the plans on several points. According to Koopmans, Wednesday's meeting was not yet concrete enough. LTO chair Ger Koopmans is still not satisfied with the progress of the nitrogen plans of agriculture minister <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">Jaimi van Essen</entity>. After five months of negotiating, according to him more should have been on the table.

title: Lecturer Nouhaila el Guebli is on a theatre tour: 'I understand the white Dutch and I also understand the Moroccans, Surinamese and Turks'
The view of osteoarthritis is shifting, and that is leading to new treatment options
How political culture makes the difference between a working minority cabinet in Scandinavia and chaos in the Netherlands
lead: While minority cabinets in Scandinavia function perfectly well, the first attempt in our country almost immediately turned into a fiasco. Why does it work in Denmark and Sweden but not here (yet)? According to political scientist Tom van der Meer, this is not only down to the coalition but also to political culture: "This cannot be solved with a magic wand."

title: Vmbo pupils better at arithmetic, havo and vwo pupils slip back
lead: Pupils in the vmbo-basis and vmbo-kader streams have improved at arithmetic in recent years. At the same time, fewer and fewer havo and vwo pupils are reaching the higher levels for arithmetic and mathematics. This is according to research by the <entity id="org:inspectie-van-het-onderwijs">Inspectie van het Onderwijs</entity> among pupils at the end of their second year.

title: Land policy is back on the agenda: which levers can governments pull?
lead: With a new measure, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> removes 'the biggest sting' from land policy. What other options are there?

title: Even without major decisions, the talks between Xi, Putin and Trump are harmful to Europe
lead: Xi spoke with Putin, Xi spoke with Trump, Trump spoke with Putin. Then they spoke, all three of them. Afterwards they issued a 'Peace Declaration', as if to show that these three men naturally have leadership of the world, and that this responsibility has been entrusted to them.

title: Dead animals and debris washed ashore in Mexico after Starship launch
lead: The partly failed launch of Elon Musk's Starship last week may have unpleasant consequences for the company. Debris and dead animals have been found on a Mexican beach, and Mexico wants SpaceX to take responsibility. However, the company denies that it caused the damage.

title: Nimble minister Van Essen must get the country out of the nitrogen deadlock
lead: Can the agricultural sector carry the nitrogen plans of Agriculture Minister Jaimi van Essen (D66), and will the Netherlands actually get out of the deadlock? Those questions remain after the adjustment, last week, of the nitrogen plans presented on 26 June.

title: Minister positive about proposal to ban political dual roles
lead: Minister of the Interior <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Pieter Heerma</entity> (CDA) is positive about a plan by D66 and PRO to ban certain dual roles within politics. The parties want it to no longer be possible to be politically active within a municipality or province alongside being a member of the House of Representatives.

title: Albert Heijn recalls spinach à la crème: 'Do not eat the spinach'
lead: Albert Heijn is recalling the 750-gram spinach à la crème as a precaution. The product may contain plastic particles. "Do not eat the spinach", warns the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity>.

title: Commemorative Medals for International Missions presented in the Nieuwe Kerk
Rob Jetten briefs Luxembourg prime minister in WhatsApp group ahead of European summit: 'This is how Europe should be'
lead: Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden (CSV) represents the whole of the Benelux at the informal European summit in Dublin. Rob Jetten and Bart de Wever are not present on behalf of the Netherlands and Belgium. According to Frieden, representing the three countries is an 'honourable but easy task'.

lead: Woo decision on lawyers' costs Download file: Documenten set 1.pdf (PDF) Download file: Documenten set 2.pdf (PDF) Download file: Documenten set 3.pdf (PDF) Download file: W2026019 Inventarislijst.pdf (PDF) EISN2403 Thu, 11-12-2026 5 November 2026 Show header image To Document 20261105 W2026019 besluit advocaatkosten_Geredigeerd.pdf (1.79 MB)

title: Eleven dead during arrest of Mexican drug lord: 'Considerable blow'
lead: During an operation around the arrest of Mexican drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro', at least eleven people have died. They are four Mexican soldiers and seven people suspected of being members of a cartel. Mexican authorities report this.

title: VVD believes PRO's tax proposal conflicts with the coalition agreement
lead: The proposal by PRO and VOLT to levy more tax on wealth conflicts with the coalition agreement, according to VVD MP Wendy van Eijk. It states that the parties want a 'fiscally stable' investment climate for businesses. "Those are the agreements we made with each other," she says in a debate on taxes.

title: Foundation risk will count towards NHG mortgages from 2027
lead: From next year, banks must take into account possible foundation problems in homes when they provide mortgages with the Nationale Hypotheek Garantie (NHG). As a result, home buyers may be able to borrow less when there is a foundation risk.

title: Cabinet breaks promise on student loan: this is why
lead: The cabinet promised a maximum interest rate on student debt, but that plan will not go ahead. A majority in the House of Representatives now wants to spend the money differently. What does that mean for students and people with student debt? Political reporter Floor Doppen explains.

title: AFM warns: 'Not whether, but when a cyberattack hits the financial markets'
Passports for sale: Romania opened the door to Russians linked to the Kremlin
lead: In Romania, forged citizenship certificates were converted into official EU identity documents for years. Sanctioned Russians reportedly benefited from this route. The Romanian authorities were warned, but are having great difficulty stopping the forgeries.

title: Minister Aartsen: 4 days of work the norm in civic integration
Closing Time | The same old scene
lead: Today I spent a bit longer in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, somewhat infected by the hype about the relationship problems that supposedly exist in the minority cabinet. May I briefly summarise it for you? I saw and heard damn familiar sounds…. Read more posts at Sargasso

title: Asylum minister Van den Brink considers Syria safe for return in new assessment
lead: Asylum minister <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> maintains the view that Syria is a safe country for refugees. He has reviewed the security situation again after the Council of State ruled that the policy was not adequately reasoned.

title: KNVB director De Jong considers Oranje's performance 'unacceptable'
lead: Director of professional football Nigel de Jong of the KNVB finds Oranje's 5-0 defeat to Germany in the Nations League on Monday "unacceptable". The former footballer wrote this on social media.

title: Government Website Outage Caused by Human Error
lead: On Wednesday morning, various government websites were offline for half an hour. The outage affected not only rijksoverheid.nl, but also, for example, the websites of the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (om.nl) and the Royal House (koninklijkhuis.nl). Services such as the <entity id="org:rijksinspectie-digitale-infrastructuur">Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur</entity> (rdi.nl), the <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-het-cultureel-erfgoed">Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed</entity> (cultureelerfgoed.nl), the <entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau</entity> (scp.nl), the <entity id="org:kabinet-van-de-koning">Kabinet van de Koning</entity> (kabinetvandekoning.nl), the Kanselarij der…

title: Electricity storage capacity must be fifty times greater by the end of 2040
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has presented plans to tackle the heavy strain on the electricity grid. More large batteries and shorter permit procedures should ensure that by the end of 2040 there is fifty times as much capacity.

title: Klaver (PRO) wants to debate Prime Minister Jetten tomorrow: 'Is there still a cabinet?'
lead: "The question is, does the Netherlands still have a cabinet at all?", said PRO leader Jesse Klaver. He would most like the top of the cabinet to account for itself as early as Tuesday in a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Cabinet comes with millions to help Ukraine through winter: 'Old stuff from the NAM is useful here'
lead: The cabinet is setting aside 55 million euros for subsidies to Dutch energy companies that help Ukraine through the winter. There is also 136 million euros in a fund to help Dutch companies get started doing business in Ukraine. <entity id="pos:minister-van-buitenlandse-handel-en-ontwikkelingssamenwerking">Minister van Buitenlandse Handel en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking</entity> <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Sjoerd Sjoerdsma</entity> (D66) announces the aid and trade plans during a visit to Kyiv.

title: Despite Bontenbal's soothing words, it is clear to everyone where this cabinet is heading
lead: Özcan Akyol writes three times a week about what concerns him.

title: Dozens of tenants demand back dubious cash payments from landlord: 'It is bleeding us dry'
lead: Landlord Marcel van Hooijdonk has in recent years already faced an order subject to a penalty, a criminal conviction and exposure by BOOS. Yet he continues to take money from tenants. Dozens of tenants are now demanding almost 20 thousand euros back through a summons.

title: Man (36) killed in shooting in Rotterdam: 'Four bangs. I knew: this is not fireworks'
lead: A man died on Monday evening in a shooting on the Evenaar in Rotterdam. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, it concerns a 36-year-old resident of Dordrecht. The victim turned out to be the driver of a car in which four people were in total.

title: A double hat for Sybrand Buma? Experts see no obstacle but do see a risk
How should Buma help the cabinet? 'The most important question is still being avoided'
lead: How should <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity>, vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>, ensure that the minority cabinet sees out its term? VVD honorary member Henk Kamp thinks the solution lies in solid financial agreements with opposition parties. But political science professor Tom Louwerse is sceptical. He fears a new battle over direction.

title: Dead woman found in house in Tilburg, possible crime
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> today found the body of a woman in a house on Berkenrodelaan in Tilburg. She may have died as a result of a crime, a police spokesperson says. The police are conducting an investigation in and around the house.

title: Opposition still rejects cabinet's offer on tax plans: 'I'm not a silly Henk'
lead: Opposition parties, both left and right, are still not happy with the cabinet's tax plans. They loudly say they will vote against the plans no matter what, but at the same time they do not do that either.

title: Minister van Wonen plant nieuw dorp op het laagste punt van Nederland
lead: De regering zet door met plannen om een nieuw dorp van 6,000 woningen te bouwen op het laagste punt in...

title: United Kingdom wants to return to the EU in baby steps
lead: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is in Brussels today to make new agreements with the European Union on trade and the free movement of young people. Recently Burnham even toyed with the idea of a new Brexit referendum and a return to the EU.

title: Everyone wants more money for the police, but the House now also wants to know exactly how the 9.4 billion is to be spent
lead: At 9.4 billion euros, the police is the largest cost item of the Ministry of Justice. It is unclear exactly how that money is to be spent. The House of Representatives now wants a more transparent budget, but <entity id="person:david-van-weel">minister Van Weel</entity> calls that "undesirable".

title: Belastingplan 2027: 1,5 mld. voor koopkracht; "vrijheidsbijdrage" geschrapt
lead: De regering stopt nog eens 1,5 miljard euro in koopkrachtverbetering, zei minister-president <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> dinsdagochtend na een extra vergadering van de ministerraad.

title: What do you want to know about the coalition crisis? Take a look and ask us your questions here
lead: Tensions in The Hague have risen sharply. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is wobbling after the agreement on the tax plans between D66 and CDA with PRO and Volt. "It has never before been seen in the Netherlands that a party has been so ambushed by coalition partners", says VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz.

title: Cabinet wants even more tax relief for wealthy business owners
'You know that full well', the police said when sovereign citizen Ed was arrested and asked why: an endless row of unpaid fines
lead: The man with over 450 outstanding fines and bills who was recently arrested is for the time being behind bars. Ed van den B. first had to serve 28 days as long as he did not pay the first series of fines, but his time behind bars has already been extended until January. This is confirmed by his lawyer Bart Augustin.

title: After yet another round of talks on the Tax Plan, only 50Plus and ChristenUnie are really satisfied
Poet and performer Babs Gons receives Johannes Vermeer Prize
Rob Jetten tries to salvage what can be salvaged: he wants a 'relaunch' of his cabinet
lead: VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz seemed to threaten the fall of the cabinet, but in Thursday's debate it emerged that her party means the same by the 'reset' she wanted as Jetten does: he wants 'talks' about a better way of working together.

title: De Graafschap wins postponed match at Vitesse
lead: De Graafschap won the postponed first division match at Vitesse 1-0. Julian Kania headed the only goal in the 82nd minute from a corner. The win moves De Graafschap up to 11th place. Vitesse has dropped to sixteenth place.

title: Escalator at Bijlmer ArenA rail station runs wild, people suffer broken bones
lead: Eight people were injured this morning at the Bijlmer ArenA rail station in Amsterdam. This happened in two separate incidents, in which an escalator suddenly started moving while people were standing on it. Two of the eight victims were seriously injured, a spokesperson for the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> told RTL Nieuws. They suffered broken bones.

title: New conflict looms between national government and municipalities over youth care funding
lead: A possible new conflict between the municipalities and the national government over the financing of youth care is once again putting strain on the relationship between the national government and the municipalities. The <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity> threatens to blow up the fresh cooperation agreements with the national government if the issue is not resolved. The national government thereby risks a 'big problem', says VNG chair <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity>.

title: Two men charged over incident at British air force base
lead: The British Public Prosecution Service charged two men on Tuesday in connection with an incident last month at RAF Fairford air base. Police suspect them of having supported Iran. They have been charged under the National Security Act.

title: Right-wing alliance: JA21, BBB and SGP now draw up a plan together for the cabinet
lead: JA21, SGP and BBB are starting a cooperation that is meant to give the Jetten cabinet a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. But they are attaching a number of conditions, including a different approach to asylum, nitrogen and medical-ethical issues.

title: Moerdijk may still survive after all, but residents not yet reassured
lead: The Brabant village of Moerdijk can probably survive after all, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has said. It is just not entirely clear yet how. The village was supposed to disappear from the map because it had to make way for industry.

title: Dead man found in Limburg village Swolgen is 46-year-old from Oss, died as a result of violence
lead: The dead victim found last Saturday in the Limburg village of Swolgen is a 46-year-old man from Oss. This was announced today by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. He had earlier been reported missing by his family. The police confirm that the victim died as a result of violence.

title: Man sentenced to four years in prison for bribing Amsterdam enforcement officer
lead: A thirty-year-old man was sentenced on Tuesday to four years in prison for bribing an official of the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">gemeente Amsterdam</entity>. The information was subsequently passed on to criminals. The judge found no evidence of a link with serious violence.

title: With new actor as Bond, the battle between luxury brands could also break out
lead: With the announcement of the new James Bond, the battle between luxury brands for a prominent place in the new film can begin. From watches to cars, and from suits to champagne: for well over half a century, the films have been a way for all kinds of brands to stand in the spotlight. This time the battle looks set to be extra exciting.

title: Minister wants 'scandalous' and 'dangerous' online fake pharmacies taken offline faster
lead: <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Minister Hermans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> (VVD) wants online fake pharmacies taken offline as quickly as possible. lead: Should AI be banned in primary schools? The House of Representatives wants to intervene firmly in the classroom, but teachers are not waiting to have a solution spoon-fed to them from The Hague either. "Dit is het kind met het badwater weggooien."

title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action protest in London, police remain alert in Frankfurt after looting
lead: A wave of student and secondary school protests is sweeping through part of Europe. In countries such as France, Germany, Switzerland, Portugal, Albania and England, these demonstrations are being hijacked by troublemakers and criminals. In the Netherlands, Spain and Belgium too it was sometimes unruly on Saturday, but major riots did not occur. By now it is calm again in most places. Follow all developments regarding the disturbances in our liveblog below.

title: ABN Amro returns as main sponsor of Ajax after almost twenty years
Prisoners up to 4 weeks early release due to shortage of places, but sentence reduction could increase further
lead: Prisoners can be sent home up to four weeks early due to the shortage of places in prisons. State Secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> (Justice, D66) had already kept that option open, but is now 'forced' to use that possibility.

title: No delivery ban for Uber Eats in Amsterdam: insufficient consideration of the consequences, rules Council of State
Tanzanian Jigar Ganatra made award-winning film about a chameleon: 'This animal was there the whole time. It saw you, but you did not see it'
lead: Tanzanian Jigar Ganatra made the film Chameleon Corridors on a small budget, which was internationally awarded. For him the chameleon is more than an animal. "It is a mirror for how we treat nature."

title: 'The mission remains: prosperity must bring wellbeing to all Arubans'
Tram driver mistook man for garbage bag: 'If I had thought something was wrong, I would have stopped'
lead: HTM tram driver Paul A. (44) mistook a man lying on the tracks for a garbage bag. The 37-year-old man did not survive the collision with the tram. The Public Prosecution Service demands that the driver be found guilty but receive no punishment. "There was a misjudgement with fatal consequences," says the public prosecutor.

title: Bird flu confirmed in Hierden
Grave cleaner Jaco (60) developed COPD and is now a shadow of his former self
lead: 60-year-old Jaco van Heijst developed the chronic lung disease COPD because of his work as a grave cleaner. Like Jaco, around 5,000 people a year develop COPD through their work, for example because they work with chemical agents. The Longfonds draws attention to this and is launching a special check.

title: Renewed problems with ICT system in Amsterdam, city may be missing out on ground lease income
lead: Hermes, the system with which the municipality of Amsterdam collects ground lease payments, has largely been running without technical support since October. This could affect the budget the city must submit before 15 November: ground lease income is an important pillar of the municipal finances.

title: Nationwide chaos in politics, in Hilversum there are already elections now
lead: While attempts are being made in the woods of Hilversum to save <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, a little further on in the centre a campaign is being run for local elections. Hilversum is merging with Wijdemeren, and therefore residents go to the polls on Wednesday. But many voters are completely fed up with politics.

title: Nearly all arrested troublemakers in The Hague are free again
lead: Of the 34 people arrested yesterday during the disturbances in The Hague, 33 are free again. One of them is still in custody, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reported a day later. The mostly underage youths were arrested.

title: Small saver rescued, but cabinet sees both right and left bloc leave grumpily anyway
lead: In an ultimate attempt to gain support for the tax plans, the cabinet received three groups from opposition parties for negotiations on Friday. Behind the scenes it was delicate, and no deal is forthcoming. But there is hope for small savers and investors, insiders say.

title: Netherlands wants to deter asylum seekers with a return hub in Rwanda: 'No evidence that it works'
lead: Five European countries want to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda for reception and further procedures. The Netherlands, Germany, Austria, Denmark and Greece are together in discussions about this. But the question is whether it will go ahead.

title: Is that even allowed? Applying for another job during working hours as a civil servant
lead: The central government wants to cut 25,000 civil service jobs in the coming years. Municipalities are also cutting their staff. For example, <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> wants to eliminate as many as 2,500 fte by 2030, roughly one in nine jobs. The municipality has meanwhile introduced a tightened vacancy freeze, after dozens of civil servants were nonetheless hired despite an earlier freeze. For employees who fear for their jobs, that may be reason to start looking for other work in advance. But are you actually allowed to do so during working hours…

title: European football body UEFA wants chairman of the French federation as Infantino's successor at FIFA
lead: At the last moment, UEFA has found a candidate to beat the controversial Gianni Infantino in the race for the FIFA presidency. Infantino long appeared unchallenged on his way to a fourth term.

title: The 'Scandinavian model' comes remarkably late: 'As if they are only now realising it'
lead: The Dutch experiment with a minority cabinet has not yet definitively failed. The coalition is turning to the far north of our continent to make the arrangement workable. But a Dutch variant of the Scandinavian model requires a radical change in behaviour, especially from the VVD.

title: Cabinet to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda: 'Must become a win-win situation'
lead: The Netherlands is going to open a 'return hub' in Rwanda. Initially a handful of rejected asylum seekers will be sent to the African country. The cabinet mainly hopes to prove with this that it can be done: sending asylum seekers back to a country other than their homeland. Because once the return hub is there, a one-way ticket to Kigali must deter asylum seekers.

title: House of Representatives lacks an approach to rapidly growing homelessness: 'You would expect urgency'
Elodie Verweij: VVD has gone missing since the deal on the left, we don't know where parliamentary leader Brekelmans is
lead: Reporter Elodie Verweij is in The Hague and tells about the latest state of affairs. 'The bizarre thing is: since the deal the VVD has gone missing. We don't know where parliamentary leader Brekelmans is. If all goes well, <entity id="person:dilan-yesilgoz-zegerius">Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius</entity> will come out with a statement later in the evening."

title: British navy picks up third rubber boat with Dutch millionaires
lead: Han van der Horst: 'The millionaires hope that a new House and a new <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> will put an end to the misfortune that has befallen them'

title: GTA VI publisher: sales bring in 3.8 billion dollars on first day
lead: Sales of the new computer game Grand Theft Auto VI generated 3.79 billion dollars in revenue on Thursday, the first day of release. That is what developer Rockstar Games reports. According to the company, this sets a record for the sale of a new computer game.

title: Bram Wouterse and Aart Gerritsen new academic partners of the CPB
lead: The <entity id="org:centraal-planbureau">Centraal Planbureau</entity> (CPB) welcomes Dr. Bram Wouterse and Dr. Aart Gerritsen as academic partners. Wouterse becomes academic partner of the Healthcare programme. Gerritsen brings his scientific expertise in the field of taxation and government policy and is connected to the Taxation programme.

title: Brexit proves to be an 'unnecessarily expensive joke' for Britons, reunification with EU beckons
lead: Almost seven years ago the United Kingdom officially left the European Union, but now that Brexit itself is being chipped away at, new trade agreements and even reunification with the EU are beckoning. That makes the separation, which among other things cost the Britons a great deal of economic growth, appear to be turning into an 'unnecessarily expensive' joke.

title: Appointment of Inspector-General of Mines
The VVD is in a tight spot, but the party may also benefit from that
lead: These are crucial days for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. Will it manage to find a way out of the tax maze by Thursday? If not, the survival of the Jetten cabinet seems seriously at risk.

title: Max Verstappen does not want to share his heart rate with fans, and this expert agrees with him
lead: Soon Formula 1 fans will be able to see live on TV how fast a driver's heart beats during a race. Max Verstappen thinks this goes too far for him and refuses to take part in the plan. Privacy expert Bart van der Sloot completely agrees with him: "There is hardly any privacy left for athletes."

title: Crisis talks at country estate begin: will the parties move closer together?
lead: The crisis talks between D66, VVD and CDA at the De Zwaluwenberg country estate in Hilversum have begun. Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> of D66, VVD leader and deputy prime minister Dilan Yesilgöz and deputy prime minister…

title: Voters find the restart unbelievable: 'Doomed to fail'
lead: After days of intensive talks, the three coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA have found a way to continue. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> remains in office and talks are under way about restoring trust. Do voters believe in it and what are the consequences of the crisis? We put the question to the RTL Nieuwspanel.

title: OM employee with a political role in Brabant suspected of electoral fraud
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> on Tuesday arrested an OM employee on suspicion of corruption and electoral fraud. The 38-year-old man also held a political position in East Brabant.

title: College for Human Rights lacks funding for oversight of AI systems
lead: The College for Human Rights is seriously concerned about the funding of its fundamental rights oversight of AI. The College receives only half of what is needed and can therefore put less than half of the required specialists to work.

title: Court: Crisp must repay €5 mln, but did not mislead investors
lead: The online supermarket loses a lawsuit against its investors, but the outcome is nuanced. Crisp did not mislead investors, the court says. The amount is also not immediately due.

title: Derk Boswijk (Defence) on stake in new institute: 'The Netherlands must cooperate better'
lead: <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-defensie">Staatssecretaris van Defensie</entity> Derk Boswijk was today in Stroe for the launch of the National Institute for Defence Technology (NIDT). This institute must ensure that more is produced and that it can be scaled up faster. Companies and startups can sign up for an assignment. In the barracks, Sven Kockelmann spoke with Boswijk.

title: Your Move
New elections can only take place in May, but are no solution to the poisoned relations
lead: Hatred is now dripping from the walls in The Hague. The question is whether anyone can still avert a cabinet collapse. In Belgium, the king managed this week to get parties back to work. But in the Netherlands, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> thought it could handle everything itself. Not so. title: Moment of drone strike close to Dutch embassy in Kyiv
lead: A drone has struck close to the Dutch embassy in Kyiv. Footage shows the moment of impact.

title: Wooden houses gain ground, but do not solve the housing shortage
lead: From roof structures to complete homes, building with wood is quickly gaining ground. The share of new wooden homes in the Netherlands has more than tripled in five years. Even so, this sustainable building method turns out not to be enough to tackle the housing shortage.

title: President of Paraguay removed and arrested over role in banking crisis that left millions of residents without their money
lead: In Paraguay, President Santiago Peña was arrested on Friday evening, shortly after he was removed from office by <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> over his role in a major banking scandal, which left millions of Paraguayans without their money.

title: Jensen Huang back as chief executive of chipmaker Nvidia after affairs
lead: Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia. A week and a half after he stepped down, the board has reappointed him as director with immediate effect.

title: Enhertu for stomach cancer and Skyclarys for now not in the basic package
Housing associations increasingly have to choose between new build or sustainability upgrades
lead: The financial position of housing associations remains under pressure. As a result, landlords increasingly have to choose between new construction or making existing homes more sustainable. This is shown by a benchmark from Aedes, the umbrella organisation of housing associations.

title: 60,000 addresses received a letter this year that the tiger mosquito has been spotted in the area

title: More countries come up with serious plan for the end of oil, gas and coal
lead: Some 30 countries now have a clear plan to bid farewell to fossil fuels or are seriously working on one. Some of the ministers of those countries announced this today at the climate summit in Turkey. A year ago, not a single country had drawn up such a roadmap, and half a year ago there was still only one.

title: Verstappen expects a 'tough' race at the Las Vegas Grand Prix
lead: Max Verstappen expects a tough Las Vegas Grand Prix. The four-time Formula 1 world champion will start from pole position tomorrow, admittedly, but he expects formidable competition from the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli in particular.

title: Sybrand Buma must get the cabinet back on the right track before the end of the year
Cabinet wants to keep village of Moerdijk but does not yet decide definitively
lead: Moerdijk will continue to exist, that is the cabinet's aim. lead: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death for "cowardice", taking part in a mutiny and refusing orders. With these harsh penalties, <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> wants to improve discipline within the army.

lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is planning to allocate 350 million euros extra to reduce the burden on workers. The box 3 overhaul is also all but certain to be postponed by a year. The plans do not yet have support in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: How safe is Syria now? 'The country is still in a transitional phase'
lead: On Tuesday the EU is meeting in Damascus to discuss improving investment ties with Syria. <entity id="pos:minister-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Minister van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Sjoerd Sjoerdsma</entity> has already announced that the Netherlands will put an additional 15 million euros into Syria's reconstruction. lead: Short track skater Teun Boer has won the 500 metres in the World Tour for the first time in his career. The 25-year-old Dutchman finished ahead of fellow countryman Jens van 't Wout and Mathieu Pelletier of Canada in the final.

lead: The high-speed train route from Amsterdam to Paris celebrates its 30th anniversary this year. The route is a success and Eurostar wants to run to more cities. But opening new international train routes is difficult, the chief executive of Eurostar tells RTL Z.

lead: The Dutch short-trackers have also won the third mixed relay race in the World Tour. Jens van 't Wout, Selma Poutsma, Zoë Deltrap and Teun Boer kept the teams of Russia, China, South Korea and Canada behind them.

title: Klaver and Dassen pleased with deal: 'Hope the way is clear for a majority on the tax plan'
lead: Jesse Klaver of PRO and Laurens Dassen (Volt) are pleased with the breakthrough that now seems to have been reached to help the tax plan get a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. If the amended amendment from both parties is adopted, the two left-wing opposition parties will agree to the tax plan, Klaver says when asked.

title: Video | Willem-Alexander welcomes Zelensky with an embrace at audience
Breakthrough in 32-year-old case: man arrested after DNA match for 1994 rape of 15-year-old girl
lead: A 57-year-old man from <entity id="org:gemeente-helmond">Helmond</entity> has been arrested after 32 years for the rape of a 15-year-old girl in the <entity id="org:gemeente-sint-michielsgestel">gemeente Sint-Michielsgestel</entity>. Detectives tracked down the suspect through a DNA match.

title: The lower your income, the less you play sports
lead: People from the lowest income group play sports less than people with a higher income. That gap has widened over the past ten years. <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> carried out an analysis between the years 2014 and 2024.

title: Health insurance premiums are rising sharply again. More market competition was meant to make healthcare better and more affordable twenty years ago. How is that working out now?
lead: All adults may once again choose a health insurer. Mainly healthy people switch, to the lowest price. Insurers were also meant to compete on quality, the intention of the Health Insurance Act in 2006. That turned out to be an illusion: an insurer that invests in quality also helps its competitors.

title: Ombudsmen worldwide put their heads together on digitalisation
lead: How is the role of <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">de ombudsman</entity> changing in the digital age? On 10 December, International Human Rights Day, ombudsmen from many countries will gather in New York to answer that question and to explore cooperation with the United Nations.

title: Rotterdamse bestuurders gaan overleg voeren met Feyenoord over vuurwerk dat de wedstrijd tegen Inter onderbrak
lead: De gemeente Rotterdam is van plan het vuurwerkincident van dinsdag met Feyenoord te bespreken, bevestigde de woordvoerder van burgemeester <entity id="person:carola-schouten">Carola Schouten</entity>.

From wine regions to air quality in aircraft: 181 advisory clubs advise the central government on these matters

title: New mayor in Reusel-De Mierden

title: How does the Dutch influencer economy work? 'Every day scrollers are born, and TV viewers die'
lead: Influencers are the new advertisers. Their managers strike ever bigger deals with ever bigger brands. What lies behind the ever-expanding 'creator economy' in the Netherlands? "The lesson is: you can make money from anything, but the art is not doing that. Credibility is the most important thing."

title: New application round for the Expeditie-regeling opens on 16 November
Schools get more grip on truancy with the Terugdringen Schoolverzuim act
Don't let housebuilding drown in water requirements
lead: The Netherlands must build in a climate-resilient way. There is hardly any debate about that. But a familiar phenomenon threatens here: a respectable policy goal is standardised too extravagantly, while the associated bill lands in a different letterbox.

title: Growing embryos for science and better care
lead: Today <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> votes on a bill that is meant to make it possible to grow embryos for scientific research. At present only leftover embryos from IVF treatments may be studied. As a result, an important phase is missed: the actual fertilisation and the first few days that follow. "A number of very important biological processes take place there", says clinical embryologist Sebastiaan Mastenbroek in De Rode Draad.

title: Did the top boss of the Italian police actually help the mafia, instead of fighting it?
lead: He was the top boss of the Italian police, who gained fame as a mafia hunter and crime fighter: Gianni de Gennaro. On Saturday morning news came that he had committed suicide. He was found dead at his holiday home in Tuscany. He is said to have actually helped the Sicilian mafia. According to correspondent Angelo van Schaik it was the talk of the day in Italy: "On all the websites of all the newspapers it was the most important news all day."

title: VNG: Brussels is getting in the way of municipalities with European housing market plans
lead: Municipalities fear that new European rules will make it harder to take measures against the housing shortage. With these plans, Brussels is getting in the way of local governments, the VNG believes.

'My kung fu teacher can split a brick in two. When we were allowed to try it with planks, I got quite far'

lead: Alongside high-tech, green education also lays a foundation for our future. Caring for plants, animals, soil and water is linked to how we wish to live, work and get by. That is why green education deserves more room in the National Talent Strategy of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, argue Rien Komen and Cyrille van Bragt.

title: Conscription often turns out badly for young people: 'Income lags behind for a long time'
lead: On Friday, pupils and students walked out of lecture halls across the Netherlands to protest against the possible return of conscription. What is often overlooked: such a compulsory period in the military can still have negative consequences for your career and income years later.

lead: The European Commission states that Temu's controls and sanctions system structurally fall short in preventing illegal and unsafe products being sent to Europe.

Revised guidance on transferring digital archives
lead: The revised Archives Act takes effect in January 2027. This is the reason for the <entity id="org:nationaal-archief">Nationaal Archief</entity> to update its guidance 'Digitaal overbrengen in de praktijk'. Many government organisations do not yet have much experience with digital transfer. To put it bluntly: no experience at all.

lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham dined together at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam last night. lead: With the vote in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, D66 and CDA have found a majority with centre-left parties, without the VVD.

title: Nearly half of examined PHP applications run on an outdated or affected version
lead: Tens of thousands of web applications used by employees of Dutch organisations are still running on an outdated version of PHP or one affected by recent security vulnerabilities. That is what research by cybersecurity company MindYourPass shows, two days after critical vulnerabilities in the programming language led to numerous government websites going temporarily offline.

title: Dirty grandpa
lead: I am sitting on the sofa chatting with my wife and our granddaughter Feline, 7 years old, when she suddenly says: "That dirty grandpa always calls me Chantal." We are startled and…

lead: Tension in The Hague: can this <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> still be saved, or is it curtains? Our political reporter and commentator Hans van Soest explains the three scenarios. "Either way, the mutual relations are completely poisoned. Between all parties."

title: High reward for finding missing mountaineer, China fears accidents
lead: The family of missing Chinese mountaineer Chen Jie (25) has offered a reward of over 68,000 euros to whoever finds him alive. The Chinese embassy in Japan warns that the high reward could lead people to head into the mountains unprepared. It therefore calls on hikers not to recklessly climb Mount Fuji.

title: Klaver (PRO): 'The cabinet lacks the political will to work together with us'
lead: According to PRO leader Jesse Klaver, the cabinet does not want to make agreements with him and Laurens Dassen (Volt) about the tax plan. The right-wing bloc of JA21, BBB and SGP says it still sees points of contact to keep talking.

title: Utrecht investigates ban on spy glasses, VNG previously saw no need
lead: The municipality of Utrecht is investigating whether smart glasses with built-in cameras can be banned in municipal buildings. The municipality is also looking at whether secret filming can be restricted through the General Local Regulation (APV). With this, Utrecht is taking a more active approach than the Association of Dutch Municipalities (VNG), which previously saw no need for specific rules.

title: Full tank ten euros more expensive, price of speciality beer not up: this is what happens if the tax plan fails
lead: If the tax plan of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> does not get support from the opposition, your daily life will not change significantly. In fact, costs will go down, but on the other hand there is more pain at the pump.

title: Zoo issues statement on death of hippo: 'Fiona could not be saved'
lead: The 9-year-old hippo Fiona could not have been saved in any way. That is what the zoo in Cincinnati in the American state of Ohio reports, where the animal lived her whole life. Two weeks before her death, Fiona had swallowed a knitted children's hat that had accidentally ended up in her enclosure. That proved fatal on Thursday.

title: Statues made of pumpkins: from Super Mario to Barbie, the traditional pumpkin festival in Ludwigsburg is 'a form of escapism'
lead: With more than 450,000 pumpkins from over six hundred varieties, the Kürbisausstellung in Ludwigsburg is the largest pumpkin festival in the world. Artists created sculptures and artworks from them. Some two hundred thousand visitors marvelled at them. "I love the European festival culture."

title: Real Madrid avoid dropping points after falling behind against Celta
lead: Real Madrid managed to avoid dropping points on Saturday evening in the home match against Celta de Vigo. Despite an early deficit against the club from Galicia, Real won 2-1. This brings the Madrid club level on points again with FC Barcelona, which still plays on Sunday.

title: From the terrace on the Plein, ADO hooligans 'defend' their city. 'If anyone is going to destroy this city, it is still us ourselves'
lead: In The Hague, riots and looting were expected on Saturday after online calls in recent days. In the end, mainly hooligans turned up. The hard core reflects. "We prefer to fight an opponent, and otherwise with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>."

title: Climate morality must not depend on what others do or fail to do

title: AI sceptics focus on the wrong threats
lead: They overlook how vulnerable the status quo is and how much AI can help defenders, writes Anne Neuberger.

title: 'Getting a fine sent to you afterwards doesn't really help much'

"Being stopped on the spot by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has much more impact on your behaviour than getting a fine sent to you afterwards", says Damiaan Hage, editor-in-chief of AutoWeek .

title: Across the border: French mayor bans tiger mosquito by decree
lead: The Asian tiger mosquito has officially become established in the French municipality of Saint-Just-Saint-Rambert. Mayor Olivier Joly has banned the insect by municipal decree. The mosquito may no longer remain on the municipality's territory. Anyone who does not comply risks prosecution, according to the mayor.

lead: Hello and welcome to this live blog. Here, political reporters Priscilla Slomp and Edo van der Goot will keep you informed about the coalition crisis.

title: AI threatens science, independent and critical thinking will soon be gone
lead: Individual scientists are almost powerless against the AI threat to the scientific foundations, write Leo Lucassen and Jan Lucassen.

title: Explosive statement from witness who saw video footage of 'Bolle Jos' shortly after Overasselt
lead: "I am Jos, you may recognise me. I am described as Bolle Jos in the media." That is what the most wanted criminal, a few hours after the explosive attack in Overasselt, is said to have told a corrupt transport employee via a video link. While the employee is walking the dog in the street, he is told to stay away from Jan G. and that 'something in the news' will come out later that day. The statement is a crucial lead for <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the justice system, linking Jos Leijdekkers to the attack by 35 heavily armed criminals.

title: Hoekstra objects to 'countries throwing sand in the machine'
lead: European Commissioner for Climate Wopke Hoekstra is objecting at the climate summit in Antalya to a number of countries that are 'throwing sand in the machine'. Those involved say that oil giant Saudi Arabia, among others, is obstructing.

title: Cabinet wants Buma's help to secure opposition support after all: 'It really must be different'
lead: The cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA is continuing with a series of good intentions about a different way of working. Vice-president of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> must help with a plan to involve the opposition better. title: KNMI warns of dense fog across the entire country
lead: The KNMI warns of dense fog. The weather institute has issued a code yellow for the whole country. Previously this applied only to the north.

title: Crispy rösti from the baking tray
Barça heads to Baku: the sweet fairy tale of football minnows Sabah
Leaked bank documents: Hungarian partner of ING facilitated Russian money laundering practices
lead: One of Hungary's largest banks facilitated a money-laundering operation with a central role for a Russian oligarch closely linked to the Kremlin. After European competitors had written off the bank, the Hungarian bankers ended up at the Dutch ING.

title: Missing toddler found after five hours in Arizona desert
lead: A two-year-old girl who had been alone in the Arizona desert for hours has been found after a large search operation. A neighbour finally found her under a bush.

title: Sylvia abused her son: 'It was normal for me'
lead: Child abuse occurs in all sections of the population. Even so, many people wonder: who does something like that? The 54-year-old Sylvia from Tilburg was one such person. She abused her son and could not stop without help. Now she speaks about it, in order to urge other parents to seek help too.

title: Municipality of Utrecht: Professional footballer Redouan El Yaakoubi (30) did not misuse subsidy money
lead: Professional footballer Redouan El Yaakoubi (30) came under fire last year after suggestions that he had earned money from his foundation Durf te Dromen. The municipality of Utrecht now concludes that there is no reason to suspect misuse of the hundreds of thousands of euros in subsidy that were received.

title: Cabinet sets aside half a billion for protection of tropical forest
lead: Over a period of ten years, the cabinet wants to invest a maximum of half a billion euros in a new fund for the protection of tropical forests. The wealth fund will structurally reward countries that preserve their rainforest.

title: Documentary on the 1969 Curaçao uprising shown again: 'Still relevant'
lead: A historic date for Curaçao: 30 May 1969. On that day a strike began at Shell, which led to a massive popular uprising against exploitation and colonialism. Parts of Willemstad went up in flames, and the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> sent marines to restore order. John Leerdam made a documentary about it in 1995, 'Gritu di un pueblo'. The documentary can be seen again from today during the IDFA documentary festival.

lead: Follow all developments in American politics here.

title: Lorry driver who ran over 16-year-old Guusje gets community service: 'You wonder what he has learnt'
lead: The lorry driver who ran over Guusje Roelofs (16) in Eindhoven in November 2024 has been sentenced to 240 hours of community service and a twelve-month driving ban, four months of which are suspended. title: Garages are busy: APK inspections for 416,000 cars expire in November
lead: The APK inspections of just over 416,000 passenger cars expire in November. 30 November in particular will be a busy day: that concerns 30,545 cars. Anyone who does not have their vehicle inspected risks a fine of 190 euros, even if the car is standing still.

title: Slight decline in sickness absence in Amsterdam
lead: Sickness absence at the City of Amsterdam is declining slightly. Where absence in the organisation was still 9.7 percent in 2025, the 'rolling annual average from October 2025 through September 2026 is now 9.3 percent. That is according to the second progress report on organisational change 2030' that Hendrik Jan Biemond, alderman for Personnel and Organisation, sent to the municipal council on Thursday. 'The decline is still too recent to be regarded as a structural result', it does add.

lead: The feast of Sinterklaas is exciting and mysterious. A Sinterklaasjournaal is fine, but this current chaotic stimulation party, according to Iris Rijsman, leaves absolutely nothing to the imagination.

title: Cabinet supports EU Kids Act, but has concerns about privacy and fundamental rights
Lieke no longer has extreme menstrual symptoms thanks to this treatment
lead: For some women, menstruation is so severe every month that it greatly affects their daily lives. There are various treatments, such as a hormonal coil or removing the uterine lining. Separately, these treatments do not always provide sufficient relief, but the combination of both now appears promising.
