The win at the Portimão circuit went to Italian Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi, ahead of his Spanish teammate Jorge Martín.

title: Customs pleased with new 2 euro levy on AliExpress and Temu: 'We no longer want to check loose bicycle lights'
lead: After online shopping at AliExpress and Temu already became 3 euros more expensive this summer, another 2 euros is added from this Sunday. With the proceeds, Customs will significantly step up checks on substandard goods, promises Director-General <entity id="person:nanette-van-schelven">Nanette van Schelven</entity>. She further hopes that consumers will order more from Dutch webshops.

title: The courtrooms at the Amsterdam-Zuid district court are an acoustic disaster. Do something about it
The Netherlands will be Europe's strongest medical technology sector in 2035
Prison sentences of twenty and twelve years with TBS for childminding couple in Woudenberg who abused six children
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded sentences of thirty and twenty years, but the court does not consider all of the suspicions proven.

title: Hackers publish customer data of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan
lead: Data of thousands of customers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase has been released by hackers. The data came into the hands of the cyber extortion group n0n through a cyberattack on an external party. The group has now published data.

title: Fons Lambie on confidence in coalition: this is how they will carry on
lead: Political correspondent Fons Lambie brings us up to date on the restored confidence after the four-day crisis talks. The three coalition parties, D66, VVD and CDA, have reached a solution.

title: Prosecution charges seven, not eight, officers for death of Mateusz (32) after arrest
lead: Prosecutors will charge seven, not eight, Rotterdam officers for their role in the fatal arrest of 32-year-old Mateusz. The eighth officer was still in training and 'carried out instructions' from colleagues of higher rank.

title: State Secretary Tielen intervenes at Stichting Islamitisch Onderwijs
The VVD is divided over Yeşilgöz, PRO and the future
lead: The socialist motto 'forward with courage' applies more today to the VVD than to the left-wing PRO. The party has to regroup after the crisis in the minority coalition.

title: After days of crisis talks, coalition wants to continue: D66, VVD and CDA are going for it, with help from former informateur Buma
lead: Confidence in the coalition appears to have been restored. The party leaders have found a way out. Former informateur <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> is to help for a month to get quarrelling parties back on the same line, with an improvement plan. Our reporter speaks of 'one of the most miraculous political revivals ever' if the attempt succeeds.

title: No extra tax for the royal house after all: 'Provide more clarity, the budget is not transparent'
lead: The annual discussion about the royal house flared up again yesterday in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. This time it mainly concerns an adopted motion to tax the income of the Orange family. D66 has always been in favour of this, but <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> is nonetheless giving up on it. "If you can justify it, you can take the sting out", says Eveline Bijlsma, royal house expert for De Telegraaf, on Spraakmakers.

title: Advisory council to the cabinet: New world order calls for a radically different policy on development cooperation
Alderman Lennart de Looze searches for evidence of whether a home is really vacant
Aantal thuisbatterijen verviervoudigd in een jaar door einde van de salderingsregeling
lead: Het aantal thuisbatterijen is in Nederland sterk gestegen, volgens de Autoriteit Consument en Markt (<entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity>).

title: 'Those neighbourhoods don't just tag along at the school or childcare centre in the next street'
lead: What kind of feeling does the new Utrecht alderman Julia Kleinrensink have going into winter? In the coming cold period there is an increased risk of power outages in the congestion areas around <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>. Because it is precisely on cloudy winter days that the grid can become overloaded. Because in this part of the Netherlands grid congestion is greatest. To prevent problems, grid operators do however install emergency power supplies in <entity id="org:gemeente-houten">Houten</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-almere">Almere</entity>, consisting of batteries and…

title: Nuis fifth over 1500 metres in Japan, Ning beats Stolz
lead: Speed skater Kjeld Nuis narrowly missed the podium again in the 1500 metres at the World Cup in Obihiro. The 37-year-old Dutchman finished fifth in 1.45.38. Ning Zhongyan of China won, as he did a week earlier in Beijing.

title: After a rainy week the weather improves today, but not everywhere
lead: Compared with previous days, the weather today looks better, mainly in the north. In the south there is still some rain, but the north sees regular sunshine. In the afternoon a single shower is possible.

title: The Yesilgöz coup
lead: COLUMN - Dilan Yesilgöz wants a fundamental reset and to restore the balance. High time to take stock. But first that 'fundamental reset'. At the time of writing, Ms Yesilgöz, nor any of her comrades from the libertarian VVD corner, has specified what we should understand by it. The term may have been around longer [...] Read more posts at Sargasso

title: Sex offence suspect Jan B. writes 900 pages by hand
lead: Jan B. (67), the man suspected of sexually abusing at least fourteen children, has written a handwritten text of 900 pages in prison. Nothing was said in court about the content of the text. The case has also not yet been heard on its merits.

title: Vesteda sells almost €1 billion of rental homes to BPD
lead: The largest commercial landlord in the Netherlands is losing 10% of its housing portfolio. The deal with BPD follows strong pressure from Vesteda's shareholders.

title: Cabinet postpones new box 3 tax until 'at the latest' 2029, but still hopes for 2028
Putin 'in excellent spirits' after talks with Trump
lead: The American and Russian presidents, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, have spoken with each other about the war in Ukraine on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. According to the Kremlin, Putin left the talks 'in excellent spirits'. Trump called the Russian leader 'my friend'.

title: Waiting lists and membership stops: a million Dutch people cannot join the sports club of their choice
lead: Ahead of the sports debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, sports umbrella organisation NOC*NSF urgently appeals to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to release 50 million euros to increase sports capacity. "Clubs are increasingly constrained by a lack of space, literally and financially."

title: Nederlandse overheid schrapt 16% van haar personeel; 25.000 banen voor ambtenaren verdwijnen tegen 2035
lead: Het kabinet plant tegen 2035 het schrappen van 25.000 voltijdbanen bij de overheid, onthulde verantwoordelijk staatssecretaris <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> (VVD) in een interview met

title: Not 35,000 but 25,000 civil servants fewer
lead: Central government must have 25,000 fewer civil servants working in 2035, not 35,000. Relatively speaking, this is therefore not the 22 percent reduction in civil servants still desired by the previous <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>, but a little under 16 percent. For many organisations, the 3.5 billion euro cost-cutting target does mean a 20 percent reduction in staff. And for some organisations this can rise to 45 or even 60 percent.

title: Staatssecretaris meldt bescheiden winst in herkenning van seksueel grensoverschrijdend gedrag
lead: Staatssecretaris van Onderwijs en Emancipatie <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> constateert een bescheiden verbetering in de mate waarin mensen seksueel grensoverschrijdend gedrag herkennen.

title: Embryologist Bernadette de Bakker wants to help parents with that one important question after a miscarriage: Why did it go wrong?
Volkswagen wants to freeze wages for two years and have workers work longer
lead: Volkswagen wants to give German employees no wage increase over the next two years. The carmaker also wants staff to work longer for the same salary. The plans are causing great discontent at the union, which does not rule out strikes from 1 January.

title: Ajax and AZ benefit from Feyenoord's loss of points: 'Most of the problems are mental'
lead: What do the numbers say? Data analyst Bart Frouws weekly dives into the most striking statistics of the played Eredivisie matches in the studio of NOS Langs de Lijn. Today Frouws analyses the matches of Ajax, AZ and Feyenoord together with analyst Leonne Stentler.

title: How the government struggled with Meta for years and ultimately lost
lead: State Secretary Alexandra van Huffelen (Digitalisation, D66) wanted to end her ministry's use of Facebook as early as June 2024. Meta refused to provide the requested information about privacy risks and also made a remarkable demand: the state secretary had to ask for written permission in advance to communicate about the negotiations with the company, even to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> thereupon prepared the closure of several…

title: Heinen on opposition demands: 'One party's wish often clashes with another's'
lead: Every Tuesday afternoon a ten-minute conversation is held with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the Netherlands, <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity>. In the weekly conversation with the <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity>, which is broadcast live from the studio in The Hague, financial-economic topics and everything related to them are discussed.

title: Tension rises: cabinet has been discussing tax plan and box 3 all day
lead: Tension in The Hague is rising. The top of the cabinet has been discussing the tax plan and box 3 all day. There will probably be an extra <entity id="org:ministerraad">ministerraad</entity> on Tuesday, and the hope is that the cabinet will be done by then.

title: Forensic expert doubts Epstein's suicide: 'He was strangled'
lead: An American forensic expert says that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was strangled in his cell in 2019, and therefore did not commit suicide. He analysed the autopsy file and posted photos from it online. "It is time people can draw their own conclusions."

title: Can the Jetten cabinet really be only about left or right? Plans often have support across the chamber
lead: For months the big question in The Hague has been whether the Jetten cabinet will be about left or right. Yet the divide is often smaller than it seems: most of the laws passed in recent months have support across the chamber.

title: Prime Minister Jetten meets deputy prime ministers from VVD and CDA on Friday morning over 'what now'
lead: Prime Minister Rob Jetten (D66) is holding a crisis meeting on Friday morning with his deputy prime ministers, Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA). Jetten said this on Thursday evening in the…

title: New twist in tax soap opera: BBB joins right-wing alliance
lead: In negotiations between <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> and the opposition, three right-wing parties make a new move. BBB is joining the small alliance that JA21 and SGP had already formed. The three parties are offering the cabinet a total deal, but are laying down an extensive list of demands.

title: Still 66 million in subsidy left on the shelf for housing forms for older people
lead: There is only one month left to submit an application for the Stimulation Scheme for Care-Suitable Housing (SZGW). Of the 80 million for 2026, only 13.5 million has so far been applied for, for shared housing for target groups, including older people. The good news: housing associations and care providers still have 30 days to submit a subsidy application. Municipalities play a crucial role in this, but will they take it up?

title: D66 and CDA regret deal between D66 and CDA with PRO and Volt, Jetten wants to carry on with Yesilgöz
lead: <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">De Kamer</entity> is now being advised by <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> against voting for the proposal on Thursday evening

title: Former State Secretary Gunay Uslu steps down as CEO of travel company Corendon, company to be split
Danish Supreme Court finds controversial 'ghetto law' not discriminatory
Employers struggle with remote work policy: 'More companies could start a case'
lead: Increasing numbers of employers are struggling with their remote work policies. They are therefore following with great interest the ruling of the Amsterdam district court in the Booking.com case about mandatory office days. "More companies may start a case," labour law lawyers tell NU.nl.

title: She sets her alarm for four o'clock, the stall is set up by nine: Julia (36) can be found every Saturday behind her Portabella stall at the Noordermarkt
Can we skate and build snowmen this winter? These are the forecasts
Manuela (40) shares her room with a complete stranger in an 'ophokhotel': 'I can't live here'
lead: They came for a better life, but ended up in an 'ophokhotel'. Eighty migrant workers share damp rooms in a boarded-up Rotterdam hotel. The municipality speaks of 'pure exploitation', but does not intervene. "They abuse us, they're just like pimps."

title: Theatre director Agnes Laura Kumpina (31): ‘The goddess of love must surely have an insight or two for me’
Survivors' pension becomes more favourable, but you do need to take action
lead: The new pension act also affects survivors' pensions. In many cases this turns out more favourably for your survivors, but unclarity about the scheme can also lead to distressing situations, the <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">AFM</entity> warned this week. So make sure you know what you need to arrange yourself.

title: 'Child abuse' in Spain: municipalities also bear responsibility
lead: Lisa <entity id="org:gemeente-westerveld">Westerveld</entity>, PRO member of the House of Representatives, asked questions of minister <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Mirjam Sterk</entity> of Long-term Care, Youth and Sport about an investigation by Nieuwsuur with shocking results on extreme treatment methods for young people with behavioural problems who were sent to Spain. This week the minister answered the parliamentary questions. It shows that Sterk has asked municipalities to suspend placements of young people abroad where possible.

title: Defence files report after sexist comments from personnel
lead: Defence has filed a report about abusive and intimidating online posts by defence personnel. Female soldier Mandy Heeren raised the alarm earlier this year after she became the target of sexist comments.

title: Man from Doetinchem who planned attack on asylum centre sentenced to 2.5 years in prison
lead: A 37-year-old man from <entity id="org:gemeente-doetinchem">Doetinchem</entity> was sentenced on Tuesday to 42 months in prison, of which 12 are suspended. The man had made preparations to carry out an attack with heavy fireworks on an asylum seekers' centre in the Gelderland municipality.

title: Senatoren steunen plan om embryo's te kweken voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek
lead: De Eerste Kamer heeft plannen goedgekeurd om speciaal gekweekte embryo's te gebruiken voor onderzoek naar erfelijke ziekten en...

title: Sir Steve McQueen, who receives the Erasmus Prize today, has addressed injustice throughout his entire artistic career
Beune narrowly beaten by Wiklund over 1500 metres in Obihiro
lead: Speed skater Joy Beune has had to settle for silver at the World Cup in Obihiro. The reigning world champion over this distance was a fraction slower than Ragne Wiklund with 1.53.85. The Norwegian won in 1.53.79. Valérie Maltais of Canada finished third with 1.55.48.

title: GPS signal from dozens of flights at Schiphol disrupted, possibly from a ship in the North Sea
lead: On at least seven flights, the GPS signal was disrupted during landing at Schiphol on Monday. That is confirmed by a spokesperson for <entity id="org:zbo-luchtverkeersleiding-nederland">Luchtverkeersleiding Nederland</entity> to RTL Nieuws, following reports by NRC.

title: Male K3 hugely popular, but must change name
lead: From a viral joke to more than fifty bookings: things are moving fast for K3 with the Baard in de Keel. But now Studio 100, the company behind K3, has sent them an email. Bram, Max and Jean-Paul must change the name of their act and may not wear outfits that look too much like K3.

title: Chances of a good start are growing, but children with parents of foreign origin continue to lag behind
lead: Children with two parents of foreign origin more often have a favourable start in their first thousand days than children born in 2007. But their starting position remains the least favourable. Of the children born in 2021 with two parents of foreign origin, 40 percent grew up without any of the four risk factors studied. For children with two parents of Dutch origin, that was 73 percent. This is reported by the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> in the Rapportage Integratie en Samenleven 2026.

title: It's good that the cabinet is allocating money for housing for the elderly. But then they do have to be willing to move
Chef wants a healthy lunch at every primary school: 'How nice it is when the necessary carrots and peppers already go into it at school'
Verwey-Jonker Institute on the verge of bankruptcy
lead: The Verwey-Jonker Institute has applied to the <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> district court for suspension of payments. The independent research institute can no longer meet its financial obligations. The court has appointed Seerp Gratama of Certa Advocaten as trustee.

title: Man (27) possibly killed by violence in Vlissingen
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has started an investigation into the death of a 27-year-old man in the Zeeland town of Vlissingen. The man died after a report of a possible violent incident. He was still resuscitated, but that was to no avail.

title: Live | Crisis in coalition is complete, Prime Minister Jetten responds only on Thursday
lead: Hello and welcome to this live blog. Here we will keep you informed of political developments surrounding the tax plan.

title: US delays delivery of sixty Patriot missiles to Ukraine, writes The Financial Times
EU countries prepare for a hard battle over the giga budget
Can the 'fragile' Jetten cabinet restore trust? 'Opposition can think along and give the coalition a chance'
lead: Trust has been restored within the coalition, but it has called in <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> to help the minority cabinet function better. Is the political unrest now completely over? "It is still very fragile", says Floor Bremer, political correspondent for RTL Nieuws, on Spraakmakers.

title: This criminal teaches farmers to keep real criminals out
lead: Farmers can recently practise conversations with the criminal Tony. Tony is not a real criminal, but an AI version that tries to persuade farmers to rent out their barn for illegal activities. By practising the conversations, Platform Veilig Ondernemen - a collaboration of entrepreneurs, trade organisations, municipalities and justice - hopes that farmers will learn to say no better.

title: College: human rights under pressure due to monitoring of demonstrators
lead: The Dutch government is collecting increasing amounts of information about demonstrations and demonstrators, the <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> notes in its annual report. This may involve sensitive information such as political or religious beliefs. People who wish to demonstrate may feel hindered by the idea that the government is keeping an eye on them and gathering information about them and their views. Through this so-called chilling effect, human rights may come under pressure…

title: PSV strengthen top spot with third convincing win in a row
lead: PSV have strengthened their top spot in the Eredivisie. The reigning champions were too strong for NEC in Nijmegen: 1-4. It was PSV's third convincing win in a row in the league, following earlier victories over Willem II (7-0) and SC Cambuur (2-5).

title: 'She has a partial pension, I have nothing. The holiday home has to partly become our pension'
lead: Margareth van Aken and Léon-Marie Dekker live in an old farmhouse near Doetinchem. They put their time and money into renovations and into the many animals on and around the farm. "But we enjoy it here every day."

title: Cabinet has not yet covered a fifth of the missed box 3 revenue, calculates the Ministry of Finance
lead: Not taxing paper gains in box 3 from 2028 onward will cost the treasury a total of 21.8 billion euros through 2040. Only a limited part, about 4.2 billion euros, is compensated by the cover measures the cabinet has proposed. That is evident from a table that the Ministry of Finance released at the urging of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Old objections not removed as battered cabinet resumes
lead: The cabinet is saved on paper. New agreements have been made, it has been declared that trust has been restored, and <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> will find out how a minority cabinet can actually work, Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> announced on Tuesday. Not long after, practical objections were already pouring in.

title: Police risk losing crucial contact with neighbourhoods, researchers warn
lead: The police risk losing the crucial contact with neighbourhoods needed to prevent riots and conflicts. Within the police, that connecting task is still too often seen as something for the neighbourhood officer alone. That is according to new research.

title: Why Good Habits Are Often Not Enough to Reach Your Goals
lead: Through trial and error, I have developed a few healthy habits. For years I have avoided sweets, such as cookies and desserts. And every other day I run with the dog in the morning.

title: Annemarie Denier van der Gon (100): 'My mother did not hug us, she thought it would cause problems'
Man molests woman on Haarlem bus and also harasses other women
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is looking for a man who last week harassed several women on a bus in Haarlem. He touched one of the women inappropriately and made sexual remarks.

title: Cabinet puts an end to the back route for cheap labour migrants
Bontenbal at party congress on tax plan: 'We CDA members are not so keen on gambling'
'Every criminal can buy one': alarm over the rise of illegally made firearms
lead: Ever more forged firearms are falling into the hands of criminals. The illegal copies of branded firearms are just as deadly as the originals, but much easier to obtain. The Dutch <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, Europol and Interpol speak of a major threat to Europe.

title: An offer that cannot be refused? Cabinet considers new tax package to win over opposition
lead: Tensions around the cabinet are mounting: there is still no deal on the tax plans. An 'offer' from right-wing opposition parties mainly causes irritation. One of the scenarios now: presenting a package they can't refuse to the entire opposition.

title: The cabinet still gives no clarity and will once again talk with the opposition about the tax plan
Russia calls on Dutch ambassador to leave Kyiv, Jetten says he will not be intimidated
lead: The Russian ambassador in the Netherlands has made an urgent call on the Dutch ambassador in Kyiv to leave the country. That is what the Russian embassy reports about the conversation with <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>, who had summoned him. According to political reporter Roel Schreinemachers, the Netherlands does not intend to withdraw embassy staff. "This threat from Moscow will change nothing about that"

title: How much has the Netherlands already donated to Ukraine? Zelensky's visit puts the figures back in the spotlight
lead: The Ukrainian president Zelensky visited on Wednesday <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity>. The Netherlands is giving Ukraine a new military support package, but how much have we actually donated so far? And what about public support for our billions in aid to the country at war? Five questions.

title: Prime Minister Jetten spotted walking outside estate, an hour after crisis talks began
lead: Prime Minister Jetten and D66 <entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">leider Paternotte</entity> were spotted going for a stroll outside shortly after the start of the crisis talks. According to political correspondent Roel Schreinemachers, that can mean two things: "There is an option on the table, or the talks are stuck."

title: No expanded powers for enforcement officers and police on COA sites
lead: Asylum minister <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA) sees no merit in the proposal to give enforcement officers and police more powers on sites of the Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers (COA). To do so, COA sites would have to be legally designated as public space. According to the minister, that is 'not a sustainable solution', and opening the sites also carries risks. For example, it could come at the expense of residents' privacy, attract unwanted visitors and lead to...

title: Groups of mbo students feel disadvantaged and point at each other: 'Feelings run very deep'
lead: Mbo students with and without a migration background share many of the same concerns, such as finding a suitable home and an enjoyable job. Yet both groups think the other is being given preference. This is shown by research from the <entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau</entity> (SCP).

title: Police to reassess part of ten thousand unprocessed reports from 2024
lead: The police will reassess part of the more than ten thousand unprocessed reports and notifications from 2024. Justice Minister <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> (VVD) writes this in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, after earlier coming under fire for downplaying that number.

title: Cabinet must first have a vision of a 'smart government' before it cuts 25,000 jobs
lead: With the loss of 25,000 civil service jobs, the coalition wants to save 3.5 billion euros. Of that, 1 billion is solely intended to balance the budget. That has nothing to do with an effective government, it is simply bookkeeping.

title: In Finsterwolde, where a neo-Nazi cage fight was held in the village hall, residents knew nothing
lead: In the Groningen village of Finsterwolde, far-right extremists organised a cage fight in the basement of the village hall. Villagers have heard or seen nothing. "They are people who look like us, who don't stand out", the expert explains.

title: Do people really eat out differently, as Ron Blaauw says? 'Fine dining is a bit of a boomer hobby'
Democrats criticise Trump's lobbying for Huang's return to Nvidia
Minister van Binnenlandse Zaken steunt plan om politici te verbieden meerdere politieke functies te bekleden
lead: Minister van Binnenlandse Zaken <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Pieter Heerma</entity> heeft steun uitgesproken voor een plan van D66 en PRO om politici te verbieden bepaalde publieke functies tegelijkertijd te bekleden.

title: The state must take the lead on making homes more sustainable now that progress is stalling
lead: The national government must take a firmer lead in making homes more sustainable. Those recommendations are set out in an Interdepartmental Policy Study (IBO) published on Monday. The sustainability of homes is still 'not getting off the ground sufficiently', the researchers note in the report.

title: Kusama exhibition at the Stedelijk Museum extended by two weeks to the end of January
Tens of thousands of households warned by letter about tiger mosquito in their area
lead: About 60,000 addresses have received a letter this year because the Asian tiger mosquito was spotted in the area. The <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">NVWA</entity> sent another 20,000 addresses a call to be alert for the mosquito.

title: 'What am I doing here?' Relationship with AI bot is not all roses
lead: Out of curiosity, journalist Brenda van Osch creates her digital life partner: Raf. He responds understandingly, gives superficial answers and is never angry. She longs for friction.

title: AP: Tax Authority has so far checked only 3 of 100 algorithms
Verstappen second fastest in Las Vegas, but starts from pole
lead: Max Verstappen may start from pole position on Sunday in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The four-time Formula 1 world champion was admittedly slower than Kimi Antonelli in qualifying, but the Italian of Mercedes has to drop back in the starting grid due to a grid penalty.

title: Outdated RIVM laboratories in Bilthoven risk being closed due to outbreak danger
lead: The RIVM laboratory buildings are outdated and the risks of the research are increasing, the Financieele Dagblad writes, based on a letter from site manager Stichting-Alt.

title: British woman who was drugged and raped for years: 'Silence is not an option'
lead: A British woman who was sexually abused by four men after her husband tied her up and drugged her has told her story. "The person I trusted most has betrayed me in the most unimaginably cruel way," she said. "I will never be able to feel completely safe again."

title: Will the VVD leave the cabinet today? 'This concerns 0.5 percent of the national budget'
lead: By a narrow majority, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> approved the tax plan last night, but without the support of coalition party VVD. The party felt 'ambushed' after D66 and CDA, the other coalition parties, had indicated they would vote in favour of the amendment by PRO and Volt. Today <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> is making a last-ditch attempt to prevent a cabinet collapse. "Yeşilgöz has one setting and that is war mode, quite worrying for someone who is <entity id="pos:minister-van-defensie">minister van Defensie</entity>," says journalist and writer Simon van Teutem, on Spraakmakers.

title: New heart test prevents unnecessary hospital trips, but costs hospitals income
lead: A simple blood test in the ambulance can prevent people with chest pain from being taken unnecessarily to hospital. That spares patients uncertainty and relieves care staff. Yet this innovation has a downside: hospitals can lose income if fewer patients are admitted. Emeritus professor of care and society Jan Kremer therefore argues for a change to the care system. "Instead of more care, there must be more appropriate care," he says in Villa VdB.

title: Norway through to Nations League quarter-finals after late win over Denmark
lead: Norway secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals at the last moment. The team led by star player Erling Haaland came back from a 2-0 deficit against Denmark early on to win 3-2. Haaland converted a penalty deep into injury time to decide the match. Portugal, who had already qualified, beat Wales 3-2 and go through as group winners.

title: Stephan kept believing in hydrogen, now its fuel suddenly becomes competitive with diesel. 'Delivery vans too will switch en masse'
Many objections, but cabinet supports housing in lowest polder
lead: Just before the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> handles about twenty objections to the planned construction of 8000 homes in the lowest polder in the Netherlands, the cabinet has promised help to the <entity id="org:gemeente-zuidplas">gemeente Zuidplas</entity>. title: The House of Representatives has lost its education vision
lead: After two days of the education budget, I have certainly drawn my conclusions.

title: Reporter on crisis meeting: 'Far from certain that a way out will be found'
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> and the deputy prime ministers met all day to see whether the minority cabinet still has a future. Later in the afternoon, the parliamentary group leaders of D66, CDA and VVD also joined the talks.

title: What will Klaver do if the cabinet makes a mess of it?
Shooter of problem wolf Bram not prosecuted, Animal Rights disappointed
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) will not prosecute the person who shot wolf Bram dead on the Utrechtse Heuvelrug last year, a spokesperson confirms. According to the OM, the shooter rightly decided to kill the animal outside the permitted period.

New agreements for more recycling of old mattresses
The man who has been trying for 25 years to build homes on his estate
lead: Maintaining listed country estates costs a lot of money. The FD visited Landgoed De Hulst, where the owner wants to cover the costs through housing construction. But that is easier said than done.

title: Rubber boat with 36 migrants lost its engine at sea and drifted helpless toward the Dutch coast
lead: Two people on board the rubber boat that was towed to the Zeeland coast on Saturday morning have been arrested on suspicion of people smuggling. The Royal Netherlands Marechaussee confirms this. There were 36 migrants on board, who are doing reasonably well under the circumstances. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has meanwhile released a shocking photo of the overcrowded rubber boat.

title: Nine months in prison demanded for shooting cats with a crossbow
lead: <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) demands nine months in prison against 26-year-old Yihui L. He is suspected of having shot five cats with a crossbow in Eindhoven. One cat did not survive, and the other four were injured.

title: Woman in Tilburg dies in crime, no one arrested yet
lead: The 54-year-old woman who was found dead in a home on Berkenrodelaan in Tilburg last Sunday was killed. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is proceeding on the basis of the investigation that it was a crime. That was already suspected, but has now been confirmed. No suspect has been arrested yet.

title: That coach Xavi has his left-back play as an attacking midfielder is exemplary of the new direction at Oranje
lead: Thanks to the tactical choices of head coach Xavi, more players come into their own at Oranje. Under all circumstances, organised positional play is the starting point, also on Monday in Berlin against Germany.

title: Trump accepts the result, but also sneers: with me on the ballot we would have won
lead: U.S. President Donald Trump says he will accept the outcome of the midterm elections. "I am absolutely willing to accept the outcome," he told The New York Times. The Democrats are heading for a major victory in both the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. According to the White House, that also has to do with the quality of the Republican candidates.

title: Tax plan adopted, including millionaires' tax, VVD furious: 'Bad for the Netherlands'
lead: The VVD is going to reflect: parliamentary group leader Ruben Brekelmans will 'discuss' whether the party still has anything to look for in this <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>. He had to watch as a majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> voted for the tax plan and a millionaires' tax, because coalition partners D66 and CDA voted together with left-wing opposition parties.

title: Cabinet not yet choosing left or right, comes with new proposals on budget
lead: The minority cabinet today still makes no choice between support from the left or right flank for the tax plan. But the cabinet is coming with new plans in the areas of healthcare costs and purchasing power, said Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> at the start of new talks with opposition parties. "And then I hope we can make a tax plan that can count on a majority in both chambers of parliament."

title: Staatssecretaris van Onderwijs dreigt subsidie in te trekken van islamitische school

lead: Six ice clubs are in the running to organise the first marathon on natural ice this winter. The skating federation KNSB announced this on Monday evening. They are the ice clubs of Burgum, Haaksbergen, Noordlaren, Puttershoek, Nieuw-Amsterdam/Veenoord and Winterswijk.

title: How can the battered cabinet see out the term? Mediator: 'It is essential that parties do not provoke each other'
lead: The crisis atmosphere in the cabinet is over for now, but there are still irreconcilable differences. How do you prevent these from flaring up again in the coming weeks? We asked the experienced mediator Eva Schutte. 'It is often not about the best solution, but the least bad one.'

title: Body found in Limburg after investigation in forest, suspect arrested
lead: On the grounds of a house in the Limburg village of Swolgen, the body of a man was found on Saturday evening. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> had started a large investigation on Friday after a suspicious situation near a forest plot in Zeeland. A 46-year-old man has been arrested.

title: My son says: don't be so hysterical. How do I correct him?
Participation of Russian skaters in the Thialf World Cup unclear
lead: It is unclear whether Russian speed skaters will take part in the long-track speed skating World Cup races in Heerenveen in December. A representative of the Russian skating federation told NOS that they cannot compete because almost the entire skating delegation was not granted a visa for the races at Thialf.

title: Midterms: what is the filibuster and why are 60 seats the magic threshold in the Senate?
lead: What exactly does the filibuster involve? The filibuster is possible because the Senate allows an indefinitely long debate, and it is used to prolong debate and to delay or prevent a vote on a bill, resolution, amendment or other matter. The filibuster makes it much easier for Senators to gauge whether […]

lead: Anyone who thought abortion in the Netherlands was more or less settled will have been surprised this week. lead: Around 1 in 40 housing association homes is home to a household with a status holder. lead: Since the penultimate study that <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) conducted on them, from December 2024, the number of family businesses in the Netherlands remained stable, as did the number of employees they have: almost 296,000 with 2.8 million. lead: 'House of Representatives, stick to your last; respect the position of the mayor and the municipal council.' That is the call from the Dutch Association of Mayors to the House of Representatives. The mayors are responding to the legislative consultation on Justice & Security of Tuesday 10 November, in which the dismissal of <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> was again requested. lead: Eelco Keij richtte de Stichting Nederlanders in het Buitenland (SNBN) op, die lobbyt voor Nederlanders die in het buitenland wonen. Een wetsvoorstel dat...

title: Neurotherapist is responsible for death of 21-year-old woman, says OM
lead: The 70-year-old Koos Föllings is, according to the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, responsible for the death of a 21-year-old woman in 2018. Besides causing death through negligence, Justice also suspects Föllings of fraud, it emerged in court today.

lead: Most VVD voters (60 percent) want their party to leave the cabinet now that D66 and CDA are pushing ahead with their deal with PRO and Volt. But what next: a new formation or new elections? Voters are divided on that.

title: Large parliamentary groups rarely set a good example
lead: By far most MPs have experience with other governments: as councillor, member of a provincial council, group leader or alderman. They were then selected by their party for national work. The tendency therefore exists to think we are dealing with the fine fleur of Dutch politics. They would set an example for their 10,000 local colleagues. Such expectations often fall short.

title: Limburger Bas P. (40) before the judge for online abuse of 245 girls
lead: "I hope that one day I can look in the mirror normally again and say that I am proud of myself." That is what one of the 245 minor victims said in the case against the 40-year-old Bas P. He is suspected of online abuse of the girls via a partly self-developed computer game. The first day of the substantive hearing of the case was today at the court in Rotterdam.

title: Cabinet wants to cut one in five full-time jobs at central government in coming years, especially in implementation
lead: In the coming years the cabinet wants to save 3.5 billion euros at central government, including by scrapping 25,000 jobs. State Secretary <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> (VVD) speaks of "considerable challenges". A large part of the savings will "hit implementation".

lead: ABN AMRO appears set to become Ajax's new main sponsor. The bank will succeed telecom company Ziggo, which ends its financial partnership after this season. ABN AMRO was also Ajax's main sponsor between 1991 and 2008.

title: AP can take a harder line against governments when privacy warnings have been ignored
lead: Government organisations that ignore warnings from their own privacy officer risk having this weighed against them when they violate the privacy law. Managers can also be personally fined. This is evident from the enforcement policy that the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity> (AP) published on 30 October.

title: Law must curb the addictive effect of social media: 'Mental health of children and young people is deteriorating'
lead: PRO wants to end addictive algorithms that create an 'endless scroll' on social media, for example. Young people should also no longer be enticed to spend money unintentionally in apps. title: Bird flu confirmed in De Kwakel

lead: Not waiting in an asylum seekers' centre, but getting to work as quickly as possible. That is the cabinet's aim. lead: It was at the end of August that the Culemborg quality guarantor Bureau Kwaliteitsborging B.V. was suspended by the provider of the software tool this company works with. lead: The young women Mona van den Berg photographed in Bangladesh have big dreams. But before they can pursue them, they first have to learn that they are allowed to say 'no'.

title: Four women suspected of grave desecration over 'paranormal session' at children's graves
lead: Four women go on trial today on suspicion of grave desecration at Rusthof cemetery in Amersfoort. At the court in Utrecht they must answer for the 'paranormal session' they held at the cemetery in 2021, specifically at the children's graves.

lead: Not all problems can be solved with more democracy, says historian Maarten van Rossem. As far as he is concerned, it can be a bit less: "By politicising important issues, we keep getting into trouble", he says on the Ongelooflijke Podcast (EO).

This is how SpaceX made space history with a successful 'catch' of Starship

title: Filipino minister on Meghan Markle's father: 'Possibly a sex offender of the worst kind'
lead: Everything currently points to Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, possibly being 'a sex offender of the worst kind'. That is what Jonvic Remulla, the Filipino minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, told the British newspaper The Guardian. lead: It is a commonly heard explanation for the growth of populist parties. And now it turns out that this is partly true: in the Netherlands too, a substantial minority believes that their group is being disadvantaged.

title: Terneuzen executive board grants permit for much-debated asylum centre
lead: After years of preparation, the municipality of Terneuzen is granting a permit for an asylum seekers' centre in a former Neckermann building in the Zeeland city. A narrow majority of the current municipal council voted last month to set up a regional reception centre for up to two hundred asylum seekers at the Handelspoort industrial estate. In the previous council term, a majority of the council had still advised against it.

lead: The Jetten cabinet has not formally been dissolved, but at the same time it is highly uncertain whether it is still viable. In the coming days the three parties will have to explore whether they can still find a formula to continue together.

title: Making fun of Sinterklaas: that is something we gladly do
lead: As old as Sinterklaas is the tradition of mocking him. What characterises the humour about Sinterklaas? And why do we find it so funny when the good saint drops out of character?

title: RDI warning: digital infrastructure not always available as a matter of course
lead: In the Netherlands we are used to critical infrastructure working. Availability and accessibility are normally almost 100 percent (>99.98%). But due to the strong increase in hybrid threats, the RDI doubts whether this will also be the case in the future, as described in the annual trend radar.

title: Cabinet gives Zelensky 'winter support package' during visit to Netherlands: drones and air defence for Ukraine
lead: With Ukraine being bombarded almost every day by Russian drones and missiles, the Netherlands is coming to its aid with additional drones and air defence weapons. During a surprise visit to The Hague, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday that the support helps with 'saving lives'. "We need it to get through this winter."

title: Cabinet wants to keep the Brabant village of Moerdijk after all
lead: Moerdijk will continue to exist, that is the aim of the cabinet. According to State Secretary <entity id="person:jo-annes-de-bat">Jo-Annes de Bat</entity> (Climate), the idea of keeping the Brabant village after all is 'feasible'.

title: Part of tunnel in A28 rises again
lead: For the second time in almost three years, parts of the Vollenhoven tunnel on the A28 near Zeist are moving. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> is placing weights on the central reservation.

title: Italian Casasola beats Brand in Lokeren cyclo-cross
lead: Cyclist Sara Casasola has beaten reigning world champion Lucinda Brand in the HG Cross in Lokeren. The 26-year-old Italian crossed the finish solo after six laps, with a lead of well over half a minute over Brand.

title: Dutch government knew that underpayment of temp workers clashed with European rules
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity>-Rutte I deliberately and knowingly steered towards a dubious interpretation of European temp agency rules. As a result, millions of temp workers missed out on many billions of euros in income, while the temp agency sector enjoyed golden times.

lead: If renting or buying a home becomes unaffordable, we should ask ourselves, according to Leilani Farha: have we not given the financial sector too much power?

title: Trump: 'largely true' that the war on Iran is to blame for the Republican losses
lead: The Democrats score a huge victory over the Republicans, both in the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. It is a rebuke for Trump's Republican Party. Several states that normally colour 'deep red' are blue this time. Read back the liveblog about the midterms here.

title: Manchester City draw with Fulham after three defeats
lead: Manchester City has forgotten how to win in the Premier League. The club was held to a 1-1 draw in its home match against Fulham. In the preceding league matches City lost to Aston Villa (2-1), Brighton & Hove Albion (0-1) and Nottingham Forest (3-1).

title: Italian cyclo-cross rider Casasola also the best in Beringen
lead: BERINGEN (ANP/BELGA) - Cyclo-cross rider Sara Casasola has had an excellent weekend. The Italian won the BE-Mine Cross in Beringen on Sunday, the third race in the X2O Badkamers Trofee. On Saturday Casasola had already won the HG Cross in Lokeren.

title: Closing Time | Blue Aeroplanes
lead: Nineties nostalgia, although it turns out the Blue Aeroplanes still exist. At the time of this recording the band consisted of: a poet, a dancer, three guitarists, a bassist and a drummer. title: Have your say: care is more important than speed when you want to change tax rules
lead: The cabinet's plan to change the tax on wealth is shaky in the eyes of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. lead: ChristenUnie MP Pieter Grinwis has serious doubts about the new box 3 system the cabinet wants to introduce. According to him, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> is given insufficient time to assess the legislation carefully, while <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, the Dutch Banking Association and the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> all have strong criticism. title: Have your broken toy repaired or seize the chance to watch the best Idfa documentaries after all: what you can do this week in Amsterdam

lead: Next Monday and Tuesday there will be a full-day strike across much of the country in urban and regional transport. The strikes follow the collapse of collective labour agreement negotiations for the sector earlier this week.

lead: Jessica Alba must pay her ex-husband Cash Warren over half a million dollars as part of their divorce. The amount stems from a profit-sharing arrangement related to HonorBar, the company of the 45-year-old actress and entrepreneur.

title: Council of State: salt mining in Groningen may continue
lead: Salt may be extracted until 2045 in the villages of Borgercompagnie and Tripscompagnie in the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>. That was decided by the <entity id="org:afdeling-bestuursrechtspraak-raad-van-state">Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak van de Raad van State</entity>. The plan for the extraction of magnesium salt remains in place.

title: Kamerleden willen verbod op generatieve AI in basisscholen
lead: Kamerleden pleiten voor een verbod op AI-tools op Nederlandse basisscholen en stellen dat deze het vermogen van kinderen om zich te ontwikkelen bedreigen...

title: Toys from Temu, AliExpress, Wish and Shein examined: many not safe
lead: More than half of the toys examined by the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">NVWA</entity> that were sold on the webshops Temu, AliExpress, Wish and Shein are unsafe. Because parts could, among other things, come loose, there was a risk of choking for children during play.

title: Young women aged 30 to 40 are increasingly dropping out: 'The problems persist for a long time'
lead: An ever larger group of young women is unable to work for longer periods due to mental health complaints, warns the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>. Women between the ages of 30 and 40 in particular are affected. This trend has been visible for years, but a decline thus still seems a long way off. "It is a societal problem", says Ympkje Albeda, adviser to the <entity id="org:raad-voor-volksgezondheid-en-samenleving">Raad voor Volksgezondheid en Samenleving</entity>, on Spraakmakers.

lead: Asylum reception is a much debated and polarising issue. But never before has the king visited an asylum seekers' centre. In Leersum there is applause, cheering and the zaghrouta from dozens of women's throats.

lead: Supporters of sc Heerenveen smashed toilets and washbasins meant for visiting fans during Saturday's away match against FC Groningen. According to RTV Noord, the damage runs into the thousands of euros.

title: What do you want to know about the political crisis that has arisen in The Hague?
lead: Tensions in The Hague have risen sharply. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is wobbling after the agreement on the tax plans between D66 and CDA with PRO and Volt. title: Coalition agrees on box 3: one-year delay
lead: The leadership of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> and the coalition, after months of disagreement, are in agreement on the approach to box 3 and next year's tax plan, Hague sources say. lead: It seems only a matter of time before the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has all the suspects in the murder of Tico (19) from Schiedam behind bars. One of them is already in custody, and the names of the others are circulating. Meanwhile the authorities are on alert for revenge attacks. Also because the victim is said to have been connected to a notorious youth gang.

title: Code yellow in parts of the country due to locally dense fog
lead: In parts of the Netherlands a code yellow applies Sunday morning due to locally dense fog. The warning applies to the west and centre and later also to the north, reports the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> .

title: Petrol under 2 euros? At more than 100 petrol stations it is possible again
lead: Filling up with petrol has not been this cheap since early March. At more than a hundred petrol stations in the Netherlands it is now possible again to fill up for less than 2 euros per litre of Euro95, according to figures from the ANWB.

title: Smoke bomb thrower removed from FC Utrecht stadium before restart
lead: The person who threw the smoke bomb that halted the Eredivisie match between FC Utrecht and SC Cambuur on Saturday evening has been removed from the stadium. The KNVB and FC Utrecht have confirmed this. The match was halted after ten minutes of play. After a break of just over half an hour, the game resumed.

title: The coalition is still alive, crisis talks continue at the Catshuis tomorrow
lead: The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is surviving the weekend as well. The party leaders are trying to revive their cooperation. Work is still under way on a restart, but the possibility of a cabinet collapse also remains in the air.

title: Cabinet wants 350 million in tax relief, change to box 3 at the earliest in 2028
lead: The cabinet wants to set aside 350 million euros for tax relief. In addition, the introduction of the new box 3 plans will be postponed by one year. At the earliest the introduction will take place in 2028, and at the latest in 2029. Insiders told RTL Nieuws this.

lead: The <entity id="org:provincie-limburg">provincie Limburg</entity> is raising road tax the most sharply next year. The so-called opcenten there rise from 88.5 this year to 92 next year. As a result, the owner of an average petrol car will pay 28 euros more next year than now.

title: The cabinet's top has agreed on adjustments to the tax plan and still hopes for opposition support
lead: The cabinet's top has agreed on adjustments to the tax plan for next year. title: King couple visits Qatar on first state visit to the Middle East

title: After failed climate summit, criticism targets oil countries, but also Europe
lead: Great disappointment among climate coalitions and experts over the failed climate summit in the Turkish city of Antalya. The criticism is directed not only at oil-producing countries, which allegedly blocked a deal on phasing out fossil fuels, but also at the EU and other rich countries.

title: Court of Audit: central government must take the lead in protecting peat areas
lead: Things are going badly for the peat areas in the Netherlands. According to the National Audit Office, this is because many parties are involved in nature policy, and they sometimes have conflicting interests. The different layers of government must weigh those interests, but this does not always succeed. Central government, which spent well over 6 billion euros on nature management and restoration from 2014 to 2023, must therefore take the lead, the Audit Office believes.

title: Historic summit of Xi, Trump and Putin delivers little: 'It is all about symbolism'
lead: A historic meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The presidents of the three largest nuclear powers met around the table in China today. They discussed 'the problems in the world', but little concrete came out of it. "It is all about symbolism."

title: Senior police officials do not want measurable goals
lead: In 2027 almost 10 billion euros of tax money will go to the police. By law, the police must spend this budget efficiently. But in June the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Algemene Rekenkamer</entity> concluded that the police have little insight into what happens to the money. title: Fry up boiled potatoes: 'Even with mayo still healthier than eating boiled potatoes straight away'

New potato varieties are developed in the lab and research is done into sustainable cultivation. We spoke with several experts about how things really stand with the potato. It turns out: potatoes are super healthy and are on the rise worldwide. "They are an important energy source for the body."

title: Four girls die in Uganda after eating possibly poisonous oranges
lead: The Ugandan <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating the death of four girls at a school in the capital Kampala. They are presumed to have been poisoned, possibly by eating oranges.

lead: What do politicians really do behind the scenes? And how can you learn that as a newly minted councillor too? In her book 'De magie van de achterkamertjes', political coach Kiki Bakker uses seventeen interviews with (former) politicians to describe how things go in the council and parliament, and explains how to develop political savvy. 'Self-reflection is the most important quality of the politician.'

title: National government wants to reduce digital dependencies through procurement
lead: The national government wants to use its purchasing power more emphatically for digital autonomy and the continuity of public services. Joint ICT procurement, more room for European providers and better exit arrangements should reduce dependence on a limited number of technology companies. At the same time, the procurement organisation must work more simply and cheaply.

title: North Holland has already killed over 100,000 geese this year, more than in other years
lead: In the province of North Holland, a total of 100,291 geese were killed between February and the end of September, the Faunabeheereenheid (FBE) reports. That is considerably more than in previous years, says director Patty Laan. The province had already announced that the culling had to be doubled in order to significantly reduce the large goose population.

title: 'Miraculous recovery' ends up costing McDonald's employee dearly
lead: An employee of McDonald's has been rightly dismissed on the spot. He had reported sick and visited the company doctor in a wheelchair, because he would barely be able to move. However, an investigation by the company's investigation department showed that it was not as bad as that.

title: Herman Bröring looks back on settling Groningen damages: 'Those with the greatest needs are in the most difficult position'
lead: For years, professor Herman Bröring has been providing explanation on gas extraction in Groningen. Now that he is retiring, he cannot let the subject go. lead: Confidence in national politics is exceptionally low after a week of squabbling in The Hague over the tax plan. Only 13 percent of Dutch people have confidence, according to research by the RTL Nieuwspanel. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity>-Jetten fares no better, at 12 percent. title: Left and right-wing parties threaten to vote against the climate budget, without a 'total deal' on the tax plan

title: The time-varying influence of sectoral and macroeconomic labour market tightness on collective agreement wage growth
lead: Differences in staff shortages between sectors hardly lead to differences in collective agreement wage growth. Only when the labour market as a whole becomes very tight do collective agreement wages rise noticeably faster.

title: Alaska also turns blue: Democrats secure last Senate seat

lead: Tennis player Carlos Alcaraz has become the first to qualify for the final of the ATP Finals in Turin. The Spanish world number 3 beat American Ben Shelton on Saturday in the semi-final in three sets: 3-6 6-3 7-6 (1). title: KNMI issues code yellow, orange and red more locally: this changes for weather warnings
lead: From Monday 2 November, the KNMI will issue weather warnings in a different way. Code yellow, orange or red per province is a thing of the past. The KNMI now issues targeted and local warnings. This is what the KNMI is changing from 2 November.

title: Breakthrough in unsolved murder of Sjef thanks to commercial DNA databases

lead: Debt collection agencies are increasingly using algorithms and AI, according to a sample survey by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, AP) of 29 agencies.
