title: King and Prime Minister receive President Zelensky of Ukraine
Time is running out for cabinet: still no white smoke after another round of speed dates
lead: No breakthrough, no white smoke. A new round of talks with opposition parties has not yet produced a deal for the cabinet on the tax plans. And time is ticking on.

title: Coalition tensions rise: D66 wants to talk about millionaire tax, the VVD does not and points to 'the pain threshold'
lead: The protracted handling of the tax plan of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> enters a next episode that further increases the pain within the coalition. D66 is open to a plan by PRO and Volt to introduce an additional millionaire tax. The VVD does not and warns its coalition partners: "This proposal is unthinkable for us."

title: Jason Bhugwandass, who exposed abuses in youth care, dies aged 28
lead: Jason Bhugwandass (28) is no more. He became known for his struggle against abuses in closed youth care. With his report Eenzaam Gesloten, he brought serious abuses in heavily secured youth care wards to light as an experienced expert. Partly as a result of that report, these wards were permanently closed in 2024. The documentary Jason, which came out in 2021, also made a deep impression.

title: Digital billboards in Egypt hacked: porn instead of advertising
lead: Porn images appeared on billboards along an important highway in Egypt the day before yesterday. The work of hackers, says the Egyptian ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>.

title: Senate narrowly approves law that makes culturing embryos possible
lead: The Senate has approved a law that makes it possible for embryos to be created for scientific research. A majority of 38 of the 75 Senate members voted for the initiative bill defended by House of Representatives members Jan Paternotte (D66) and <entity id="person:hilde-wendel">Hilde Wendel</entity> (VVD).

title: Cabinet wants to cut costs on civil servants: 25,000 fewer in the coming years
lead: By 2035, 25,000 full-time civil servants fewer must work for the central government than is currently the case. That is what state secretary <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> (VVD, Slagvaardige Overheid) writes in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The cabinet wants to save a total of 3.5 billion euros in government.

title: Jorn (18) does not hesitate for a moment when he sees an elderly couple in a sinking car
lead: 18-year-old Jorn Kappert did not hesitate for a moment this morning when he saw that a car with two occupants had ended up in the water in Harlingen, Friesland. He took off his trousers and jumper and jumped into the cold water to help. "I thought: this is going to be really shit, but if I do nothing, these people will probably not survive it."

title: Extra Council of Ministers meeting this morning on tax plan and box 3
lead: An extra, unscheduled Council of Ministers meeting will be held this morning at 09.00. The meeting follows a day of frantic consultation at the top of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> about the problems that arose around the tax plan and box 3.

title: The Nota Ruimte sets out the rules for the redevelopment of the Netherlands, and everyone will be affected by it
lead: No more buildings in floodplains, room for nature restoration; the Nota Ruimte states that every square metre must be used as efficiently as possible.

title: Bags of cash, crypto and empty cartridges. How Russia uses one company to get roubles out of the country and evade sanctions
Live | Jetten and deputy prime ministers have been talking for over six hours about the future of the cabinet
lead: Hello and welcome to this live blog. Here we will keep you informed of political developments in The Hague.

title: Minority cabinet muddles on for a while longer, Buma becomes relationship therapist for the coalition
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> can postpone his visit to the king for a little while longer

title: Premier Jetten: “Serieuze nieuwe start” beter dan val van het kabinet te midden van coalitieonrust
lead: Minister-president <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> wil de huidige driepartijencoalitie intact houden.

title: Prosecution demands 12 years in prison for man who chopped his father's body into 238 pieces
lead: Thijmen V. chopped his father's body into 238 pieces after killing him, presumably with a Buddha figurine. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is now demanding twelve years in prison against the 33-year-old man from Heerhugowaard.

title: Hungarian speaker at Forum for Democracy congress previously in the spotlight for Hitler salute
lead: One of the speakers at the Forum for Democracy congress last Saturday, the Hungarian László Toroczkai, previously openly gave the Hitler salute in an Italian football stadium. In a TV interview in 2019 he himself did describe it as 'a Roman football salute', but according to experts he will not get away with that.

title: Millions of square metres of vacancy: why the approach by municipalities has stalled for years
lead: The Netherlands has 17.8 million square metres of vacant space, while there is a major housing shortage. And municipalities hardly do anything about those empty properties. Buildings such as offices, shops, churches and houses therefore remain largely unused.

title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day away in space: 25.9 billion kilometres
lead: In 1977 Voyager 1 set off to map the outer planets. And now, 49 years later, it has reached a milestone: the spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth. But what does that mean?

title: A broader picture of the 'angry citizen': experienced group disadvantage in various social domains
lead: INVESTIGATION - A guest contribution by Koen Damhuis (Utrecht University), Emily Miltenburg, Leonard van 't Hul and Sander Kunst (<entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau</entity>), previously published by Stuk Rood Vlees. In recent years much has been said and written about growing social discontent and waning political trust. A frequently cited explanation for what moves 'angry' citizens revolves around [...] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: LIVE US Midterms | Democrats take majority in Senate and probably also House, even Republicans lose in Texas
lead: Democrats are heading for a major victory in the American midterms. A Democratic majority in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> is already certain: even in the conservative states of Kansas, Texas and Ohio they received the most votes. A loss for the Republicans is also predicted in the House of Representatives. Follow everything about the midterms via our liveblog below.

title: Gambling on more
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> takes the ultimate gamble. The tax plan goes to parliament without a majority in advance.

title: Fire set at town hall, police pelted with heavy fireworks at grim asylum centre protest in Bunschoten
lead: Several dozen demonstrators gathered in Bunschoten around 20.00 hours to protest against the possible arrival of an asylum seekers' centre. During the protest, heavy fireworks were thrown at the police and a fire was set.

title: Jetten wants to 'keep talking firmly', crisis not yet averted
lead: After eight hours of talks with deputy prime ministers Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> (CDA), prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> (D66) gives a press conference. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> did not fall today, but the crisis is not yet averted.

title: OM employee suspected of election fraud is a D66 councillor in Boxtel
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> employee who was arrested on Tuesday is D66 councillor Sohib Hussain, well-informed sources tell NU.nl. The 38-year-old man from Boxtel is suspected of official corruption and election fraud.

title: These are the cabinet's new tax plans: extra purchasing power, postponement of box 3 and more money for care costs
lead: Whether the cabinet will get applause from the opposition is still a question, but the tax plans have once again been significantly reworked. Citizens' purchasing power will rise slightly, special care costs remain deductible and cut flowers will also remain in the low VAT rate next year. The box 3 solution is postponed by one year.

title: Belgium sees possible Iranian role in cyberattack on cooling installations
lead: After France, Belgium too sees indications of an Iranian role in the cyberattacks on cooling installations. That was announced by the Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> en Veiligheid Bernard Quintin. "Belgian security services too speak of indications of possible links with known Iranian actors. The federal prosecutor's office is investigating those indications further."

title: Scammers increasingly sophisticated with confidence tricks: already over 14,000 reports of fake police officers this year
lead: The number of reports of fraudsters posing as police officers continues to rise sharply. Up to and including October, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> had already recorded 14,176 incidents, surpassing the total for the whole of 2025 (13,000). This is apparent from police figures that <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> requested.

title: Fewer buildings converted into homes again
lead: For the fourth year in a row, fewer homes have been created by converting existing buildings such as offices and shops. This is reported by <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS). Last year a total of 6400 homes were created by transforming buildings. In 2024 that was still 7900, a decrease of 19 percent.

title: The SCP explains the gap: "Mbo-educated people more often see society as a battlefield"
The asylum inflow in week 47 was about 920
House of Representatives: no price increase for train tickets in 2027
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> must reverse the NS ticket price increase for next year of 4.7 per cent. That proposal from the Party for the Animals is supported by a majority in the House of Representatives.

title: Nederlandse delegatie drukt India om meer ontvoerde kinderen terug te geven, waaronder Insiya Hemani
lead: Een Nederlandse delegatie is deze week in India om aan te dringen op de terugkeer van ontvoer

title: If state secretary Boswijk has his way, women will also take part in the special forces: 'We simply need them badly'
lead: According to the coalition agreement, the number of employees at <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> must grow from 86,000 to 122,000, with a much larger share of women at all levels. For women in the special forces, a trial is starting.

title: National Ombudsman: government left farmers in uncertainty for years
lead: Farmers have had to deal with an unreliable government over the past ten years. The National Ombudsman reaches this conclusion in a report to be published on Wednesday. Changing rules and contradictory policy took a heavy toll on farm businesses and families.

title: Racehorse ends up dead in a rubbish skip in Australia: owner furious
lead: A video of a dead racehorse in a skip has caused an uproar in Australia. The owner of the award-winning horse, a breeder, calls it 'a disgrace' and says that 'heads must roll'.

title: Growing grumbling in Parliament over inadequate digital direction
lead: There is broad need across the House for coordination and direction in the digital domain, especially for cyber resilience. A passage on AI camera glasses was exemplary of the fragmentation, as became clear during the extensive legislative debate.

title: Gisèle Pelicot deeply shocked by nude photos her publisher sends with a book about her rape
State Secretary presents revised tax plan, opposition irritated
lead: State Secretary <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">Eelco Eerenberg</entity> (D66) will come next week with a new version of the tax plan. It must state what <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has heard from the opposition after a week of negotiating "and what we think should be adjusted". On Monday <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> debates all day with the Tweede Kamer about the tax plan, but that is still an older version.

title: Way out of cabinet crisis still a long way off
Finally make municipalities and provinces truly in charge of their own purse
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is saving money by giving municipalities more freedom in how they spend. Contradictory? Specific grants lead to bureaucracy. Municipalities also need to collect more taxes themselves.

title: FC Groningen to share footage after Heerenveen fans' vandalism
lead: FC Groningen is going to share video footage with sc Heerenveen relating to the vandalism in the away section of the Euroborg. A spokesperson for the Groningen football club says so. Heerenveen supporters smashed, among other things, toilets and washbasins during the 'Derby of the North' on Saturday.

title: The lobby of the wealthy is stronger than that of children like Anyssa
Police shoot robber in Rotterdam after he ignores warning shots
lead: Police have shot a person in Rotterdam. This happened after a robbery at a business premises by several masked men. When the suspects did not stop after police fired warning shots, shots were fired directly. One of the suspects was hit.

title: Live | Jetten to keep talking with coalition parties 'in complete calm' in the coming days
lead: Hello and welcome to this liveblog. Here we (Priscilla Slomp, Sanne Oving and Edo van der Goot) keep you informed of political developments in The Hague.

title: Dead animal with letter about wolf delivered to Oldebroek town hall
lead: A package containing a dead animal was delivered to the Oldebroek town hall yesterday afternoon. Enclosed was a letter addressed to the board about 'what we should or should not do in the context of the wolf', mayor <entity id="person:tanja-haseloop-amsing">Tanja Haseloop-Amsing</entity> said last night in a council meeting, which the Stentor reported on earlier.

title: Strukton gives in in lengthy case around The Hague's Hubertus tunnel, reopening imminent
lead: After a delayed renovation, construction company Strukton is reopening the Hubertus tunnel by 15 December at the latest. It is dropping additional financial demands under pressure from legal proceedings brought by the municipality.

title: Jetten not attending EU meeting due to extra debate on tax plan
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> will not attend the planned meeting of European Union heads of government in Dublin tomorrow and the day after tomorrow. A spokesperson says Jetten is skipping that meeting because of 'the current political situation'. Jetten has been asked to be in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> tomorrow morning for an extra debate on the tax plan.

title: This time bomb over money has been ticking within the cabinet since July
lead: D66 and CDA appear to be heading for a sharp clash with the VVD. Their deal on a millionaire tax is a sore point for the liberals. Yet the quarrel did not come out of nowhere: it had been smouldering since July. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> put out the flames at the time, but the conflict kept raging like a peat fire.

title: Limburg to investigate whether the world's longest-running festival becomes intangible heritage
lead: The <entity id="org:provincie-limburg">provincie Limburg</entity> will investigate whether Pinkpop can receive the status of Dutch intangible heritage. Within six months, it must also be examined how feasible it is to nominate the festival in the longer term for the International UNESCO List of Intangible Heritage.

title: VVD leader Yeşilgöz: minority cabinet is a failed experiment, 'we can't go on like this'
lead: Talks within the D66, VVD and CDA minority cabinet continue this weekend. That is what <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> said during a press conference after a day of hectic talks. The atmosphere of crisis in The Hague appears to be persisting unabated. Read back the events of Friday here.

title: The pattern of 'loose sand' at unstable Oranje forces coach Xavi to make a sweeping cultural change
lead: With the arrival of Xavi Hernández at the Dutch national team, a line seemed to have been drawn under the erratic period of his predecessor Ronald Koeman. But a painful match in Berlin revealed structural problems. "Show some honour."

title: Is Amalia being given preferential treatment at Defence? It depends on who you ask
lead: Princess Amalia was promoted to sergeant nine months after her appointment as corporal. Queen Máxima became lieutenant colonel directly after the reservist training. Are members of the Royal House promoted faster than others?

title: 'Doubling the number of speed cameras? Average speed checks would be better'
lead: The car journalists of the AD Auto Podcast are astonished at the announced doubling of the number of speed cameras in our country. "Being stopped on the spot by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has much more impact on your behavior than getting a fine sent to you afterwards," says Damiaan Hage, editor-in-chief of AutoWeek.

title: Californian governor commutes 548 death sentences to life imprisonment
Poland: Russian unmanned aircraft violates Polish airspace
lead: A Russian unmanned aircraft briefly violated Polish airspace last night during a Russian attack on western Ukraine. The Polish armed forces reported this on X.

title: Minister impressed by footage of intercepted drone
lead: The image of the drone being intercepted live on TV clearly shows how Ukraine is under constant fire from Russia. So says <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> (CDA). This happened during a live conversation with RTL reporter Chris Colijn after a drone strike at the Dutch embassy in Kyiv.

title: Tax bill saved at the expense of the coalition: future of the VVD in the cabinet uncertain
lead: Tax bill saved, coalition brought down. That is more or less the outcome of an unprecedentedly turbulent week in Den Haag politics. The tax bill, the cabinet's most important law for next year, was adopted by the smallest possible majority: 76 for, 74 against.

title: Support for tax plan remains highly uncertain: 'We are all in limbo'
lead: Two days before the votes, it is still unclear whether the tax plan has enough support to be passed by both the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. In a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, many parties and <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> say they hope it will succeed. But it is still unclear how the minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA will obtain sufficient support.

title: Live | Cabinet meeting begun, followed directly by press conference by Jetten on cabinet course
lead: Hello and welcome to this liveblog. Here political reporters Priscilla Slomp and Edo van der Goot will keep you informed of developments.

title: Britt (20) has 21 Christmas trees up in November
lead: 21 Christmas trees and more than 10,000 euros' worth of Christmas decorations. At Britt's home, Christmas is a serious business. Together with her parents, she makes the house completely ready for Christmas every year, including a special Christmas tradition.

title: Young women play prominent roles in Amsterdam liquidation cases: 'Does the driver know he is transporting hitmen?'
Sinterklaas does not bring joy to everyone: 'Financial worries make the celebration difficult'
lead: It is an exciting time for all children in the Netherlands, because Sinterklaas is back in the country. For many people this is a cosy time with shoes set out and presents under the chimney, but unfortunately this is not true for everyone. On Goed Ingelichte Kring, Maaike Timmerman speaks with Bernique Tool, director of Nationaal Fonds Kinderhulp, and Talina, a single mother of four children, about the financial challenges some families face and the effort it can take to pay for presents for the children during Sinterklaas.

title: Can the cabinet mend the breach of trust? 'The damage is very great'
lead: The Jetten cabinet has had a turbulent week. Bickering over a tax plan resulted in a crisis of confidence between coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD. Still, they are carrying on together. Can trust still be restored, or is it a stay of execution? Experts have their say.

title: Podcast | Right-wing extremism at FVD? 'It keeps coming back'
lead: A shocking documentary by Zembla revealed that FVD members are part of a neo-Nazi network. Meanwhile, the crisis in The Hague seems (for now) to have been averted. And rejected asylum seekers may have to go to a 'return hub' in Rwanda.

title: Extension of Fabel Friet's permit in Negen Straatjes upheld, court rules: 'Other catering businesses also have queues'
lead: The <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">gemeente Amsterdam</entity> properly extended the operating permit of Fabel Friet, in the popular Negen Straatjes, in April 2024. According to the court, residents have not sufficiently shown why the chip shop causes nuisance.

title: Designer Outlet Roermond: how a bargain village grew into a retail magnet
lead: Designer Outlet Roermond celebrates its 25th anniversary this weekend and in that time has grown into the largest outlet centre in Europe. Each year more than 8 million visitors come, about half of them from Germany. What is the secret of the outlet centre, and does the growth not come at the expense of Roermond's city centre?

title: Senate agrees: national government takes over funding of local broadcasters from municipalities
lead: Local public broadcasters will receive their basic funding directly from the national government from 2028. The Eerste Kamer has agreed to a new broadcasting system, in which the number of broadcasters falls from over 200 to a maximum of 80. The available budget structurally rises from approximately 13 million to 31 million euros.

title: Buma may decide for himself how to advise on the minority cabinet
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> gives vice-president <entity id="person:sybrand-van-haersma-buma">Sybrand Buma</entity> of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> a free hand in advising on better relations between the minority cabinet and the opposition. "The content and organisation of your work is entirely up to you", the prime minister writes in a letter to Buma sent today.

title: Mail carrier and emergency services lose their way because of this crazy house numbering in Soest
lead: Parcel couriers have been dropping off their packages at one address for years, because they are desperate over the house numbering of twenty newly built homes on Ferdinand Huycklaan in Soest. The municipal council is now getting involved with the unfindability of those houses.

title: Mother of Tim (31), who died, angry at Tarwekamp suspects: 'Do you realise what has happened?'
lead: It is a heavy day at the court in The Hague, where the next of kin of the victims of the fatal explosion on the Tarwekamp today tell what they have been through. Other people involved, for example entrepreneurs, may also speak. Six people died, and four others were seriously injured but narrowly survived.

title: Anthropic's share gains fade, bigger AI worries remain
lead: The share of AI company Anthropic closed well over 17 percent higher on Thursday at its stock market debut on the American Nasdaq. That halved the initial gain: the share had opened 34 percent up yesterday.

title: Volt party leader Dassen calls on D66 and CDA not to let themselves be 'blackmailed' by the VVD
lead: Volt party leader Laurens Dassen made an appeal to governing parties D66 and CDA at the party congress on Saturday: "Don't let the VVD blackmail you any more." Dassen was referring to…

title: On Sunday mornings Harry Mens likes to read you the newspaper headlines
lead: Our TV critic currently has newspaper headlines read to her by Harry Mens on Sunday mornings, but she is open to other rituals.

title: Coalition crisis in The Hague: cabinet hangs by a thread, VVD angry at D66 and CDA
It could happen this winter: power outage around the city of Utrecht or Flevopolder
lead: It could happen this coming winter: a power outage around the city of Utrecht or in the Flevolder due to an overloaded electricity grid. That is stated in the new letter to parliament from State Secretary <entity id="person:jo-annes-de-bat">Jo-Annes de Bat</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kgg">Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity>, who gives an update on the FGU region every six months. This is the region in the Netherlands with the most pressing grid congestion: <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity>, Utrecht and the Flevolder.

title: Male victims of sexual violence hardly report it because of the police's 'negative' attitude. 'Too much emotion is not manly, too little is not victim-like'
lead: Men who have been sexually abused report to the police even less often than women. Complainants describe contact with the police as 'discouraging' and sometimes outright 'hostile', police research shows. "If you show a lot of emotion as a man, you are not manly enough."

title: Flevoland influenced elections to get Lelystad Airport opened and lied about it
lead: The province of Flevoland influenced the recent municipal council elections with newspaper advertisements to open Lelystad Airport, documents requested by FTM show. The provincial executive had previously denied deliberately conducting the campaign during the elections.

title: Dutch police arrest man for false bomb threat, flight to Prague
Pro and D66 want to end the stacking of political positions. That mainly affects PVV and Forum voor Democratie
Cabinet, introduce a nationwide ban on advertising that is harmful to the climate
Dutch couple sentenced to years in prison for joining IS and bringing back a baby
lead: A Dutch couple was sentenced on Tuesday for participation in the terrorist organisation Islamic State (IS), preparation of terrorist offences, and leaving their child helpless in Syria. The mother receives a reduction in sentence so that she can care for the children.

title: Walking out of class in protest: what young people say about conscription
lead: Across the Netherlands and beyond, young people demonstrated today against conscription and the militarisation of education. They believe defence spending could be better spent on other social provisions.

title: The brick-laying robots are hidden: homes from a factory
lead: What is happening here at a large housing factory on the Hearrenfeanster Kanaal, on an industrial estate in <entity id="org:gemeente-heerenveen">Heerenveen</entity>, is the necessary future. That is what the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-vro">Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening</entity> (VRO) thinks, what the housing association umbrella organisation Aedes thinks, what administrators in <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> think, and what the big construction companies of the Netherlands think.

title: Limburg benefits from facilities across the border, but misses opportunities
lead: Residents of Limburg municipalities benefit most from facilities across the border. That is shown by the new version of the Atlas voor gemeenten, published by Atlas Research. But the potential across the border is not automatically used. Especially when it comes to jobs, the gap between potential and use is large: while in <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity> two thirds of the reachable jobs are to be found in Germany and Belgium, only 1 percent of Maastricht residents work abroad.

title: National campaign Nieuwe Energie calls on the Dutch to avoid electricity peak
VVD against PRO: 'Am I supposed to put up with you calling me far-right?'
lead: The plan for a deportation centre in Rwanda opens the door to the far right, said PRO MP Lisa Westerveld in the debate on the asylum budget. Right-wing parties reacted indignantly to that remark. "Are you really calling me far-right?"

title: Trump punished at midterms: Democrats reclaim House and Senate
lead: The Democrats have won both <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> and the House of Representatives in the US midterms. The party won a majority in typically Republican states such as Texas and South Carolina. President Donald Trump says he accepts the loss.

title: These farmers want to look after nature, but still have great difficulty with the nitrogen plans. 'If you look at it closely, it simply doesn't make sense'
lead: Actually they should be considered the epitome of the reforming agricultural sector: the organic farmers. They have an eye for nature and do not use artificial fertiliser or concentrated feed. Yet they find the new nitrogen policy threatening.

title: The British are back in Brussels to make agreements
lead: Proudly, British Prime Minister Burnham shows how he has tightened ties with the European Union. Trade in food is becoming simpler, young people can more easily cross over to the other side, and CO2 levies are being streamlined.

title: A winning formula for a minority cabinet? Visiting Scandinavia, MPs see how it can also work
Across the border: Not just dog poo, but also wiping away urine
lead: Dog owners in the Italian city of Livorno must not only bring poo bags, but also a bottle of water. With it they must rinse their dog's urine off pavements, street furniture and even car tyres. The municipality introduced the rule in May for the summer months. In September it decided that it will become permanent policy of the municipality of Livorno.

title: Elbow work is now visible everywhere: 'Trump 2.0 is increasingly looking like Trump 1.0'
Cabinet continues talks with opposition at Catshuis on Saturday
Nearly 1,000 kilometre tailback: second-busiest morning rush hour of the year
lead: Traffic is again very heavy on the roads. Around 08.00 there were roughly 1000 kilometres of traffic jams, according to the ANWB. That makes it the second-busiest morning rush hour of the year.

title: Coalitiepartijen willen tegen elkaar stemmen over belastingplannen
lead: De regerende coalitiepartijen hebben laten weten dat zij bij amendementen op het belastingplan 2027 mogelijk tegen elkaar zullen stemmen voordat...

title: Cabinet looks at its own role after chaos: 'Time for less The Hague fuss'
lead: The cabinet is taking "the blame on itself" and acknowledges that it must do things differently. According to Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity>, it is time for "less The Hague fuss and internal discussion and more calm and clarity".

title: Will more homeless people come to Amsterdam? Right-wing parties are afraid they will
Belongings of missing kitesurfer (18) found, search ends
lead: In the search for the missing kitesurfer near Scheveningen, belongings of the kitesurfer have been found. Among other things the kiteboard and the kite have been found, reports the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>.

title: Avian flu confirmed again in Hierden
Bomb threats and warming freezers: are the Russians behind it? 'We are only seeing the tip of the iceberg'
lead: Bomb threats at dozens of aircraft, warming freezers in European supermarkets and threats against Irish and British media: are the Russians behind it? That increasingly seems to be the case, says intelligence expert and former <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> officer Tim Bos in Dit is de dag (EO).

title: Nore (22) gets 2119 euro per month, does not go out and drinks no alcohol: 'I always look at the price'
Pieter Baan Centre examines woman (34) who allegedly poisoned her partner
lead: The 34-year-old Maxime A., suspected of poisoning her partner, is being examined at the Pieter Baan Centre (PBC). This emerged at a new preliminary hearing at the court in The Hague.

title: Coalition written off: D66 and CDA do not give in after VVD power play
lead: After months of fruitless negotiations between <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> and the opposition, unity within the coalition has definitively fallen apart. PRO has wriggled its way between D66 and CDA on one side and the VVD on the other. Carrying on without any damage is no longer an option.

title: Child of married couple no longer automatically receives father's name
Bayern Munich drop points and lose Kane and Olise
lead: Bayern Munich were unable to celebrate the return of coach Vincent Kompany to the bench with a win. The Bundesliga leaders could only draw 1-1 against lowly-placed FC Köln. Harry Kane and Michael Olise were forced off with injuries at Bayern.

title: Dead and seriously injured after collision with a train in Eindhoven: 'Fatal accident'
lead: Two men were hit by a train shortly after 00.30 last night. One of them, a 49-year-old man from the <entity id="org:gemeente-leudal">gemeente Leudal</entity>, died on the spot. A 37-year-old man from Belgium was seriously injured and is in hospital. Police assume it was a fatal accident.

title: Jetten, Yeşilgöz and Van den Brink arrive at De Zwaluwenberg
How agricultural knowledge from Wageningen can contribute to the suppression of Uyghurs
lead: In the Chinese region of Xinjiang, Dutch scientists are working on optimising agricultural production. They are doing so together with scientists from the XPCC, a powerful paramilitary organisation that is increasingly appropriating farmland and harshly suppressing Uyghurs and other minorities.

title: LIVE Coalition crisis | Coalition resuscitation attempt continued this morning, Jetten cabinet hanging by a thread
lead: The survival of the Jetten cabinet is at stake if the coalition partners meet again on Sunday for political crisis talks. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> still wants to carry on, but Dilan Yesilgöz (VVD) is gloomy and calls the minority cabinet 'a failed experiment'. In this liveblog we will follow the latest developments throughout the day.

title: Rotterdam-West directs road cyclists, moped riders and fatbikes to the carriageway: 'Many conflicts on the bike path'
lead: Think you're enjoying your bike ride, only to be nearly knocked off your feet by a fatbike... To prevent this, in Rotterdam-West road cyclists, moped riders and fatbikers are now being directed to the carriageway. "There were a lot of conflicts," says alderman Chantal Zeegers.

title: Contrary to expectations, more students are enrolling at universities of applied sciences and universities, thanks to MBO students and international students
When the market fails: Kidney Foundation and health insurers develop new artificial kidney themselves
lead: Because companies were not willing to invest in a portable dialysis device, the Kidney Foundation and health insurers decided to innovate and develop it themselves. The artificial kidney is in the final testing phase.

title: This is how games studio Rockstar wants to squeeze every euro out of GTA 6
lead: Gamers have had to wait for years, but tonight GTA 6 finally arrives. The game reportedly cost 1.5 billion dollars to make. But with over 15 million gamers having already pre-ordered the game, games developer Rockstar has already earned back its investment before the official launch.

title: After hallelujah over plastic, Rijkswaterstaat scratches its head
Eerste sneeuwvlokken van het seizoen gespot in Eindhoven; mist en ijs hinderen vluchten
lead: De eerste sneeuwvlokken van het seizoen zijn gevallen. Rond Eindhoven maandagavond ging het mistige weer, dat bij Eindhoven Airport tot meerdere annuleringen leidde, over in sneeuw.

title: Car in the water, Jorn jumps in after it: 'Otherwise they wouldn't survive'
lead: The 18-year-old Jorn does not hesitate for a moment when he sees a car with an elderly couple in the water in Harlingen. He jumps into the cold water and, together with another man, manages to rescue the couple. "Fortunately, those people are doing well."

title: Live | Jetten: 'This cabinet is neither deaf nor blind to criticism'
lead: Hello and welcome to this liveblog. Here, we (Priscilla Slomp and Edo van der Goot) keep you updated on the debate about the cabinet's tax plan.

title: Heinen expects support for tax plan: 'Good talks with CU, 50PLUS, Groep Markuszower'
lead: In the search for support for the tax plan in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, the minority cabinet has held 'good talks' with the ChristenUnie, 50PLUS and the Groep Markuszower. <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> said this during the weekly conversation with the <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> on RTL Z, when asked which opposition parties support the tax plan of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>.

title: Steering on IT costs? Many executives have no idea how
lead: As an economist and IT specialist, Maarten Jonker notices that IT is a difficult file in the boardroom. As CTO and CIO in government and in business he saw executives struggle time and again with bringing IT costs down. He decided to write a book about it together with Marc Welters, chair of NOREA, the professional organisation of IT auditors, with the fitting title 'Grip on IT: from cost item to management choice'.

title: The grainy photos of Bontenbal with Denk are now being held against the CDA
lead: What drives Henri Bontenbal? The CDA leader has always been regarded as a more left-leaning CDA member, and now he is also opting for a deal with DENK. The criticism is fierce. But there is a story behind Bontenbal's choice, and a measure of vexation, says political reporter Niels Klaassen, who has followed the CDA leader ever since he entered politics.

title: These neighbours save 50,000 euros by sharing their parking spaces
lead: In the Utrecht neighbourhood De Nieuwe <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> residents share their own parking spaces in parking garages with neighbours and acquaintances via the LokaalParkeren app. If they do not use their space, someone else can reserve it temporarily.

title: Owner of bridal fashion shop to suspects: "You should be deeply ashamed"
lead: The owner of the bridal fashion shop, and the intended target of the attack, has spoken out in court. In doing so she addressed the suspects directly.

title: SC Cambuur beat FC Utrecht in match halted by smoke bomb
lead: SC Cambuur won their away match against FC Utrecht in the Eredivisie 3-2. With the victory, Cambuur have for now climbed to eighth place in the standings with 18 points. FC Utrecht sit fifteenth with 12 points after a disappointing start to the season.

title: Coalition leaders to continue talks on Sunday at estate about cabinet crisis
lead: The coalition leaders are expected to continue talks on Sunday at the De Zwaluwenberg estate about the political crisis that has arisen, a spokesperson for Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> reports. The coalition talks got under way on Saturday at the Hilversum estate.

title: Ukraine's hospitality sector held out for a long time, but now it is going quiet in the cafés of Kyiv
lead: Ukraine's hospitality sector is feeling the effects of the heavy Russian air attacks. 'In five years of war it has never been this difficult.'

title: After consultation with farmers, the cabinet postpones new nitrogen plans 'a few days'. 'We need to dot the i's and cross the t's'
Entrepreneur Diederik Beker: 'In the Netherlands we are not bound by traditions'
lead: Diederik Beker (42) is founder of the Betuws Wijndomein in Erichem. The first ten years were pioneering. 'You can't be stocked at HEMA with your wine and at a restaurant with a star.'

title: Cabinet crisis not over yet: parties keep talking at estate in Hilversum
lead: The political crisis in <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is far from over. Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> and the leaders of coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA continue talking from 11.00 about the future of the cabinet. They are doing so at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum. The parties are still diametrically opposed, says political reporter Fons Lambie.

title: Man sentenced to ten years in prison for imprisoning and raping two women
lead: The <entity id="org:rechtbank-amsterdam">rechtbank Amsterdam</entity> has sentenced a 34-year-old man to ten years in prison for raping, robbing and imprisoning two women in the capital. The assaults took place earlier this year.

title: Pupils and students walk out of class against conscription: 'Nothing is being invested in us'
lead: In at least sixteen cities, pupils and students are leaving their school or lecture hall at 13.00 today. They are protesting against a possible return of conscription and for 'an affordable future'. "War is not flashy", says Evy Kras of the Landelijke Studentenvakbond, who is taking part in the action.

title: Climate summit crucial for islands: Dutch lawyer plays key role
lead: What is agreed at the climate summit in Turkey is vital for an island group in the Pacific Ocean. Residents see the sea creeping ever further inland. In their fight against climate change a Dutch lawyer plays a key role, who is also in Antalya these days.

title: Measures after the violent death of Tico (19) and two explosions in Schiedam
lead: Residents of Schiedam are deeply shaken after the violent death of 19-year-old Tico and two subsequent explosions. Cameras will be placed in the affected neighbourhood, reports mayor <entity id="person:harald-bergmann">Harald Bergmann</entity> of Schiedam in a letter to the municipal council. "These cameras are being deployed to better monitor the area", he writes.

title: Deputy ambassador in Kyiv on drone impact: 'Very intense'
lead: A Russian drone came down behind the Dutch embassy in Kyiv on Thursday. The deputy ambassador in Kyiv, Joop Nijssen, was in the building at the time and, in an exclusive interview with RTL Nieuws, describes how he and his staff experienced the drone impact

title: Land war between municipalities and housing developers to be settled with new calculation method, housing minister hopes
'We need to talk and think more about child sexual abuse'
lead: For thirty years Iva Bicanic has campaigned against child sexual abuse. She first did so as a psychologist and director of the National Centre for Sexual Violence. Since the end of last year she has been professor of Sexual abuse of children: consequences and treatment. On Thursday she gives her inaugural lecture, 'Giving silence a voice'. With this, her chair officially begins. Research by Bicanic shows that children on average stay silent for fourteen years about the abuse they have experienced. With her research she hopes to bring about change in this.

title: Give female entrepreneurs a platform, or they will not be seen
lead: When <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> discusses start-ups, female entrepreneurs are not mentioned. Yet those very women can be a strong driver of economic growth.

title: A new pre-mbo track in Groningen for students who have gotten stuck. 'My parents and I immediately thought: this is what I have to do'
lead: Small classes of ten students and intensive guidance. In Groningen, a new pre-mbo track targets young people who are still subject to compulsory education but cannot find their feet in vocational education (mbo). "You have to approach all participants differently."

title: Searching the brain better than ever thanks to software from Delft researchers
lead: The human brain contains many billions of cells. Scientists are building an atlas to map all those cells. The first part is finished. It shows 21 million cells in their interconnected context.

title: Facial scanner gains ground, but figures on the scale of fraud are lacking
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is working on a legal basis for the use of facial scanners when applying for a travel document or identity card. More than half of municipalities already use automatic facial comparison for identity verification on their own initiative. But nobody knows how big the problem of passport application fraud at the municipal counter really is.

title: Is Britain ready for net-zero migration?
lead: Getting what you want isn't all it's cracked up to be.

lead: The coalition maintains during the eight-hour debate that mutual trust has been 'restored'. But the opposition does not believe it at all. The relations between D66, VVD and CDA still appear exactly the same as before the crisis. And that bodes ill.

title: Tackling debts without fear of the bailiff
lead: It is a nightmare for people in the Netherlands with debts: the bailiff standing on the doorstep with yet another claim. But that is going to change. Because if someone with problematic debts asks for help later on, for example at the municipality, they no longer need to fear bailiffs.

title: Former Finance Ministry employee has solution for stalled tax system: 'Fix the technology first, then there is a chance of success'
lead: Former civil servant Oscar Schouw of the Finance Ministry outlines a data-driven tax system on which politicians should be able to agree.

title: Stay engaged with the Sahel, our important neighbouring region

lead: Kenyan marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir (33) has been suspended for three years for doping. The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) has announced this. Traces of the banned substance EPO were found in her blood.

title: Aldermen want help from central government to tackle crack problem
lead: Aldermen want help from central government to tackle problems surrounding crack addiction. Manouska Molema (<entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>) and Alexander Scholtes (<entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>) made this clear on Wednesday in a discussion with MPs about the growing use of crack in the Netherlands.

title: Why the failure of the climate summit could be a 'wake-up call'
lead: Quarrelling, finger-pointing, chaos and no joint final declaration: the climate summit in Turkey was historic, but not in a positive sense. Yet the hard clash between countries does not necessarily have to mean only bad news for the climate.

title: Male prostitution hugely popular, police worried: 'Hidden world'
lead: Male sex workers are hugely popular. Yet the police are rarely tipped off about abuses. Detective Suzanne sees that when clients are in a dubious situation, they are more likely to write a bad review than call for help.

title: Karin (59) once wanted to become mayor, but long covid makes working impossible: 'That is what I miss most'
lead: Karin Lambrechts (59) used to work from early in the morning until late at night. Now her life runs on a battery of at most three hours because of long covid. The upcoming cuts from <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> frustrate her, especially when she thinks of her younger fellow sufferers. "How are they supposed to go on now?"

title: After Fortuyn and Omtzigt, the shutters in The Hague close a little further again
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> nearly fell, so the coalition is reaching for a familiar recipe: the Torentjesoverleg is back! Controversial after Pim Fortuyn and Pieter Omtzigt, but at least useful. Because a new governing culture sounds fresh, until every difference of opinion turns into a crisis. Political correspondent Hans van Soest writes weekly about Hague affairs that concern us all.

title: From 'acquired right' to mandatory office days: this Booking ruling could help employers across the Netherlands
lead: May you require employees to work 40 percent of their time in the office? Yes, the court now says in a case between Booking and its own works council. And that could also have consequences for other workplaces. "Employers facing the same situation will certainly invoke it."

title: Provinces and water boards struggle with archiving emails and chats
lead: Provinces and water boards often have not yet arranged the management of emails and chat messages. Many requests under the Open Government Act (Woo) are also not handled within the set time limit. This is shown by new monitors from the <entity id="org:ipo">Interprovinciaal Overleg</entity> (IPO) and the Unie van Waterschappen.

lead: The province of Noord-Holland invites its residents to help create a new and contemporary song 'for and by all North Hollanders'. Until and including 30 November, anyone can answer in three words the question on the province's website: What do you think of when you think of Noord-Holland?

lead: What digital developments are currently taking place and what policy choices is our organisation making? These are questions to which most governments can at best give only a partial answer. And plug-in vehicles could make the armed forces less dependent on fossil fuels. But for now the diesel engine still wins on range. So it will be a while before more Fenneks are converted.

title: CPB: few indications of effects of the subsidy scheme for improving basic skills
lead: The CPB is publishing the final evaluation of the subsidy scheme for improving basic skills. Since 2022, this scheme has given schools temporary additional funds for measures from the Masterplan for Basic Skills. We examined the effects on learning outcomes and on the deployment of education staff in primary and secondary education. Overall, we find few indications of effects.

lead: A new history of confiscation sheds light on modern economic warfare.

lead: The Utrecht Provincial States have agreed to changes to the environmental vision and environmental regulation, which also include standards for nitrogen emissions. title: One in five employees is mentally exhausted from work. 'Jobs have become more complex'
lead: The number of employees who are mentally exhausted by their job has almost doubled over the past ten years, according to the National Working Conditions Survey. After flu, mental health complaints are the main reason for sick leave. "When people become ill due to stress complaints, they are often out of action much longer than with a bout of flu," says <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-organisatie-voor-toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk-onderzoek">TNO</entity> researcher Noortje Wiezer.

lead: A 23-year-old Dutch national was seriously injured on Sunday after being assaulted in the German town of Schüttorf, just across the border near Enschede. The man was chased by a group of people. He was then kicked and beaten. German police report this today.

lead: How long does it take before a vulnerable fridge connected to the internet is hacked? Less than six hours and a flood of unrelated other hacking attempts later, the thermostat of NRC's fake supermarket had already been turned up by half a degree.

title: SGP, JA21 and BBB form bloc with hard demands: why this could backfire for the right
lead: Opposition parties JA21, BBB and the SGP say they support the tax plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, but they only do so if all their conditions are met. The deadline is Monday, so with these demands they are putting up the pressure.

lead: <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-organisatie-voor-toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk-onderzoek">TNO</entity> ranks seventh among research institutes in Europe with 142 patent applications in 2025.

title: Xi Jinping's plan for a China-centric world order
lead: A 'community with a shared future' sounds soft, but is backed by muscle.

title: Cyclist Roglič (37) moves to NSN Cycling
lead: BERN (ANP/DPA) - Cyclist Primož Roglič will ride for the Swiss team NSN Cycling next year. The contract of the 37-year-old Slovenian with Red Bull-Bora-hansgrohe expired after three years.

title: FC Twente stay top of the Women's Eredivisie, Ajax also win
lead: FC Twente remain top of the Women's Eredivisie after the eleventh round too. The record champions won 1-0 away at Feyenoord on Sunday and now have 25 points. Ajax are the new number 2 and, after a 5-0 win over De Graafschap, also have 25 points. PSV drew 0-0 at home to PEC Zwolle and are now third with 23 points.

title: When does sabotage by Russia become an act of war? 'NATO deliberately keeps the line unclear'
lead: Russia is no longer the aggressor, but 'our enemy'. The House of Representatives debates tonight the words of minister Dilan Yeşilgöz and the Russian threat. Are we then also at war? "That we are not at war does not mean we are living in peace."

title: The company went bankrupt and mistakes were made, but it was not improper management
lead: The two directors let the company's debts rise too high and filed annual accounts late. The trustee holds them liable for the bankruptcy of the interior design company. The court weighs the matter differently.

title: Before the demonstration even begins, police already step in: 'We never take sides'
lead: An announced Gen Z protest by young people was recently reason enough to put The Hague city centre on the highest level of readiness. Behind the scenes, the police scour thousands of social media posts every day. Anyone who crosses the line into criminal conduct online can sometimes be arrested even before a demonstration has begun.

title: LIVE Midterms VS | Supreme Court rejects Trump's bid to stop ballots in California from being counted
lead: Americans are preparing for the midterms, which could significantly change the balance of power in Congress. Residents vote on Tuesday for the House of Representatives, <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">De Senaat</entity>, governors and local representatives. Follow everything about the midterms via our liveblog below.

title: Verstappen sets thirteenth time in second practice session in Las Vegas
lead: Max Verstappen set the thirteenth time in the second free practice session for the Las Vegas Grand Prix. In the first practice session no times were recorded. The drivers could not go flat out due to the heavy rainfall.

title: Van de Zandschulp and Griekspoor end tennis year in top 50
lead: Tennis players Botic van de Zandschulp and Tallon Griekspoor have ended the tennis season in the top 50 of the world rankings. The 31-year-old Van de Zandschulp is the best Dutch tennis player in fortieth place. Griekspoor (30) is number fifty.

title: 'We are on the American AI drip'
lead: The Dutch <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>-Jetten is on the brink of falling, and this is not going unnoticed in Europe either. The departure of Dick Schoof was followed with great astonishment in Europe, but what if <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> holds on even less long?

title: Eliminating racism and discrimination from the world? Couson, Ava and Xer know how
lead: The UNESCO world summit against racism and discrimination is taking place in The Hague. There is therefore still much 'work to do', warned prime minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity>. Because it is something that many children still have to deal with.

title: FNV members vote down final offer in regional transport, strikes threaten
lead: The rank and file of the FNV union have not accepted the final offer that employers in regional transport put forward for a new collective labour agreement. This makes new strikes in public transport seem imminent. CNV members are still considering the proposal.

title: Most nitrogen rules survive political pressure from the cabinet, House majority for the plans
lead: According to Minister of Agriculture <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">Jaimi van Essen</entity>, the cabinet is 'on the right track towards a strong and sustainable agricultural sector, restoring nature and getting permit granting moving'.

title: Iran feels strengthened by Trump's defeat at the ballot box, and the US is reacting nervously
lead: The US and Iran both gambled in recent months that they could economically exhaust the other. But both countries held out. Meanwhile, escalation of violence seems likely again.

title: Dentist allowed neo-Nazi cage fights, now his professional association suspends him

lead: The debate on the tax plan of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> did not produce a breakthrough on Wednesday evening. Negotiations must take place behind closed doors again between coalition and opposition. New danger also threatens D66, VVD and CDA. The parties are divided among themselves over a plan for a millionaire tax.

title: Nitrogen plans overhauled: provinces make their own plan for vulnerable nature
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has adjusted the nitrogen plans on a few points after consultation with farmers' organisations. In the zones around vulnerable nature areas there will be room for tailored measures, and the calculation lower limit will be introduced half a year earlier.

lead: Oil and gas markets will continue to function even if almost no oil and gas flows to the rest of the world via the Strait of Hormuz. Although work is under way on alternatives, this shift 'will not be simple or quick'.

title: We agree. But on what?
lead: What do we expect from the National Investment Institution (NII)? Helping companies with financing, tackling societal challenges, or binding the government to long-term policy? CPB economist Jurre Thiel explains why the goal must first be clear: that determines what the institution will look like.

Booking may require employees to return to the office
lead: Travel platform Booking.com may require employees to come back to the office. According to the court in Amsterdam, it is not unreasonable to require employees to be in the office for 40 percent of working hours. "A lot of other employers are watching this with great interest."

title: Why is the redistribution of the municipal fund so complex?
lead: Once again, the plans to arrive at a new distribution of the billions from the municipal fund were postponed this spring. What makes the 'recalibration' so complex? The ambitions are very large, says <entity id="org:raad-voor-het-openbaar-bestuur">ROB</entity> member Peter Verheij.

lead: A man ran at King Willem-Alexander on Friday afternoon during his visit to the North Holland village of Ursem. He was then calmed down by the king.

title: Action must pay 15.000 euros to wrongfully dismissed pregnant woman

lead: Djuna Farjon on the accommodating attitude of the Amsterdam municipality towards arms manufacturer Thales

lead: The number of employees suffering from psychological complaints has risen sharply over the past ten years. The increase is stronger among women than among men, according to the National Working Conditions Survey (NEA) of the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) and <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-organisatie-voor-toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk-onderzoek">TNO</entity>.

title: Tax plan appears headed for debate in House of Representatives without a majority
lead: There is a real chance that the minority cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA will have to submit the Tax Plan for 2027 to the House of Representatives without a secured majority.

title: Code yellow again due to dense fog, warning applies to almost the entire country

The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> reports in the night from Monday to Tuesday that the chance of fog is spreading to more places. lead: The Netherlands will have many heirs in the coming decades who will receive large sums in their accounts. They run a greater risk of becoming victims of fraud, warns <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">Autoriteit Financiële Markten</entity> (AFM). The shift in wealth also causes more inequality on the housing market.

title: New rules for holiday rentals from 1 November 2026
Halsema makes appeal in India for kidnapped girl Insiya: 'Mama can reach you'
lead: Mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity> is making an appeal via Instagram to draw attention to the case of the kidnapped Insiya. The girl was abducted by her father from <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> in September 2016, when she was 2 years old. She has been living in India since then.

title: Fierce opposition to Rwanda plan for rejected asylum seekers: 'Inhumane and dangerous'
lead: Aid organisations are fiercely opposed to the plan for a so-called return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. MEP Tineke Strik (PRO) is also critical. The European CDA and VVD, by contrast, support the plan.

title: Sweden does not want Russian athletes at the Nordic skiing World Championships
lead: STOCKHOLM (ANP/AFP) - The Swedish government, like Finland and Norway, does not want to see Russian athletes competing within the country's borders. "We do not intend to turn Sweden into a platform for Russian war propaganda, or for attempts to normalise their illegal war of aggression in Ukraine", said Minister of Migration Johan Forssell during a press conference.

title: 7 screens in the car: Australian motorist gets fine
lead: A motorist in Australia must pay a fine of around 700 dollars (420 euros) after police found a very unusual setup on and around his dashboard. The man had as many as seven screens at his disposal, including one on which he could watch YouTube videos.

title: Integrity centre for sport is further away than ever; Council of State criticises bill
Data center protest: a blue caterpillar clashes with police. 'We are only building so that Big Tech can earn incredible amounts of money'
lead: Activists occupy the construction site on Friday where a controversial data center is to rise in Amsterdam. "We want a moratorium on the construction of new data centers across all of Europe."

title: 'I think almost every coach of a top club is on the verge of being overworked.' Football coaches talk about their exhausting existence
lead: Vincent Kompany is back as coach of Bayern Munich, after collapsing on the pitch. Coaches and psychologists talk about the workload at the top of football, a theme that was long underexposed. "Now and then I come close to madness."

title: Water board tax up again by tens of euros
lead: The water board tax will again rise by a few tens of euros next year for households with an owner-occupied home. For tenants, the tax also rises by an average of 7 percent, and for farmers and nature managers by 7.5 percent. The Association of Water Boards expects this based on the proposals on the table in the 21 water boards. They are setting their rates for 2027 in these weeks.

title: Is there hope for the cabinet? There are reasons why the tax plan may still pass
lead: Once again the cabinet is reworking its tax plans, hoping to still win support from opposition parties. They are grumbling, but note that they are not closing the door completely either. Three reasons why the cabinet could still succeed.

title: Is Sint-Maarten also celebrated in your municipality? See the map
lead: From Venlo to <entity id="org:gemeente-almere">Almere</entity> and from <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> to <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>: tomorrow Sint-Maarten is celebrated in many parts of the Netherlands. Notably, not every city takes part. Why is that? "It no longer has anything to do with Catholicism."

title: Possible burglars brought down from roof with cherry picker in Groningen
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested seven possible burglars in Groningen. They were brought down with a cherry picker from the fire brigade. The suspects have been arrested and taken to the police station.

title: Terror suspects, including a 16-year-old from Rotterdam, prepared an attack according to prosecutors: 'Spraying with AK47'
lead: According to prosecutors, they were actively searching for Kalashnikovs and Glocks. The four terror suspects arrested last summer, including a 16-year-old from Rotterdam, reportedly wanted to 'spray' bullets during an attack.

title: Better land policy must reduce financial deficits at municipalities and speed up housing construction
Imam used WhatsApp not to call for riots, yet police came to his door
lead: Imam Azzedine Karrat had police at his door because he allegedly called for riots. That was based on a misunderstanding. According to the imam, it feels to people with a certain background and religion as if they are "under a magnifying glass". Police Rotterdam says it "deeply regrets" the incident.

title: Ferrari boss slams Leclerc after new clash: lack of respect
lead: LAS VEGAS (ANP/RTR) - Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur has sharply criticised Charles Leclerc after the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Monegasque again caused a collision with teammate Lewis Hamilton. "Frankly, I find this completely unacceptable and it shows a lack of respect. A lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, but above all for the people who work on the car."
